text:
Nov 8, 1800. Washington, D.C. A fire breaks out next door to the War Department, spreads, and burns nearly every military record the young United States had. Much of the paper trail of the Revolution went up in one night.

The government had only just moved to the new capital that year. The city was still mostly woods and mud. The War Department was set up in a three story building on Pennsylvania Avenue, not far from the unfinished White House where John Adams had moved in a week earlier.

On the night of Nov 8, a fire started in a neighboring building. It jumped to the War Office. Clerks and neighbors tried to save what they could, but most of it was gone: letters, orders, accounts, records of Indian affairs, records of the Army and Navy since 1784, and many of the papers left over from the Revolutionary War.

Two weeks later, Secretary of War Samuel Dexter wrote that all the papers in his office had been destroyed.

The losses hit real people. Starting in 1818, Congress offered pensions to veterans of the Revolution who could prove their service. But many of the records that would have proven it were ashes. Old men in their 60s, 70s, and 80s had to piece together their service from memory, sworn statements, old discharge papers if they'd kept them, and testimony from surviving comrades. Their applications, full of personal memories of the war, are now some of the richest sources historians have.

Then it happened again. In August 1814, during the War of 1812, British troops captured Washington and burned the Capitol, the White House, and other government buildings. More records were lost.

For decades the federal government had very few original records from the Revolutionary army at all. In 1873, the War Department started buying collections back from private hands, including papers kept by Timothy Pickering, a Revolutionary officer who'd served as adjutant general and quartermaster general. Over time, records from other agencies and states were gathered and copied. In 1938 the collection went to the National Archives.

The story has a modern twist. Historians spent years tracking down copies of the War Department's lost papers that had survived in other archives and libraries, letters that had been sent out before the fire. Tens of thousands of them have now been reconstructed and put online in a project called the Papers of the War Department.

The fire of 1800 burned the originals. It took two centuries to start getting them back.

The etymology of Barbelon can refer to a few different concepts depending on whether you mean the Gnostic figure Barbelo (frequently seen with variant or inflected endings like Barbelōn in Greek texts) or the surname Barbelon / Babilon. 

1. Barbelo / Barbelōn (Gnostic Aeon)
In Gnostic texts (such as the Apocryphon of John and other Nag Hammadi writings), Barbelo is the supreme female principle, the first emanation or "first thought" (Ennoia) of the invisible Spirit. 
Scholars and ancient writers have proposed several possible etymologies for the name:
Barba-Elo: A composite derivation suggesting "God the Father/Mother" or a Semitic-influenced root (combining barba / bar with Elo / Elohim).
Paravela / Parthenos: Theories connecting the name to Greek words for virginity or higher/transcendent principles (parthenos meaning virgin).
Balal: A Hebrew-derived or Semitic root connected to mixing or mingling.
Coptic Origins: Connections to Coptic terms or verbs like berber (meaning "to overflow" or "to boil over"), which matches her role as the overflowing, generative first thought of God from which creation spills forth.
Greek Inflection: In Greek Gnostic manuscripts, the name often appears in oblique cases with an -ōn or -ōnos ending (e.g., Barbelōn), leading to "Barbelon" in certain translations or later discussions. 

2. Surname Etymology (Barbelon / Babilon)
As a family name, Barbelon (or its variant Babilon) has roots tied to lineage and geography: 
Hebrew and European Roots: Some genealogical sources trace the surname Barbelon to the Hebrew element bar (meaning "son of") combined with a personal or place name (Belon), suggesting a patronymic or locational origin within Jewish diaspora communities in Europe, particularly Eastern Europe.
Connection to Babylon: Phonetically and historically, forms like Babilon trace back to the ancient Mesopotamian city of Babylon (from Akkadian bāb-ilu, meaning "Gateway of God"), which occasionally adapted into various continental European surnames.

Night of the Living Dead is a 1968 American zombie horror film directed, photographed, and edited by George A. Romero, written by Romero and John Russo, and produced by Russell W. Streiner and Karl Hardman. The independent film's ensemble cast—which includes Duane Jones, Judith O'Dea, Marilyn Eastman, Karl Hardman, Judith Ridley, and Keith Wayne—star as a group of people trapped in a farmhouse in rural Pennsylvania, under assault by flesh-eating reanimated corpses. Although the monsters that appear in the film are referred to as "ghouls", they are credited with popularizing the modern portrayal of zombies in popular culture.

Plot
Siblings Barbra and Johnny drive to a cemetery in rural Pennsylvania to visit their father's grave, where a pale man in a tattered suit kills Johnny and attacks Barbra. Fleeing to a nearby farmhouse, she finds the resident's corpse lying half-eaten on the stairs. A growing horde of ghouls surrounds the house as a stranger, Ben, arrives and initially mistakes Barbra for the homeowner. After driving back several ghouls, he boards the windows and doors. A traumatized Barbra falls into a near catatonic state, forcing Ben to look after her. While searching the home for supplies, he locates a lever-action rifle upstairs.

Barbra is surprised to find people already taking shelter in the home's cellar. Harry Cooper, his wife Helen, and their young daughter Karen fled there after ghouls overturned their car and bit Karen on the arm, leaving her seriously ill. A teenage couple, Tom and Judy, took shelter after hearing an emergency broadcast while they were at a nearby lake. Tom and Ben secure the farmhouse while Harry protests that it is unsafe above ground, before returning to the cellar. Tension rises in the group as more of the ghouls arrive to besiege the farmhouse.

Through radio and TV reports, the survivors learn that cannibalistic corpses, referred to as "ghouls", are reanimating and committing mass murder across the East Coast of the United States and that posses of armed men are patrolling the countryside to exterminate the living dead. Reports confirm that the ghouls can die again from heavy blows to the head, bullets to the brain, or being burned. Various rescue centers offer refuge and safety, and scientists theorize that radiation from an exploding space probe returning from Venus caused the reanimations.

John D. “Jay” Rockefeller IV, the progeny of one of America’s most famous and wealthiest families who during three decades in the U.S. Senate sought expanded healthcare for the poor and excoriated President George W. Bush’s handling of the Iraq war, died on Friday at his home in Washington, the Washington Post reported. He was 89.

His ⁠family did not provide a cause, the newspaper added.

Rockefeller, a tall, soft-spoken Democrat with liberal views, was elected in 1984 to the first of his five six-year terms representing West Virginia in the Senate after two terms as ​governor of the poor coal-mining state.

Rockefeller voted in ​2002 in favor of the Republican Bush’s measure authorizing ​the Iraq war, which began with a U.S.-led invasion in 2003. He later expressed regret over that vote and, as head of the Senate intelligence committee, accused Bush of taking the nation to war on “false premises.”

He was a great-grandson of oil tycoon John D. Rockefeller and the scion of a family that formed a political dynasty that included his uncle, New York Governor Nelson Rockefeller.

New ⁠York-born Jay ‌Rockefeller’s life changed direction after he graduated from Harvard and served in a national service program in ⁠impoverished rural West Virginia from 1964 to 1966.

When he was put in public office, he worked to increase healthcare access, fight poverty, provide health benefits to coal miners and assist military veterans. As a senator, he had a role in shaping the program created in 1997 under which the U.S. government helps states provide medical coverage for millions of uninsured children.

Rockefeller backed Democratic President Bill Clinton’s failed proposal for near-universal health insurance coverage in the ‌1990s and then fought for Democratic President Barack Obama’s successful quest for a healthcare overhaul law, signed in 2010.

In the debate over Obama’s measure, Rockefeller unsuccessfully sought to have the federal government offer a medical insurance program to the general population — in addition to existing programs for the poor and elderly — as an alternative ​to private insurance plans that could be costly and exclusive.

“Championing those most in need has been my life’s calling and I will never stop fighting to make a difference for the people who mean so much to me,” Rockefeller said in 2013 when he announced at age 75 he would not seek a sixth Senate term.

Before the Iraq invasion, Bush’s administration built the case for war by touting intelligence indicating Iraq owned an arsenal of weapons of mass destruction — they actually did ⁠not exist — and alleged ties between Iraqi leaders and the al Qaeda network responsible for the September 11, 2001, attacks on the U.S.

“If I had known then what I know now, I would have voted against it,” ‌Rockefeller told the Charleston Gazette newspaper in 2004, referring to the 2002 war authorization measure.

“I think the intelligence was ‌shaped,” he continued. “And I think the interpretation of the intelligence was shaped. You had a president who we now know was determined to go to war.”

‘Fundamentally misleading’
A report from the intelligence committee issued in 2008, when he served as its chairman, asserted that Bush, Vice President Dick Cheney and other leading officials exaggerated intelligence findings and ignored disputes within U.S. intelligence circles about Iraq’s weapons and the hotly disputed ties to al ⁠Qaeda.

The report rejected pre-war statements by Bush and Cheney that Iraq might give al Qaeda weapons of mass destruction.

“Representing to the American people that the ⁠two had an operational partnership and posed a single, indistinguishable threat was fundamentally misleading and led the nation to war on false premises,” Rockefeller said as the ⁠report was released.

During his Senate tenure, he also headed the Commerce, Science, and Transportation and Veterans Affairs committees.

Rockefeller was born on June 18, 1937, weeks after the death of his great-grandfather, who had been America’s richest man.

The Rockefeller name came with high expectations. His father was ​a famous philanthropist. His uncle Nelson served as U.S. vice president, as well as governor of ‌New York. His uncle David Rockefeller headed Chase Manhattan Bank and uncle Winthrop Rockefeller was governor of Arkansas.

He was elected to West Virginia’s legislature in 1966 before age 30, then elected West Virginia’s secretary of state in 1968.

He lost a bid to become governor in 1972, then served as a college president before being elected governor in 1976. Rockefeller, who became one of the wealthiest members of the U.S. Congress, spent millions of dollars of his own money to bankroll his successful campaign for the U.S. Senate in 1984.

Rockefeller sometimes found himself overshadowed by his state’s other senator, Robert Byrd, who died in ​2010 at age 92 as the longest-serving member of Congress in U.S. ‌history.

He usually backed his state’s coal and steel industries but angered coal executives in 2012 by fighting Republican efforts to prevent regulation of emissions from coal-fired power plants.

He was married to public television executive Sharon Percy Rockefeller, with whom he had four ​children.

President Trump just dropped another bombshell on Truth Social. He offered the White House Press Secretary job to Dana White, the longtime UFC CEO and one of the most no-nonsense figures in America. Trump called White a "violent Fighter and Warrior" and made the pitch clear: we need someone who will not roll over for the media. He even asked White to bring along top UFC fighters as aides to help defend the administration against what he called the Lunatic Left.

White did not shut it down. He posted a photo of himself standing at the White House briefing room podium with the caption "On to the next chapter." Hours later, at a press conference in London, he told reporters he was flying straight to Washington for a meeting with Trump on Monday. He noted that he already has plenty of jobs, but he never said no.

text:
Key eligibility rules
The official must have served at least one full year of the current term before a recall petition can be offered for filing.​
Ballotpedia
After one recall petition and election against the same officer during a term, no further recall can be filed against that person for the remainder of the term.​
Ballotpedia
As of November 8, 2026, incumbent Gov. Tony Evers (term ending early January 2027) has long met the one-year requirement. Governor-elect David Crowley (elected November 3, 2026) will take office around January 4, 2027, and would not be subject to recall until after one year in office.​
Jsonline
Signature requirement
Valid signatures of qualified electors equal to at least 25% of the votes cast for the office of governor in the last preceding gubernatorial election, statewide (for the governor).​
law.justia
Based on the 2022 election (~2,656,490 total votes), this is roughly 664,123 valid signatures. The exact figure is determined by the filing officer using official canvass results. Once the 2026 election results are the “last preceding,” the threshold will update to 25% of those votes.​
Uselectionatlas
Basic steps
Register the effort: A qualified elector (U.S. citizen, 18+, resident of the relevant district for the required period) must file a campaign registration statement and a Statement of Intent to Circulate a Recall Petition with the proper filing officer before circulating any petitions. For statewide offices such as governor, this is typically the Wisconsin Elections Commission / Secretary of State office (the same officer who receives nomination papers). Circulating before proper registration invalidates signatures.​
law.justia
Circulate the petition:
Petitions must be clearly headed “RECALL PETITION.”
Circulation is limited to 60 days from the date of registration. The completed petition must be offered for filing by 5:00 p.m. on the 60th day.
Only signatures dated within that 60-day window count. Each sheet needs a completed Certification of Circulator.
Signers must be qualified electors of the relevant jurisdiction.​
Ballotpedia
File and verification: The petition is filed with the same officer. The officer reviews it for sufficiency. The targeted official has a short window to challenge; petitioners can rebut. If certified as sufficient, a recall election is ordered.​
law.justia
Recall election: Held on the Tuesday of the 6th week after the certificate of sufficiency (or the next non-holiday if needed). The incumbent continues in office until results are declared and is automatically a candidate unless they decline within 10 days. Other candidates may file as in a special election. For partisan offices, it generally functions as a regular election for the remainder of the term; a primary may apply in certain multi-candidate nonpartisan situations. The winner serves the rest of the term.

text:
🇮🇳🪂 MARTIN-BAKER TO BUILD EJECTION SEATS IN KARNATAKA

📌 WHAT: British ejection seat maker Martin-Baker to invest ₹380 crore in an aircraft ejection seat manufacturing facility in Karnataka
🏢 WHO: Martin-Baker Aircraft Co. (UK) | Announced by Karnataka Industries Minister M.B. Patil
📅 WHEN: Announced Nov 2026

🎯 WHAT IS THIS?
An ejection seat is what saves a fighter pilot's life when a jet is going down: a rocket-powered seat that blasts the pilot clear and opens a parachute within seconds.

📊 KEY FACTS
• Investment: ₹380 crore (as announced)
• Jobs: 500+ expected
• Builds on Martin-Baker's existing presence in Bengaluru

💺 WHICH SEAT DOES TEJAS USE?
• Model: Martin-Baker IN16G, an Indian version of the Mk16 family
• Fitted on: Tejas Mk1 & Mk1A
• Proven: Tejas pilots have ejected safely using it, including in the 2024 Jaisalmer crash
• Next-gen: Mk18 seat offered for Tejas Mk2 (production), AMCA & TEDBF

⚙️ TECH SPECS (Mk16 family, typical)
• Zero-zero capability: saves the pilot even on the ground at zero speed
• Works up to ~600 knots airspeed
• Rocket motor lifts the seat high & clear of the aircraft
• Electronic sequencer automatically picks the right sequence for speed & height
• ~2.5 seconds from handle pull to parachute
• Lightweight design for modern fighters

✈️ MARTIN-BAKER IN INDIA
• Seats also fitted on IAF Hawk trainers & Jaguars
• Planned (2025) to maintain & manufacture IAF seats from Bengaluru
• Martin-Baker seats have saved over 7,800 lives worldwide

⚡ WHY IT MATTERS
• Making life-critical seats in India means faster supply, repair & support
• Huge pipeline: Tejas Mk1A, Mk2 & AMCA will all need seats
• Builds a high-skill safety-systems supply chain in India

🧠 OUR ANALYSIS
Every fighter India builds needs a seat that works perfectly, every time. Local manufacturing by the world leader is a big step. The next goal should be real technology transfer, so Indian firms can design seats too.

❓ WHAT WE DON'T KNOW
• Exact location & timeline of the plant
• Level of technology transfer

Ezekiel 5-6 & Hebrews 13 | November 9th | 2026 Global Bible Journey

Experience the Word of God in a new, immersive way.
It’s About Growth, Not a Checklist

As we continue through November 2026, remember that this journey is about genuine spiritual growth, not just "checking a box" for the day. Our goal is to let these scriptures transform our perspective and our priorities. If you missed a few days or are just joining us for the first time—don’t worry! Just jump right in with us today. The path to growth is always open, and there is no "behind" in this study.

Today’s Reading

In Ezekiel 5–6, the sobering reality of divine judgment is dramatically portrayed as Ezekiel is commanded to shave his head and beard with a sword, dividing the hair into thirds to signify the destruction, scattering, and exile awaiting Jerusalem due to her flagrant rebellion and idolatry. Chapter 6 pronounces judgment upon the mountains and high places of Israel, tearing down pagan altars so that the remnant who escapes among the nations will remember the Lord and know that He alone is God. In Hebrews 13, the letter concludes with practical, heartfelt exhortations for Christian living: letting brotherly love continue, showing hospitality to strangers, remembering prisoners, keeping marriage honored, and remaining content with the promise that God will never leave nor forsake us. The author centers our steadfastness on Jesus Christ—the same yesterday, today, and forever—urging us to offer up a continual sacrifice of praise and to go to Him outside the camp, bearing His reproach while looking for the lasting city to come. This video is designed to help you focus on the text without distraction, featuring modern visuals and a clear, read-along experience.

Join the Global Community

This project is an outreach of the Richmond Church of Christ in Kentucky, connecting brothers and sisters from across the globe—including our communities in Nigeria, India, and South Africa. While our videos are "text-first," our teaching and discussions reflect the views we espouse at our local congregation.

Read With Us—Don't read alone!

text:
Linda Evangelista, the supermodel who said "we don't wake up for less than $10,000 a day," sued the maker of CoolSculpting for $50 million. She says the fat-freezing treatment left her "brutally disfigured."

CoolSculpting is made by Zeltiq Aesthetics, a company owned by Allergan. She went in to lose fat. Her lawsuit says the fat grew instead.

I wrote up the full record below.

October 1990: In Vogue, about herself and Christy Turlington, she says: "We don't wake up for less than $10,000 a day."

August 2015 to February 2016: She has seven CoolSculpting treatments.

Around June 2016: She is diagnosed with PAH, a rare side effect in which the treated fat hardens and grows.

Then came the offer. Her lawsuit says Zeltiq would pay for corrective surgery only if she signed a non-disclosure agreement. She refused and paid for it herself.

September 2021: She goes public on Instagram. "PAH has not only destroyed my livelihood," she writes. "I have become a recluse." She sues Zeltiq for $50 million in federal court in New York.

July 2022: She settles. The amount has never been disclosed.

The case for Zeltiq: PAH is listed on its own website as a possible side effect, and she chose a cosmetic treatment seven times.

The case for Evangelista: her lawsuit says she was never warned, and she refused to stay quiet even when silence came with free surgery.

$50 million is 5,000 days at the rate she once named. A fair price for what she lost, or did she take the risk when she signed up?

text:
Every couple of months like clockwork, crypto twitter suddenly discovers a new panic thread asking if MEXC is about to implode. You see the exact same pattern repeat across your feed. Someone posts a screenshot of a restricted withdrawal, someone else claims their profitable futures balance got wiped under an abnormal trading rule, and immediately people start wondering if user funds are actually safe or if another exchange domino is wobbling.

To understand what is actually happening right now, you have to separate two completely different types of risk: actual platform insolvency and aggressive counterparty risk management. When retail asks if their money is safe, they usually mean is MEXC going to pull an FTX and vanish overnight with user deposits. But the reality of what most people are experiencing on the ground is something much more mundane and yet deeply frustrating for traders.

MEXC carved out its entire market share by doing what larger, heavily regulated exchanges refuse to do. They list every single microcap token, meme coin, and experimental asset within minutes of launch. They offer rock-bottom fees, zero fee promotions on spot pairs, and leverage multiples that would give compliance officers at Western institutions a nervous breakdown. That exact business model attracts two specific demographics: everyday degen retail chasing fifty-x leverage, and sharp arbitrageurs exploiting pricing inefficiencies across thin order books.

That second group is where almost all the horror stories originate. Over the past couple of years, nearly every major complaint about frozen funds or clawed back balances traces back to MEXC enforcing its risk control terms of service. When an account makes massive profits trading illiquid pairs, low-cap perpetuals, or rapid latency arbitrage, the risk engine flags it. The platform freezes the balance, initiates extended manual review, and in some documented cases, zeroes out profits by citing market manipulation or abnormal trading activity.

Is that a sign that the exchange is broke? Not necessarily. It is a sign of an offshore platform aggressively defending its own house book against toxic order flow and predatory trading strategies. If an exchange has to act as the counterparty or provide internal liquidity to exotic pairs that have no organic depth, they will protect their balance sheet first before they honor an adversarial trader payout. Whether you think that practice is fair or completely unethical, it is operational reality, not an indicator of sudden systemic bank run insolvency.

When it comes to pure solvency, on-chain balances and third-party tracking have consistently shown substantial proof of reserves across major assets like USDT, Bitcoin, and Ethereum. The exchange has weathered multiple severe market drawdowns, massive cascading liquidations, and waves of coordinated FUD withdrawals without halting general network processing. Ordinary deposits and regular spot withdrawals for average users continue to clear through automated rails every single day. If there were a balance sheet hole of catastrophic proportions, general withdrawals on mainstream chains would simply freeze across the board, and that has not happened.

However, saying an exchange is solvent does not mean your money is completely safe in the way a traditional bank account is safe. There is zero legal recourse for an offshore account holder if things turn sour. Regulatory pressure is tightening globally, from European MiCA frameworks pushing non-compliant operators to the fringes, to regional enforcement actions forcing sudden geo-blocking and mandatory KYC upgrades. If you wake up tomorrow and your jurisdiction gets abruptly blacklisted, your account might get locked behind mandatory verification tiers you cannot pass.

The real issue is that far too many people treat centralized exchanges as high-yield savings accounts or permanent custodians. You should never be parking long-term portfolio capital on a venue whose primary value proposition is listing obscure shitcoins and offering high leverage. An exchange is an execution terminal, not a vault. You deposit the exact capital you need for the trade, you take the trade, and the moment you close out the position, you sweep the capital back to a self-custody wallet where you hold your own private keys.

If you are an average trader using the platform to flip spot tokens or manage reasonable derivatives positions, your daily funds are operating normally under standard platform liquidity. But if you keep your life savings there, hold millions in unhedged assets, or try to run aggressive latency arbitrage strategies across illiquid books, you are taking an unnecessary gamble with platform risk. Manage your counterparty exposure accordingly, stop leaving dormant funds on centralized rails, and trade defensively.

It is important that My followers keep alert to any new pope that may come forward for he will not be from God. Please urge all My sacred servants to prepare for the terrible challenges, the most daunting they will ever have to face in their ministry. It will take great courage to stand up to the Truth of My Teachings. So many of My sacred servants are blind to the promises I made, when I said I would come again. When did they think this would be? So used are they to reciting My Teachings that they have forgotten that they may witness these events at any time and, perhaps, even in their own lifetime. For this is one of the greatest challenges today.

If I sent prophets into the world thousands of years ago, then of course, I will send them again in the period to prepare the world for when I will come again.

Wake up to the lessons you teach your congregation. Realise that it is I who speaks to you now. Many will come in My Name, but few will speak the Truth. This Message comes from Me, your Divine Saviour. Pray for the discernment to recognise My True Voice when it is given to you. Open your hearts now and listen to what I have to tell you. The time has come, to inform you, that the prophecies contained in the Book of Revelation are about to unfold before your eyes.

You, My beloved servants, must fight with bravery, through your love for Me, against the obstacles placed by the deceiver that will challenge you to the end of your endurance. You must acknowledge that the false prophet is about to seduce you. Charm you. Convince you that he represents the Truth. You must now show your allegiance to Me, and My Eternal Father. Please do not despair. For although these events will frighten you and disturb you, your allegiance and loyalty must be to Me.

For the first time in your ministry, your faith will be truly tested now. The Church of Peter is My Church. But when the Keys are handed back to God the Father, which they will be now, the Church becomes part of My Kingdom. I Am the Truth. Follow the Truth at all times.

Pray to Me now, for the graces required to ensure you will rise above the deceit of Satan in time. Otherwise the false prophet will ensnare My beloved children through his charismatic, charmful ways, the ways of the deceiver, with whom he is entangled. Satan will not win over My Church if My servants are alert to the deceit and see it for what it is. A diabolical lie, from which, if you become involved and swear allegiance to this new abomination, there will be no return!

Hear Me now. Turn to Me for guidance and the special graces required to lead My flock back to Me and My Heavenly Father. For when you do, I will bestow such graces that it will not be long before you will find the strength to defend My Word, at all costs.

I love you all and yearn for your support during these end times.
Jesus Christ

text:
Immortalis Book One: The Jester and The Immoless
Act One

Scene XII: The Immoless and The Jester

The 1stDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
The Shipwreck Sombre, Sapari

Allyra woke on her shipwreck. It was her shipwreck because no one else wanted it, and Allyra adored the sea. The shipwreck sat wedged on the rocks surrounding the Clachdhu Beacon. The interior was largely intact, and Allyra had provided furnishings for the galley, which she used as a torture chamber for uncooperative lords and vampires, and her cabin.

She awoke on deck surrounded by bottles that she was not entirely convinced she had drunk from. The bottles were empty and rolling about by her feet. She looked up at the cloudy sky, but the air was not chilling and there were no signs of rain. Allyra could not remember how she got to the ship. Her baers often accompanied her, but their nobby was visibly absent as was the sounds of their loud voices. Both Banshee and BaerNedi talked far more loudly than necessary, especially after a drop of rum, whisky, ale, or all three.

Equally, there was no indication of any resident vampire ready for torture. No screams, no threats, no complaining. The only noticeable sound was the sweet lull of the sea crashing around the ship and rocks.

Allyra’s head thrummed as if she had drunk excessively, but a quick breath test on her hand proved she had not, and there was a dizziness about her that caused her eyes to wander in all directions, one on the mast, the other on the stern.

She forced herself to stand and shuffled to the bulwark where she leaned on the wood and stared out towards the archipelago of Sihr. Her eyes closed and she imagined herself living alone, in peaceful solitude, self-sufficient, independent, and happy in the fort that rose from Sihr’s rocks and glistened between the crystal sky and its reflection in the mirrored surface of the sea.

She had heard tales of the eccentric necromancer who lived on Sihr from the baers and her father, but she believed there was enough room for the both of them, even if the necromancer was a sadistic lunatic. She even envisaged dividing his palace down the middle with shared facilities where necessary. Occasionally she considered refitting The Sombre and living on board, docked at one of the islands adjacent to the necromancer’s home, and reasoned that he could not argue with that.

Her impending death gave her free reign to imagine whatever she wished, since it was not likely to happen anyway.

Nicolas sat on the mast watching. He had lowered his hood and crouched like a raven. Observing.

Allyra drummed her fingers on the wood. She was used to her turns and blackouts, and used to waking up in strange places, so it did not phase her. In her mind Sihr whispered her name.

Nicolas stepped off of the mast and floated down behind her, silently. His breath warmed her neck, but she did not turn or speak, just waited to see what her companion would do. As she waited her hand slid to the hilt of her dagger. Nicolas watched its subtle journey,
‘That won’t work on me, Immoless,’ he whispered.
Allyra turned, but there was no one there. She closed her eyes tightly, opened them and blinked a few times, then removed her boots as softly as possible and took a slow walk about the deck.

The two suns cast a deep amber kiss on the mast.

A scuffle alerted her to one of the old kegs that she used as a seat. She crept over to it and flung open the lid. It was empty. An albatross circled above, then landed in the crow’s nest. Allyra sighed.

‘Why do you stare at Sihr?’ The voice asked.
Allyra took a deep breath, hoping that her episodes were not worsening, then elected to answer. Either someone was listening, and she did not want them to think she was easily spooked, or she was going insane and it would be rude not to answer herself,
‘It’s my dream,’ she sighed, ‘I can escape the Electi there, and in my mind, I can live in peace. I can watch the tide and listen to the gulls. I can swim in the crisp waters and hide in my own turret. I could wake every morning knowing that I was safe, and the ocean would give me company.’

Breath warmed her neck again,
‘You would be lonely.’
She turned full circle but could see no one.
‘I have been lonely since I lost my mother. She was my best friend and the Electi killed her. Slit her throat in front of me. All she did was love my father. That is all. And now, it’s my turn. Which doesn’t matter as I’m already losing my mind. Perhaps death will be a relief.’
‘That is a terrible thing to say!’
Allyra shuddered and put her head in her hands. Her eyes closed and she muttered to herself,
‘Voices in my head, voices in my head, voices in my head.’
She looked about her again and thought of Chester worrying about her disappearance. She thought of her father frantically combing through the house, and she thought of her death in the dungeons of a hungry demon.

Her mind drifted in a hazy lake of confusion. Her body wandered back to the bulwark, and she stared at the furious sea below, fighting frantically against the immovable rocks.

The mesmerism, Allyra’s ‘turns,’ always caused a deep melancholy; a hangover of sorts, which was all consuming. The melancholy, the dreams, and the dreary expectations of her personal sacrifice sickened her. Knowing that her own father stood as an Electi priest willing to throw her to the jaws of the Immortalis sickened her. Her man happy to share her around whilst indulging his libido with other women also sickened her, although she considered it unfair on Chester to complain. A single tear leaked from her left eye.

‘Why are you sad?’ The voice whispered again, closer than before. Allyra startled and turned, but no one was there,
‘I was in the tavern today, and there were families there. Sitting together, belonging to each other. My so-called family just want me to die. I had a plan but it’s stupid. Just a stupid idea.’
‘What plan?’ Nicolas asked, blowing the hair on her neck. Allyra did not bother to turn,
‘It seemed so clever a few days ago, now it has melted into a complex mess.’
‘How so?’
‘Today has just been… Strange. I want it all to just be over with.’
‘You WANT to die?’
Allyra sighed,
‘I don’t want to exist like this. I had so many dreams.’
‘What dreams?’ The voice called from the mast. Allyra looked up. Only the albatross looked back at her,
‘Silly dreams. They change with the tide. I thought I might be an admiral of a fleet or a great warrior. I should like to learn music, or medicine, perhaps one day be a mother and grandmother. I always wanted to ride a wild beast, dive to the depths of the ocean, write my own book, go to a circus, drop into the lowest levels of the mines and swim in their cool waters, fight with a sword in hand, have an operational ship rather than a wreck, but all I have been learning is how to survive, and that’s thanks to my baers, not to the Electi. I have never been to a theatre, such things that people take for granted. And on days like today, I dream of sleeping at the bottom of the sea, but even those dreams have monsters.’

Allyra turned and headed back to the pile of kegs, and opened one, pulling out a small bottle of Ashurrel wine. She tore the cap off with her teeth and took a slug, then returned to the bulwark and perched the bottle on the handrail,
‘Cheers to the voices in my head.’
The voice did not answer.

Allyra closed her eyes and slumped down with her back pressing into the wood. She inhaled the sea air slowly, not noticing the crafty hand that squirted some obnoxious green fluid from a pipette into her drink.
‘What was your plan, Immoless?’ The voice whispered again.
Allyra jumped and opened her eyes,
‘I don’t call myself Immoless, not even in my most insane moments because I am not a true Immoless.’
‘What was your plan?’
‘It’s stupid.’
‘Tell me anyway.’
‘The plan was to use Irkallan contract law and force one or another of the Immortalis to protect me, whilst I seek, shall we say, my own path to freedom by ridding myself of my position as Immoless.’ Allyra stood up again and took a long drink from her bottle, ‘Like I said, stupid.’

Nicolas considered her plan,
‘It’s not half as stupid as the Electi sending two Immolesses to Corax at once, is it?’
‘What?’ Allyra snapped. ‘Now, I know you’re not in my mind, Mr Voice. Do you know why? I did not know they had dispatched Lucia. Where are you? Come out or I will find you.’ She finished the bottle of intoxicated wine, as Allyra was not one to turn down alcohol, then searched the ship.

First, she checked the mast and crow’s nest, where Bigglesworth’s fat albatross sat, then circled back and forth about the deck before descending into the galley and the lower quarters, opening every drawer, cupboard, and ottoman that she had lovingly placed in her private home. Finally, she went to her cabin.

Allyra had decked her cabin out in purple textures, a double bed, and some bizarre wall tapestries that she had sewn herself which showcased pictures of tentacle laden sea monsters.

Finding nothing and no one, she did another circuit of the ship shouting,
‘Hello?’ No one answered. She was not worried about The DarkBadb Brotherhood hearing as the waves drowned out any noise between the beacon and the ship, and the DarkBadb suffered from severe selective hearing problems anyway.

She returned to her bottle only to find it full again. Allyra scratched her head. On the label in crude yellow pen the words ‘drink me’ beckoned
‘Don’t mind if I do!’ Allyra nodded, tipping the lot down her throat. Her brain fogged momentarily, and she went woozy, spinning slightly. Allyra steadied herself, then headed back to her cabin. She stripped off and climbed into her bed. Her eyes closed, and a sinking feeling soothed her troubled soul.

No sooner had she started to drift off when the voice came again, and, as it spoke, the side of the bed next to her dipped.
‘I have a proposition for you, Madam.’
Allyra opened her eyes and glanced sideways. A man was laying next to her, quite comfortably, his hands rested behind his head and his feet crossed at the bottom of the bed. His cane hung on the bedpost, and his orange and green suit unashamedly bore a nice big hole in the crotch.

‘YOU!’ Allyra snapped.
‘Now, Madam Immoless, don’t start that aggression again, it’s unbecoming in someone of your sex!’
‘You were at my house. Did you bring me here?’
‘Do I look like I can fly?’ Nicolas asked.
‘No, but I was at home, with Ches. What did you do with Ches?’
‘Nothing, we tossed a coin and Ches said I could take you.’
‘What rubbish,’ Allyra snorted.
‘Anyway, Madam, I have a proposition for you and that’s what matters, not your personal problems with your men friends, which I don’t approve of by the way. No need to go around sharing yourself like a lemon tart, is there?’
Allyra leaned up on her elbow,
‘I didn’t ask for your opinion. I don’t even know you, and in my opinion what I do is none of your business!’

Nicolas mulled over Allyra’s comments, then decided that she was simply wrong. It was his business,
‘Madam, Confusius informed you of our impending nuptials, and our nuptials shall arise soon enough. Yes, they shall. You will fight it, of course, and as a gentleman I expect that of a lady, but I strongly suggest you do not fight hard enough to irritate my good selves as we shall return in kind any such transgressions.’
‘I’m imagining strangely insane men now!’ Allyra muttered.

Nicolas looked around the room,
‘Where, Madam? Worry not, I shall defend your honour gallantly.’
Allyra slowly put her hand out and poked Nicolas’s chest,
‘You’re real!’
As she spoke, Nicolas clasped her hand and pressed it against his firm body,
‘A declaration of love on your part, a touch, most welcome.’
‘What?’ Allyra asked, ‘I was checking if you were real.’
‘No, my love, you were checking out my fine body.’
‘I can see your fine body through the inappropriate hole in your pants,’ Allyra replied.
‘Oh yes that, well you see there was this tribute and she was not being particularly nice to me, she was a little spiteful. You know the sort, and one thing led to another, and I had to get Chives to order a new suit. But fear not, I shall be selecting your wedding dress, not Chives. I gave him two days, by which I meant today, so tomorrow you will see me in all my finery.’

The drink, and Nicolas’s added secret sauce, caused Allyra’s eyes to blink and she lay supine. Nicolas moved close to her. Very close.
‘I have heard your plan, and I am willing to offer you a counterplan, come to Corax with me and be my bride. If you agree, I shall show you what a gracious lord I am and permit you to live!’
‘You’re Nicolas DeSilva!’ Allyra cried out.
Nicolas’s face lit up, and his whole being quivered with excitement,
‘Yes, see you’re not as slow as Confusius said. He thought you were a bit simple, said you struggle to open doors, but he did inform me that he relayed the message concerning our marriage quite clearly, and that you went down on him. That’s no way for a lady to behave, especially when she is already betrothed. He hinted you have a sex addiction as you got quite excited, Smythe concurs. I said, ‘Good for her, when is it my turn?’ Because one likes to sample the goods before buying them.’
Allyra frowned,
‘What’s wrong with you?’

Nicolas put his arm around her and pulled her close to his body. Allyra attempted to resist, but her body was too weak from the alcohol, amongst other noxious substances,
‘I am a god, Madam. Your superior in every way, and I get lonely. We all do, so we decided to lower ourselves and marry you. That way, I shall be happy. I think we should consider tonight our first official, official date as opposed to just the official date as we have already had one of those.’

Allyra yawned,
‘Shouldn’t you ask me on a date or something? Isn’t that how these things go?’
‘I don’t have to. I have saved you the time and effort of acting coy by deciding on your behalf. You are welcome. I have not been engaged before, so you must follow my lead on all matters. Now let us commence our date by taking sex off the table, as it is unseemly on a first date, even though you have been throwing your body at men all day, which will stop,’ Nicolas hesitated, then added, ‘unless you want sex???’

Nicolas looked down at Allyra, who had fallen asleep.
‘Immoless,’ he whispered. No answer came, ‘Immoless. Immoless. Immoless.’ Nicolas grew impatient and gave Allyra a swift kick in the shin.
‘What?’ She said, as her eyes blinked open.
‘Guess you can’t sleep either, must be the excitement of our wedding.’
‘There is no wedding,’ Allyra replied, yawning again. Nicolas ignored her ladylike protests,
‘I have decided that I shall allow you, as an engagement present, to ask me any questions you see fit. To put your mind at ease.’

Allyra thought for a moment then asked,
‘Are my sisters still alive?’
Nicolas raised his eyebrows,
‘Why? Are you close?’
‘Not really. I don’t think they like me anymore than the Electi do, except my father Tempus, of course. But are they alive?’
‘Currently, yes.’ Nicolas replied, ‘But tradition dictates that they won’t be for much longer.’
‘Tradition dictates you will also kill me, am I right?’
Nicolas nodded,
‘Yes, but that is no excuse for not marrying your fiancé.’
‘I think it’s a bloody good excuse.’
Nicolas’s eyes reddened,
‘I am a god, you can’t speak to me like that, woman. You must learn your place. Shiverton raised concerns about your attitude problem, but he did say you tasted good.’
‘So, you’re going to eat me?’
‘Never say never, that’s what I say.’ Nicolas replied, ‘However, if you chose me to protect you then it would make matters easier, don’t you think?’

Nicolas did not wait for a response, instead he sat up, turned his back to Allyra, pulled a pocket watch out of his jacket, opened it, and started whispering at it,
‘I think we are getting somewhere, Webster!’
Allyra’s ears pricked up. Webster, according to some of the lords she had worried, was assumed to be Nicolas’s Evro, and a necessary part of the plan she had earlier considered foolish.
‘No, Webster,’ Nicolas continued, ‘I can’t lobotomise her, she hasn’t been dispatched and The Ledger would not approve… You know he wouldn’t approve… No, I can’t change his mind. And you need to make a stronger serum; she is all lucid and eavesdropping… Well work on it… I will tell you later… Later I said.’ Then he closed the watch, returned it to its home, and lay back down as if nothing had happened.

‘Who were you talking to?’ Allyra asked.
‘My voice of reason, Madam, he hides in my watch. Sometimes he hides in mirrors or in my laboratory, but the watch makes him portable.’
‘Are you nuts or something?’

Nicolas’s eyes rolled backwards halfway into his head leaving only half an iris and a dot of a pupil in each socket. Blood dribbled from his lips, and he let out a long low growl before responding,
‘No, Madam, I am not nuts, I am a psychiatrist. I would know if I was nuts. Dr Smythe thinks you are nuts and he says he wants you referred to Dr Dick, you may know him as Riesigerschwanz, perhaps we could have couples’ therapy.’
‘We aren’t a couple.’
‘Will you sleep with me now? We decided that even though it is improper that you might consider it, remember?’ Nicolas asked, ignoring her latest modest comment.

‘No!’ Allyra groaned.
‘But you sleep with everyone else. Everyone but your husband, poor Nicolas.’
Allyra’s foggy mind slumped on the precipice of sleep,
‘We aren’t married.’
‘You are confused again, that sort of behaviour lands you in the sea.’
Allyra’s eyes narrowed,
‘Have you been throwing me in the sea?’
‘Me? No. Of course not. What a suggestion, why would I throw my bride into the sea? I can say with a doubt or without or without a doubt’s doubt that that should be not a no. In fact, as a psychiatrist, I propose that you have been sea sailing, a common ailment among single women desperately seeking a loving spouse.’
Allyra grunted,
‘I wake up in the sea, not in a boat.’
‘You’re obviously not very good at sailing then, are you?’
Allyra rubbed her head and tried not to drift back to sleep,
‘I dream of sea monsters.’

Nicolas raised a hand,
‘One second Madam,’ and pulled a pencil and notepad from his jacket, ‘lucid dreaming, sleep-sailing, wants sex with sea monsters, blackouts, delusions, daydreams, and forgets her long-suffering spouse. Any other symptoms?’
‘I don’t want to be assessed by you or your drunk doctors. I want to be left alone!’
‘Argumentative, unreasonably hostile, suffering the ills of isolation. Have I missed anything?’
‘I’m not answering you!’
‘Silence which is not normal for her gender. Funny enough…’ Nicolas continued, ‘I diagnosed some wayward tributes as insane earlier today. Yes, one thought she was not a spider and the other desperately wanted her breasts clipped off. Sad times. Tell me, do I frighten you?’
‘Not really.’ Allyra sighed, ‘I came to terms with my fate a long time ago. Doesn’t make me happy, but it is what must be.’
‘Random bouts of melancholia,’ Nicolas added, ‘and a very poor response to potentially life threatening situations.’
‘Are you threatening me?’ Allyra asked.

Nicolas’s mouth opened and his eyebrows raised,
‘Madam, I am both hurt and offended. I have not harmed you in anyway. No, indeed. I am forced by virtue of my position and the laws of Irkalla to commit acts that seem so horrific, and it saddens me to do so, but such is the requirement for peace in the world. I sacrifice my feelings for the population. I am a philanthropist marred and soiled with a cruel reputation, not befitting of my own suffering.’
Allyra’s eyelids grew heavy,
‘None of what you say makes sense, Nicolas.’
‘Master!’ Nicolas replied.
‘Master who?’
‘No, Immoless, you must call me Master or Sir, a sign of respect for my station that is so substantially greater than yours.’
Allyra sighed,
‘How rude!’

‘How rude, Master.’ Nicolas replied.
‘You’re forgiven,’ Allyra smiled, ‘are you truly as maligned as you say.’
‘Terribly so,’ Nicolas said, his eyes widening.
‘So, you don’t murder your tributes?’
‘Murder?’ Nicolas looked astonished, ‘No madam. Murder indeed. No, they are provided with rooms, beds, water, even affection, and remain forever under Corax’s roof.’
‘Is that true?’
‘Yes.’ Nicolas said, shaking his head.
‘But you said the Immolesses are killed according to tradition.’
‘Alas, this is my brother’s burden to bear.’
Allyra held enough information to have a rudimentary, though often flawed, understanding of the Immortalis,
‘Theaten or Kane?’

Nicolas put his hand to his chin,
‘Robert.’
‘Who is Robert?’ Allyra asked.
‘The one you call Theaten. He is definitely a Robert. He has Robert’s overbite. He prizes the Immolesses and takes care of them in a humane manner. He even washes them and provides hair. They like the hair. I suspect he gives them a lot more if you know what I mean. I do not. They are too skinny for my liking. Now accept my proposition and we shall return to Corax, and you won’t have to endure the hardships destined.’
‘What hardships?’
‘Hardships that will befall you if you do not co-operate. Those hardships. Come willingly now and I shall sign a contract offering my full protection.’
Allyra rubbed her eyes and yawned,
‘Sounds like a trick or a trap.’
‘It is a kindness!’ Nicolas replied.

Allyra did not answer. Nicolas looked down at her and watched as her eyes closed. She could fight the serum no more,
‘Don’t hurt me, Nicolas,’ she whispered. ‘Not tonight.’

Nicolas did not answer. He waited until she was sleeping, then wrapped his arms about her, hung his face over hers, and held her whispering,
‘I will never let you go,’ as a sneer spread over his delighted face.

Nicolas remained hovering over Allyra in a rather unpleasant and creepy fashion until she started snoring, then he launched his romantic, contractual bombshell,
‘Immoless, I should like to propose an agreement of sorts. A truce. A contract built on the love you so obviously hide from my perceptive eyes. The Final Irkallan contract. As such, Allyra, will you marry me?’ Allyra was so entranced by his words, and in such a deep sleep, that she elected not to answer directly but allowed her silence to speak for her.

Nicolas’s smirk widened, and his eyes rolled upward,
‘Qui tacet consentire videtur, she who is silent is seen to consent.’ Allyra let out a rather loud and highly unattractive snore. Nicolas’s eyes rolled back down, and his eyebrows danced with glee, ‘I appreciate the enthusiasm, Immoless. I appreciate it very much. And tomorrow you shall offer me the same proposal, whether in truth or in jest, and it shall stand.’ Nicolas’s irises glazed over, ‘Hear me, Immoless, you shall make the same proposal tomorrow.’

Allyra fidgeted against his body, inadvertently causing an arousal in Nicolas that was quite plain to see, especially given the tattered state of his trousers. Her lips parted and she whispered,
‘I shall propose tomorrow, Nic. Tomorrow. I’m tired tonight.’
‘Then rest,’ Nicolas replied, almost as if he cared, ‘you have a long and rocky path ahead.’
‘Like Lucien Nerison,’ Allyra whispered.
Nicolas’s eyes narrowed,
‘What?’
Allyra pressed against his body, her hand drifted under his waistcoat and shirt, and pressed into his flesh,
‘Nicolas,’ she whispered, then drifted into a deeper sleep.

Nicolas took out his notebook, and noted her new declaration of love, then took the opportunity to impress upon her sleeping mind some of his other fantastic ideas.

text:
Immortalis Book One: The Jester and The Immoless
Act One

Scene XI: The Prowler

The 1stDay of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Tempus Cottage, Thanata

Chester was sleeping. Allyra had awoken to him sleeping and could not believe her luck in securing such an honest and caring boyfriend. He often slept. He called it napping, and napping was an integral part of his day.

Allyra did not know where Chester resided when he was not staying with her, and though she had raised the matter on several occasions, Chester would not disclose any personal information. This state of affairs had been going on for some five years and was a reflection of the overall state of their relationship; Chester openly slept with a plethora of women for pleasure, mainly their pleasure, and Allyra openly slept with a number of lords for information. There was no contractual agreement, but an implied agreement perpetuated nonetheless, and both parties were happy with it. Allyra could not ask for more given her impending destiny.

Allyra could not fault Chester’s attentiveness to her. He was always there when she needed him. She never had to seek him out or concern herself that he would not be by her side when she was lonely or worried. He seemed to have a sixth sense and would simply appear and stay with her for as long as needed at the required moment.

Her father Tempus did not approve, as he did not approve of a lot of her behaviour with men, or ‘menfolk’ as he called them, as if these magical, male creatures had simply sprung from some garish folktale, but he had learned to ignore Chester’s presence to an extent.

Chester did have one fault; he always curled up to sleep, like a cat, taking up most of her tiny bed. It was a double bed, as Tempus was generous in providing her with reasonable living space, a luxury other immolesses did not enjoy. Her bedroom faced the Getsug sea and offered a crisp view of the Archipelago of Sihr. Outside of her window stood an orchard where peaches and apples flourished, which Allyra nurtured faithfully under the trying conditions of the perpetual dusk.

Inside of the cottage, Allyra had her own bedroom and bathroom. The bedroom was a simple affair; a bed with purple soft sheets and blankets, an old mahogany dressing-table and chair that had seen better days, a wardrobe made of oak that made the room feel somewhat thrown together, and a bookcase next to her bed with a small oil lamp perched on top. The window had a built in window seat that Allyra had crafted herself from old pallets she had gathered from the granary stores in Thanata town, and she had crocheted a purple pillow set to sit on top of the seat for her comfort. That way, when she was not on her private shipwreck, The Sombre, she could gaze longingly at Sihr and dream of her own private island.

Allyra could not sleep as Chester was hogging all of the room. Instead, she sat reading her new book, Molluscs and Boners’ Taken by the Tentacle. Allyra’s bookshelf spread across three tiers; Molluscs and Boners’ great romantic novels, all written by Carmilla Fanu sat on the bottom shelf. The middle shelf housed books about the science of the occult and natural history, and on the top shelf a wealth of popular psychology books penned by the formidable Dr Otto Von Riesigerschwanz sat proudly. Allyra had a huge crush on Dr Riesigerschwanz, even though she had never met him personally. However, she had a current fancy for a little of the morally grey hero, not complex pop psychology.

Chester’s rapid transition from romantic prince to Rip Van Winkle had pushed Allyra’s mindset into the most romantic of moods. She loved nothing more than to read tales of tall, dark villains who would soften under the influence of true love. She had hoped that Chester would soften and offer some level of commitment but reasoned that it would be unreasonable of him to do so given that she was destined to die within a moon. Her death, Allyra believed, would cause some difficulty in sustaining a long-term relationship.

One hand held her book, whilst the other stroked Chester’s magnificent mane of red ringlets. His purple top hat, which often covered the best part of his crown, hung on Allyra’s bed post, and his nose blessed her with the sound of a purring snore. Chester liked nothing more than to be fussed by women, especially Allyra.

The windows of the bedroom stood open, so that Allyra could hear the sounds of the sea and inhale the salty air. Her curtains blew in and out in rhythm with the breeze, and Allyra teetered on the edge of the bed, leaning into the bedpost for dear life whilst reading her book.

As her clock struck ten, her reading was interrupted by a rustling of leaves. She looked up from her page, gazed out of the window, and, seeing nothing, returned to her book. Molluscs and Boners was a prolific series about big, horny, tentacled lovers who wanted nothing more than to protect the innocent heroine. Every page gifted Allyra with the dream of the perfect match, something the Electi had denied her, or at least tried to.

The Electi presented themselves as priests, but it is quite fair and academically defensible to say that they were, in fact, a death cult. During the fifth year of each century the Electi would provide additional tributes to Behmor in exchange for the rental of two demonesses. The selected demonesses were destined to give birth to Immolesses fathered by selected priests of the Electi.

On paper, the Immolesses were a weapon of the thesapiens, the people, spawned to fight the great demonic deities known as ‘The Immortalis.’ The Immolesses would be born in the sixth year and raised and allegedly trained to become great slayers. However, in practise, the training was non-existent beyond some highly fabricated classes about the Immortalis, and the general idea was the Immolesses would, on turning thirty, challenge one of the Immortalis and attempt to slay them.

The unprepared, virginial soldiers soon found that the dark princely vampires they expected were nothing of the sort, and after some excruciating torment found themselves quite dead. The thesapiens would revere the Immolesses, the Immortalis would sate their hungers, and Behmor gave the green light to raise taxes to fund next century’s spectacle. As such, Allyra’s existence was hardly worthy of any romance, dark or otherwise.

Allyra was not a virgin, as I have said, but equally, she was not one to fall in love as she had a slightly negative view of men. As paternal as Tempus tried to be, he was still planning to send her to her death. As much as the Electi feigned being kin and family, they too intended to send her to her death. Her relationship with Chester was the closest thing to love Allyra hoped to experience, and Chester was forever shagging other women.

Allyra was not entirely happy with the prospect of dying, and so, with the help of her closest friends, the great lycan baer warriors; Banshee and BaerNedi, she had created her own educational program.

The lords and vampires who held knowledge of the Immortalis were usually more than eager to trade information for a few hours of Allyra’s coital company. These experiences somewhat dampened Allyra’s view of men further, and Chester’s secrecy did not fill her with any indication that a good man would be any better than a bad one. As such, she lived vicariously through the sordid romances penned by Fanu.

Allyra was lost in a rather crude chapter involving octuple penetration, a giant squid and some nubile trollop, when another sound broke her damp concentration. This time it was not rustling that drew her from octuple-tentacle penetration, this time it was the sound of footsteps and then a clatter as if someone had fallen over one of her plant pots. Tempus Cottage sat on the west of the island, far from the towns, the mines, and the villages. Allyra had always felt safe with her windows open as no one trod in that rugged wilderness. The only night Tempus insisted on them being shut was the sixth night of every week.

On the sixth night of every week, the necromancer of Sihr, known locally as Elyas, would manifest on the nearby Inoclas Cove and retrieve his tributes. The tributes were always two women bred in the Tributiary of Thanata for one purpose: to please Elyas. By rights, tributes were only bred for Immortalis, but overtime this had drifted, and both Elyas and Count Tepes also received tributes at the Immortalis’s insistence. Lilith also received tributes, as did Ducissa Anne, Tepes’ wife. Banshee often called this ‘The Great Drift of Nicotism,’ but BaerNedi would tell her to be silent on the matter. Allyra did not understand what she meant and BaerNedi refused to discuss it, or allow Banshee to discuss it, further.

The Electi knew surprisingly little about Elyas as Elyas was quite happy minding his own business providing his tributes were chained and ready for collection on the specified day. Tempus, however, knew enough about the dangers of Elyas to yell at Allyra until she closed both her windows and the external shutters.

Outside of Tempus Cottage, the footsteps continued to trudge about, drifting to and from the window, as if the bearer of those feet was somewhat lost or mildly confused. Allyra waited. She was prone to delusions and hoped this noise could be categorised as a delusion, and not some weirdo trying to break into her home.

The footsteps continued, so eventually she sat up and swung her legs out of the bed, grinding her feet into the teak floor, just as Chester had taught her, to ground herself and ensure that she was not confused. Chester considered himself something of an expert in these matters, but Allyra had no idea why, since he claimed to work as a postman. Allyra was not convinced about either the foot grinding, or the postman story. She closed her eyes, and started to count backwards from ten, another of Chester’s psychotherapy tips that seemed dubious at best. She had barely reached five when another ruckus aroused her.

A stumbling came first, followed by something that sounded like the thud of a body falling, and then her plant pots shattering on the concrete path that surrounded the cottage.

‘Ches.’ Allyra whispered. ‘Ches, there’s someone outside.’
Chester stretched and growled,
‘Fuck off Demus, I’m having my afternoon nap.’
Allyra squinted,
‘What’s a Demus?’
Chester did not answer but instead let out a prolonged snore. Allyra tutted, and turned off the oil lamp,
‘Some help you are!’

The two suns hovered just below the horizon, depicting the night, and the moon cast light from above. A few clouds roamed about the sky, but there was more than enough light for Allyra to scope out her orchard for oddballs.

She slid off the bed, and crawled along the floor, slowly, testing every floorboard for any creaks before pressing her weight into it. As she edged towards the curtain, Allyra grasped her trusty iron rod that sat between the window and her bed, a gift from Banshee to ward off Elyas or any other threats should they arise. She gripped the rod with both hands and pressed her back into the wall beside the curtains. Her thighs elevated her to a standing position. She eased back the nearest curtain with care.

The voice and person appeared together, an over-zealous man wearing an orange and green silk lounge suit with a hood,
‘Good dusk, Madam, I was wondering…’
Allyra shrieked. The man yelled in response, mirroring her shriek. Without hesitation, Allyra drew back the rod and twatted her visitor around the head. He fell to the ground instantly,
‘Madam, that’s no way to treat a…’
Allyra hopped out of her window and gave him another crack. And another,
‘Pervert! Disgraceful pervert!’ She threw the rod back inside, then took to kicking her cloaked assailant whilst berating him, ‘Thinking you can break into my home. Me?! A poor, innocent,’ another kick caused the man to groan loudly. ‘Defenceless,’ the next kick was carefully aimed at his balls, ‘weak woman. Unable to fend for herself!’

She grabbed one of the broken plant pots and dropped it on his head. He let out another groan, then went silent.

Allyra stopped moving, only the sound of her panting and the ebbing tide could be heard. She clambered back through her window, inelegantly splattered on the floor, then jumped on Chester,
‘CHES! CHES! Wake up.’
Chester rubbed his eyes,
‘Again? You’re insatiable woman!’
Allyra shook him,
‘Ches, there is a man trying to kill me! He’s there. I think I killed him. CHES!’

Two thuds hit the wall between Allyra’s room and Tempus’s room,
‘What’s going on in there, Lyra?’ Tempus growled, ‘I hope it’s not that ginger-haired idiot!’
Chester was up like a shot, and thumped back,
‘Who are you calling an idiot, Grandpa? Why don’t you take a pill and settle down.’
Allyra sighed,
‘You’re not helping, Ches. There’s a man outside the window.’
Chester hissed, and placed his top hat on his head and his suit jacket on his back,
‘Fine, I shall take a look.’
Chester crawled from the bed, dropped to the floor, and padded to the window. Allyra followed, grasping the tails of Chester’s jacket,
‘He’s there. Do you think I killed him?’

Chester leaned out of the window,
‘There’s no one here, Lyra. No one.’
Allyra shoved Chester to one side and stared at the ground,
‘He was there; look my plant pots are broken.’
Chester turned and faced her, placing his hand under her chin,
‘Did you break them?’
‘No, why would I break my own plant pots?’
Chester nodded, knowingly,
‘In your delusion, did you use the plant pots as weapons?’
‘Yes, no. It wasn’t a delusion. He broke the plant pots, and I hit him on the head.’
Chester raised his eyebrows,
‘Lyra, there is no one there. There is no blood. Nothing. If you beat someone to such an extent you thought they were dead it is unlikely they got up and vanished, is it? Hmmm?’

Allyra dropped her head into the palm of her hand,
‘Please believe me, Ches. Please.’
Another two thuds hit the wall,
‘Keep the noise down in there!’ Tempus bellowed.

Chester lifted Allyra and carried her to the bed,
‘Look, my love, whatever happened you are safe now. I am here. I will always be here. I promise.’ He eased her head back onto the pillow, and slunk under the sheets besides her, propping himself up on one elbow.

‘There was a man outside,’ Allyra whispered, ‘there was a man…’ Her fist pressed against her forehead and two streams of tears fell from her hazel eyes, ‘Outside.’
‘Of course there was,’ Chester soothed, ‘yes, of course.’
He lifted her hair from her neck, twisted it, and laid it on the pillow. ‘Lyra, I will always be here. No one is going to hurt you.’

Allyra sat bolt upright,
‘That’s not true, Ches, soon I will be sent to die, and there is nothing you can do. I know you think it doesn’t bother me or doesn’t matter but it has been on my mind for weeks.’
Chester smiled,
‘You won’t die. You are sharp, skilled, and you’re a survivor. Whether there was a man at the window or not, you believed you had killed him. That is a testament to how strong you are! Now STOP!’
‘He was there.’ Allyra mumbled.
‘AND’ Chester barked, drowning her out, ‘you have me, you have the Baers, you have knowledge that you, YOU have discovered. You are not the same as the other Immolesses. I believe in you.’

The skull on Chester’s hat held a secret, behind the skull was a little hidden compartment. He reached up, flicked the skull down, and pulled a mini deck of cards from the hidden pocket that lay behind it.
‘Cards always calms you down. Would you like to watch me shuffle?’
‘Yes. Yes please,’ Allyra replied.
Chester tipped the cards from their box, and shuffled, then dropped them between one hand and the other. His eyes darkened, and reddened until they matched his hair,
‘Look at me,’ he ordered. Allyra’s eyes fixed on his, and her hazel irises drifted into a red hue. ‘Now,’ Chester continued, ‘watch the cards.’

The cards floated from one hand to the other forming steps. They hung in the air, then looped and grew in her face. They spun and formed cubes, then prisms, then cubes again. Chester’s fingers twitched and danced elegantly between each twist and shake, melting into the cards.

The deck grew opaque, each character or icon waltzing before Allyra’s fixed gaze. The clubs paired with the hearts, and the diamonds with the spades. The jokers laughed at her, the kings rebuked her, the queens cried, and the jacks herded the sixes about. Chester pulled three more sets of cards from the inner pocket of his jacket, and they too joined in the merriment.

Only the queens were unhappy, until the kings found them, and threatened execution for such privileged melancholy. The queens knelt, the kings rejoiced, and Chester’s cock was inside of Allyra.

Allyra could not differentiate one moment from the next. Her nightdress was wrenched up about her hips, and Chester slinked in and out of her with both stealth and carefully planned positioning. His body pressed against her in the most agonisingly sensitive manner.

The cards continued to float and turn. Chester smiled, gripping Allyra’s face. For a brief moment she fancied that he had bitten his own lip and allowed the blood to dribble into her mouth. His stride grew as he laughed and groaned. Her hips rose up to welcome his body. Her stomach ached and the ache swelled into an electricity that sparked between her thighs. Her eyes closed. She gripped the pillow.

Chester’s smile expanded. His eyes rolled back, and a long black tongue poured from his mouth. The tip caressed her breasts, focusing on each nipple, then drove down her belly and between her legs. There the tongue split into two suitors, each claiming her delicious pearl with absolute tenacity, each demonstrating an entitlement to feast on her, driving her legs to bend upwards and outwards. The sensations merged and collapsed on her. The electricity spread into lightening and Allyra screamed out a pulsing, desperate release. The cards fell. Chester quickly followed suit, then rolled off leaving Allyra in her trance.

‘Ches,’ a voice came at the window just as Chester was relishing the afterglow of his sordid, and very one-sided encounter, ‘Chester!’
Chester sat up,
‘What now, Nicolas?’
‘I want to take her to The Sombre.’
Chester sighed,
‘Why?’
‘Because she must meet her husband, otherwise she will make an awful scene at the wedding.’
Chester collected the cards that were scattered about the bed,
‘She will be confused. One minute she is here, the next on The Sombre. How about I play bad sheriff, and you play good sheriff and I take her to The Sombre, if that’s the plan.’
Nicolas pulled a silver coin from his pocket,
‘Toss you for it.’

Nicolas liked a good tossing. He liked his odds too since the coin had Nicolas’s head on both sides.
‘Fine. Toss away.’
The coin was flipped into the air, and landed on the back of Nicolas’s hand,
‘Heads!’ Nicolas snapped, revealing immediately that he had won.
‘I’m always the nice boyfriend,’ Chester mewed.
‘Then you should learn to wager better, shouldn’t you?’

Nicolas clambered through the window and stumbled on the floor.
‘Sshhh,’ Chester whispered.
Almost immediately Tempus started banging,
‘Tell that ginger prick to go home!’ He bellowed through the wall. Chester thumped back,
‘She can’t talk; she’s got her mouth full.’
Tempus muttered to himself but opted not to enter the room.

‘I’m taking her now,’ Nicolas insisted, ‘I have a plan, and then I have a backup plan. I have had a very hard day, and I can’t have all these problems hurled at me at once.’
‘Fine,’ Chester agreed, ‘Oh, I forgot to tell you, the second Immoless Lucia arrived yesterday. I didn’t know what to do with her, so I put her in one of the spare dungeons. I did mention it to Chives, but he was changing Ball’s towel and ignored me. And that’s another thing; you need to do something about Chives ignoring the Nicolai.’

Nicolas tutted,
‘I can’t have two living Immolesses roaming about Corax at once, it’s an asylum, not a hotel. What are the Electi thinking? Does Corax have ‘B and B’ signposted outside? No, it does not! And how do we know for sure she is an Immoless?’
‘She was selling dumplings and looked like an idiot.’
Nicolas smiled, but not with his eyes,
‘Fair enough. Today has been an unnecessarily busy day. Once I have seduced Allyra, OUR Immoless, I shall consult Webster and Demize, kill Stacia and give her to Theaten and then play with Lucia. I have a long-term plan for her. You will like it. My new suit should be arriving soon too.’

Chester shrugged, he didn’t care about Nicolas’s ludicrous plans, nor his new suit. He did wonder why Nicolas was walking about with a hole in his crotch, but not enough to bother asking about it.

Nicolas walked over to Allyra, carefully dressed her, and lifted her into his arms. A cloak manifested from the back of his suit and drew about his body, followed by bones and muscle, organs and blood, flesh and finally feathers,
‘Two Immolesses at once,’ he muttered as the raven’s body engulfed him, ‘Like I don’t have enough on my plate.’

The bird swooped up, out the window and into the night sky.

Chester pulled out his pocket watch and decided it was still early enough to pull three or four of the nice ladies who loitered about under the Sapari streetlamps and allowed Clive, his own raven, to transport him to the mainland.

After a tasty serving of red-light lady, Chester found himself a little irate. The ladies guessed he was in a foul mood when he tore their throats out, tied them to an abandoned old anchor, and introduced their dying bodies to the sea floor. The ladies were not happy, but the Getsug sharks had a field day.

Chester returned to Tempus Cottage, via his raven of course, and resumed his nap. Napping always made Chester tired, as did riding and eating dubious women. He hoped another nap would reduce the irritation. It did not.

In the early hours Chester identified the source of his irritation, it stemmed from Allyra beating Nicolas, largely because Chester was Nicolas and he didn’t like being twatted with lumps of metal. It was almost rude behaviour. He decided to get a bit of revenge by humping his way through the many women of Neferaten who he had fallen in love with earlier in the year. It had not occurred to Chester that said women may have moved on.

Equally, it had not occurred to the proud piranha of the only lake of the Twin Lakes that the sharks would steal their thunder.

The sharks had done such a good job of tearing Chester’s ladies to shreds that their tethers to the anchor were severed, and the studs of the sea went wanging about the ocean showing off to the lady sharks, until they got bored.

The following morning a young couple from Serphage, one Mr Wilhelm and one Mrs Lordes, were surprised to find precisely two heads, three arms, half a leg and a torso on the beaches of Serphage during their morning ‘walk.’

Mr Ledgerly, a notable journalist from Togaduine, happened to arrive on the scene before the sheriff, Sheriff Cadence. Mr Ledgerly, being the good citizen that he was, held the couple at the scene, as they were the only witnesses, by cutting their Achilles tendons. They made a bit of noise about it but piped down when he threatened to remove their legs entirely.

Nicolai-Mr Ledgerly sent for Nicolai-Detective Cedric, via his raven, who just happened to be circling, and Detective Cedric, a renowned criminologist, assessed the situation at great haste.

By the time the sheriff had arrived, Detective Cedric had analysed the scene and come to a conclusion. Cedric assured Sheriff Cadence that the bodies were the result of a common late night water sport known as Getsug Blade Roulette, and that all four women had lost the game equally.

The sheriff asked Cedric how he knew there were four women, and Cedric replied that it was obvious since the boxed game, which came with knives and dice, was listed as being for four to six players, and he was assuming the bear minimum.

By the time the body parts were brought to the mortuary, a pamphlet had been distributed around Serphage, and the front page news screamed,
‘The Infidelity of Wilhelm and Lordes.’

Mrs Wilhelm and Mr Lordes had their partners instantly committed to Corax Asylum and eloped together.

The sharks made pages two and three, which caused the piranha a great deal of sorrow, and they endeavoured to enlist a public relations expert.

Page four raised concerns about the pirates which had caused uproar in Sapari. Page five mentioned some stolen wood that no party had claimed responsibility for, and page six detailed the upcoming nuptials of one Nicolas DeSilva, although his secret and ‘much beloved’ bride’s name was not mentioned ‘for her own safety.’

Lord Finkelstein of Serphage complained to Count Tepes about the whole mess. Tepes complained to Theaten. Theaten wrote to Nicolas who was too busy to reply, but he did receive a reply from someone named Nicolai-Binky
