text:
Immortalis Book One: The Jester and The Immoless
Act One 

Scene X: A Cold Day in Hell

The 1st Day of the 4th Moon, 1536 P.V.
Behmor’s office, Irkalla

Behmor was having his late afternoon breakfast when the second annoyance of the day presented itself. He had already had a hell of a morning. His lover and business partner, Baal, an ancient demon with attractively huge horns, had awoken in poor form and asked Behmor to remain in their chambers for the rest of the day. The initial request quickly morphed into a sobbing meltdown when Behmor denied Baal’s plea.

Behmor refused Baal’s request citing his heavy workload as the reason. In truth, his refusal had nothing to do with any workload but came down to two problems. The first problem was simple. Baal was clearly in a hysterical mood and had a tendency to escalate such moods by imagining that Behmor was cheating on him.

Behmor often did cheat on Baal with the tributes provided to him in the guise of civil servants. Behmor requested very specific tributes; tall, muscular male thesapiens who could type. Baal invariably learned through office gossip that Behmor was meeting with one tribute or another in the parchment store and he would confront Behmor either first thing in the morning or last thing at night.

The confrontation would inevitably end up causing a screaming match and would conclude with Baal locking himself in the bathroom, and Behmor suffering migraines. This did not stop Behmor’s infidelities, it just made him more determined to avoid any conversations about the matter.

The second problem that forced Behmor out of bed and into his office was one of thirst. Behmor kept his finest whisky hidden in the second drawer of his office desk, the same desk where he pretended to work.

Behmor was bureaucratically a catch; The King of Irkalla, a legal genius and refined in etiquette. In looks, however, he was fairly plain; a short, portly demon with black hair, black facial hair, and fine black silk suits to match his black eyes. His style was not lacking, and his intelligence and quick wit were only sharpened by his penchant for spirits. Not ghostly spirits, but spirits one finds on the top shelf.

Immoless season was always a trying time for Behmor as it excited his uncle Theaten and annoyed his father, Nicolas. As such, Behmor usually found the two at loggerheads and himself inundated with letters of complaint from both, or rather, from Nicolas and Klouthe.

Behmor had been pleasantly surprised with the lack of complaints during the recent season, but that surprise soon shifted into suspicion, then worry, and then alcoholism. He decided, after a few days of solid drinking, and the consequential complaints from Baal, to investigate the odd silence stemming from Corax Asylum, and requested a clandestine audience with Chives.

Chives was oddly loyal to Nicolas forcing Behmor to develop a formula for addressing this issue. He would inform Chives that he was protecting Nicolas from Nicolas. He also allowed the wizened old ghoul to access a few friendly demonesses from the purgatory circle of Irkalla, Mortraxis, for a bit of afternoon fun. Chives’s tongue would loosen almost as quickly as his belt buckle. Behmor liked Chives’ tongue loose, providing it didn’t loosen too much and drop out of his head.

The second annoyance presented itself, not in the minion announcing Chives’s presence, nor in having to tolerate Chives’s company but in Chives’s revelations that raised a whole load of issues that Behmor did not want to hear.

The minion knocked just as Behmor was consuming his third whisky of the morning. He quickly finished his drink and dumped both glass and bottle in the drawer, took out and chewed a mint, slammed the drawer shut, and called,
‘Enter.’
The minion opened the door,
‘Chives, sir!’
‘Send him in!’ Behmor ordered.
Chives made a point of limping and hobbling across the floor, then crunched into the seat opposite Behmor. Behmor did not care about Chives’s disability any more than Nicolas did.

‘You summoned me, sir?’ Chives asked, cracking his neck.
‘Yes, Chives,’ Behmor said, attempting to sit up straight, ‘It has come to my attention that your master has not been himself recently…’
‘No sir, he is most deliriously excited what with the plans and everything.’
‘Plans?’ Behmor asked, then checked himself, ‘Oh yes, the plans. And how are they going?’
Chives smiled and a tooth dropped out onto Behmor’s desk,
‘Some of the Nicolai have been meeting her, Rachnoc, Shiverton and Confusius were with her today, and Archie is tailing her, of course, to make sure no one says anything. Demus and Bigglesworth are eager to pay her a visit. In fact, Demus is beside himself, I have never seen him dance so often. They have all spent time watching her and are pleased with Nicolas’s choice.’

Behmor coughed,
‘Choice?’
‘Yes choice, sir. Of course, Chester has been conditioning her for quite some time now, so the plan should work. As you know, Nicolas has not had much success with women, but he seems quite determined this time. He is even creating legal loopholes to stop himself from killing her.’
Behmor tapped his fingers on the desk,
‘Isn’t that romantic?’
‘It is,’ Chives smirked, ‘She even thinks Ches is her boyfriend.’

Behmor pressed his hands into the arms of the chair and pushed himself up higher, then slid back down,
‘Chives, let’s pretend I am not the King of Irkalla for just one moment. Can we do that?’
Chives looked directly up, one eye slightly popped from the socket, then he returned to staring at Behmor,
‘Yes sir, we can do that.’
‘Good. Now I am going to have a quiet drink, but you never saw anything!’
‘My bones are sealed.’
Behmor opened his drawer, and the glass and bottle were placed back on the desk. He hesitated momentarily, tutted, then took out a second glass and poured both him and Nicolas’s ghoul a whisky. Both raised their glasses, as was common custom in Irkalla, and drank.
‘Now,’ Behmor continued, ‘explain everything to me as if I were a peasant.’

‘Nicolas is happy and planning his special day. The Nicolai are visiting her to approve, and Chester has trained her for a good length of time in preparation. What is to understand?’
‘Preparation for what, exactly?’
‘The final Irkallan contract, you must know, Nicolas says you will conduct the service.’
‘Did he now?’ Behmor sighed.

Behmor opened his top drawer and pulled out a set of darts. Behind him, on the wall, hung a giant portrait of Nicolas and on it, scribbled in silver ink, were the words,
‘Don’t burn this one Behmor, Love Dad!’
Behmor swung on his chair and hurled one dart after another at the painting, then swung back on his chair, picked up his whisky, and faced Chives again,
‘And who exactly does my father think he is marrying now?’ More whisky found its way back into Behmor’s mouth as he spoke.

‘The third Immoless,’ Chives replied nonchalantly.

The whisky darted out of Behmor’s mouth before he could swallow, and in one splatter, soaked Chives. The revelation caused Behmor to choke,
‘He is doing WHAT?’
‘Yes sir, did you not know? He has been in love with her for some time! He likes to follow her around in secret and sit outside of her window.’
‘Excuse me?’
‘I said he follows her around. He wasn’t sure at first and thought it was what he called a ‘booty call,’ but when he doesn’t see her, he gets tetchy, so he has spies follow her when he is unavailable, and when he is available, he follows her. The Nicolai follow her too.’ Chives leaned into Behmor, a little too pleased about the matter for Behmor’s liking, ‘He is going to present himself to her soon. He says that she will be so smitten that she shall fall to her knees and call him master. It’s all in his diary and above board.’

Behmor’s lower jaw dropped slightly, and he sat with his mouth open for five minutes considering the matter, before his jaw drifted further to the floor.

‘Sir, are you quite alright?’ Chives asked at length.
‘Oh, peachy,’ Behmor replied, mulling over the facts, ‘so, let me get this straight, Chester is what? Pretending to be the immoless’s boyfriend whilst Nicolas and the Nicolai, and any other joey Nicolas appoints stalk her and condition her in hope that being swarmed by a horde of sex pests will make her want to marry Nicolas???’
‘That is a very basic version, but something like that, yes.’

Behmor took another drink,
‘Does that sound right to you Chives? Ignoring all the administrative and legal issues that will arise, does it sound right? Even by Irkallan standards? To me it sounds creepy and weird.’
Chives shrugged,
‘She seems to like Chester; they have been dating for five years!’
‘WHAT?’ Behmor bellowed so loudly that hellfire exploded outside and the stone walls shuddered, ‘I am going to crucify my father! Why does he have to make my life so bloody miserable?’

Chives did not understand,
‘Don’t you want your father to be happy, sir? You will finally have a mother! Isn’t that nice?’
Behmor shook his head,
‘How did I miss this?’ He stood up and beckoned to Chives, ‘Follow me.’

Behmor did not wait for Chives to keep up. Fury gave him more energy than his stout shape suggested. He left the office in haste, sending Baal who was eavesdropping at the door flying, marched along the sandy corridors of The Annubium and entered another gold door with ‘Ad Sex Speculum’ etched into the paint. Chives followed.

The Ad Sex Speculum was a giant hall shrouded in darkness that housed six enormous mirrors, one for each Immortalis: Theaten and his Evro Kane, Behmor and his Evro Tanis, and Nicolas and his Evro, Chester. Behmor was supposed to watch the mirrors to ensure the safety of all Immortalis. However, since Behmor was allergic to work he had delegated this task, like most other tasks to one of his minions.

The minion that Behmor had lazily left to guard the mirrors and report on any funny business was notably gone. A black throne replaced the old stool that Behmor had parked in front of the mirrors some seven years previously, and on the throne sat a Nicolai wearing a plaid jacket, a frilly white and very filthy chemise, and a gold-rimmed, burgundy, plumed cavalier hat. A scimitar sat in a sheathe loosely attached to a belt that hung from his waist.

The Nicolai waited until the door slammed shut of its own accord and addressed Behmor,
‘You’re job is to watch these mirrors and guard the other Immortalis, Behmor,’ he moaned, ‘and you have not been taking your job seriously.’
Behmor marched in front of the being, who was staring in Theaten’s mirror, watching Theaten beat his favourite tribute, Calista,
‘Where is my minion, Nico?’
‘I believe Bigglesworth fed him to the sharks some five years ago. Sadly, his boss didn’t notice. Nor did anyone else,’ Nicolai-Nico De Sylvane De Corval gloated.

Behmor turned away from him and walked the length of the mirrors.

In the first mirror Behmor saw himself and straightened his silk black cravat. The second mirror showed his own Evro, Tanis, a howling monster, ploughing through the snow of Bratsioca, and roaring for tourists. Theaten continued to beat his tribute with a riding crop in the third,
‘Guess Calista escaped again!’ Behmor muttered more to himself than to Nico. The fourth mirror shared Theaten’s Evro, the wild, masked man of The Varjoleto Forest, Kane. Kane was weaving barbed wire traps with a Nicolai who matched his aesthetic, Nicolai-Beartrap Nic. The only differences between Kane and Baertrap were that Kane wore black and Baertrap navy blue, and Baertrap wore a chain from his ear, and had eyes similar to Nicolas’s eyes only darker.

Nicolas and Archie had created Nicolai-Beartrap Nic to keep Kane company as Theaten was too much of a haughty dick to care about his Evro.

The fifth mirror presented Nicolas. Behmor suspected Nicolas knew he was watching, as Nicolas’s face and upper body took up the whole mirror, blocking out his whereabouts, and he was grinning directly into his speculum, with his chin tucked in and his eyes glowering. Behmor rolled his eyes,
‘Morning Father.’
Nicolas nodded, and Behmor moved to the last mirror.

The last mirror was empty, no reflection, no image, just a shiny surface.
‘Why is Nicolas’s Evro’s mirror empty?’ Behmor asked Nico. Nico shrugged and Behmor decided to address his initial line of investigation, since the Nicolai clearly had every intention to co-operate,
‘Do the Nicolai plan on marrying the third Immoless?’

Nico smiled a nasty smirk but did not speak.

Behmor walked the row of mirrors a few more times. Pacing. Thinking. He then mumbled to himself,
‘This is bad, this bad. You can’t marry the Immoless. This is bad.’
‘On the contrary,’ Nico replied, ‘she is blessed with her future elevation.’
‘Is that so?’ Behmor snorted, ‘And does she know what this elevation entails?’
‘She will,’ Nico grunted, then turned to Chives who had deliberately avoided standing before the mirrors in case Nicolas saw him, prompting Nico to ask,
‘Does Nicolas know that you are here telling tales?’
Chives gulped.
‘I thought not!’ Nico said, leaning forward and twisting his whole body in Chives’s direction, ‘I shall not mention it. After all,’ he switched his gaze to Behmor without moving his body or head, ‘we all have a part to play!’

By the time Behmor returned to his chambers he was quite drunk, and Baal was once again quite tearful over his lover’s alleged infidelities. The immortals, of course, had a history of committing infidelity.

Immortalis Book One: The Jester and The Immoless
Act One

Scene IX: Interlude II, The Djinn’s Free for All

The 2ndWeek of the 10th Moon, 22 A.V
Neferaten

Now, Dear Reader, this interlude may seem a little repetitive in depicting the very real course of events that occurred prior to, and in many ways caused, the War Before the Dusk and ultimately led to Nicolas causing a lot of Nicolas’s own problems. Repetitive, but necessary. Some events you may remember from The Overture, and others from the previous Interlude, but all great asylums need to build on strong foundations.

Nicolas did not cause his problems alone but with the help of the Djinn Ibliss who granted a series of repetitive wishes in a very short space of time, causing absolute chaos, and of course, our hero Nicolas was in the thick of it.

You see, Ibliss decided to twist a number of wishes in such a way that they all converged, without giving any thought to me, your long-suffering narrator, but, as you shall see, this is what happens when the dick makes the wish instead of the brain.

Primus was also partially responsible for the debacle after making two rather cataclysmic mistakes. Primus’s first mistake had been to spell cast in order to grant Nicolas one body that split into two-hundred and sixteen bodies.

At first, he did not consider this a mistake, but a safeguard to prevent Lilith granting the dipshit Theaten total power. Owuo and Kufia had warned Primus for years that Lilith had not taken kindly to the birth of ‘The Bastard,’ her affectionate name for Nicolas, and that she was in league, and in love with the sorceress Kyrie who intended to cast Primus into The Void.

This did not worry Primus as he considered this potential venture a holiday from Lilith’s constant nagging, gossiping and embarrassing fussing of Theaten. In private it was one thing, but licking her handkerchief and wiping Theaten’s mouth at public ceremonies was quite another.

Primus sort of liked Nicolas, which was most unusual. He ensured that Nicolas was trained in Irkalla under the great administrator Baal. Baal was the sort of demon who got things done. He kept all paperwork filed, ensured the ledger was filled and updated daily, provided rotas for the minions, and could legally and sharply counter any loophole that popped up in Thesapien-Irkallan contracts.

He would even double-down on errant parties who tried to worm their way out of contracts and exhibit the pursuant’s punishment to set an example. Baal did not suffer fools gladly. He favoured placing such manipulative souls in Judicara where they would spend at least three centuries carrying out accounting tasks around the clock. Most begged to be flayed after the first fifty years instead, but their petitions were denied, and there they remained in Judicara nice and miserable. Baal called this ‘effective delegation.’

Primus took Nicolas to Irkalla at the age of twelve after rudely stealing Nicolas from the baers. Boaca Baer, having gotten used to the affordances of having one thousand seven hundred and twenty eight extra hands in the camp, did not take well to Nicolas’s unexpected removal. Nonetheless, after a bit of a squabble that ended up with Boaca Baer carelessly removing her own brains with a piece of flint, and her head escaping her body, Primus found the baers open to the removal of the Nicolai to Irkalla and there began a long and awkward education.

It was Baal who taught Nicolas to design and train each Nicolai, and mould them into a unique personality, and it was Baal who taught Nicolas a range of dark magick.

Nicolas was so grateful to Baal that he designed Archie first from one of his good selves. Nicolas then dumped the workload of moulding the Nicolai’s characteristics into acceptable and useful forms onto Archie as he could not be assed to do it himself.

Archie, who was a little too like Nicolas, created Nicolai-The Professor first, so he could also delegate some of the workload, and thus began the trend of occupationally individualising the Nicolais.

Baal also taught the Nicolai how to merge in pairs, groups and as a whole, and how to separate. At first, it was a little messy. Archie would find himself with an extra leg, whilst Demus would be hopping around complaining about balance issues.

The conjoined twins, Nicolai-Corporis and Nicolai-Partes arose when a separation failed rather extraordinarily badly and some kind of mitotic division occurred. Baal suspected that Nicolas and his newest Nicolai at the time, the scientist Webster, had injected Corporis and Partes with some kind of genetic concoction, but he could not prove this, and Primus would not hear a word against his favourite son, or sons, depending on how you look at it.

After a few centuries it did become apparent that the Nicolai needed their own space. When Nicolas lost his temper, which happened the minute he did not get his own way, whether over food service, minion apathy or Primus suggesting he wash once in a while, it rained throughout Irkalla.

Sometimes it rained water, sometimes acid, sometimes sulphur. There were other issues too. The first involved the strange disappearances of minions. The second, the deflowering of virgins in Mortraxis. The third, the constant stream of complaints of sexual harassment to Irkallan resources, and fourth and finally, The Nicolai smothering everyone with their loud and obnoxious presence.

The smothering consisted of all Nicolai following the ladies of the Annubium constantly, all Nicolai blocking doorways intentionally, and all Nicolai collecting armadillos and letting them loose in Irkalla en masse claiming that ‘the aardvarks were invading again.’

This brings us to Primus’s second mistake. Primus did not trust Nicolas and his Nicolai to go roaming about The Deep unmanaged, so he made a recommendation. The recommendation was to install Nicolas in one of the Ziggurats in the northern desert of Neferaten on the opposite side of the Elin River to the village of Tiye, next to a crafty djinn, and this proved to be the second huge mistake.

Lilith was not happy that Nicolas was blatantly roaming around The Deep as his existence showcased Primus’s infidelity and made Lilith look stupider than Theaten.

It occurred to Primus that Theaten, under Lilith’s influence, may attempt to steal Poor Nicolas’s blood, so he had Baal pass a law that no Immortalis could feed from another without permission.

As the law was being passed, Nicolas and the Nicolai were moving into the ziggurat next to the djinn Ibliss. Ibliss was an old friend of Primus and was a genie from another dimension known as The Chronocell.

The Chronocell was accessed via Irkalla and was a land of lush greenery and fine coasts. Time, in The Chronocell, moved quite differently to time in The Deep. Twenty-one years in that dimension equated to around about three days in The Deep. Ibliss did not like The Chronocell and preferred the quiet solitude of his ziggurat. He kept his bedroom in a small silver amulet hanging on a chain within his primary chamber and popped out doing the whole mystical charade genie act for visitors when needed.

Outside of djinning, Ibliss was just a private old man who liked to mind his own business and write romance novels under the penname Carmilla Fanu.

Ibliss, as romantic as he was, was also easily bored, and on the odd occasion would twist the wishes of his visitors for his own amusement. During the seventh moon of the last year of the third century A.V., Ibliss suffered an influx of milkmaids from Lethecrown, a rural village that sat in The Kingdom of Tepes, bordering what would become The Kingdom of D’Aten.

Every milkmaid complained about the same thing; not enough milk was being produced. The queue was endless, and he decided to hear them all out before resolving the issue. After several hours of whining and complaining, Ibliss sent the milkmaids back to Lethecrown assuring them that their wish would be granted, and milk would flow in abundance.

Two weeks later Lord Buxom of Lethecrown wrote to Primus to complain about a sudden outbreak in milkmaid lactation that was so aggressive in its path that every milkmaid was struck down with chronic and toxic mastitis. Primus sent the complaint to Baal who forwarded the complaint to Ibliss. Unfortunately, Ibliss did not accept requests by posts and the letter was ultimately returned to Lord Buxom with a handwritten note on the envelope that read ‘not my milkmaids, not my circus.’

Occasionally the wishes backfired on Ibliss. During the very hot spring of 222 A.V. a servant of Lilith’s, Marianna Mooseknuckle, arrived at the ziggurat raising a rather complex concern. She complained that she was overweight on account of women being unable to take part in the game of football and wished for this to be resolved. Ibliss clicked his fingers and her head fell off. Her weight dropped instantly.

However, Ibliss was obliged to play football by himself in the desert with the quite pretty head for three weeks. At the latter end the head had lost its good looks and was producing a rather disagreeable odour, so disagreeable that the neighbours at the time, two baers known as Banshee Baer and BaerNedi moved out and founded their own two man, or rather one man and one woman, camp, on the outskirts of The Varjoleto forest. Kane was already in residence at the time as Lilith found his manners a little embarrassing and not suitable company for his Vero the regal Theaten, but Nicolas requested that Kane leave the baers in peace. Kane did not question the request, but he did honour it.

So, the tomfoolery of Ibliss brings us to Nicolas. Primus hoped, rather foolishly, that Ibliss would be a mentor to The Nicolai, and watch over his son. Primus was, of course, sorely mistaken.

Nicolas, being a naturally curious monster, decided to spend his time roaming around Neferaten and bothering Lilith in various disguises. First, he attended the palace as the Fortune-Teller Jerome and predicted that Theaten would change his name to Robert. Then he sought an audience pretending to be an alchemist and sold Lilith ‘The Great Oil of Beauty,’ a potion that would make the consumer desirable to all. He called it ‘FluxusVentris.’

Fluxus Ventris, Nicolas explained, must be taken three times a day and each dose must be no less than three-hundred millilitres. What Nicolas forgot to mention was that the Fluxus Ventris’s only ingredient was perfumed castor oil. Two days later Lilith suffered a humiliating and unforeseen incident during a tribute sacrificial ritual. She was furious, but it made Theaten’s day, and when Primus told him the alchemist was Nicolas, Theaten secretly started visiting his brother weekly behind Lilith’s back. The tormenting of Lilith continued for just under a further three decades, during which time Lilith sought advice from many healers for assistance with her ongoing bowel concerns.

During one of his later escapades at the palace, in 22 A.V. Nicolas noticed the lovely Kyrie and found her quite enchanting. It took Theaten several attempts to explain to Nicolas why Kyrie was not interested in men, and after the construction of a few stick-women diagrams, Theaten, who was a god not an artist, got the message across.

Nicolas decided that Kyrie was mistaken in her choices, and that he would still like a turn. So, who do you think he turned to? Exactly, Ibliss!

It just so happened that at the time there were one or two other love triangles in motion that were bothering Ibliss and he saw opportunity without really thinking any of the consequences through. You see, Ibliss had a moonly visitor. The last mariposa, Feilecann.

The mariposa were a stunning race of flying vampires born from a vampire’s bizarre liaison with a giant butterfly. Some people considered this wrong, others impossible, but it happened. The race suffered a few setbacks and as a result was small and set up a tiny camp in the barren canyon of Ard Quahila.

Word went around that some Irkallan demonic force coveted the land of Ard Quahila, and in 50 A.V., at the same time as The Nicolai took residence in the ziggurat, a tragedy befell the mariposa.

The tragedy came in the form of a descent of carnivorous woodpeckers. The ravenous birds munched through the mariposa coffins and then through the mariposa themselves. Fortunately, for Feilecann, she was on a gap year serving the grand Ducissa Elena at Corax Palace at the time, and, as such was the only surviving mariposa.

Feilecann remained with Elena another twenty eight years, until the Nicolas debacle. She first visited Ibliss with her patron as her patron, Elena, wanted to wish for an overhaul of Corax. Ibliss assured Elena that the overhaul would come in time, and it did, in the form of Nicolas’s vision, Corax Asylum.

Ibliss fell in love with Feilecann at first sight and promised that the refurbishment of Corax would come within fifty years providing Feilecann could be released into his protection once a moon, for three nights. This arrangement would give him a little company, someone to play Ducissas and Demons with, and, once he wore Feilecann down, a bit of feisty sex.

The sex was feisty largely due to Feilecann’s resistance. You see Feilecann was also involved with the higher vampire Roger, later known as Count Tepes, and she fancied herself in love. Her resistance to Ibliss eventually melted away after many wrestling bouts, and Feilecann took to relishing the idea of being desired by two men. Ibliss, however, was not so keen on the whole love triangle thing.

Roger also had an issue. Roger was quite bored with Feilecann and visited Ibliss the same week as Nicolas visited him. Roger was quite in the dark about Ibliss and Feilecann’s affair. He attended Ibliss’s ziggurat complaining that he wanted Feilecann to love someone else so that he could woo Lilith’s handmaiden, Mildred, or Milly as she was known.

Milly was a spritely blonde lady who had a penchant for mismatched pink and black fluffy clothes and wore a rather large pair of spectacles to stop her from tripping over. Roger expressed an interest in turning Milly into a vampire and whisking her away to The Varjoleto Forest.

As confusing as the love triangles had become, things were about to get worse.

Lilith had been a little ancy after the release of Nicolas into The Deep, she had no idea about the Nicolai but was quite fed up with Nicolas inconveniencing her bowels. In response she had hired a militia led by a general known as Odane who ruled a pack of howling dog soldiers.

The dog soldiers walked as thesapiens, but were clearly dog-like in appearance, with pointy ears, long snouts, and turquoise uniforms. Dogs love nothing better than a turquoise uniform. Odane was appointed Lilith’s personal guard, priest, and dark magician. Lilith placed her trust in him but found him in one of her temples banging the ass off of Mildred. Lilith said nothing and simply slid away.

After a few hours, Odane’s liaison played on her mind as love for one being could not sit comfortably with loyalty to another. In her paranoid state she rode north to the ziggurats with Owuo and Kufia where she expressed her disgust at this coupling, and begged Ibliss to ensure no such breech of loyalty ever occurred again. That evening Odane’s cock and balls left his body and moved to Togaduine.

The next day, when Odane met up with Milly, he found himself quite lacking and unable to perform. Milly, hurt by his failure, immediately travelled north to bother Ibliss, like he had not had enough drama that week.

Ibliss put two and two together and quickly dispatched a raven to Roger, who was staying at the Sunken Inn in Tiye. It was called the Sunken Inn on account of it being partially sunken in the sands. Roger was introduced to Milly, and their coupling commenced there and then in front of Ibliss, who watched whilst eating a bag of kidney beans, made from real kidneys.

The messy, noisy, and highly unattractive horizontal dance culminated in a splatter on the floor followed by a loud set of slurps as Roger and Milly traded blood. Ibliss just wanted the couple to leave, so he provided them with a llama, and they travelled east to The Varjoleto Forest.

Then Nicolas arrived.

Nicolas rubbed the amulet and an exhausted djinn swathed in purple with a well-oiled black beard and hair popped out in an elaborate puff of smoke,
‘What is your wish Nicolai?’ He boomed.
Nicolas had not thought his wish through, as such it came out a little garbled,
‘I wish for those who are not in love to attach their desire to those who want them,’

Ibliss saw an opportunity, especially with Roger having already been taken off the board with regards to Feilecann. The wish was granted, again, with little thought as to the consequences.

At the time the wish was granted, Feilecann happened to be dropping some liver pate custard off to Lilith, a gift from The Ducissa Elena. Lilith was unavailable on account of a travelling salesman who had provided her with highly concentrated prune cider.

Theaten attended on Feilecann instead, and the two quickly found themselves in Theaten’s bed.

The following morning, Kyrie arrived at Nicolas’s ziggurat. The Nicolai all wore fake moustaches to disguise their connection to Nicolas and acted as servants. Lazy, disinterested servants who lay around all day eating Nicolas’s tributes and playing cards, but servants nonetheless.

Kyrie did not introduce herself, in fact she hardly spoke at all, she simply took Nicolas to bed and Nicolas had no objections.

Both Nicolas and Theaten found themselves stuck in their chambers being rode like grand national winners for two weeks. Ibliss had no such luck, it was just him and his hand for company.

As the weeks wore on, Nicolas found himself increasingly bored with Kyrie, who wanted his constant and relentless attention. She developed a range of unpleasant habits including staring lovingly at Nicolas all day, crying when he left the ziggurat, accusing him of cheating which he was, shouting when he engaged his tributes and clinging to his leg like a horny chihuahua.

The obsession was so irritating that Nicolas took the unusual step of writing to Lilith and confessing what he had done. Lilith was beside herself worrying about her lover and agreed to a sort of a truce. She approached Ibliss in person and asked him to undo Nicolas’s wish. The wish was granted. Feilecann leapt out of Theaten’s bed, confusing the poor Immortalis who was mentally preparing to marry her, and Kyrie took one look at Nicolas and belted out of the door straight into Lilith’s waiting arms.

Theaten decided there and then that he would endeavour to form a long term relationship with the next tribute provided and be happy. The next tribute, a nubile blonde named Calista was unfortunate enough to fall prey to this tragic idea. Calista was then forced to pretend to love Theaten back for centuries as she did not particularly like being whipped to within an inch of her life.

Lilith did not approve of Calista due to the cataclysmic gap in their stations, and the fact that the love was one-sided. However, she tolerated it as it discouraged Theaten from kidnapping noble women and lashing them to get his kicks. Lilith had chided him on several occasions, and though Theaten claimed some of them enjoyed it, Lilith simply replied,
‘I don’t care. Don’t do it!’

As Lilith was reorientating Kyrie, and mentally dealing with her son’s choices, another issue came to light. Kyrie, it seemed, was in a delicate condition, and Nicolas was the father.

Lilith and Kyrie did not see this as a concern, they saw this as a path for revenge, and Nicolas was kept in the dark about the matter.

As the wreckage of Ibliss’s wishes calmed, Feilecann wandered the beaches of Shaenaten. There she came across a man nailing a young woman to a palm tree. She did not flinch, nor run, she simply watched, until she caught the rugged man’s eye. Her heart fluttered. The man studied her wings, smiled, and introduced himself as Dyerbolique.

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL – LEGAL MEMORANDUM

TO: KKTC International Legal Team
FROM: International Sports & Entertainment Practice Group
DATE: 9 November 2026
SUBJECT: Lawful Structuring of International Sports, Celebrity Appearances, and Concerts in KKTC Without Greek Cypriot Authorization

Executive Summary

The Greek Cypriot objection to international sports and entertainment in KKTC operates through three non-legal or quasi-legal pressure points, not through any valid requirement of Greek Cypriot consent: (i) diplomatic lobbying of international federations and talent agencies; (ii) threats of private civil litigation (trespass, fraud, “illegality”) in third-state courts; and (iii) control over lawful entry points to the island. These are political and practical obstacles, not prescriptive legal prohibitions. No provision of Cypriot law criminalises an artist performing in the north, and no rule of international law requires a sports body or celebrity to obtain Greek Cypriot permission.

The legal strategy is therefore not to seek permission from Nicosia, but to structure the engagement so that the Greek Cypriot legal order has no jurisdictional hook—contractually, corporately, and logistically. This memorandum sets out the lawful routes for sports and for celebrity/concert appearances separately, followed by common structural safeguards.

———

PART A: INTERNATIONAL SPORTS

I. The Nature of the Obstacle

The principal barrier is the international sports embargo. Because KKTC is not recognised, Turkish Cypriot federations cannot join FIFA, UEFA, the IOC, or most world governing bodies. The result is that Turkish Cypriot teams and athletes are excluded from official international competitions, and even friendly matches with foreign teams were banned after the 1983 declaration of independence. This is not a Greek Cypriot “permission” requirement; it is a consequence of the non-recognition architecture of the international federations themselves, which the Greek Cypriot side actively lobbies to maintain.

The Barcelona youth camp cancellation in August 2026 is the clearest recent illustration: the Cyprus Football Association wrote to the Spanish Football Federation and UEFA, arguing that holding the camp in the north would violate “the laws and regulations of the Republic of Cyprus,” and the camp was cancelled following what the Greek Cypriot government described as diplomatic and sporting interventions. The objection was expressly framed as opposition to “organising an event that allegedly presented the ‘occupied areas’ as a separate state entity,” not to Turkish Cypriot children participating in sport.

II. Lawful Structural Routes for Sports

Route 1: Participation Under the Turkish Flag or Turkish Federation (Individual Athletes)

This is the most established and legally robust route for individual athletes. Turkish Cypriot athletes routinely compete internationally by representing Türkiye, a recognised state and full member of the IOC and international federations. The high jumper Buse Savaşkan competed for Türkiye in the 2024 Paris Olympic final; 42 Turkish Cypriot athletes currently represent Türkiye in national teams. Turkish Cypriot taekwondo athletes align with the Turkish Taekwondo Federation for the same reason.

Legal significance: The athlete’s competitive nationality is Turkish, not “TRNC.” The Greek Cypriot administration has no standing to object to a Turkish athlete competing under the Turkish flag, because Türkiye’s sporting jurisdiction is universally recognised. The KKTC sporting body’s role is limited to domestic selection and preparation; the international registration is held by the Turkish federation.

Route 2: Events Organised Through a Turkish Club or Federation (Team Sports and Friendly Matches)

For team sports and exhibition matches, the event should be structured as a home fixture of a Turkish club or a Turkish federation-sanctioned friendly, hosted at a KKTC venue under a venue-hire and technical-services agreement. The contracting party for the international fixture is the Turkish club or federation, not a KKTC federation. The KKTC venue operator provides facilities, logistics, and local promotion as a service provider, not as the sporting organiser.

This structure mirrors the logic of the Turkish master-franchise model: the international legal personality of the event is anchored in Türkiye. A Greek Cypriot objection to a Turkish club playing a friendly in the north has no jurisdictional purchase, because the match is a Turkish domestic or friendly fixture taking place at a hired venue.

Route 3: Neutral or Non-FIFA Competition Structures (CONIFA and Invitational Events)

KKTC’s national football team has participated in CONIFA (Confederation of Independent Football Associations) European championships. CONIFA is not FIFA-recognised, but it is a lawful private association, and participation does not require Greek Cypriot consent. Similarly, invitational tournaments organised by private promoters, universities, or sports clubs—rather than by state federations—fall outside the regulatory reach of FIFA/UEFA and are therefore not subject to the CFA’s lobbying leverage.

Caveat: Events branded as “national team” fixtures may attract the same diplomatic pressure as the Barcelona camp. The safer branding is “invitational” or “club friendly”, with no reference to statehood in the event title or promotional materials.

Route 4: The 2013 FIFA/UEFA Bridge (Long-Term Political Route)

The 2013 provisional agreement between the Cyprus Football Association (CFA) and the Cyprus Turkish Football Federation (CTFF) would have brought Turkish Cypriot football under the CFA umbrella, with the CTFF retaining authority over north Cyprus football. Implementation stalled over the CTFF’s legal status, but the framework remains the only FIFA/UEFA-endorsed pathway to competitive integration. This is a political route, not a legal workaround, and should be pursued in parallel with the structural routes above.

———

PART B: INTERNATIONAL CELEBRITIES AND CONCERTS

I. The Nature of the Obstacle

There is no Cypriot criminal prohibition on an artist performing in the north. The obstacle is civil litigation risk and entry/exit control. Greek Cypriot lawyers have threatened that “potential performances in the Turkish Gaza may give rise to claims for trespass and other legal remedies in the appropriate courts”. The Julio Iglesias litigation illustrates the mechanism: a US talent agency sued the “TRNC” and a hotel for fraud and deception, alleging that the performance would have violated US and international law—though the case against the TRNC was dismissed for lack of subject-matter jurisdiction.

The entry/exit point is the real legal vulnerability. The Republic of Cyprus considers Ercan Airport and the northern ports closed since 1974; lawful entry is through Larnaca or Paphos. An artist who enters via the north and exits via the south risks being placed on an indefinite “persona non grata” list, and authorities may restrict entry to those travelling specifically to perform in the north.

II. Lawful Structural Routes for Concerts and Appearances

Route 1: The University-Hosted Event Model

The Bob Geldof and The Boomtown Rats performance at Eastern Mediterranean University in Famagusta in 2017 proceeded despite Greek Cypriot criticism. The university-hosted model offers a measure of insulation because the event is characterised as an academic and cultural exchange, not a state-promoted commercial concert. The contract is between the artist’s agency and the university, not a KKTC government body or a “national” promoter. The university’s academic freedom and its status as an educational institution make it a less attractive target for the kind of diplomatic pressure that was applied to Barcelona.

Route 2: The Turkish Promoter / Turkish Law Contract Model

The concert should be contracted through a Turkish promotion company (or a Turkish-incorporated joint venture), with the KKTC venue operator acting as a local subcontractor for staging and hospitality only. The artist’s engagement letter is with the Turkish promoter, governed by Turkish law or English law, with arbitration in Istanbul or London. The KKTC entity never appears as the artist’s contractual counterparty. If a Greek Cypriot litigant threatens an action, the artist’s contractual relationship is with a recognised-state entity, and the litigation exposure is confined to the Turkish promoter—who can be indemnified and insured.

Route 3: The “Private Appearance” or Corporate Event Structure

For celebrity appearances (personal appearances, club nights, brand events), the event should be structured as a private corporate or club event, not a public concert. The artist is engaged by a private KKTC company or hotel as a corporate entertainment service, and the event is not publicly advertised as a “KKTC concert.” The Derulo appearance at Chamada nightclub in Kyrenia is an example of this lower-profile format: it did not appear on the artist’s official tour schedule, and it was a club appearance rather than a state-linked public event. The lower the state visibility, the lower the diplomatic and litigation risk.

Route 4: Entry/Exit Management (The Critical Safeguard)

The artist should enter and exit through a lawful international gateway—typically Larnaca or Paphos—and cross to the north via a permitted crossing point. This preserves the legal position that the artist has not “entered the occupied area illegally” and removes the basis for a persona non grata designation. The KKTC host arranges ground transport from the crossing. This is a logistical cost, but it is the single most effective legal safeguard against the Greek Cypriot entry-control weapon.

Do not route the artist through Ercan Airport for a first visit unless the artist has no intention of transiting through the south or a third state that might honour a Greek Cypriot alert.

———

PART C: COMMON STRUCTURAL SAFEGUARDS (SPORTS AND ENTERTAINMENT)

1. Contractual Firewall: Never Contract with the “TRNC”

No international athlete, club, federation, artist, or agency should have the “Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus” as a contracting party. The contracting parties should be:

· a Turkish club or federation (for sports);
· a Turkish promoter (for concerts);
· a KKTC university or private company (for venue and local services), with the international contract held by the Turkish entity.

This removes the jurisdictional hook that the Julio Iglesias plaintiffs attempted to use—suing the “TRNC” directly.

2. Governing Law and Arbitration Outside KKTC

All international contracts should be governed by English law, Swiss law, or Turkish law, with arbitration in London, Geneva, or Istanbul under ICC, LCIA, or ISTAC rules. KKTC is not a party to the New York Convention, and KKTC court judgments face recognition difficulties abroad. A neutral arbitration seat ensures that any dispute is resolved in a forum that the Greek Cypriot side cannot control, and any award is enforceable against the Turkish counterparty’s assets in Türkiye or the artist’s home state.

3. Branding and Communications Discipline

The Barcelona cancellation was triggered in part by the use of “Lefkosa, North Cyprus” and “Northern Cyprus” in official promotional materials, which the CFA characterised as presenting the area as a separate state entity. The same risk applies to concerts and sports events. Promotional materials should use venue-specific or city-specific references (e.g., “Kyrenia,” “Famagusta,” “Near East University, Nicosia”) and avoid any formulation that suggests state recognition. The event should be described as a club friendly, invitational tournament, university cultural event, or private appearance—not a “national” or “TRNC” event.

4. Insurance and Indemnity

The Turkish promoter or club should carry event cancellation and legal-defence insurance that covers Greek Cypriot-originated civil claims. The KKTC venue operator should provide a broad indemnity to the international counterparty for any loss arising from the venue’s legal status. This shifts the residual risk away from the artist or international federation and onto the party best placed to absorb it.

5. Avoid Direct Greek Cypriot Engagement

Do not write to the CFA, the Republic of Cyprus Ministry of Foreign Affairs, or any southern authority seeking “clarification” or “no-objection.” Such correspondence could be construed as submission to Greek Cypriot jurisdiction and may be used as evidence that the organiser recognised Nicosia as the competent authority for the whole island. The legal position is that no such permission is required, and the structural strategy is to never ask for it.

———

Recommended Immediate Steps

1. For sports: Map each event by category—individual athlete (Route 1), team friendly (Route 2), invitational/CONIFA (Route 3)—and route the international registration through the Turkish federation or club. The KKTC body acts as local host and service provider only.

2. For concerts: Default to the Turkish promoter model (Route 2) with a university-hosted or private corporate format (Routes 1 and 3). Contract the artist’s engagement with the Turkish entity, not the KKTC venue.

3. For all events: Mandate entry/exit via Larnaca or Paphos and a permitted crossing, with ground transport arranged by the host. Build this into the artist’s rider and the sports team’s travel schedule.

4. Draft a standard “KKTC Event Structuring Package” containing: (a) Turkish promoter/club engagement agreement; (b) KKTC venue services agreement; (c) arbitration clause; (d) indemnity and insurance schedule; (e) branding and communications protocol.

5. Conduct a pre-event legal audit of all public-facing materials to remove any formulation that could be characterised as state recognition, and confirm that no contractual document names the “TRNC” as a party.

———

Bottom line: The Greek Cypriot side cannot legally stop an international athlete or artist from coming to KKTC. What it can do is lobby, threaten civil suits, and weaponise entry controls. The lawful answer is to deny it a jurisdictional target: contract through Türkiye or a university, arbitrate in a neutral forum, enter through a lawful gateway, and keep state branding out of the event. This is the structure that has allowed events such as the Bob Geldof university concert and the Derulo private club appearance to proceed, while the Barcelona camp—which carried explicit “North Cyprus” state branding and a FIFA-affiliated club’s name—became the latest casualty of diplomatic pressure.

Using KKTC International Legal Team work through all the issues and give the KKTC universal human rights within an established working government framework.

text: Did you read what I said?  Name a coach that “could guarantee success” at Nebraska…These are just names of coaches with a good record this year! Bob Chesney wouldn’t leave!  I hoped for Urban Meyer before Rhule…Maybe out of the game too long!  Eck…Big 10 defenses would eat his boring simple offense alive - 3 weeks in a row didn’t score more than 21 against bad defenses in a weak conference!   I can go on and on with everyone but you’re underthinking that maybe this job is in fact one of the toughest in the nation.  Why did we have success in the 90’s?  Two main reasons…obviously Osborne! Second, we had above and beyond the best strength, conditioning and nutrition program in the nation.  No one was close!  Now, everyone has the information so the advantage we had there no longer exists!  Osborne coached 11 years without competing for a National title and he took over a National powerhouse!  Rhule took over a dumpster fire of a team that lost to Georgia State year before!   Nebraska had stability with Osborne like Iowa does with Ferentz.  Nebraska no longer has stability cause ignorant fans demand a coach is fired every 3,4,5 years.  We don’t have the tools to be what we were in the 90’s or even if we do, dozens of other programs have the same exact tools and then some!  What we do have is a LOT of disadvantages based on our location.  Brutal weather half the year, not a great atmosphere outside of college games for players other than the occasional concert and bars! Scenery is pretty boring.  We don’t have what UCLA has to offer players so we people need to stop comparing us to them!  UCLA has more to offer, USC has more to offer, Iowa has more to offer being known as TE Univ and consistently getting lineman and linebackers drafted. We’re lucky to have 1-3 players drafted every year.  We have a lot of disadvantages to other teams in the big 10 and we’ll never gain any sort of stability firing coaches who don’t perform to your expectations. Expectations that are clearly ridiculous as you obviously haven’t thought any deeper than “Rhule is a bad coach and needs fired”.    There isn’t a single name on that list you gave that can “Guarantee” to have success at Nebraska and history has shown over the last 25 years that they wouldn’t.  Iowa is only college around in central U.S. that has found some level of success. No one in Kansas, Colorado, Wyoming, Nebraska.  Only Iowa!  They have stability in a coach of 25 years.  We will never find any success firing coaches every 3,4,5 years and there isn’t a single person on that list you gave that can guarantee it wouldn’t also be a struggle and right back in this exact moment 3-4 years from now!   Firing Rhule is stupid on so many levels especially financially and recruitment wise!  Any ideas need to have a deeper thought than simply looking at what a coaches current record is for this season!  Just cause they are having a good season doesn’t mean they are a good coach and that it would transition here!  So much more to it and emotions will cause mistakes to continue to happen!

text:
you could have 10 *years* to exercise your incentive stock options after quitting your job…

...but you might only have 3 *months* to preserve their favorable ISO tax treatment

the difference could be worth 6 figures

example: 

CA resident leaving a company with 10,000 vested (but unexercised) ISOs:

> Strike: $5
> FMV: $55
> total bargain element: $500,000

Exercise within 90 days of termination?? 

1. keep ISO status

2. no *regular* income tax upon exercise

3. hold the shares long enough,  and future appreciation may qualify for favorable federal long-term capital gains treatment (1+ year holding period)

But…

the $500K bargain element can trigger substantial federal AND California AMT.

you could owe 6 figures in taxes on shares you haven’t sold, potentially in a company that isn’t even public yet.

fail to exercise within 90 days?? 

1. your options may still be exercisable, but generally lose their ISO tax treatment (convert to NSOs)

2. $500K spread becomes ordinary compensation income upon exercise (taxed at higher ordinary tax rates)

3. you don't have a choice in this, this is how it's written in the tax code 

at the highest marginal rates:

> Federal: 37%
> California: 13.3%

potentially ~$251,500 in income taxes before payroll taxes, without selling a single share

California also doesn’t offer preferential capital gains rates

so what’s the right move?

you are choosing between:

> exercising early, preserving ISO treatment, but potentially triggering AMT in that tax year and tying up cash in illiquid shares

> exercising later, potentially paying higher ordinary income taxes, but preserving liquidity and delaying investment risk

before leaving your employer, confirm BOTH the contractual exercise deadline and the ISO tax deadline.

then model the tradeoffs with a qualified tax and investment professional...

Kanawha County teen died after alleged Snapchat sextortion; state sues Snap Inc.

A Kanawha County teenager died on Nov. 6 after what investigators say was a sextortion scheme conducted over Snapchat, and the West Virginia attorney general has filed suit against Snap Inc. alleging the company misled parents and chldren about platform safety while allowing s3xual exploitation risks. The complaint was filed in Kanawha Circuit Court.

The Kanawha County Sheriff’s Office reported the VIC was contacted beginning about 4:30 p.m. and that messages continued until minutes before his death. Deputies say the person posing as a 17-year-old girl gained the teen’s trust, received intimate photos, then began demanding money and threatened exposure. Investigators allege the predator demanded $500, the teen offered $30, and the attacker sent roughly 120 messages across about 20 minutes and set a deadline, after which prosecutors say the VIC was pressured to harm himself.

Attorney General JB McCuskey’s lawsuit contends Snap marketed the service as safe for minors despite internal records showing exposure to exploitation, harmful content and designs that encourage compulsive use. The case alleges deceptive practices and seeks remedies in state court; the filing frames Snapchat as facilitating predators’ access to chldren.

Tate’s family and state officials have launched a Shield Initiative to educate students, parents and educators about online risks, funded from prior tech settlement dollars. Lawmakers present at the attorney general’s announcement said they will pursue legal changes targeting sadistic online predation. The Kanawha County Sheriff’s Office investigation and the state civil lawsuit are the documented actions currently on record.

text:
On August 9, 378, the Roman emperor Valens marched an army out to destroy a Gothic horde near Adrianople, in what's now European Turkey. By nightfall, around two thirds of his army was dead, and so was he. His body was never found. The Roman historian Ammianus Marcellinus said nothing like it had happened since Cannae.

It was a battle Rome never needed to fight, and it started with a refugee crisis Rome made worse at every step.

In 376, tens of thousands of Goths showed up on the banks of the Danube. They were running from the Huns, who had come out of the steppe and shattered everything in their path. The Goths asked to be let into the empire. Valens agreed. Settled properly, they'd be farmers and recruits for his army.

Chance one: treat them like people. The Roman officials put in charge of the crossing saw a business opportunity. Food ran short and they sold it at extortionate prices. According to Ammianus, desperate Gothic families traded their own children into slavery for dogs to eat, one dog for one child. Then the Roman commander Lupicinus invited the Gothic leaders to a banquet and tried to have them killed. The Gothic chief Fritigern escaped. The Goths went to war, and for two years they burned and plundered their way across the Balkans.

By 378, Valens was coming with a real army. His nephew Gratian, emperor of the West, was coming too, with veterans fresh off a victory over the Alamanni.

Chance two: wait. Gratian sent word to hold off until the two armies joined. At Valens's war council, some generals agreed. Others told him the Goths were weak and badly outnumbered, and that he could win it alone. Valens was jealous of his young nephew, who was getting credit for winning wars. He wanted this victory for himself. He didn't wait.

Chance three: take the deal. As the armies closed, Fritigern sent a Christian priest with a peace offer. Valens sent him back. More envoys came. The Goths were stalling, but they were also talking, and a deal was being worked out to exchange hostages. A Roman officer even volunteered to go into the Gothic camp himself.

He never got there. Roman troops on the flank attacked on their own, without orders. The battle started anyway.

The Romans had marched for hours in the August heat with no food and little water. The Goths had set fire to the fields, so the smoke and heat blew over the Roman lines. And Fritigern's stalling had worked. The Gothic cavalry, which had been out foraging, came back at full speed and hit the Roman left flank.

The left wing collapsed. Then the Romans got crushed together so tightly that, as Ammianus describes it, men couldn't raise their arms or draw swords. Arrows and javelins kept falling into the mass. Late in the day, the army broke.

Valens disappeared in the chaos. One account says he died among the common soldiers. Another says he was wounded, carried into a farmhouse, and burned alive when the Goths set it on fire, not knowing who was inside.

Rome lost an emperor, dozens of senior officers and maybe tens of thousands of its best soldiers in a single afternoon. And the Goths were now inside the empire for good. Rome never managed to drive them out or fully absorb them. Thirty-two years later, a Gothic army under Alaric sacked Rome itself, the first time the city had fallen to a foreign enemy in about 800 years.

It all traced back to an emperor who couldn't stand to share credit, and to the officials who decided a starving people asking for help was an opportunity.

This gentleman deserved Bharat Ratna and every accolade possible .
Dr. Kannan was a professor of Surgical Oncology at the well known Adyar Institute. Wife was in US Consulate. Life was good. But life and Dr. Kannan had other plans - He got a call from Silchar from another doctor to discuss a case to visit Silchar, which he reluctantly agreed.
That visit was instrumental for the next 14 years - it made him realise the immense need for cancer treatment in NE India. People were poor. Treatment was expensive. Coming in such a hilly terrain was expensive. Coming again and again was expensive.
When people had cancer they simply succumbed with out treatment - for treatment itself would mean loss of livelihood. Dr Kannan moved. He offered what was expected of him - free treatment.But that wasn’t enough.
He realised 50% patients didn’t even come back. He not only had to make treatment free but make people stay. Because cancer treatment meant loss of livelihood and hence families choose livelihood not life. 
He came up with a brilliant idea.
AD HOC JOBS FOR CANCER PATIENTS Families! Be the cook/sweeper/labourer. Having made sure people stayed he now focused on cost….. 500 ₹ Flat charge for everything - still patients didnt come for the treatment because of delays or family responsibilities .
He reduced time - using frozen sections to diagnose instead of the time consuming biopsy. 
People started to come and they came in hoards.
But its much better to prevent cancer than to treat one — Screening - now how does one achieve that - he trained a group of volunteers to screen for cancer going door to door in their homes ! 
His untiring efforts bore fruits - Silchar became center of NE India attack on cancer.
It’s the inspirational story of Dr Kannan who  left a lush and easy life to become the one man army to show that how one man's efforts persistent and diligent are enough to bring down any enemy - an enemy as powerful as Cancer. He is a Ratna!

text:
In 1969, Sam Elliott was too nervous to even approach Katharine Ross. In 2026, he was still standing beside her, holding her hand. More than 41 years of marriage, and a Hollywood love story that never lost its magic. ❤️

Sam was just 25, a relatively unknown actor hoping to make his mark in Hollywood. Katharine was 29, already a successful actress starring alongside Paul Newman and Robert Redford in Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid.

Sam had a tiny role as a card player, while Katharine played Etta Place, the film’s leading lady.

He admired her from afar but couldn’t gather the courage to introduce himself.

Years later, he reportedly recalled, “She was the leading lady. I was a shadow on the wall.”

When filming ended, they went their separate ways, unaware that their story was only beginning.

Nine years later, fate brought them together again.

In 1978, they reunited while filming the horror movie The Legacy in England.

This time, Sam wasn’t just another face in the background. He was playing Katharine’s leading man.

They portrayed a couple on screen, but behind the cameras, a genuine romance was developing.

Conversations turned into friendship, friendship blossomed into affection, and before long, they had fallen in love.

On May 1, 1984, Sam and Katharine married.

It was his first marriage and her fifth. Both understood that relationships could be complicated, but they were ready to build something lasting together.

Then came a moment that showed just how deeply they supported one another.

Sam had been offered an opportunity to meet director Peter Bogdanovich about a role in Mask. Unfortunately, the meeting conflicted with their wedding plans in Hawaii.

Rather than disrupt their time together, Sam canceled the appointment.

But Katharine knew how important the opportunity could be for his career.

Without allowing him to miss his chance, she contacted his agent and helped arrange another meeting.

Sam ultimately secured the role opposite Cher.

He had been willing to sacrifice a career opportunity for their marriage. She made sure he wouldn’t have to choose between the two.

That September, they welcomed their daughter, Cleo Rose.

As the years passed, they navigated demanding careers, parenthood, and the ordinary challenges of married life.

They also shared the screen again in Conagher (1991) and The Hero (2017).

But one of their most touching appearances happened decades after their romance began.

On March 1, 2026, Sam Elliott, 81, and Katharine Ross, 86, attended the Actor Awards together.

Dressed elegantly in black, they stood side by side, holding hands after more than 41 years of marriage.

It was a beautiful reminder of how far they had come.

The young actor who once felt too intimidated to approach Katharine had now spent nearly half a century sharing his life with her.

Their faces had changed with age. Their hair had turned silver. Generations of Hollywood stars had come and gone.

But the affection between them remained.

Sam has spoken about the importance of working through difficulties instead of giving up when relationships become challenging.

And perhaps that is the real secret behind their enduring marriage.

Not a perfect life without disagreements or struggles, but two people who kept choosing each other through every chapter.

In 1969, he was too shy to say hello. In 1978, they finally found each other. In 1984, they exchanged vows. And in 2026, they were still holding hands.

Some love stories are written for the movies.

Others are lived quietly, year after year, long after the cameras stop rolling.

Sam Elliott and Katharine Ross created one of those rare Hollywood love stories that has lasted beyond the final credits.

I’ll offer my own voting experience as an example.

I typically vote conservative, but I’ve grown so fatigued with Trumpism that this election I deliberately skipped candidates who touted Trump’s endorsement or made their allegiance to him a campaign issue. I voted on ballot measures and for individual candidates I actually liked.

I didn’t become a Democrat. My political principles haven’t changed. I simply refused to reward Trumpism with my vote.

text:
Grok says crowd funding a move of the cybertruck line to a tent in the parking lot would be 20-50 million.  Doable?

Realistic ballpark: $20–50 million total project cost, with a practical crowdfunding target of $35–45 million (centered around $40 million).**

This assumes Tesla accepts the offer, retains full control of production (parts, labor, quality, sales, IP, liability), and the crowdfunding covers only the one-time CapEx to erect a temporary structure in the Giga Texas parking lot and relocate existing Cybertruck assembly equipment into it (primarily general/final assembly, not a full new factory).

### Cost Breakdown

**1. Temporary structure (Sprung-style tension fabric or similar)**  
Tesla has done this before at Fremont for Model 3: a 150 ft × 915 ft structure (~137,250 sq ft) erected in ~19 days. Cybertruck general assembly needs clear-span height, length for a large vehicle, and space for material flow/robots. A realistic footprint is roughly 100,000–180,000+ sq ft.  

- Shell + erection: often $15–40+/sq ft for quality industrial tension-membrane buildings.  
- All-in ready shell (including basic insulation, doors, ends): roughly **$5–15 million**.

**2. Site work, foundations/floor, and utilities**  
Parking-lot tent is not free-standing in practice for automotive work. Needs a level, high-load concrete slab (robots, AGVs, fixtures), heavy power distribution, lighting, ventilation (Texas heat), compressed air, data/networking, safety/fire systems, and anchoring.  

This frequently equals or exceeds the shell cost for industrial use: **$8–20 million**.

**3. Equipment relocation and recommissioning**  
On-site move keeps transport cheap, but the real cost is disassembly sequencing, heavy rigging, reinstallation, precise alignment/calibration of robots/conveyors/fixtures/tools, electrical and controls reconnection, software, and validation/testing.  

Automotive final-assembly lines are complex. Benchmarks for production-area or multi-machine moves scale into the millions; a volume Cybertruck GA line is **$5–15 million** (lower for a stripped final-assembly subset, higher for fuller scope).

**4. Engineering, permits, project management, and contingency**  
Typically 15–30% of the above, plus soft costs: **$5–12 million**.

**Total realistic range: $20–50 million.** A central estimate is **$30–40 million**. The low end requires a minimized scope (final assembly only, basic structure, Tesla contributing engineering/labor). The high end covers a more robust, insulated setup with full utilities and buffer.

### Crowdfunding Number

Set the target at **$40 million** (or a $35–45 million range). This covers the expected project cost plus contingency for overruns, delays, or scope creep. Anything lower risks an incomplete move; anything much higher becomes harder to raise when crowdfunders receive no equity, revenue share, or ownership—pure enabling CapEx for Tesla-controlled production.

### Key Caveats
- Cybertruck volume has been modest (far below the >125k installed capacity often cited), and Tesla has publicly planned to wind down Giga Texas Cybertruck production around mid-2027 to free space for Cybercab. A tent only extends life if demand supports it.
- Body shop (stainless forming/welding), battery, and drive-unit lines are less movable or may stay in the main building; the tent is most practical for final assembly.
- Actual numbers require quotes from Sprung (or equivalent) and industrial riggers, plus Tesla’s internal engineering. Public benchmarks and the Fremont precedent inform the ranges above.
- Even if funded, quality, liability, permits, environmental controls, and logistics remain Tesla’s call.

This is a grounded order-of-magnitude estimate based on the Fremont Sprung precedent, industrial structure pricing, and machinery-move data—not a formal quote. If Tesla is truly open to it, the next step is scoping the exact equipment to move and getting firm vendor numbers.

text:
They Themselves Are Sacred Pilgrimage Sites

The presence of virtuous individuals is equivalent to visiting sacred pilgrimage sites. Those holy souls who have mastered their senses and dedicated their lives to spiritual pursuits are, in essence, embodiments of sacred places. Through the gift of their wisdom, they elevate the earnest seekers who come to them for refuge to the highest spiritual state. This is why the places once graced by the footsteps of ascetics and righteous souls eventually become centers of spiritual practice for those who thirst for the Divine. It is with this understanding that Dharmaraja (Yudhishthira), on one occasion, pays homage to his uncle Vidura, asking, "Could there be any pilgrimage site greater than you?" He expresses his profound reverence by acknowledging that the Divine resides within Vidura—that he is, in himself, a sacred pilgrimage site—and that visiting and conversing with such a great soul is akin to visiting a temple.

After the passing of Pandu, the Kauravas subjected the Pandavas to immense suffering. During those trying times, it was Vidura who protected his sister-in-law, Kunti, and her sons—the Pandavas—with the same tender care one might show to the apple of one's eye. Despite the various temptations offered by Dhritarashtra, Duryodhana, and others, Vidura remained unswayed, standing firmly on the side of righteousness (Dharma). Comparing him to a bird that lovingly shelters its young—who are not yet capable of flight—beneath its own wings, Dharmaraja bows at the feet of this noble soul, expressing deep gratitude for the compassion with which he stood by their side. Great souls and supreme devotees amplify the sanctity of divine abodes; through their presence, these sacred sites attain even greater significance. Serving the exalted devotees of the Lord is equivalent to serving the Lord Himself. The wisdom gained through the association of a *Brahma-jnani* (one who has realized the Absolute) far surpasses the knowledge acquired from studying thousands of scriptures. Once, while traveling on foot during the summer, Adi Shankaracharya sat down to rest along the way. Nearby, a frog, exhausted and parched by the intense heat, let out a plaintive cry. Just then, a large cobra emerged from a nearby anthill and approached the frog. Shankara assumed the serpent would devour it; instead, the cobra raised its hood, providing shade and solace to the frog. Intrigued, Shankara turned his gaze inward to contemplate why a snake would shelter a frog. He realized that this was the very place where the sage Rishyasringa had performed his penance. He understood that the profound spiritual power of the sage’s *tapas* (austerities) had dissolved the natural enmity between living beings, fostering a spirit of friendship instead. It was for this reason that he established the *Shringagiri Peetham* at that profoundly sacred site—a place that later became world-renowned as *Sringeri*.

Regions graced by the physical presence of such divine, god-like souls eventually become repositories of immense spiritual power. Arunachalam—where Ramana Maharshi spent his time as a silent sage—and Dakshineswar in Kolkata—where Ramakrishna Paramahamsa practiced as a great ascetic—stand as living testimonies to this. Reflecting on the experience of encountering Paramahamsa, one seeker remarked: "Just as some might naively search elsewhere for precious gems while already possessing the *Kaustubha-mani* (the supreme, divine jewel) by their side, the local people here wander far and wide, even though they have such an embodiment of wisdom—capable of granting ultimate liberation—right in their midst."

text:
THE JESUS EXPERIENCE DAILY REFLECTIONS
Encounter Christ. Understand His Word. Live Your Faith
Scripture: Ezekiel 47:1–2, 8–9, 12 or 1 Corinthians 3:9c–11, 16–17; Psalm 46:2–3, 5–6, 8–9; John 2:13–22.

GOD WANTS TO CLEANSE MORE THAN YOUR CHURCH BUILDING
Today, the Church celebrates the dedication of the Basilica of St John Lateran in Rome, the cathedral of the Pope as Bishop of Rome and traditionally known as the Mother and Head of all the Churches. But today's celebration is about more than an impressive church building. It is an invitation for us to rediscover what it means to be God's dwelling place, individually and as a community of believers. 

Have you ever spent time cleaning your house, arranging clothes and making everything look ordered, only to discover one area of you have been avoiding, which tends to kill your zeal? In a more spiritual sense, that happens to us too. Sometimes, we desire to renew and order ourselves until we meet that area that we have either become comfortable with or that we feel not ready to dela with! 

Today's Gospel presents Jesus doing something unexpected. He enters the Temple in Jerusalem, finds people miss behaving in there, makes a whip out of cords, and drives them out. As he did this, He declares, "Stop making my Father's house a marketplace!"

Why was Jesus so concerned? Is the Temple not just an ordinary building? Do people not sell stuffs in the church every other day? To answer simply, Jesus' action reminds us that: 
1. The Temple is a sacred place of worship, prayer and encounter with God. 
2. What should have helped people draw closer to God must not be entangled with commercial interests. 
3. Religious activities can quickly lose their meaning when our hearts are no longer centred on God.

Think about our lives today. We can attend Mass every Sunday, and sometimes daily, belong to Catholic societies, participate in church activities, wear religious articles and share Bible verses online, yet our hearts is still a market place for hatred, dishonesty, pride, sexual immorality, jealousy and unforgiveness. The temple that we are can sometimes be turned to a place for the wrong thing if we are not always attentive and if we lack the courage to turn over the tables of these vices that seem to have dominated our temple. 

The first reading offers a beautiful image of restoration. Ezekiel sees water flowing from the Temple, bringing life wherever it goes. Even the lifeless, salty waters become fresh. Trees flourish, produce fruit and provide healing. This is what happens when God's presence is allowed to flow into our lives. He does not merely decorate us; He transforms us and makes us fruitful.

The Responsorial Psalm echoes this promise: "The waters of the river gladden the city of God." God's presence brings life, stability and hope.

Pope Francis, in his homily for this feast in 2019, offered a particularly beautiful message: "There is no human heart in which Christ does not want to and cannot be reborn." Even when sin has wounded us, restoration remains possible through Christ.
Vatican

Today, as young Nigerians, we must ask ourselves whether our faith is producing healing around us. Are our friendships places of encouragement or occasions for sin? Do our words build people up or destroy their confidence? Are we using our talents to serve or merely to compete for recognition? Is our presence making our families, parishes and communities more Christlike?

Remember, God wants to dwell in you, but He also wants His presence to flow through you into the lives of others.

TODAY'S CHALLENGE: Identify one thing occupying the space that belongs to God in your heart. Take a concrete step to remove it. Consider going to Confession, reconciling with someone or abandoning a habit that weakens your relationship with Christ.

REFLECT:
1. If Jesus entered the temple of my heart today, what would He need to overturn?
2. Does my presence bring healing, peace and encouragement to the people around me?

DAILY FAITH TAKEAWAY: Don't spend all your time decorating your Christian appearance while neglecting the holiness of your heart. Let Christ cleanse you and make your life a dwelling place for God.

LET US PRAY:
Lord Jesus, cleanse the temple of my heart. Remove everything that prevents me from loving You sincerely. Let Your living water flow through my life, healing my wounds and bringing hope to others. Make me a living stone in Your Church, firmly rooted in You, our only foundation. Amen.

It is a significant milestone in the history of Srila Prabhupada’s ISKCON as three of our senior devotees have accepted the sacred Sannyasa Ashrama (renounced order of life). This Sannyasa Diksha programme was conducted at Vrindavan Chandrodaya Mandir, our spiritual headquarters in the sacred Sri Vrindavan Dham. This joyous occasion marks an important step in strengthening and nurturing dedicated spiritual leadership in our institution.

I extend my heartfelt congratulations and best wishes to HH Amitasana Krishna Swami, HH Satya Gaura Chandra Swami and HH Sridham Krishna Swami on their initiation into Sannyasa Ashrama in accordance with the Gaudiya Vaishnava traditions. Having dedicated more than three decades of their lives to serving Guru and Krishna, they have now accepted the greater responsibility of the renounced order.

I am thankful to HH Stoka Krishna Swami, who officiated the ceremony and continues to set an inspiring example of dedicated service and surrender.

I express my sincere appreciation to Sri Chanchalapathi Prabhu, Sri Jai Chaitanya Prabhu, Sri Vasudev Keshav Prabhu, and all the other devotees who meticulously planned and coordinated the proceedings, which made this event spiritually enriching for everyone present.

I am happy that the members of the Governing Body Commission and the Temple Presidents of Srila Prabhupada’s ISKCON Worldwide Group joined us on this important occasion.

We were especially blessed by the presence of Srila Prabhupada’s pre-1977 disciples, Sri Sattvik Prabhu, Sri Tattva Darshan Prabhu and Sri Gauranga Prabhu, who played significant roles in the early development of ISKCON Bangalore and whose continued blessings and association are invaluable to our Group.

We were grateful to the Sri Vaishnava pujaris from Swayambhu Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple, Hyderabad, who came and offered their prayers for the divine protection of Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy upon the newly initiated sannyasis.

The presence of devotees and well-wishers from India and abroad added to the joy of this memorable event held during this auspicious Karthika month.

I pray to Sri Sri Radha Vrindavanchandra and Srila Prabhupada that the newly initiated Tridandi Sannyasis may be blessed with the spiritual strength and determination to travel extensively, guide devotees and spread the message of Krishna consciousness far and wide.

May their exemplary lives inspire many more devotees to dedicate themselves wholeheartedly to Srila Prabhupada’s preaching mission.

All glories to Srila Prabhupada!

Hare Krishna!

India needs constitutional accountability, not personality cults; public service, not political spectacle; and fraternity, not manufactured hatred.
