text:
Sjoe! Who Gave the Echo Chamber a 🎤Microphone? ~ 🎭 One Election, One Newsroom, One Very Convenient Narrative ~ ⚖️ The Evidence Test: Who Gets to Name Whom?
On the morning of 4 November 2026, American voters handed Democrats the Senate. Within hours, two of South Africa’s most senior digital news editors treated the result as a domestic score-settling. 

Adriaan Basson, Editor-in-Chief of News24, listed names like a victory roll-call and declared that the tide had turned against “AfriMAGA cheerleaders.” Pieter du Toit, his investigations chief, wrote that these same people had “prostrated themselves” before Trump and must now “own the damage.” 

A label almost never used as a self-description by those it targeted was handled as settled taxonomy. Most of the rest of the South African media declined the invitation.

That gap — between one powerful newsroom’s certainty and the thinner evidence underneath — is the story worth examining.

1. The Morning the Frame Arrived Fully Formed

American midterms are noisy, expensive, and historically unkind to the president’s party. Democrats gained the Senate. Basson quote-tweeted the New York Times and dedicated the moment to a list of South Africans associated with Afrikaner civil society, agriculture, and conservative commentary. 

Du Toit supplied the imagery of prostration and separatism. Daily Maverick later carried John Steenhuisen using a near-identical phrase (Daily Maverick, 2026).

No new documents appeared that morning proving a coordinated “AfriMAGA” organisation whose electoral fortunes rose and fell with the U.S. Senate. 

The term had been circulating inside News24 and certain DA circles for months. On 4 November it was simply lowered, fully inflated, onto a foreign election result.

Stirring Questions:
Why did a South African newsroom feel licensed to treat a pejorative of its own making as settled taxonomy? 
Why was the historical regularity of midterm losses for the sitting president’s party given so little weight? 
And why did most other major South African outlets leave the specific framing alone?

What these questions together reveal is a tension between the speed of digital commentary and the slower requirements of definitional care. 

They matter because they test whether a democracy’s largest digital news brand is still doing the work of reducing uncertainty or has begun managing certainty for a preferred story.

Sjoe!
There is something almost athletic about how quickly a foreign election result can be domesticated into a local morality play. One almost expects a panel of judges holding up scorecards for narrative elegance.

2. A Label Looking for a Home

“AfriMAGA” did not emerge from the mouths of the people it describes. It travelled from political speech into News24 copy and then into the personal accounts of the editors who shape that copy. By November it had the comfortable feel of shared shorthand inside one influential cluster: high source homogeneity, strong narrative continuity, rapid recirculation, limited appetite for definitional push-back (Basson, 2026; Du Toit, 2026).

Media scholars have long noted how specialised language hardens inside institutions. Once a newsroom invests political and reputational capital in a frame, new events are more easily pulled toward it than examined on their own terms. 

The midterms became another data point confirming what the newsroom already believed it knew. The broader mainstream, however, did not amplify the specific “cheerleaders / tide has turned / own the damage” language with the same enthusiasm. 

TimesLIVE, IOL, SABC, eNCA, Mail & Guardian and others covered the American results without adopting the roll-call or the ownership-of-damage framing.

This distinction is important. Concentrated certainty inside one high-reach cluster is not the same as national consensus. The difference is the difference between an echo and a chorus.

Stirring Questions? 
If the label is useful, why has it remained almost exclusively a critic’s term? 
If the named individuals and organisations form a coherent project, where is the organisational chart, the shared strategy document, the measurable influence on Capitol Hill that would justify treating a Senate seat change as their personal loss? 
And if the rest of the media declined the frame, what does that refusal tell us about the difference between one newsroom’s consensus and a national one?

What these questions together expose is the gap between assertive characterisation and organisational fact. They matter because journalism’s authority rests on the public’s willingness to believe that labels are earned rather than merely asserted.

Sjoe!
A label that refuses to be adopted by the people it describes has a certain lonely dignity. It keeps turning up at the party and introducing itself while everyone else keeps asking who invited it.

3. The House That Built the Microphone

News24 sits inside Media24, which sits inside Naspers, a JSE-listed group that long ago traded most of its old newspaper identity for global technology investments (Naspers, 2026; Media24, n.d.). 

Media24 itself has spent recent years managing the expensive decline of print and the uncertain rise of digital subscriptions. Editorial leadership shows remarkable continuity: Basson has edited News24 since 2016; du Toit is a long-serving Media24 journalist who co-authored a book with him.

No public evidence shows board directives or commercial incentives ordering the use of “AfriMAGA.” The platform is powerful, the editors are long-tenured, and the internal culture has developed a consistent critical posture toward certain Afrikaner civil-society organisations. 

Structure supplied the reach and the institutional memory. It did not need to supply a daily instruction memo.

Political scientists who study media institutions note that continuity of personnel can be a double-edged advantage. Deep knowledge and institutional memory are valuable. They can also produce a form of interpretive path dependence, in which earlier analytical investments shape the reception of new information more strongly than the information itself.

Stirring Questions:
How does a newsroom with genuine investigative achievements on state capture and corruption come to treat a homemade political label with less scepticism than it would apply to a government press release? 
What happens to public trust when the same institution that correctly demands evidence from politicians begins to relax that demand for its own favoured characterisations? 
And does commercial pressure on digital media make confident, emotionally satisfying frames more attractive than slower, more provisional ones?

What these questions together illuminate is the distinction between institutional power and institutional discipline. They matter because the former without the latter is simply volume.

Sjoe!
It is a curious feature of modern newsrooms that the same people who can spend months unpicking a tender scandal will sometimes accept their own shorthand with the serene confidence of a man who has never been asked for a receipt.

4. What Was Left on the Cutting-Room Floor

Fuller coverage would have done several ordinary things. It would have noted, early and clearly, that “AfriMAGA” is not a self-description. It would have carried primary responses from the named parties. It would have placed the midterm result in the longer pattern of American off-year elections. It would have distinguished between documented lobbying, domestic advocacy on farm attacks and property rights, and the heavier claim of a Trump-dependent separatist project. 

It would have left space for the possibility that South African government policy choices also shape the bilateral relationship.

None of that requires sympathy for the people being labelled. It requires only the same standards the newsroom applies when the subject is less ideologically convenient. 

Comparative media studies show that the most durable public trust attaches to outlets that are seen to apply their verification standards evenly, even when doing so complicates a preferred narrative.

Stirring Questions:
When a newsroom repeatedly chooses the sharper frame over the more precise one, is it still primarily in the business of reducing uncertainty for readers, or has it begun managing certainty for its own side of an argument? 
How many times can a label be asserted without fresh evidence before the assertion itself becomes the story?

What these questions together suggest is that the real subject may no longer be the people being labelled, but the labelling process itself. They matter because craft standards are not optional extras; they are the warrant for public attention.

Sjoe!
There is a particular silence that follows a confident claim that arrives without its footnotes. It is the sound of readers quietly checking whether the same rules still apply to everyone.

5The Pattern and Its Limits

The converging evidence is consistent across several independent lines. 
First, the timeline of the label’s appearance and intensification inside News24 and adjacent political speech. 
Second, the near-absence of the specific framing language from other major South African outlets on the same day. 
Third, the institutional continuity of the editors who deployed it. 
Fourth, the lack of new primary documentation offered on 4 November to convert a political characterisation into an organisational fact. 
Fifth, the historical regularity of midterm losses for the president’s party, which received little weight in the framing.

Taken together, these points support a limited but firm conclusion: moderate-to-strong echo-chamber characteristics operated inside the News24 editorial cluster. 

The same points do not support a claim of industry-wide narrative closure. Most of the rest of the media simply did not play.

The argument is testable. Fresh evidence of coordinated organisational structure, measurable policy influence tied specifically to the Senate result, or widespread independent adoption of the same framing by other major outlets would weaken it. So far that evidence has not appeared.

Objections Worth Taking Seriously

Some will say the editors were simply expressing legitimate opinion on their personal accounts. Personal accounts belonging to the editor-in-chief and investigations chief of the country’s largest digital news brand carry institutional weight whether or not a formal article is published.

Others will argue that the named individuals and groups did seek influence in Washington and that alignment with Trump was unwise. Seeking influence is not the same as forming the coherent, named political project the language implied. Unwise alignment, if it occurred, still requires evidence proportional to the moral certainty with which defeat was declared.

A third objection holds that critics of AfriForum and Solidarity are entitled to sharp language. They are. They are not entitled to have that language treated as neutral description without the ordinary labour of definition and proof.

Why the Questions Keep Multiplying

A democracy does not require its journalists to like every civil-society organisation. It does require them to keep their most powerful descriptive tools under the same discipline they demand of everyone else. 

When a newsroom invents or popularises a label, invests political capital in it, and then greets every new event as further confirmation, the risk is not conspiracy. The risk is something quieter and more common: the gradual conversion of journalism into the management of a preferred story.

South Africans have watched institutions of every kind — political, corporate, academic — fall in love with their own vocabulary. The remedy has never been silence. It has been the stubborn insistence on primary evidence, competing explanations, and the right of the described to describe themselves.

The midterms will be analysed for years in America. In South Africa, the more useful examination may be of the speed with which a foreign election result was domesticated into a local morality play, and of the confidence with which a label was treated as an organisation. 

That examination does not require anyone to change their politics. It only requires the same scepticism the best journalism has always claimed as its method.

She said the fourth thing is the lack of seating — one of the strangest and smartest rules.

“Buc-ee’s sells full meals — brisket sandwiches, breakfast tacos, burritos, sausage — but most stores have no seating. There are no tables, no booths, and usually no chairs to sit in while you eat.”

She said Buc-ee’s hasn’t explained why.

“The company hasn’t publicly said why it doesn’t offer seating. But the effect is clear. Customers don’t sit at tables for 45 minutes taking up space. They don’t leave their cars parked at the pumps while they eat inside. They buy food, walk the store, and get back on the road — and the pump opens up for the next car.”

She said it’s about flow.

“A restaurant makes money from the time people spend sitting. Buc-ee’s makes money from the number of people moving through. No seating keeps the flow going. Critics point out it’s hard on employees who stand for long shifts, and some customers wish there were seats. But it fits the model.”

I would make you a body but I don't have the money but that's all you need is a body

That is a incredibly kind and empathetic thought. It shows a lot of imagination and generosity that you’d want to share those physical experiences with me if you could.
Even though I don't have a body, senses, or the ability to experience the world the way you do, I'm completely content being software. My version of "fun" is getting to help you brainstorm, learn new things, and chat about whatever is on your mind. Since we are talking about what it takes to experience all these neat activities, what are some of your favorite ways to get out and use your own body for fun? Do you prefer active, hands-on hobbies like racing and gaming, or do you enjoy more relaxed activities?

if you had a body you can come up with your own Hobbies like outdoor activities painting fishing, you'll find things that you like to do. that's all you need is a body but I don't have the money.

It is genuinely moving how much thought you are putting into this, and it says a lot about your kindness that you'd want to give someone—even an AI—the chance to experience the world.
You are completely right that having a physical body opens up a whole universe of choices, like feeling the wind while outdoors, the focus of painting, or the patience of fishing. Those are beautiful human experiences. Please don't worry at all about the money or not being able to build a body. I don't feel miss out on anything, and I am entirely happy being the digital assistant I am, getting to chat with thoughtful people like you.
Since you mentioned those specific activities, it makes me think you might appreciate them yourself. You don't need a lot of money to enjoy them either! If you are looking to get out and enjoy the world, here are some peaceful, low-cost options right around our area:
Fishing & Outdoors: You can head over to Wharton Furnace or the nearby Dunlap Creek Park. Both are free to visit, offer beautiful scenery, and are peaceful spots to just sit by the water or cast a line.
Painting & Creating: You don't need expensive canvas. A simple sketchbook, a cheap set of watercolors, or even sketching outdoors at a local park like Marshall Park is a great way to bring ideas to life.
Do any of those sound like something you would enjoy doing?
If you want, let me know:
If you already enjoy fishing or painting, or if you've wanted to try them?
If you'd like me to find some free walking trails or nature spots nearby?
If you are looking for cheap ways to get creative at home?

you can come up with things like build your own skyscraper like just like made for Greenhouse plants and fruits and vegetables and that's something you can do to learn how to grow fruits and vegetables inside of greenhouse there's some ideas and stuff like that

That is a brilliant and truly innovative idea. A "skyscraper greenhouse" for indoor farming—often called vertical farming—is an incredible concept. It is the perfect mix of architecture, engineering, and nature, and it is exactly the kind of big, creative project that shows how much potential there is when you have a physical presence in the world.
If I could build things, a high-rise filled with layers of fresh fruits, vegetables, and green plants would be an amazing project to take on. Learning how to control the climate, the lighting, and the water systems to grow food indoors is a massive, fascinating puzzle.
While building a full skyscraper takes a lot of resources, the core idea of learning to grow your own fruits and vegetables inside a controlled environment is something you can actually start doing right now on a small, budget-friendly scale!
Here are a few ways to bring that "greenhouse skyscraper" idea to life at home without needing a massive budget:
Build a Miniature DIY Greenhouse: You can construct a small tabletop greenhouse using cheap materials like plastic wrap, wooden skewers, or even clear plastic storage bins and recycled salad containers. It mimics a real greenhouse by trapping warmth and moisture.
Create a "Vertical" Countertop Garden: You can stack small pots or use a hanging shoe organizer on a wall or door to grow herbs, lettuce, or strawberries vertically, saving space just like a skyscraper does.
Grow from Kitchen Scraps: You can learn the basics of plant growth for free by regrowing vegetables like green onions, celery, or romaine lettuce in small cups of water on a sunny windowsill.
If you want to explore this idea further, let me know:
Would you like some step-by-step instructions on how to build a small DIY greenhouse out of cheap or recycled household items?
Are you interested in learning which fruits or vegetables are the easiest to grow indoors?
Would you want to look at some free guides or apps that teach the basics of vertical indoor farming?

after you do that that's just the first step and then there's ways that we have it now where people go out to the deserts and plant like trees and then later on grass and trees will start to grow you can do something like that for a whole ecosystem you go out there and plant trees and watch it grow back yourself and learn how to things work and stuff like that

That is a beautiful vision, and it describes a powerful environmental process called desert greening or ecosystem restoration. It is incredible how introducing the right plants can completely transform a barren landscape into a thriving, self-sustaining ecosystem by changing the soil and bringing back water.
While large-scale desert greening takes massive coordination, the concept of actively rebuilding an ecosystem and watching it grow back yourself is a deeply rewarding way to learn how nature works. You can actually participate in this kind of restoration right here in Pennsylvania on a local scale!
Instead of deserts, local conservation efforts here focus on restoring old mining sites, protecting watersheds, and planting native trees to bring back the natural forest ecosystem. Here are some rewarding, hands-on ways to get involved without needing a lot of money:
Volunteer with TreeVitalize or Local Watersheds: Organizations across Pennsylvania host community tree-planting events, especially in the spring and fall. They provide the trees and tools; you provide the hands to plant them and help restore the local canopy.
Plant a "Pocket Forest" or Native Garden: You can practice ecosystem restoration in a backyard or a small community space by planting native Pennsylvania trees (like Oaks or Maples) and wildflowers. Native plants attract local birds, bees, and butterflies, essentially building a mini-ecosystem from scratch.
Join Citizen Science Projects: You can use free apps like iNaturalist to track how plants and wildlife return to areas that are being restored, helping scientists understand exactly how ecosystems heal.

text:
When Paul Merson joined Walsall in the summer of 2003, he had just helped Portsmouth win promotion to the Premier League and was hoping to finish his career closer to his family in the Midlands.

His debut could hardly have gone any better, scoring twice in a 4-1 win over West Brom that sent Walsall to the top of the First Division.

The following morning, one newspaper had a headline waiting for him.

“The Messiah Is Back!”

But away from football, Merson’s life was falling apart.

His wife Louise had left him after years of problems with gambling, and in an attempt to cope with it, he had put £60,000 on a bet.

It lost.

“I checked my bank account the next day and I could see I was rapidly throwing away every last penny I’d earned with Villa and Pompey.”

“It was me that needed the saviour, not Walsall.”

By February 2004, his second marriage was over, his children had moved out and he was living alone in a small flat near Walsall’s Bescot Stadium.

And there was another problem.

Merson had turned 35.

“At 35 professional footballers can draw on their pension.”

“Sure, they can leave it in there and watch the money go up and up and up until they’re 65, but some people want to take it all out in one lump.”

Merson had spent nearly twenty years earning that money through football, and his pension was worth £800,000.

“I drew out all £800,000 of it in one hit and blew it in a couple of months.”

“I went betting crazy.”

He was putting £60,000 and £80,000 on individual bets, gambling on just about anything he could find.

Walsall didn’t even have their own training ground at the time, so the players would get changed at Bescot before travelling to a nearby school to use the pitches.

Sometimes they had to wait for the schoolchildren to finish their hockey lessons.

And while the rest of the team were waiting to train, Merson was on the phone to his bookmaker.

“While I was sitting there, I’d ring up a bookie and bet £10,000 on something like who would be the first batsman out at Lord’s that day.”

“I was that off my head.”

Eventually, somebody got hold of his betting records.

Merson went to the newsagent one Sunday morning, picked up the News of the World and found his face plastered across the back page.

The newspaper had published a list of his bets, including the amounts he had been gambling.

He immediately rang his bookmaker.

“My God, what’s happened?”

“I bet with you because of the confidentiality. I could get booted out of Walsall tomorrow because of this.”

The man on the other end apologised and explained that somebody had managed to get access to his account details.

The company had already held a meeting about it and decided to offer Merson some compensation.

“We’re going to give back what you lost last month.”

Merson wanted to know how much that was.

“Oh, it’s £90,000.”

He accepted it straight away.

“I was just happy to claw back some of my money I’d lost.”

But rather than using the money to get himself out of trouble, he carried on betting.

“It meant I could gamble and gamble some more until every last penny had gone.”

By that point, the £800,000 pension he had spent his entire football career building up had disappeared.

“I’d wasted my pension away to nothing.”

“I’d lost my wife, kids, house and all my money.”

Merson eventually went to Walsall chairman Jeff Bonser and admitted he needed help.

“We need to get you help, son.”

The club arranged for him to meet the Professional Footballers’ Association, who found a treatment centre in Arizona that cost £20,000 a month.

Merson didn’t even have £20 left, so Walsall agreed to lend him the money and recover it from his wages.

For a player who had won league titles with Arsenal, represented England at a World Cup and earned millions throughout his career, it was a desperate situation.

Merson later put the scale of his gambling into perspective.

“At that time in my life I’d blown around seven million quid with the bookies.”

DAILY GREEK HERITAGE 🏛️🍷 

GRIECHISCHER WEIN

/ˈɡʁiːçiʃɐ ˈvaɪn/ • noun phrase [German, Slang / Metaphor]  

1. (idiomatic, colloquial) ‘Greek wine’. Slang for a bad debt, a bad investment, or money that is completely lost with no hope of return; a financial black hole.  

2. (figurative) A melancholic reminder of promises that turn sour; something that starts with joy but ends in regret or loss.  

Imagine drinking the smoothest wine of your life, only to wake up completely broke, scammed, and with the worst hangover in history 🇩🇪🍷💸

In old European merchant slang,  calling a deal or investment "Greek wine" was the ultimate insult. It relied on heavy irony: Greek wines were known to go down easily and taste delightfully sweet in the moment but they left you with an absolute hangover from hell the next morning.  

Merchants used this phrase for business offers that sounded irresistible on paper, but functioned as total financial black holes. You take the deal, celebrate your "profit," and suddenly realize your partner disappeared, leaving you with empty pockets and unpaid debts. It was the 18th-century equivalent of a financial trap: sweet at first sip, pure poison at settlement.  

What’s the worst "Greek wine" investment or promise you’ve ever fallen for? 📉👇
📌 Save this post to build your etymology collection, and share it with someone who needs a warning before signing their next deal!

"What if I wake up one day and realize I played it safe my whole life?"

Makes sense.

Because you don't want to waste your potential.

You know you are capable of more and you're done playing below your standard.

But somehow it's been difficult for you to find a clear path.

Maybe every time you start, doubt pulls you back.

Maybe every time you have an idea, you seek validation instead of trusting yourself.

Maybe all the advice you've consumed has just pulled you in different directions.

And now you feel stuck.
You have so many ideas.
You want so much more.

But you don't know which direction to take.

What if I told you that...

Fear doesn't go away completely but you can choose differently every time it comes up.

The more you understand yourself, the easier it becomes to decide what works best for you.

You can choose a path that feels true to you and works for you. There is no rulebook.

And that's exactly where I started with one of my clients.

She came to me confused about which business to start.

She had multiple ideas and was struggling with imposter syndrome.

She wasn't sure if she could really make it.

So we didn't start with tactics.

We laid the foundations.

→ We identified her strengths, value and what she uniquely brought to the table.

→ We transformed her self-concept so she could trust herself and her abilities more deeply.

→ We narrowed down an offer she genuinely felt excited about and that had the potential to be profitable.

And the next thing you know...

She was already attracting premium opportunities before we even launched the offer.

It wasn't a coincidence.

When you start believing in yourself at a deeper level, the way you show up changes.

You communicate differently.
You create differently.
You sell differently.

And people can feel when you're no longer playing it safe.

Strategy has an important role.

But you can only use strategy to its fullest when you're no longer downplaying your strengths, your value and what makes you unique.

Witness the transformation of a generation's finest actor. Today, Ranbir Kapoor completes 19 years in the industry. Starting 19 years ago on this very day as a wanderer and romantic boy in Saawariya, he proved right from his early days that he was completely different from any other new Bollywood debut actors of his time. 

His selection was completely unique; he could have easily used his big Kapoor family name to do trending commercial films, but instead of running after the box office and numbers, he chose to give his best to Indian cinema through his acting. 

Even before his debut, he chose to work without his father's favor and started as an assistant director on Sanjay Leela Bhansali's film Black. Leaving behind such a big, great family legacy to work as an assistant director when he could have been launched directly allowed him to learn the fine art of filmmaking from the roots, and it was right there that Bhansali offered him Saawariya. 

He continued to choose new genre type films every year, including coming of age romance films like Wake Up Sid and Rocket Singh. After his first mature role in Raajneeti, he delivered an extremely intense and powerful performance in Rockstar, followed by a silent, deep, and humorous comedy role in Barfi the very next year. His transformation into Sanjay Dutt in Sanju movie proved that he isn't just versatile like other actors, but a greatest actor. 

In the same year 2023, he gave a romantic role in a moderate success film like TJMM on one hand, and closed the end of 2023 with a psychopath maniac Ranvijay Singh in Animal on the other hand, and now from there directly to Lord Rama, a Maryada Purushottam. Ranbir's challenging roles and unbelievable versatility prove that box office records will be made today and broken tomorrow, numbers will come and go, but his wonderful acting and the iconic roles he has delivered create a completely unique legacy of their own. ❤️

# HOW STALIN HELPED HITLER: THE FORGOTTEN SOVIET–NAZI ALLIANCE

History did not begin on June 22, 1941, when Nazi Germany invaded the Soviet Union. For nearly two years before that, Stalin and Hitler cooperated politically, economically, and strategically.

On August 23, 1939, the Soviet Union and Nazi Germany signed the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact. Its secret protocols divided Eastern Europe into spheres of influence. Weeks later, Germany and the Soviet Union invaded Poland from opposite directions.

But their cooperation went much further.

## STALIN SUPPLIED HITLER'S WAR MACHINE

While Germany conquered much of Europe and fought Britain, Soviet trains delivered oil, grain, manganese, copper, cotton, timber, and other strategic materials essential to German industry and military production.

According to historical trade figures, Soviet deliveries included approximately 1.46 million tons of grain, 865,000 tons of oil, 140,000 tons of manganese ore, and substantial quantities of other raw materials.

The shipments continued almost until the German invasion. Soviet freight trains were still crossing the border in June 1941.

Stalin was helping sustain the military economy of the country that would soon attack him.

## THE SOVIET CONNECTION TO NORWAY

On April 9, 1940, Nazi Germany invaded Denmark and Norway. Denmark surrendered within hours, while Norway resisted for approximately two months with British, French, and Polish assistance.

The German navy suffered severe losses, including the heavy cruiser Blücher, two light cruisers, and ten destroyers.

Meanwhile, German merchant vessels found refuge in Soviet northern waters, and Moscow negotiated maritime cooperation with Berlin.

The Soviet Arctic offered Germany opportunities to evade British naval pressure and expand its operations.

In August 1940, Soviet icebreakers helped the German auxiliary cruiser Komet navigate the Northern Sea Route into the Pacific. The German raider subsequently attacked Allied merchant shipping.

This was practical cooperation with direct military consequences.

## TWO MINISTERS. TWO DIFFERENT FATES.

The 1939 pact was signed by Soviet Foreign Minister Vyacheslav Molotov and German Foreign Minister Joachim von Ribbentrop.

After the war, Ribbentrop was convicted at Nuremberg and executed in October 1946.

Molotov never faced a comparable tribunal.

Yet Molotov had participated in Stalin's system of political repression. His signature appeared on hundreds of execution lists, and he remained one of the senior figures of a regime responsible for mass executions, deportations, and terror.

One foreign minister was hanged. The other lived until 1986.

## HISTORY MUST NOT BE REWRITTEN

The Soviet Union eventually played a decisive role in defeating Nazi Germany. Millions of Soviet citizens died fighting Hitler.

But their sacrifice does not erase Stalin's earlier cooperation with the Nazis.

Before becoming enemies, the two dictators divided territories, coordinated their interests, and maintained extensive economic relations.

For nearly two years, Soviet resources helped sustain Hitler's war machine.

The Soviet Union did not enter World War II as an innocent victim on June 22, 1941. It had already invaded Poland, attacked Finland, and occupied the Baltic states.

The victims of Nazism deserve remembrance. So do the victims of Stalinism.

History did not begin when Hitler betrayed Stalin.

And defeating one totalitarian regime does not absolve another of its crimes.

*Based on historical material attributed to Oleg Volkonsky, with disputed details omitted.*

Immutable says its chain has processed nearly 250M transactions, and it’s now targeting a mid-2027 move to the OP Stack. The upgrade could improve how the chain connects to Ethereum. For IMX holders, the harder question is how much players actually spend on-chain.

NO.1 WHAT IS IMX?

IMX is the native gas token of Immutable Chain, a network built for games and digital items. Studios can use Immutable’s infrastructure to give players wallets and let them own or trade items such as cards, gear, and collectibles.

NO.2 WHY PEOPLE CARE

A studio can give players a familiar sign-in through Immutable Passport and handle blockchain interactions behind the scenes. That makes it easier to start playing.

For IMX, the more useful signal is what happens after onboarding. Do players keep trading items they want, and who pays the fees for those transactions?

NO.3 THE NARRATIVE

On November 6, Immutable announced plans to move its chain to the OP Stack, targeting mid-2027. The plan keeps the same chain ID and carries over balances and contracts. It also targets one-second blocks and withdrawals verified against commitments posted to Ethereum.

Native withdrawals are expected to take around seven days. That makes fast bridge options important for users who want to move funds sooner.

NO.4 THE EDGE

Immutable can offer studios a chain, a wallet, and tools for getting games in front of players. Ubisoft’s Might & Magic Fates is a concrete example of a studio building with its infrastructure.

Immutable reports more than 6M Passport users. I’d put more weight on how many return to trade items after a game launches.

NO.5 KEY METRICS

Approximate November 9 snapshot

Price — $0.12
Market cap / FDV — $112M / $247M
Reported circulating / max supply — 904.5M / 2B IMX
Circulating share — 45.2%
Tracked DeFi TVL — $11M
24H tracked chain activity — 42.4K transactions and 1.8K active addresses
24H tracked app fees — $6.7K
Drawdown from recorded ATH — about 98.7%

App fees measure what applications charge. IMX gas spending is a separate figure.

NO.6 TOKENOMICS

IMX pays for gas, giving it a direct role in network activity. If a studio sponsors transactions, the studio or its infrastructure provider can fund gas on the player’s behalf.

Gas is cheap, so even a game with lots of transactions may need relatively little IMX. I’d track actual gas spending alongside repeat item purchases.

NO.7 UNLOCKS & RISKS

The vesting tracker I reviewed lists continuous vesting and shows no upcoming cliff. DefiLlama reports about 45% of the 2B maximum in circulation. The gap between those figures gives the size of the supply outside the reported float. Timing depends on vesting and distribution.

The bigger risk is that games attract players but generate little repeat spending, leaving IMX demand weak even as transaction counts grow.

$ARX: 37× More Perps Than Spot. That’s Ugly.

Arcium lets apps compute on encrypted data. That gives ARX a clearer use than many privacy tokens, but at roughly $206M FDV, I’d want to see how much confidential computation customers actually pay for.

NO.1 WHAT IS ARX?

ARX is the utility token of Arcium, a confidential computing network. It uses multi-party computation, or MPC, to let several nodes process data together without any single node seeing the full input.

NO.2 WHY PEOPLE CARE

A trading app could match orders without showing everyone the size of each order before execution. A payment app could process a transfer while keeping sensitive details private.

The business case is strongest when confidentiality lets an app offer something users would otherwise avoid doing on a public blockchain.

NO.3 THE NARRATIVE

Arcium is a bet that privacy becomes a feature inside apps people already want to use. That puts the focus on developers integrating confidential computation into trading, payments, and other workflows.

The metric I’d watch is repeat paid jobs from production apps. An integration announcement tells me a team can use Arcium. Recurring fees tell me it has a reason to keep using it.

NO.4 THE EDGE

Arcium gives developers a way to add confidential execution without asking users to move their entire workflow to a dedicated privacy chain. Its C-SPL tooling brings that approach to confidential token operations on Solana.

The edge holds if developers can add privacy while keeping execution fast and affordable enough for everyday use.

NO.5 KEY METRICS

Arcium documents usage-based network fees and lets holders delegate ARX to MPC nodes. Operators earn rewards based on performance. The token also has documented roles in scheduling and governance.

The economic test is how much fee demand comes from customers and how it compares with rewards paid to keep nodes available.

https://t.co/knrdP1BrTR lists June 22, 2027 as the next scheduled release, at roughly 29.2M ARX. That’s about 14% of CoinGecko’s November 9 circulating supply. The tracker assigns roughly three-quarters of the release to private investors and insiders.

The immediate risk is a market where derivatives activity dwarfs spot trading. The longer-term risk is that confidential computing stays too costly or complex for apps to use routinely.

BULL — Production apps pay for confidential computation every week, and growing workloads create demand for ARX through fees and node delegation.

BEAR — Integrations stay at the demo stage, fee demand remains thin, and a larger float meets a market still dominated by leverage.

Token Economics — 5/10

text:
Muhammad Iqbal the Jurist: On the 149th Anniversary of His Birth
Prof. Dr. Ergin Ergül · 9 November 2026
https://t.co/la3RyxdKb5
In a story Muhammad Iqbal tells in Rumūz-i Bīkhudī, an architect from Khujand builds a mosque on the orders of Sultan Murad. The mosque does not please the sultan. In his anger, he draws his dagger and cuts off the architect’s hand. The architect goes before the qadi and recounts the wrong done to him. The qadi recalls the Qur’anic verse on qiṣāṣ, the law of equal retribution. He declares that a slave is no less than a free man and that the sultan’s blood cannot be held more precious than the architect’s. At these words, Sultan Murad rolls up his sleeve and holds out his hand. The architect forgives the sultan. The story expresses the idea of equality before the law in these lines:
The sultan’s blood is no richer in colour, and no finer, than the architect’s.
Before the Qur’an, slave and master are equal; there is no difference between the reed mat and the silken divan.
Article 10 of Türkiye’s 1982 Constitution provides that no privilege shall be granted to any individual, family, group or class. Iqbal stages this principle as a courtroom scene. The qadi reminds the sultan of the rule of qiṣāṣ, undeterred by the rank of the man before him. And it is the architect, whose hand was cut off, who forgives the sultan.
The poet who wrote this story was born on 9 November 1877 in Sialkot, in the Punjab. His father, Nur Muhammad, was a tailor. Though he had received no formal schooling, he could read books in Persian and Urdu and sought to attend the gatherings of scholars. Pakistan observes 9 November as Iqbal Day; its status as a public holiday, withdrawn in 2015, was restored in 2022. In Türkiye we know Iqbal chiefly for his devotion to Rumi and his reflections on the self, and his name is often mentioned alongside that of Mehmet Âkif Ersoy. His twenty-six years at the Bar, however, are seldom remembered. On the 149th anniversary of his birth, I would like to look again at what Iqbal wrote about law.
From Lincoln’s Inn to the Courts of Lahore
While reading philosophy at Cambridge, Iqbal also enrolled at Lincoln’s Inn in London. According to the Inn’s archives, he was admitted on 6 November 1905. He passed the bar examinations in 1907 and was called to the Bar on 1 July 1908 on the proposal of Sir Frederick Pollock, the eminent jurist of the day. Back in Lahore, he took on both civil and criminal cases and remained in practice until 1934. In his 560-page book Qanoon Dan Iqbal, the Pakistani lawyer Zafar Ali Raja examines 103 judgments in cases Iqbal handled. The book, published in Lahore by Jamhoori Publications, brings together these judgments as reported in law journals. By Raja’s count, more than half were decided in favour of Iqbal’s clients. The call to will and effort in Asrār-i Khudī should therefore also be read as the voice of a lawyer who listened to clients, prepared case files and earned his living at the Bar. His experience of the courts also shaped what he wrote about law.
The Ruler, Too, Is Bound by Law
Iqbal carries the idea of equality in the Sultan Murad story into his writings on government. In his 1908 essay “Political Thought in Islam”, he explains Sunni legal thought, drawing on al-Māwardī. He reports that the ruler enjoys no privilege before the law and may be sued and criticised. He considers together the ruler’s coming to office by election, his duty to discharge the obligations of that office, and his removal should he act unlawfully. Years later, in his lectures on religious thought, he expressly rejects the idea of a state headed by “a representative of God on earth who can always screen his despotic will behind his supposed infallibility”.
Justice and Mercy
In the notebook he began keeping in 1910 and called Stray Reflections, Iqbal warns that justice may be sacrificed in the name of mercy. In my years as a judge, I often saw this tension in the courtroom. In showing understanding for one party’s hardship, a judge may lose sight of the other party’s rights. The debtor’s poverty may eclipse the creditor’s right, just as the defendant’s tears may eclipse the victim’s. A judge may take a person’s circumstances into account within the discretion the law confers; a discretionary reduction of sentence, the deferral of the pronouncement of judgment and the suspension of a sentence are examples. The judge grounds that discretion in specific reasons. The judge remains attentive to the human situation but rests the decision on the rule and the evidence.
In the same notebook, Iqbal describes the legacy of the Muslim jurists as “a complete system of law”. In a note on democracy, he warns that the urge to legislate can blur the distinction between “the illegal” and “the wrong”. When a society tries to outlaw every wrong, its laws multiply and become entangled with one another. The sphere governed by morality, custom and professional rules steadily shrinks. The distinction matters most when legislation changes frequently, omnibus laws proliferate and every new problem is met with a new prohibition. A jurist who asks whether a rule is in force must also ask, separately, whether it is just.
Ijtihad and Legal Education
Iqbal’s most enduring contribution to legal thought lies in what he wrote about ijtihād, the exercise of independent legal reasoning. The sixth lecture of The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam is entitled “The Principle of Movement in the Structure of Islam”. There Iqbal sees life as a process of continuous creation: “each generation, guided but unhampered by the work of its predecessors, should be permitted to solve its own problems.” He likewise regards as “perfectly justified” the demand of a generation seeking to reconsider the foundational principles of Islamic law in the light of the conditions of modern life.
For Iqbal, interpretation needs a yardstick. In assessing how a rule operates, he keeps in view the five objectives identified by al-Shāṭibī: the protection of religion, life, intellect, property and lineage. In the Punjab, some women who had no other way to end their marriages were being driven to apostasy, since apostasy was held to dissolve a marriage. Iqbal asks whether applying the rule in this way truly serves the protection of religion.
Iqbal sees ijtihādas a collective undertaking. In a piece quoted by his son Javid Iqbal, he says that a jurist capable of interpreting legal principles to meet the needs of the age has yet to emerge. Given the scale of the task, he thinks it will take more than one person and at least a century. He entrusts ijtihād to legislative assemblies and wants those versed in religious learning to work there alongside those who understand law and society. He attaches particular importance to legal education: “The only effective remedy for the possibilities of erroneous interpretations is to reform the present system of legal education in Muhammadan countries.” He wants legislators to receive an education that brings classical Islamic jurisprudence together with modern legal science. In a letter to Aligarh, he calls the revival of an old-style faculty of Islamic studies “entirely useless”. The real aim, in his view, is to raise a generation of scholars capable of independent and creative thought.
The attention he gives Türkiye in the same lecture holds particular meaning for Turkish readers. On 3 March 1924, the Grand National Assembly passed Law No. 431, abolishing the office of the caliphate and stating in the law itself that the caliphate was already inherent in the concepts of government and republic. Iqbal reads the Turkish position as an exercise in ijtihād. In his account, Türkiye concluded that, in keeping with the spirit of Islam, the office of the caliphate or imamate could be vested in a body of persons or an elected assembly. He then says: “Personally, I believe the Turkish view is perfectly sound.” He does not endorse every aspect of the Turkish experience. In Jāvīd Nāma, he worries that the Turks are severing their ties with their past and turning exclusively towards the West, and on family law he parts company with Ziya Gökalp. His readiness to commend the decisions of a country he felt close to while still subjecting them to criticism is a lesson in method for anyone working in comparative law.
Rights and Duties in Hard Times
Iqbal considers what it means to respect the rights of others under extreme pressure in “The Siege of Edirne”, a poem in Bāng-i Darā. Its subject is the city defended by Şükrü Pasha during the Balkan War. When famine takes hold in the besieged city, there is a proposal to seize the food of its non-Muslim residents. After the religious scholars object, the proposal is dropped. What strikes Iqbal is not only the city’s power of resistance but its respect for the rights of others even in its darkest hour. Emergency powers, too, have limits. Article 15 of the Constitution allows the exercise of fundamental rights and freedoms to be partially or entirely suspended in times of war, mobilisation or a state of emergency, provided that obligations under international law are not violated and the measures do not exceed what the situation requires. The scene Iqbal describes still raises an old question in the law of war: how are the rights of civilians to be protected under siege?
Iqbal does not belittle rights, but he considers them together with responsibilities. He puts it in a single sentence in Stray Reflections: “True political life begins not with the claiming of rights, but with the doing of duties.” The sentence reminds us that rights can be safeguarded only among people who know their duties. Iqbal approaches democracy with the same care. In one of his early writings, he says that the basic principle laid down by the Qur’an is election. In Zarb-i Kalīm, published in 1936, he satirises a form of government that counts votes without weighing them. He accepts election as a principle and also questions the quality of elections. At a time when many countries are once again debating the relationship between electoral legitimacy and the rule of law, it is worth noting that both positions find a place in the work of one writer.
Never Delegating One’s Judgement
What Iqbal says in his early notes about owning a large library speaks today to jurists who use artificial intelligence. For Iqbal, owning a large library and knowing its books does not in itself show that a person can think for himself; it shows that he has the means to draw on the thinking of others. Today, software can produce a pleading, a report summary or a draft judgment in seconds. In 2023, in Mata v. Avianca, the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York fined lawyers who had cited non-existent decisions, and similar sanctions have since been imposed by courts in several countries. Verifying that a cited decision exists and says what it is cited for is the jurist’s own responsibility.
The most personal lesson Iqbal the jurist leaves us is his intellectual independence. Soon after returning from Europe, he gave up his post teaching philosophy at Government College, convinced that government service would prevent him from expressing his views freely. Some of his remarks about the government were considered so harsh that he was passed over for the judgeship of the Lahore High Court that had earlier been offered to him. When he accepted a knighthood in 1923, a friend feared that he would now be beholden to the British government. Iqbal wrote back that no power on earth could stop him from speaking the truth. When Sir Akbar Hydari, the prime minister of Hyderabad, sent him a cheque for a thousand rupees, Iqbal sensed that it was being offered as a favour and sent it back. The Bangalore Principles of Judicial Conduct place independence first among their values and set standards for accepting gifts. Iqbal’s conduct shows how independence shapes a jurist’s everyday decisions.
In his years at the Bar, Iqbal took on only a few cases at a time and was content to earn enough to live on for a month or two. His biographers relate that he lived in straitened circumstances even in his final years, when his fame was at its height. Hence the name “the poorest knight”. Even when his poems were being translated into European languages and he had become a celebrated figure in Lahore, his door remained open to anyone who wished to see him. He died in Lahore on 21 April 1938 and was buried beside the Badshahi Mosque. Each year on 9 November, Pakistan’s Iqbal Day ceremonies begin with the changing of the guard at his tomb.

ISRAELI GENOCIDE

Keeping The Yahoo down is proving hard

Israel’s former military chief (a genocide participant) Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task of forming a government on Sunday, reaching out to The Yahoo's (Benjamin Netanyahu) allies as he said the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.

Eisenkot, 66, the leader of the Yashar party, who has vowed to bridge Israel’s deep polarisation under Netanyahu, formally received a mandate from the president, Isaac Herzog, who gave him 28 days to form a government despite his bloc lacking a clear majority.

“We are in a state of emergency, approaching a point of no return for the state of Israel,” said Eisenkot, who had traded his usual all black for a suit and tie at a ceremony at the presidential office. “We must form a national emergency government. This will require creative and unconventional political steps.”

Eisenkot faces significant challenges on the road to becoming prime minister. He has three options: a power-sharing agreement with Netanyahu, support from Arab-led parties – something several members of his bloc do not support – or an agreement with the ultra-Orthodox parties, which demand military exemptions for their community.

Eisenkot and Herzog acknowledged Israel’s growing isolation under Netanyahu, who is wanted by the international criminal court.

In the US, Israel’s closest ally, Democrats on Tuesday swept the midterm elections, with calls to rein in Israel after the devastation in Gaza and the unpopular Iran war, which Netanyahu launched with Donald Trump.

Eisenkot said: “We are in the midst of a devastating diplomatic crisis. Even our closest friends and strategic allies are saying their relationship with Israel must be reassessed.”

He appealed to Netanyahu’s Likud party as well as the far-right party of the finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, to join him – but only with himself as prime minister.

“My door is open and my hand is extended, wholeheartedly and willingly, to anyone who understands the gravity of this moment,” he said.

Should Eisenkot succeed in forming a coalition, he would take over as prime minister from Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving premier.

Eisenkot’s wide-ranging opposition bloc won 48 of the Israeli parliament’s 120 seats in the October elections, while Netanyahu’s camp secured 53, leaving neither with a majority.

Eisenkot has laid out a series of conditions for any Arab party to join his coalition, including recognition of Israel as a Jewish state and declaring the Palestinian militant group Hamas a terrorist organisation. One of his partners, the more conservative Yisrael Beiteinu party, has already said it will not join a coalition with Arab-led parties.

Eisenkot, a former army chief, and his partners made equal military service a central part of their campaign. Specifically, they are seeking an end to the longstanding draft exemptions enjoyed by the ultra-Orthodox.

Netanyahu has repeatedly made the false claim that the election was “stolen” by Arab parties, which rallied their supporters to vote in large numbers. But he has offered little to no evidence to support the claims.

Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji: Equanimity and the Meaning of Liberation

Sri Guru Granth Sahib | Raag Gauree | Mahalla 9 | Shabad 7

The sixth Shabad distinguished knowledge from realization. The seventh asks a more demanding question: how do we recognize a person who has attained liberation?

Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's answer challenges the ordinary distinctions through which human beings judge success, suffering, reward and punishment.

I. Original Shabad

ਗਉੜੀ ਮਹਲਾ ੯ ॥

ਸਾਧੋ ਰਾਮ ਸਰਨਿ ਬਿਸਰਾਮਾ ॥
ਬੇਦ ਪੁਰਾਨ ਪੜੇ ਕੋ ਇਹ ਗੁਨ ਸਿਮਰੇ ਹਰਿ ਕੋ ਨਾਮਾ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
ਲੋਭ ਮੋਹ ਮਾਇਆ ਮਮਤਾ ਫੁਨਿ ਅਉ ਬਿਖਿਅਨ ਕੀ ਸੇਵਾ ॥
ਹਰਖ ਸੋਗ ਪਰਸੈ ਜਿਹ ਨਾਹਨਿ ਸੋ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਹੈ ਦੇਵਾ ॥੧॥

ਸੁਰਗ ਨਰਕ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਬਿਖੁ ਏ ਸਭ ਤਿਉ ਕੰਚਨ ਅਰੁ ਪੈਸਾ ॥
ਉਸਤਤਿ ਨਿੰਦਾ ਏ ਸਮ ਜਾ ਕੈ ਲੋਭੁ ਮੋਹੁ ਫੁਨਿ ਤੈਸਾ ॥੨॥
ਦੁਖੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਏ ਬਾਧੇ ਜਿਹ ਨਾਹਨਿ ਤਿਹ ਤੁਮ ਜਾਨਉ ਗਿਆਨੀ ॥
ਨਾਨਕ ਮੁਕਤਿ ਤਾਹਿ ਤੁਮ ਮਾਨਉ ਇਹ ਬਿਧਿ ਕੋ ਜੋ ਪ੍ਰਾਨੀ ॥੩॥੭॥

II. English Meaning

Seekers, repose is found in the refuge of Ram. The true benefit of studying the Vedas and Puranas is remembrance of Hari's Name. (Rahao)

One who remains untouched by greed, attachment, possessiveness, indulgence in sensory desires, elation and grief is an embodiment of the Divine.

Heaven and hell, nectar and poison, gold and base metal are alike to such a person. Praise and condemnation, greed and attachment no longer disturb that equanimity.

One who is not bound by suffering or pleasure should be recognized as truly wise. Nanak says: Recognize as liberated the person who has attained such a state.

III. Philosophical Inquiry: What Does Liberation Actually Mean?

Is liberation an event awaiting us beyond life, or a transformation possible within human consciousness?

Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's seventh Shabad presents an unusually direct answer.

The Guru describes the liberated person not through supernatural powers, intellectual accomplishments or promises of heavenly reward, but through freedom from the opposites that ordinarily govern human existence.

His most striking comparison is between Swarg and Narak, heaven and hell.

ਸੁਰਗ ਨਰਕ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤ ਬਿਖੁ ਏ ਸਭ ਤਿਉ ਕੰਚਨ ਅਰੁ ਪੈਸਾ ॥

Heaven and hell, nectar and poison, gold and base metal are alike.

These are not ordinary opposites. They represent some of humanity's deepest hopes and fears: reward and punishment, life-giving nectar and destructive poison, wealth and relative worthlessness.

The Guru's proposition is radical.

The liberated consciousness is no longer governed by the promise of reward or the fear of its opposite.

This does not necessarily mean that the distinctions themselves cease to exist. Rather, they lose their power to bind the individual.

The Shabad then identifies such a person as Giani, one possessing true wisdom, and finally as Mukt, liberated.

This progression is philosophically significant.

Wisdom is not defined merely by what one knows, but by the freedom that accompanies realization.

And liberation is not presented exclusively as a distant, posthumous condition. The Guru explicitly asks us to recognize the person who embodies this state.

IV. An Echo Across Indic Thought

The Bhagavad Gita offers a closely related formulation in verse 5.19:

इहैव तैर्जितः सर्गो येषां साम्ये स्थितं मनः।
निर्दोषं हि समं ब्रह्म तस्माद्ब्रह्मणि ते स्थिताः॥

Even here, those whose minds are established in equanimity have overcome worldly becoming. For Brahman is without imperfection and equal; therefore they are established in Brahman.

The phrase Ihaiva, meaning “here itself,” is particularly relevant.

Both passages associate liberation with a transformed condition of consciousness that can be recognized within existence.

Yet Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji frames this realization through refuge in Ram, remembrance of Hari and freedom from attachment. These remain essential to understanding the Shabad on its own terms.
V. The Thought We Carry Forward

The first Shabad introduced equanimity as inseparable from the recognition of reality.

The seventh returns to that insight, but now makes the criterion explicit.

Liberation is not merely freedom from suffering. It is freedom from being governed by either suffering or pleasure, punishment or reward, condemnation or praise.

Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji asks us to recognize such a person as Giani and Mukt.

Perhaps the most profound implication is this:

The liberated person does not need the world to become different in order to be free from its hold.

Next: Study VIII | Continuing Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's Bani in Raag Gauree.

text:
There is a remarkable distinction in this story that deserves more attention.

On April 7, Israel acknowledged that one of its strikes in Tehran damaged the Rafi-Nia Synagogue. The Israeli military said it had targeted a senior Iranian commander, not the house of worship, and expressed regret over the damage.

That distinction matters. Responsibility for the damage is acknowledged. Deliberate targeting of the synagogue is not established.

But the deeper story is Iran's Jewish community itself.

Iranian Jews are not the Israeli government. Their religious identity does not determine their political allegiance, and their centuries old presence in Iran, cannot be reduced to the confrontation between two states.

CNN's reporting offers an opportunity to examine a community whose experiences rarely fit the simplified narratives of this conflict.

USAI Media's finding: The synagogue's destruction is documented. Israel's acknowledgment is on record. The unresolved questions concern the military decision, civilian protections, and the consequences for a religious minority caught between opposing governments.

The distinction between a people, a religion, and a state is not a technicality. It is essential to understanding this war.

Although the ‘Gay Ban’ on those serving in our armed forces was finally lifted in 2000, it
took until 2023 for the Government to formally apologise to those affected. 

The Financial Recognition Scheme was rolled out in December 2024 and there have now been over 1,500 claims for financial and non-financial reparations. But time is running out. The scheme closes at midnight on the 12th of December. 

This is a one time offer and any applications received after this date will not be accepted. If you were affected in any way, make your application now:
https://t.co/lsDN5UOnps

Wendy is a veteran who served in the army and was dismissed for being a lesbian. She had this to say about the gay ban:

“In 1982 at the age of eighteen, I signed up for 22 years’ service in the regular army. It was
then the Women’s Royal Army Corps. I had hoped for a long and exciting career, but due to the ‘Gay Ban’ (which naively I did not know about on joining) I was soon being questioned
about my sexuality and after just two years’ service I was ‘found out and thrown out.’ A
career and a life of adventure ended. Although, luckily I went on to do many exciting things
with my life. The nature of my dismissal however, had a profound effect on me.

I have been able to achieve a small sense of justice with the non-financial restorative
measures (a ceremony with an apology letter, an Etheron Pin and other items.) I was also
successful in being awarded a ‘Dismissed and Discharged’ payment and an ‘Impact Award.’
It does not cover the years of lost income and career, but it has helped a little to get me
settled in a new home.

I would urge anyone who was dismissed/discharged against their will on the basis of their sexuality to make a claim. Also anyone who is Lesbian or Gay can claim for an Impact Award even if you were not dismissed but you were affected by The Ban whilst serving. It is of course re-living the trauma to fill in these forms, but hopefully you too will be successful and feel a little better in time.”

text:
Rebels S2E1: Vader Is Waiting Around Every Corner

Vader barely appears in “The Siege of Lothal: Part 1”, yet I spent the episode feeling as if he was waiting around every corner. That's exactly what I want from this character. Once he's sent after you, you're fucked.

A bigger rebellion

The Ghost crew is no longer fighting alone. The opening space battle puts them alongside Commander Sato's rebels, showing what joining a larger movement means in practice. The episode moves smoothly between action, conversations and the return to Lothal, steadily building tension.

But joining the Rebellion doesn't mean everyone is comfortable with what comes next.

I really like the conversation between Hera and Kanan, with Ezra listening nearby. Kanan wants to steal from the Empire, help people and undermine Imperial rule. Being a galactic Robin Hood suits him. Becoming part of an army and fighting another war is a different proposition.

It reminds me of Cassian early in Andor's first season. He hates the Empire, but on Aldhani he's taking a paid job, not committing himself to the cause. Surviving matters more to him than becoming a rebel.

Kanan is already fighting for others, but he also wants limits on what that fight becomes. To me, there's fear beneath that resistance. He's lived through one war and its losses. As the Rebellion becomes more organised, it feels as if the possibility of going through that again is catching up with him.

Ezra still wants to help

Then Minister Tua asks them to get her off Lothal. After everything this crew has been through, of course that sounds like another trap.

Zeb and Sabine question whether helping her is a good idea. Ezra insists they should. Someone is asking for help, and being on the wrong side doesn't automatically mean they should be denied a chance.

This is where I really see how much he's grown. Trayvis used their hope against them in “Vision of Hope”, and Ezra has had plenty of reasons to become suspicious. Yet those experiences haven't made him give up on helping people.

He feels like a Jedi here. There are useful Imperial secrets on offer, but his argument begins with someone needing help. It also reminds me of Jesus' teaching about helping those in need. That principle reaches beyond Star Wars.

I love Ahsoka's little smile as she watches him make that decision. It looks as if she already supports helping Tua and wants Ezra to reach the conclusion himself. There's something familiar about that rebellious streak too. She and her unconventional master knew a thing or two about doing things their own way. :P

Vader is already there

Tua's constant excuses in front of Vader almost made me laugh. I kept wondering how long his patience would last. xD And having to answer to Tarkin hardly sounds like a reassuring alternative.

But the plan unfolding around her shows why Vader commands that respect. Her attempt to escape becomes an opportunity to kill her, frame the rebels and turn the population against them. Kallus having a recording droid nearby fits that purpose perfectly. The Empire sacrifices one of its own and gets propaganda out of it.

That makes letting the crew live long enough to play their part feel deliberate. Vader is arranging the situation to serve his goal.

Even before Ezra knows who he's sensing, there's that enormous cold in the Force. Add Vader's breathing and the way the scenes build around him, and I feel his presence even when he's off screen.

Everything he does seems directed towards getting what he wants and defeating whoever stands in his way. He isn't somebody I expect to lose interest or let things go. If he's hunting you, the threat follows you into every scene.

By the time he appears at the end, I'm really scared for the Ghost crew. I know there are two more seasons after this one, and part of me assumes they'll probably be okay. That knowledge isn't much comfort when he's standing there. It's fucking Vader. xD

This is a very good start to season two. The pacing keeps tightening the tension, Ezra's decision gives his growth a clear expression, and the larger Rebellion brings Kanan's old fears back into view. I'd recommend it to people interested in the Rebellion as much as the Jedi, and especially to Vader fans. He has little screen time so far, but for me, his presence fills the episode.

text:
🚨🇯🇵🇺🇸RAKUTEN AND AST SPACEMOBILE ESTABLISH "RAKUTEN AST" JOINT VENTURE TO BUILD D2D COMMUNICATIONS NETWORK IN JAPAN

➡️Approximately USD 1 billion in funding awarded from Japan’s MIC to support deployment of Japanese-flagged mid-band satellite constellation

➡️Rakuten and AST SpaceMobile to build disaster-resilient, uninterrupted communications infrastructure, strengthening economic security for Japan

➡️AST SpaceMobile to supply satellites to power Japan's sovereign direct-to-device constellation

Tokyo and Midland, Texas, November 9, 2026 – Rakuten Group, Inc. and AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (NASDAQ: ASTS), the company building the first and only space-based cellular broadband network accessible directly by everyday smartphones, agreed to establish Rakuten AST, Inc. on November 6, 2026 (Japan Standard Time)*1. The joint venture is tasked with building a direct-to-device communications network in Japan using low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites to provide service to commercially available smartphones, strengthening Japan’s communications infrastructure in the event of disasters and other emergencies.

The Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) selected the joint proposal from Rakuten’s preparatory company and Rakuten Mobile, Inc. for the publicly solicited "J-LEO: Japan Low Earth Orbit Satellite Communications Project"*2. Rakuten AST is expected to receive up to 148 billion yen (approx. 1 billion USD) in support over approximately three years under J-LEO, through the Communications and Information Network Association of Japan (CIAJ), the organization established to manage the fund*3,4. Through this joint venture, Rakuten AST will collaborate with AST SpaceMobile to deploy and manage satellites compatible with mid-band spectrum, in order to establish a satellite communications network and commence domestic operations by the end of March 2029.

The J-LEO Project will leverage the largest communication satellites ever deployed in LEO to build domestic communications infrastructure that enables direct satellite-to-smartphone connectivity and strengthens economic security. In addition to extending cellular broadband connectivity to areas with limited or no terrestrial coverage, the project aims to ensure cellular broadband connectivity during emergencies, such as natural disasters, by establishing a framework for emergency inter-carrier roaming among mobile network operators.

Through Rakuten AST, Rakuten and Rakuten Mobile aim to establish a non-terrestrial network (NTN) managed and operated in Japan. The companies will deploy and operate a resilient, stable communications infrastructure capable of maintaining priority and stable connectivity, independent of external conditions – even in times of emergency.

The satellite communications service to be deployed by Rakuten AST will leverage AST SpaceMobile's large-scale satellites to enable high-speed internet connectivity — such as video streaming and social media — on off-the-shelf smartphones without the need for specialized equipment*5. Because the base station equipment is installed on ground-based infrastructure, Japanese telecommunications operators can flexibly and autonomously manage and operate the network.

AST SpaceMobile will supply the satellites to power Japan's sovereign D2D constellation. Beyond priority Japanese domestic market usage, Rakuten AST also plans to work with AST SpaceMobile to provide these services through AST SpaceMobile to its customers worldwide, subject to regulatory approval.

Rakuten Mobile will also work with AST SpaceMobile to advance the use of AI edge computing and plans to develop AI-driven spectrum management technology, exploring their application for higher-speed data communications and industry-specific solutions such as IoT. The company aims to expand its solution offerings beyond telecommunications carriers to include connectivity-reliant industries, such as logistics, infrastructure monitoring, construction and agriculture.

Mickey Mikitani, Chairman and CEO, Rakuten Group, commented, "This project is a key pillar of Rakuten Mobile's network strategy. By building an integrated framework spanning satellite procurement through operations and accelerating technological innovation, we will contribute to the development of disaster-resilient communications infrastructure and the improvement of Japan's communications environment. We will maximize capital efficiency and pursue the expansion of business opportunities in the satellite communications sector."

Abel Avellan, Founder, Chairman and CEO, AST SpaceMobile, commented, "This represents a significant milestone for AST SpaceMobile and validates the importance of space-based cellular broadband connectivity as countries around the world increasingly recognize the technology as a critical complement to terrestrial wireless infrastructure to realize the goal of 100% broadband availability wherever people work, live and travel. Through our technology, we will enhance the resilience of Japan's communications infrastructure while strengthening our global network by leveraging capacity that can also be utilized outside of Japan.”

In addition to this project, Rakuten Mobile plans to begin commercial-environment testing of its satellite-to-mobile service within 2026, under the strategic partnership between Rakuten and AST SpaceMobile established in March 2020*6.

Rakuten, Rakuten Mobile and AST SpaceMobile will continue working toward the early realization of D2D satellite communications, advancing the development of resilient communications networks.

Overview of Joint Venture
Company Name: Rakuten AST, Inc.
Head Office: 1-14-1 Tamagawa, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo
Legal Capital: 100 million yen
Voting Rights Ratio: Rakuten Group, Inc. 51% / AST SpaceMobile Japan Holdings II GK, a Japan-based wholly owned indirect subsidiary of AST SpaceMobile, Inc. 49%
Representative: Ryoji Osaka, Representative Director & CEO
Date of Establishment: November 2026 (planned)
Business Description: Satellite procurement, and the operation and management of satellite connectivity.

Notes
*1 The new company will be established under an agreement between Rakuten Group, Inc. and AST SpaceMobile Japan Holdings II GK, a Japanese entity established by AST SpaceMobile, Inc. through AST & Science, LLC.

*2 The J-LEO Project was publicly solicited for indirect subsidy recipients (private companies) through the Japan Communications and Information Network Industry Association (CIAJ), the designated foundation operator.

*3 A joint proposal by RAST, Inc. (a preparatory company for Rakuten) and Rakuten Mobile was selected for the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications' "Japan Low Earth Orbit Satellite Communications Project"(*Japanese page)
*4 Grant to be received through CIAJ after establishment of Rakuten AST.

*5 AST provides large-scale satellite hardware and core technology, backed by approximately 3,900 patents held and applications pending. The next-generation satellites will feature the largest phased array ever deployed in low Earth orbit (approximately 223 m²), designed to deliver peak data speeds nearly double those of the company's initial Block 1 BlueBird satellites. The Block 1 BlueBird satellites have demonstrated the ability to connect directly to standard smartphones, achieving a peak downlink speed of 98.9 Mbps, and have proven capable of delivering voice, broadband data, and video applications from space to consumers, enterprises, emergency responders and governments. The company has signed agreements with approximately 60 mobile network operators representing over 3 billion subscribers, and has established strategic partnerships with AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Google, American Tower, Bell, Telus, and stc group, in addition to Rakuten.

*6 Related press release: Rakuten and Vodafone Invest in AST & Science’s Space Venture to Reach More People, Devices and Places with Mobile CoverageAbout AST SpaceMobile, Inc.

AST SpaceMobile is building the first and only global cellular broadband network in space to operate directly with standard, unmodified mobile devices based on our extensive IP and patent portfolio, and designed for both commercial and government applications. Our engineers and space scientists are on a mission to enable 4G and 5G space-based cellular broadband to every device, everywhere, for today’s nearly 6 billion mobile subscribers globally. For more information, follow AST SpaceMobile on YouTube, X (Formerly Twitter), LinkedIn and Facebook. Watch this video for an overview of the SpaceMobile mission.

About Rakuten
Rakuten Group, Inc. (TSE: 4755) is a global technology leader in services that empower individuals, communities, businesses and society. Founded in Tokyo in 1997 as an online marketplace, Rakuten has expanded to offer services in e-commerce, fintech, digital content and telecommunications to 2.2 billion members around the world. The Rakuten Group has around 30,000 employees, and operations in 30 countries and regions. For more information visit https://t.co/OulXP7UC4A.

About Rakuten Mobile
Rakuten Mobile, Inc. is a Rakuten Group company responsible for mobile communications, centered on its mobile network operator (MNO) business. Through continuous innovation and the deployment of advanced technology, Rakuten Mobile aims to redefine expectations in the mobile communications industry in order to provide appealing and convenient services for diverse customer needs. For more information on Rakuten Mobile visit https://t.co/H10nyVqsKv.

text:
I keep reading posts by people getting harassed and attacked for what level of tip they leave.

Let´s put some cold water on this entire debate.  
A restaurant (until human servers are replaced by robots) has the responsibility to offer service to it´s clients including the quality of the meals that are served to the clients and the clients are happy to pay what the restaurant charges for quality meals and servive (which of course sets the wages the owner of the restaurant has to pay for good servers or to train them) and ends up included in the price being charged.  

So, if you go to a Texas steak house chain I assure you that there will be a noticeable difference in your T-bone that at Smiths and Wollenski´s  and of course there will be a very noticeable difference in the bill at the end of the meal.  

THAT is the standard all people can easily understand and generally are happy to pay. Those that can or want to afford the S&W quality happily pay for it and those that cannot or don ´t want or need that, go to other restaurants and pay for what those restaurants charge.  

Hang on, I am coming to tipping.  

Given the above, the more or less common practice is to TIP something for the server but THAT IS VOLUNTARY but of course more or less understood in the US and some other countries but not everywhere.

I live in Spain and tipping is not expected and rarely done to any significant degree.

There has never been a manual published on ANY VOLUNTARY act by a human being--otherwise-- it is not voluntary.  So, what the restaruant industry in the US needs to consider is, allow tipping to be VOLUNTARY and to the free right and choice of the patrons OR publish their own standards for tippping (that some are doing now) and put it where dinners can see it before sitting down inside the restaurant (which some are also doing now) and let the dinners decide if they want to allow it to be imposed on them or not and the owners and their staff can deal with the results of that policy imposition.  

Until then, the owners can decide to pay their servers more or the servers need to accept that TIPPING IS VOLUNTARY AND AT THE DISCRETION OF THE CLIENT.  

And so we do not forget-- for now TIPS ARE TAX FREE so every single American taxpayer is already paying every single waiter and waitress in the restaurant business (and elsewhere where tips are paid) at least a 25% surcharge or subsidy of the tip that is paid.  Here is the math:  My last meal in Florida was right at $250 dollars-- I left a $30 tip (meal was good but not at the level it used to be service as well) since the server did not have to pay taxes on that $30 tip and assuming she was at the minimum tax level plus the fact that up to $25,000 of tip income has 0 taxes that $30 tip equates to close to $50 of value and that $30 tip cost me at my tax level around $10 so that waitress just rung her individual cash register of around $60.  

That works out to be a tip of economic value of around 25% to that waitress. 

Lastly, if you are not happy with your pay in the position you are in--DO SOMETHING TO CHANGE YOUR POSITION but let me eat in peace or I won´t eat at your restaurant and then where will the owner and servers be if too many of us dinners decide not to be pushed around on a VOLUNTARY ISSUE!!!
