text:
The Green Wave keeps rolling in the 2027 cycle.

While the current team battles through a challenging season, Tulane’s recruiting staff under Will Hall has continued stacking talent for the future. 

The class sits at roughly 26 commitments as of early November 2026, with the latest wave of additions giving the roster more size up front, speed in the secondary, and versatility at linebacker.

Caleb Unger set the tone in late October. 

The 6-2/6-3, ~300-pound interior offensive lineman from Madison-Ridgeland Academy in Madison, Mississippi, flipped from Mississippi State and became one of the highest-rated pledges in the class. 

A high-motor, technically sound lineman with good leverage and quickness, Unger held offers from Power Four programs including LSU, Colorado, Oregon, and others before choosing Tulane. 

He plans to enroll early and is viewed as a potential early contributor, especially as the program looks to solidify the offensive line. 

That momentum has continued. The two most recent additions are Trevor Caudle and Special Henry.

Trevor Caudle, a 6-0 corner from James Clemens High School in Madison, Alabama, brings elite track speed (10.55 in the 100m, 21.06 in the 200m). 

The Green Wave landed the track-athlete corner after a strong official visit. He projects as a lockdown outside corner with recovery speed, ball skills, and the willingness to tackle, exactly the kind of multi-phase defensive back the staff has targeted. 

Special Henry, a 6-3/195-pound linebacker from Melissa High School in Texas, flipped from Iowa State. 

With verified 4.44–4.50 speed, an 82–83-inch wingspan, and hybrid versatility (listed at times as OLB/CB), he offers sideline-to-sideline range, length in coverage, and the frame to add strength. 

He held a long list of Division I offers and chose Tulane for the fit and opportunity.

November 9, 2026
Dear Mr. President,

I am writing to you today not as one of your political supporters, but as an American citizen, a taxpayer, and a proud Haitian-born American who believes you have an extraordinary opportunity to accomplish something that no American president has ever accomplished.

Following the recent midterm elections, perhaps this is an opportunity to begin a new chapter in your presidency, one that future generations will remember for something truly extraordinary.

Mr. President, you are a businessman, a real estate developer, and a man who understands the importance of location, investment, and opportunity.

You know the expression: Location, location, location!

I want to introduce you to a remarkable opportunity in the Caribbean, just a short flight from Miami.

That opportunity is HAITI!

I followed your proposal to transform the Gaza Strip into the Riviera of the Middle East. Why not consider applying that same ambition to Haiti, through a peaceful partnership with its government and people?

Imagine transforming Port-au-Prince into a modern international city comparable to Dubai, Singapore, or Hong Kong.

Imagine Haiti becoming the Taiwan of the Caribbean, with semiconductor-related industries, automobile manufacturing, electronics factories, technology centers, international banking, and world-class tourism.

Imagine modern airports, highways, seaports, luxury hotels, cruise terminals, beautiful beaches, and thousands of new businesses creating hundreds of thousands of jobs.

And imagine a magnificent Trump Tower rising above the waterfront of Port-au-Prince, perhaps the tallest Trump Tower in the world!

Mr. President, you have friends and relationships throughout America's business community.

Imagine inviting leaders from Tesla, SpaceX, Oracle, NVIDIA, Meta, Microsoft, and other major corporations to participate in a historic investment summit dedicated to rebuilding Haiti.

American businesses could benefit from new markets, manufacturing opportunities, and investments close to the United States, while Haitians could benefit from employment, education, infrastructure, and economic independence.

Of course, security must come first.

Haiti needs a comprehensive strategy to dismantle criminal gangs, strengthen its police and military institutions within the law, modernize intelligence capabilities, and establish secure correctional facilities with educational and rehabilitation programs.

You could work with the Haitian government and draw lessons from President Nayib Bukele of El Salvador, while ensuring respect for human rights and the rule of law.

But I want to suggest something even more ambitious.

Imagine establishing a genuine, internationally accredited Trump University of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Business in Haiti.

A university where young Haitians could study artificial intelligence, robotics, aviation, semiconductor technology, medicine, agriculture, and entrepreneurship.

Mr. President, skyscrapers can transform a city's skyline, but education can transform a nation's future.

There is also something personal I want you to understand.

In 2018, your remarks about Haiti and other countries deeply offended many Haitians around the world.

I am not writing to condemn you for those remarks. I am writing to offer you an opportunity to change the story.

Imagine that one hundred years from now, historians write that Donald John Trump helped transform a country he once disparaged into one of the most prosperous nations in the Caribbean.

Imagine your name becoming associated not simply with luxury buildings and political controversies, but with peace, nation-building, industrial development, and economic opportunity.

Such an extraordinary achievement, if it brought lasting peace and prosperity to millions, might even deserve consideration for the Nobel Peace Prize.

Mr. President, I am a descendant of Africans who were brought to Saint-Domingue in chains, fought for their freedom, defeated Napoleon's armies, and established the independent nation of Haiti in 1804.

Haiti is the land of Jean-Jacques Dessalines, the land my ancestors fought to leave to future generations.

It is not a country for sale, nor a territory to be occupied.

It is a sovereign nation that needs genuine partners, investment, security, technology, and responsible leadership.

I am not asking you to spend unlimited American taxpayer dollars.

I am proposing a mutually beneficial partnership involving American private investors, the Haitian government, international financial institutions, and the Haitian diaspora.

A partnership that could benefit both nations.

Mr. President, I would be a hypocrite if I told you that I have always been your admirer. We have political differences.

But as an American citizen, I recognize that you are my president, and I believe we should work together whenever there is an opportunity to accomplish something beneficial for humanity.

I would welcome an opportunity to meet with you at the White House, face to face, to present my ideas and discuss a practical plan for Haiti's transformation.

I am willing to contribute my knowledge, experience, and time to help make such a project possible.

Mr. President, you have built towers around the world.

Now imagine helping to rebuild an entire nation.

Imagine Haiti becoming the Dubai of the Caribbean, the Taiwan of the Americas, and once again the Pearl of the Caribbean.

Imagine future generations remembering Donald John Trump as the American president who helped make that transformation possible.

That would be a legacy worth pursuing.

Respectfully,

Wilner Nau (Nènè)
Haitian-born American Citizen
Publisher, Wilner Nau Magazine

text:
European peoples required the land, resources, and demographic outlet of North America and Oceania to reach anything like their present absolute numbers and global share.** Without those continents, their populations would have remained far smaller relative to Asia (and, increasingly, Africa), constrained by Europe’s limited land base and historical Malthusian pressures.

### Geographic and Historical Constraints in Europe
Europe is a relatively small landmass with historically high population densities. For centuries it operated near agricultural carrying capacity under pre-industrial technology. Population growth was repeatedly checked by famine, disease, and conflict—classic Malthusian dynamics. Estimates show Europe’s population rising from roughly 70–90 million around 1500 to about 200 million by 1800 and ~400 million by 1900, but this was the upper end of what intensive European farming, trade, and later industrialization could sustain on the existing land.

Asia, by contrast, supported far larger absolute populations earlier through intensive rice agriculture and larger contiguous land areas. Europe could not simply “grow like China or India” on its own territory without technological leaps that only fully arrived later. Emigration was the practical safety valve once growth accelerated.

### Mass Emigration and the Settler Multiplier
Between 1500 and the mid-20th century, roughly 60–65 million Europeans left the continent. The overwhelming majority went to the Americas; a smaller but significant share went to Australia, New Zealand, and other temperate zones. In the key period 1821–1932 alone, the United States received about 32 million, Canada ~5 million, and Australia nearly 3 million, with additional large flows to Argentina, Brazil, and elsewhere.

These were not mere transfers. In the temperate “lands of recent settlement” (United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand), settlers found vast underpopulated territories after indigenous populations collapsed from Old World diseases (mortality estimates often 80–90% in the Americas within a century of contact). Low density, fertile land, better nutrition, and high fertility produced rapid natural increase. Descendants of those emigrants now number in the hundreds of millions.

Today, estimates of people of predominantly European descent worldwide range roughly from 0.8–1.1+ billion (one detailed 2025 analysis put it near 1.12 billion, ~14% of global population). Europe itself holds ~740–750 million. The Americas account for the large majority of the rest (North America hundreds of millions of European ancestry; significant shares in the Southern Cone), with Oceania contributing another ~22–23 million.

Remove North America and Oceania and you remove the primary demographic multipliers. The European-descended population would be limited largely to Europe (plus smaller residual populations in Latin America, southern Africa, and Siberia). Absolute numbers would be dramatically lower, and the global share would shrink further against Asia’s multi-billion population and Africa’s ongoing growth.

### Why These Specific Continents Were Essential
- **Scale and ecology**: North America and Australia/New Zealand offered large temperate zones compatible with European crops, livestock, and settlement patterns. They could absorb millions without immediately recreating Europe’s density problems.
- **Resource base**: They supplied the agricultural surplus, minerals, and space that supported higher living standards and continued population growth among European-descended populations long after Europe itself began the fertility decline of the demographic transition.
- **Timing**: Emigration peaked as Europe industrialized and its population grew fastest. The colonies absorbed the surplus while the new societies themselves expanded rapidly.

text:
Taraji P. Henson is crying because Hollywood “underpaid” her $150,000 for a supporting role in a $335 million movie.

She was third on the call sheet behind Brad Pitt and Cate Blanchett. She asked for $500k. They offered $100k. She took $150k and paid her own hotel bills. After taxes and her team’s 30% cut she walked away with roughly $30k.

Fifteen years later, with an Oscar nomination and a long career behind her, she’s still framing it like the studio cheated her because she’s a Black woman. Meanwhile she herself has said Pitt and Blanchett deserved their bigger checks because their names sold the tickets.

The industry is brutal. Almost nobody gets paid what they think they’re worth. But turning a standard supporting-actor deal from 2008 into an ongoing story about systemic robbery is a choice.

How many other actors have quietly taken the same kind of money and never turned it into a crying clip?

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
The chunkiest “squid” ever found sat in a drawer for years. Then it got a name. 🦑

Wyoming’s Sundance Formation preserves an ancient inland sea that once stretched across much of the western United States, and it has yielded millions of belemnite fossils, squid-like creatures. Now an international team from the US, UK and New Zealand has described a 160-million-year-old fossil from that formation that looks unlike anything researchers have seen. One scientist said he was deeply surprised to find such an odd specimen in a group that had already been studied extensively, and its unusual proportions may offer clues about how it lived and hunted. It is one of the chunkiest cephalopods ever discovered. Scientists discover a bizarre Jurassic “squid” unlike anything ever seen.
The twist: the specimen remained unstudied in a museum collection drawer for many years. 
The human story is why this one stays with me. The species, W. linsterorum, is named in honour of Cliff Linster, who helped discover it. He died in June, before the research was published, but he knew scientists were studying his find and was excited to see it recognised. 

Two lessons from one fossil: museum drawers hold surprises, and every discovery has a person behind it who deserves a name on the label.

What would you name a ridiculous-looking animal?
🦑 After the person who found it
🏞️ After where it was found
😂 Something unprintable

text:
Israel cannot, however, sustain a favorable regional order alone. Saudi Arabia and the Gulf states possess energy resources, capital, and strategic geography. Turkey commands formidable military capabilities and serves as a key bridge between Europe and Asia. Their interests do not always coincide. The growing rivalry between Israel and Turkey presents Washington with a particularly difficult challenge. American leadership is necessary to organize these capabilities into a regional balance that constrains Iran, manages rivalries among American partners, and limits opportunities for China and Russia to exploit regional disorder.

This brings us to the contradiction in the restrainer challenge to Trump. Alliances allow Washington to maintain influence while shifting more of the military burden to capable local powers. Weakening the alliance with Jerusalem in the name of restraint risks undermining the very objective restrainers claim to serve. The less America wants to fight in the Middle East, the more it needs Israel.

Nor can Trump resolve the problem simply by ending the war with Iran. The fighting may stop, but the strategic questions will remain. What prevents Tehran from rebuilding its military capabilities and pursuing nuclear weapons? What balance of power will emerge in the Persian Gulf? Who will protect the energy routes on which America’s Asian allies depend? And what role will China play in shaping the answers? A ceasefire is not a regional order.

Vance’s challenge is partly of the president’s own making. Trump deliberately surrounded himself with officials whose strategic instincts differ sharply from his own—Colby at the Pentagon, Vance in the vice presidency, and many others throughout the national security bureaucracies—believing he could manage their disagreements while preserving his freedom of action. But the Iran war has exposed the limits of managing a strategic disagreement as a personnel problem. The two camps disagree not merely about tactics or the costs of particular operations, but about the international order America needs and the responsibilities required to sustain it.

The vice president has aligned himself with the restrainers while leaving the door open to the Groypers on their radical fringe. Trump’s strategy depends on precisely the regional partnerships that maneuver places in question. The case for those partnerships is a strategic one, and it can be contested on its merits.

But the Groyper premise forecloses rational debate. If the alliance is the product of a conspiracy, every argument for it becomes evidence of the hidden hand. The questions on which American strategy turns cannot even be considered on their merits.

Concessions offered without a strategic rationale will not resolve the problem either. Trump’s aid announcement was followed the next day by his vice president’s placing the relationship itself on the table. A concession presented as shedding a burden risks validating the premise that the alliance is inherently burdensome.

Since first taking office in 2017, the president has been riding two horses. The Iran war has sent them in opposite directions, and his vice president has chosen the restrainer side. The question is no longer only how Trump manages his coalition, but which foreign policy his movement inherits: the one Trump has practiced, which treats Israel as an instrument of American power, or the one Vance is increasingly embracing, in which the alliance itself becomes suspect. If Trump does not make the case for his own strategy, his vice president’s choices will define it for him.

5/end

text:
Good morning from Virginia. 🇺🇸

On the morning of November 9, 1862, in the chill fields north of Warrenton, Ambrose Everett Burnside formally took command of the Army of the Potomac. George McClellan was gone—relieved by a president who could no longer abide his caution after Antietam. Lincoln wanted the war pressed, the Confederacy broken, and the Emancipation Proclamation given the muscle of a victory on Southern soil. Burnside was the man ordered to deliver it.

He had refused the post twice. After the Peninsula and again after Second Manassas, he had told the president he was not the man for an army. Loyalty to McClellan and an honest assessment of his own limits kept him from grasping what others craved. This time the choice was stripped away. If he declined again, the army would pass to Joe Hooker, a man Burnside neither trusted nor respected. So the modest Rhode Islander, inventor of a failed carbine, conqueror of the Carolina coast, and the officer whose name would forever be attached to the bridge at Antietam, accepted the burden he had spent months trying to avoid.

His first order to the troops carried no swagger. “With diffidence for myself,” he wrote, “but with a proud confidence in the unswerving loyalty and determination of the gallant army now entrusted to my care, I accept its control with the steadfast assurance that the just cause must prevail.” The men knew the face: the extravagant whiskers that would give the language a new word, the easy manner, the reputation for personal courage. They also knew he was not McClellan. The old commander had been idolized; the new one arrived with the quiet of a man who understood the weight he had just shouldered.

Within days the army was moving. Burnside’s plan was simple and audacious: steal a march on Lee, seize the crossings of the Rappahannock at Fredericksburg, and place the Army of the Potomac between the Confederates and Richmond. The pontoons that were to make the crossing possible were delayed by confusion in Washington. By the time they arrived, Lee’s veterans were already on the heights behind the town. What followed on December 13 was not a battle so much as a slaughter—repeated, ordered assaults up the open slopes of Marye’s Heights against stone walls and entrenched rifles. Roughly twelve thousand Union soldiers fell. Burnside, watching from across the river, offered to lead one final charge himself. His subordinates talked him out of it.

He took the blame without evasion. The man who had never wanted the command accepted full responsibility for the catastrophe it produced. In that, at least, he proved more honest than many who later judged him from safer distances.

The episode stands as one of the starker lessons of the war: the cost of placing an army in the hands of a man who knew he was not equal to it, and the price paid by soldiers when political necessity overrides military judgment. Burnside stepped forward when ordered. The ground around Fredericksburg recorded the result. History does not always reward duty. It merely records who answered when the call came—and who paid for the answer.

America 250 🇺🇸

🤔Last week India's financial crimes agency, the Enforcement Directorate, searched two crypto platforms in Bengaluru, one of them India's best-known exchange, reported by Indian business media. The case is under India's foreign-exchange law, not its money-laundering law.

What investigators allege is the interesting part. They say when Indian customers deposited rupees, the exchange converted them into a dollar stablecoin and shipped them abroad to some of the biggest offshore exchanges in the world, through an account held by what the agency calls a "paper entity" in Costa Rica. They say the platform's futures trades were copied one-for-one on those offshore venues and settled overseas. And the "tokenized" shares of big American tech companies it offered were, they allege, really derivative bets placed on a decentralized platform outside India.

If that's right, customers thought they were trading at home, and their money was actually working somewhere else.

Look at the same week from Washington. The Treasury cut a major offshore crypto exchange off from the American banking system, citing billions in flows tied to Russian illicit finance. And in a New York courtroom, a group backed by major market players is suing the American derivatives regulator over the same new product India is pursuing: crypto-style bets on ordinary stocks. A federal judge said the challengers are likely to win.

Washington is closing the offshore exchange. New Delhi is closing the local door into it. A New York court is weighing the product itself. Three fronts, one direction: control where the money comes in and where it goes out.

Timelines. Patterns. Their words, not mine. All I did was read the receipts. 

I am the guy on the couch, and you have been debriefed.

🤔THE DEBRIEFING: THE PRINCE GROUP, I LOVE PARIS & THE NAME ON THE PAPER

My thesis, so you can judge it for yourself: you don't dismantle a global scam empire by catching the man at the top. You dismantle it by going after the people whose names are on the paperwork. On Thursday, two countries went after one empire on the same day.

The empire is a Cambodian conglomerate that the United States and Britain sanctioned last year as a transnational criminal organization. Prosecutors allege it was built on scam compounds and forced labor. Its founder was sent to China at the start of this year. American prosecutors are pursuing a massive bitcoin forfeiture tied to him.

But an empire like that doesn't hold its property in the founder's name. It holds it through local companies with local directors, people who sign the leases, file the forms and open the accounts. Those signatures are what make dirty money look clean.

On Thursday, Singapore police arrested one of those directors at Changi Airport, reported by Singapore media from a police release. She's accused of being a director of Singapore companies police believe the founder owns. The charge isn't laundering. It's paperwork: prosecutors say she had an agreement falsified and submitted it to a state landlord to take over a property lease. A judge ordered her held while police keep digging.

Singapore police also say they've now seized or frozen more than seven hundred million Singapore dollars in assets linked to the group, nearly five times the figure a year ago.

The same day, the U.S. Treasury hit the same empire with its fourth round of sanctions, dozens of companies and the people behind them across Asia and offshore.

So in one week: a nominee director in Singapore, a payment-company chairman in Vietnam, a fake ship-flag business in India and a bought judge in Mexico. Each time, the target is the person whose name makes the system work.

Timelines. Patterns. Their words, not mine. All I did was read the receipts.

💰 Some investors are still deploying billions

⚖️ Others are demanding greater protection, 
better returns and more convincing evidence before taking additional risk

📅 Here's what actually changed on November 9

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1) 🛢️ IRAN - OIL PRICES ARE FALLING WHILE ENERGY INFRASTRUCTURE IS STILL BEING DESTROYED

🛢️ Brent lost approximately 16% last week 
- its biggest weekly decline since the beginning of the pandemic

🤔 Why?
- 🇺🇸 Trump says another major attack on Iran is highly unlikely if negotiations continue progressing
- 🇶🇦 Qatar is still mediating
- ⚖️ But Secretary of State Marco Rubio says the negotiations have been unproductive because Iran's demands remain unacceptable
- 🏛️ And today, the Qatari prime minister is expected at the White House for further discussions

⚠️ THE MARKET IS PRICING A LOWER PROBABILITY OF PROLONGED WAR

🔍 But now look at what happened in Iraq:
- 💥 A suspected drone attack forced the shutdown of the Khor Mor gas field
- ⚡ Approximately 2.8 GIGAWATTS of regional power generation were initially knocked offline
- 🏭 The operator has confirmed that production remains suspended while damage is assessed

❓ No group has claimed responsibility

🚨 THIS IS THE PART THAT MATTERS
- 🔥 A gas field doesn't just sell fuel
- ⚡ It supplies power stations
- 🏥 Those power stations supply businesses, hospitals, factories and households
- 🔗 When that gas stops flowing, the disruption spreads far beyond the original attack
- 🇶🇦 Meanwhile, Qatar is still dealing with damage to facilities representing roughly 17% of its LNG export capacity
- 🏗️ Restoring that capacity is expected to take years

🤔 So why can oil prices fall despite continued destruction?
📊 Because oil futures also reflect expected global supply and demand

🏦 JPMorgan estimates that global oil supply exceeded demand by around 1.4 million barrels per day in October
📉 That surplus can pressure crude prices even while individual regions face serious energy shortages

💡 GLOBAL CRUDE SUPPLY AND LOCAL ENERGY SECURITY ARE NOT THE SAME THING
🌍 There can be enough oil globally while a particular country struggles to generate electricity

⚠️ And even if Iran reaches a deal, damaged infrastructure, shipping insurance, replacement supplies and security spending won't disappear immediately

💰 The longer-term demand for reliable energy infrastructure may survive a diplomatic settlement

🎯 THE PRICE OF OIL CAN RECOVER OR COLLAPSE IN A DAY
💵THE COST OF RESTORING ENERGY SECURITY CAN LAST FOR YEARS

🚨 SHARE PRICES CAN REACT IMMEDIATELY TO A GOVERNANCE RISK EVEN WHEN CUSTOMER ORDERS HAVEN'T CHANGED

🎯 They must also consider financing, contracts, regulation, execution and governance

🎯 A TECHNOLOGY CAN DOMINATE THE FUTURE WITHOUT EVERY INVESTMENT CONNECTED TO IT BEING SAFE

🇪🇺 European, Japanese and American producers now face additional competition from Chinese companies seeking growth outside their home market

🌐 It's Chinese production, investment and competition increasingly reaching foreign markets

🎯 WHEN DOMESTIC DEMAND CAN'T ABSORB ENOUGH PRODUCTION, GLOBAL MARKETS BECOME THE NEXT BATTLEGROUND

⚠️ They don't want to inherit expensive obligations from a settlement they had little influence over

🎯 THE NEGOTIATIONS ARE ABOUT ENDING THE WAR
💰 THE DISAGREEMENTS ARE ALSO ABOUT WHO CONTROLS AND FINANCES THE SECURITY SYSTEM THAT FOLLOWS

🔍 And the situation is becoming more interesting than a simple bearish chart

💸 −$1.28 BILLION

🏦 The funds have now moved into net outflows for 2026

👀 Now look at derivatives positioning

⚠️ But we need to interpret that correctly
🛡️ A short position does not necessarily mean its owner expects Bitcoin to collapse

🌍 And one exchange cannot represent the entire crypto market

🚨 The more important issue is leverage
⚖️ When large traders build leveraged positions around a narrow price range, the market becomes sensitive to sharp moves in either direction

📉 Falling prices can liquidate leveraged longs
📈 A sudden rebound can force leveraged shorts to cover
💥 Both can generate violent price movements without establishing a sustainable investment trend

🧠 And remember the bigger question

💸 The ETF withdrawals show that one major source of regulated demand has been weakening

📉 A market can produce impressive rebounds while still struggling to attract enough durable capital
🌪️ And the closer traders position around important liquidation levels, the more violent the short-term moves can become

🎯 A SHORT SQUEEZE CAN SEND BITCOIN HIGHER
🚨 IT CANNOT, BY ITSELF, PROVE THAT LONG-TERM INVESTMENT DEMAND HAS RETURNED

text:
The growing optimism surrounding US–Iran diplomacy deserves considerably more scrutiny.

The latest developments suggest an increasingly uncomfortable disconnect between what mediators are communicating and what is actually happening on the ground.

Start with Iran’s much-publicised proposal to implement an agreement within two days.

It sounds encouraging. But what exactly is being offered?

Tehran continues to insist on its seven conditions, including sanctions relief, removal of the US naval blockade, release of frozen assets, compensation for war damage and an end to hostilities across the region, including Lebanon.

Broader demands concerning regional security arrangements and the US military presence further complicate the picture.

Some of these conditions are politically unacceptable to Washington. Others would require negotiations involving multiple governments, substantial military redeployments and potentially months of implementation.

The proposed 48-hour arrangement appears to involve preliminary confidence-building measures, not the resolution of these fundamental disagreements.

Two days to implement initial steps is not two days to achieve peace.

And Washington’s response hardly suggests convergence.

Marco Rubio described Iran’s demands as “outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic”, adding that negotiations had not been particularly productive. These are hardly the words of an administration preparing to announce a diplomatic breakthrough.

Now consider what has happened militarily over the same weekend.

• Iraq announces an understanding with Washington concerning an oil-export corridor through Hormuz, near Oman.

• On the same day, a drone attack strikes the Pearl Petroleum-operated Khor Mor gas complex in Iraqi Kurdistan.

• The Houthis announce further operations against Saudi energy infrastructure, including Abqaiq, Khurais and Pumping Station No. 8 on Aramco’s strategic EW pipeline. These damage claims remain unverified.

• An Aramco building in Riyadh was damaged by a Houthi ballistic missile.

• The US conducts further limited strikes against Iranian air defences, with explosions reported around Qeshm and Jask.

• More tankers reportedly hit and catch fire in Hormuz, as commercial shipping continues to face severe disruption.

The individual incidents require careful attribution. But collectively, they hardly resemble the behaviour one would expect around an imminent, comprehensive cessation of hostilities.

There is an additional strategic consideration.

The East–West pipeline is Saudi Arabia’s principal alternative to exporting crude through Hormuz. Threatening that infrastructure alongside the Strait itself raises the stakes considerably, even without confirmed physical damage.

Meanwhile, Qatar’s Prime Minister is meeting Trump at the White House today.

Is this evidence of meaningful progress, or an increasingly urgent effort to prevent a wider escalation that could further jeopardise regional energy exports?

Qatar and Pakistan have understandable economic incentives to secure a rapid reopening of Hormuz. Iraq now has equally pressing reasons to restore reliable oil exports.

But restoring maritime trade is not synonymous with resolving the nuclear dispute, sanctions, regional security arrangements or the fundamental US–Iran confrontation.

And February should remain a cautionary lesson: optimistic mediation can coexist with preparations for military escalation.

We should distinguish diplomatic urgency from diplomatic convergence.

The real test is not how quickly an agreement could theoretically be implemented, but whether the parties have agreed on the concessions necessary to make implementation possible.

Rubio’s remarks suggest they have not.

Until there is verifiable movement on those substantive issues, I would be cautious about interpreting the latest diplomatic activity as evidence that a durable settlement is within reach.

text:
Humans do not operate based on rational probabilities; most of our decisions stem from a code that even we ourselves cannot see. This has been demonstrated in economics, where it is feasible to establish a science based on measurement, whereas psychology is a field that navigates primarily through qualitative assessments.

Our decisions are shaped by incomplete information, limited time, cognitive overload, emotional states, social pressure, habits, and systematic biases. For this reason, Herbert Simon argued that human rationality is bounded: people do not always optimize; instead, they often search until they find an option that is sufficiently good, a behavior known as satisficing.
This recognition has profound implications in the age of artificial general intelligence (AGI). Mathematically, AGI may offer more rational solutions than humans for complex problems.

text:
The most interesting part of Vangrid's Quickstart is that the platform has two entry points.

One is for people who collect spatial data.

The other is for people who need to buy it.

That distinction says a lot about the business @vangrid_io is trying to build.

Contributors can connect a wallet and use smartphones to capture requested locations. Buyers can create funded bounties, review submissions and accept work that meets their requirements.

The documentation also describes a workflow where AI agents can commission real-world captures through an API, paying in USDC on Base or Arc using x402.

For someone building robotics or autonomous systems, the starting question is different from a contributor's.

Instead of asking how to earn points, they should ask what physical-world information is missing from their existing datasets.

The Bounty Board offers a practical example.

A new bulk order requests nine captures of cattle grids and field gate entrances at $280 per item.

Across the marketplace, Vangrid now records 30 bulk orders and approximately $728,627 in USDC settlements.

Its Explorer also displays more than 476,000 active nodes.

The project has reported $9 million in funding involving firms such as HashKey Capital, Borderless Capital and Animoca Brands, while its published materials highlight deep-tech and enterprise infrastructure experience.

That backing may support development, but repeat demand and reliable data delivery will determine the network's longer-term usefulness.

I think the most productive way to explore Vangrid as a builder is to identify one specific location or environment your application cannot adequately understand today.

Would you commission a capture of that environment if it helped you evaluate a robotics system more effectively?

text:
cold emails = more MRR for b2b SaaS

if done right.

but most redittors dont know how to do it.

here's the SAUCE:

1) FIX YOUR OFFER

most founders send emails like:

"we help companies with [XYZ] using ai."

nobody cares.

your prospects don't care about what you do. they care about what they get.

make your offer so sharp that your prospect wants to know more.

> focus on one specific problem
> show a clear outcome
> make it relevant to their business
> test different angles until you find what works

a good offer does 80% of the selling.

---------------------

2) KNOW YOUR ICP

you can have the best offer in the world.

but if you're sending it to the wrong people, nobody will reply.

> define the exact companies you want to target
> filter by industry, size, revenue, tech stack, etc.
> find the right decision-makers
> use buying signals when relevant
> build a clean, verified lead list

the more specific your list, the more relevant your message.

---------------------

3) EMAIL INFRA

this is the easiest part to solve.

you don't need to overcomplicate it.

> buy domains from porkbun or godaddy
> get google or microsoft mailboxes from zapmail
> connect them to instantly or smartlead
> warm up your mailboxes for 3-4 weeks

start sending at a controlled volume and scale gradually

once your infra is ready, focus on testing your offers and finding what gets positive replies.

---------------------

MY TAKE:

right people + right offer + reliable email infra = more interested replies.

cold email isn't dead.

most people just send the wrong message to the wrong people.

text:
NVIDIA $NVDA — GOLDMAN SACHS SAYS BUY. ALETHEIA DOWNGRADES. THE $165 BILLION QUESTION IS WHAT REALLY INTERESTS ME.
I've been reviewing two analyst reports published today, and they capture the biggest debate surrounding NVIDIA's position in the AI infrastructure cycle.
Goldman Sachs remains bullish on NVIDIA's earnings power.
Aletheia Capital is increasingly concerned about the financing required to sustain AI infrastructure expansion.
I think both arguments deserve attention.
THE BULL CASE — GOLDMAN SACHS
🔹 Rating: Buy maintained
🔹 Price Target: $300
🔹 Calendar 2027 EPS Estimate: $16.70
🔹 Implied P/E: ~11× at $186.64
Goldman expects NVIDIA's near-term fundamentals to outperform market expectations, supported by AI demand, enterprise adoption and expanding computing requirements.
That's consistent with my long-term bullish view.
THE BEAR CASE — ALETHEIA CAPITAL
🔹 Rating: Downgraded from Buy to Hold
🔹 Previous $340 Price Target: Removed
🔹 AI Partner Financial Commitments: Estimated at $165B
🔹 CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN: Estimated $124B funding requirement over 12–15 months
🔹 Longer-Term Buildout: Estimated $450B–$500B for another 11–12GW by 2030
These are Aletheia's estimates, not confirmed cash losses or immediate liabilities for NVIDIA.
But the underlying concern is important.
NVIDIA is increasingly helping finance the infrastructure that supports demand for its own products.
WHAT'S CHANGING
The AI investment cycle is becoming more capital-intensive.
Neoclouds need power, data centres, GPUs, networking and substantial financing before their infrastructure can generate sustainable cash returns.
NVIDIA benefits when those projects move forward.
But supporting customers financially introduces risks beyond the traditional semiconductor supply chain.
The question is whether these commitments accelerate genuinely profitable demand or create growing financial exposure to customers whose business models are still maturing.
MY TAKE
I remain bullish on NVIDIA's competitive position in accelerated computing, CUDA, networking and AI infrastructure.
I also believe inference demand offers a substantial long-term opportunity.
But I wouldn't dismiss Aletheia's concerns.
The $165B figure needs to be understood in terms of actual contractual exposure, funding requirements and potential losses, rather than treated as cash already spent.
And Goldman's attractive earnings multiple depends on its forecasts being achieved.
For me, NVIDIA's next phase isn't simply about how many GPUs it can sell.
It's about whether the broader AI ecosystem can finance capacity, achieve strong utilisation, generate sustainable revenue and ultimately earn attractive returns on invested capital.
MY CONCLUSION
I still see NVIDIA as a long-term AI infrastructure leader.
But the stronger the growth opportunity becomes, the more important capital discipline becomes.
The opportunity is enormous. The financing structure behind it deserves just as much attention as the demand.

text:
SOLITUDE SWEETENED
by James Meikle, 1730-1799

CONNECTIONS

Ignorant mortals are always rash in their conclusions on the conduct of Providence, being blinded in their views, and impatient under woes. But, to compose my combating thoughts, and make me wait the outcome of all things with patience, let me look into some remarkable scripture-narratives, and see the fair sunshine of kindness, after the storms of trouble and clouds of indignation are gone.

First, then, let me look into that which befell Abraham, the friend of God. Think what joy filled the patriarch's bosom when promised a son in his old age, and how this joy was increased when the promised seed was born, and grew up to be a pretty boy—the joy of both his parents. But, look again, and see the amazing trial, the tremendous scene that ensues! The promised seed must be sacrificed, and that by the hand of a most affectionate father! Yet, see his aged joints tremble all the way to Mount Moriah, to offer up his beloved Isaac, as it were resigning the promise again to God, trusting God to make it out some other way, though it were by raising him from the dead.

Now, let us view the beginning of the trial of his faith; how dark and gloomy, how opposite to reason, affection, and piety too; but, let us connect the beginning with the latter end—and all at once is beautiful and bright. There his faith is tried—here it triumphs. There God commands—here he commends his obedience. There he requires—here he restores Isaac. The voice of God at first seems to strike at his former promise—here it confirms all with new promises, enlarged blessings, and this glorious name superadded, "The father of the faithful." Abraham comes home full of gladness and gratitude; and we have the divine account, to teach us to await the end—before we draw our conclusions of God's providential way.

The second is the account of Joseph. In the first part of the scene, see his young heart ready to burst and break with bitter anguish! Hear many—but fruitless supplications to his cruel brethren! How melting are his cries, while his hard-hearted brethren draw him out of the pit, to sell him for a slave!! Nothing can save him; compassionate Reuben is not within the reach of his cry. The price is agreed upon, the money is paid, and away he must go; and neither his parting importunities, his piercing cries, nor piteous back-looks, can move them to relent. Later, after a little advancement in Egypt, he is thrown from the liberty of a servant—into the confinement of a prison. This at first sight is a melancholy scene; but if we look to the sufferings of a tender-hearted father, it is heightened to the highest pitch. All his sons and daughters gather around the grey-headed mourner, to comfort him—but in vain; for still he thinks he sees the wild beast tearing his beloved Joseph to pieces, who screams out for help—but none to help is near; and then he is ready to faint through the excess of sorrow.

Now, this is the first part of the providence, which indeed has a very dejecting aspect, and if we had never heard more of the matter, we would have concluded them both very miserable; but let us see how the dear connection stands. Jacob, who had mourned many years, is at last overflowed with tides of joy. Joseph, the lost, the long-lamented Joseph, is still alive! The youth who was sold into Egypt as a servant—has all Egypt at his service! He who had his feet hurt with fetters—may now bind princes at his pleasure, and teach senators wisdom! He who lately drudged about in a dungeon, to attend prisoners—becomes a father to a king! His brothers, who envied him for his dreams—now bow before him, as the accomplishment of those very dreams which bred their envy! He whose life they so little valued—saves the lives of thousands. At his word, whose supplications his brethren would not hear—all the land of Egypt is governed! The long separated relations meet, and melt in kindness on one another's neck!

We have, (not to name others,) a similar instance in the great apostle Paul, and by his own observation too, in his epistle to the Philippians. This great man, after his singular conversion, preaches Christ unweariedly in many trials and sufferings; until, at length he returns to Jerusalem. There by the enraged and unbelieving Jews he is set upon, and would have been slain, had not the Roman captain rescued him. But he is so persecuted with their cruel rage, malice, and underhand dealings, that he is compelled to appeal to an heathen emperor. Now the great apostle of the Gentiles, to the great grief of the church, is a poor prisoner; hence says he, "the prisoner of Jesus Christ." He is a long time confined in Judah, then sent to Rome, where, though shipwrecked in his passage, he arrives, and is kept two years a prisoner at large. But, says he to the Philippians, "Now I want you to know, brothers, that what has happened to me has actually resulted in the advancement of the gospel, so that it has become known throughout the whole imperial guard, and to everyone else, that my imprisonment is for Christ. Most of the brothers in the Lord have gained confidence from my imprisonment and dare even more to speak the message fearlessly."

How noble the connection! Paul intends to visit Rome at his own expenses, to preach the gospel there; but Providence, on the Emperor's expenses, brings him to make converts, not only in the royal city—but in the very palace. The Jews think they have succeeded to their very wish, when they have thus got rid of a pestilent fellow, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes; but they could not have fallen upon a better method to spread his doctrine, and support his cause. To appearance his success must end, when his imprisonment begins—but it is quite the reverse; not only Paul persists in preaching the gospel without prohibition—but the brethren are emboldened to speak the gospel message fearlessly.

What reason, then, have I to complain on the first part of providence, while the outer wheel is only seen? Should I not wait, until the inner wheel turns around—and I can read plainly the last connection? And what though that should be reserved for eternity? There every providence shall be completed to my everlasting comfort, and all things concerning me connected in the most beautiful harmony. There shall not be the least gap in my lot or life, when time is no more; but all things shall be made up to me in Christ Jesus, to the entire satisfaction of my soul.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

News Flashback

Jan-March 2026

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.

Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
Rock Bottom at Yulman: Tulsa Hangs 60 on Tulane, and the Tulane Green Wave Have Three Weeks to Answer

There's no softening this one. 

Tulane lost its Homecoming game 60-10 to Tulsa on Saturday at Yulman Stadium. It's the most points anyone has scored in that building and the program's largest-ever loss in American Conference play. 

The Wave fall to 4-5 overall and 2-3 in the league.

How it got away 
Tulsa scored on its opening drive, an 11-play, 75-yard march capped by a Baylor Hayes touchdown pass to Oran Singleton Jr. After that it was a slow bleed until the second quarter turned into a flood. A field goal made it 10-0, Hayes found Jimmy Calloway (Former Tulane) for 17-0, and then a Tulane turnover handed Tulsa a three-play, 46-yard touchdown drive for 24-0. Hayes and Singleton connected again with 53 seconds left before half, and a two-point conversion made it 32-0 at the break.

The second half offered no response. After the Wave got a stop to open the third, Tulsa scored on its next two drives, a 27-yard Singleton touchdown and a Damari Alston run, for 46-0. Cooper Helmke's 38-yard field goal early in the fourth avoided the shutout. Dagan Bruno's touchdown pass to Bredell Richardson came with one second left.

The numbers 
Tulsa outgained Tulane 562 to 204, including 338 to 112 through the air and 224 to 92 on the ground. Tulsa had 31 first downs to Tulane's 15 and six sacks. 
Hayes threw a career-high four touchdowns, tying the Yulman record. Singleton set a stadium record with 13 catches and tied the stadium record with three receiving touchdowns. 
Trace Johnson went 11-for-19 for 69 yards with an interception. Bruno went 4-for-6 for 43 yards with a touchdown and an interception. 

Johnnie Daniels led the team with 49 rushing yards on 10 carries. Destyn Hill had 4 catches for 55 yards and Anthony Brown-Stephens had 5 for 20. 
On defense, Dickson Agu had 8 tackles, TJ Smith had 7 (1 for loss) and Makai Williams had 6. Smith also returned five kicks for 130 yards.
What it means 
In Thursday's preview, we said Tulane had to set the edge, protect the football and stay ahead of the chains. It didn't do any of the three. 

Tulsa ran for 224 yards, the turnovers turned into points, and six sacks kept the Wave behind schedule all day. 
Reaction from the top took the rest of the day and answered nothing. 

Athletic director David Harris released a statement Saturday calling the performance "unacceptable" and saying he was "embarrassed by what transpired on the field." He added that the team has to "respond with urgency." Per SI's postgame transcript, Will Hall blamed a lack of execution across the board and said he has to coach better. 
The math is simple now. 

With Rice, North Texas and South Florida left, Tulane needs two wins for bowl eligibility.

What's next 
Tulane plays at Rice on Saturday, Nov. 14, at 1 p.m. CT. Tulane listed Rice at 1-7 and 0-4 in the American as of Saturday. If there's going to be a response, this is the week to show it.

#AKATU ~ And Then The World Danced

Beloved Ones Of Light!

Dance Has Always Been An Expression From Within. A Living Soul Seeks To Communicate With Others As Well As Connection To Spirit. 

These Movements Have Been Recorded On Earth Since The Beginning Of Earth Native Souls And Incarnations From Many Stars.

Archeologists Have Reconstructed Ancient Human Movements Through Analysis Of Art, Skeletal Stress Patterns, Acoustic Patterns And Relics Of Many Types.

Dance Has Been Considered To Be A Divine Cosmic Force Through The Ages. Meaning And Purpose Became Varied And The Use Of Dance For Enjoyment And Pleasure Was Not The Only Reason To Dance. 

It Was Worship, A Means Of Showing Peace Was Possible, A Way To Connect To The Powers Of The Soul's Understanding Of Deities And A Means To Change The Weather.

Modern Dances Still Reflect Styles Utilized In Ancient Rituals. The DNA Of Humans Has Coursed Through The Veins Of Tribes, Noblemen And Those That Struggled In All Civilizations.

Children Have Danced With Pets And Dolls. Lovers Have Danced As They Speak Soft Words. Everyone Has Danced To Feel Lighter And More Joyful. Even Dancing Alone Will Raise Your Frequency!

Tribal Dances Connected Communities In Efforts To Share Social Customs, Honor Traditions And To Connect To Objects As Well As Other Humans. 

It Was Believed That All Plants, Animals, People And Materials Had Living Souls. Movements Imitated Animals And Beliefs Spread That Spirits Would Assist With Dances Offered.

Dancers Prayed For Rain, Good Crops, Healing And A Good Hunt For Food. Tribes Performed War Dances Before Battles And Dances To Declare Peace. Births, Deaths And Marriages Were Always Expressed With Dancing.

There Are Ancient Relics With Rock Formations And Art Sketched In Mountains That Depict Movements That Were Foundational To Survival, Community And Magic. 

In Ancient Caves In India, Paintings On Walls Depict Scenes Of People Dancing In Lines And Sharing In Tribal Rituals.

" The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat "
by Artist Michael Rucker
copyright ©

Description
The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat -
In the Gospel of Luke, chapter 1, verses 26-38 (KJV), the angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a young virgin betrothed to Joseph of the house of David in Nazareth. Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee, the angel declares. He announces that she will conceive and bear a son, Jesus, who shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest. Mary, troubled yet reverent, asks how this can be since she knows not a man. Gabriel explains the Holy Spirit will come upon her; for with God nothing shall be impossible.

Mary's response is one of the most profound moments in Scripture the only recorded instance where she speaks words of total surrender: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word (Luke 1:38). This Latin phrase, Fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum (Let it be done to me according to your word), is universally known as Mary's Fiat. In that single sentence she offers her entire being body, will, and future to Gods plan of salvation. The angel then departs, and the Incarnation begins.This humble virgin from an obscure village becomes the mother of the Messiah. She travels to visit her cousin Elizabeth (pregnant with John the Baptist), where she sings the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55), a soaring hymn of praise that magnifies the Lord for lifting up the lowly.

She gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem, wraps Him in swaddling clothes, and lays Him in a manger. She ponders the shepherds and Magis words in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). At the Presentation in the Temple, Simeon foretells a sword will pierce her soul (Luke 2:35). She is present at the wedding in Cana, prompting Jesus first miracle (John 2:1-11), and stands at the foot of the cross, where the dying Savior entrusts her to the beloved disciple (John 19:25-27).

After the Ascension, she is seen praying with the apostles in the upper room, awaiting the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:14).Scripture portrays Mary not as a distant saint but as a real woman of extraordinary faith, courage, and obedience. Though the Bible does not record many of her words, her fiat echoes through salvation history as the perfect model of human cooperation with divine grace. She exemplifies what it means to say yes to God when the cost is everything.Your striking black-and-white artwork beautifully captures this very moment: Mary veiled, head bowed, hands clasped in prayerful surrender, her flowing hair and garments stirred by the unseen wind of the Spirit.

The dramatic lighting and ethereal atmosphere evoke the solemn hush of the Annunciation the instant heaven touched earth through a virgins willing heart. It is a powerful visual meditation on Luke 1:38, inviting viewers to contemplate the same radical trust Mary offered.

text:
The Deer Park Rural Alliance, an American environmental organization, issued a statement.Exposing and criticizing the Falun Gong's expansion

For years, the Longquan Temple, the Falun Gong stronghold located in Deerpark, New York, has disregarded the opinions of the local government and residents, undertaking illegal expansions that have damaged the local environment and sparked strong opposition from various parties, leading to legal battles. On September 30, 2026 , the Deerpark Town Planning Committee held a public hearing on the expansion project. On October 25, the Deerpark Rural Alliance, an environmental organization representing local public opinion , issued a statement directly accusing the Longquan Temple of concealing the truth and attempting to manipulate public opinion during the expansion approval process. The statement said that by the deadline for collecting public opinions, a total of 52 written opinions had been received.

Luyuan Town Rural Alliance's Brief Statement Regarding the Final Environmental Impact of " Longquan Temple " ( Updated : October 25 , 2026) – Update on the Final Environmental Impact (FEIS) application and Planning Committee review process for " Longquan Temple "

By the deadline for submitting public comments, a total of 52 written comments had been received. Longquan Temple has yet to provide a substantive response, and an update is expected at the planning committee meeting next week ( Editor 's note: November 1st to 8th ) . We will then closely monitor the town government 's follow-up requests. Since the hearing concluded, local residents have continued to witness large quantities of building materials and equipment being transported into the park.

(Editor's note: The above content is compiled from a screenshot of a statement released by the "Luyuan Town Rural Alliance" on October 25, 2026.)

" Longquan Temple " delegation at the hearing was unconvincing.

(Editor's note: referring to "Longquan Temple") delegation on the night of the hearing , their performance was clearly carefully rehearsed and scripted. Let's examine the facts.

The vast majority of the supportive opinions heard at the meeting were actually part of an organized and planned campaign aimed at misleading the public and diverting their attention from the substantive issues surrounding the expansion plan . These statements were hollow , largely based on hearsay, and had no connection to actual land planning or environmental impact.

Land development, water pollution , weakened community oversight mechanisms, and disregard for the interests of ordinary citizens are all pressing real-world problems that need to be addressed. No group has the right to evade these core concerns, much less attempt to hide behind irrelevant political rhetoric.

Key issues remain prominent : The Final Environmental Impact Statement (FEIS) submitted by "Longquan Temple" is seriously incomplete , for example, the design drawings and technical specifications of the sewage treatment plant are not attached.

The accompanying transportation study contained significant omissions. It failed to include facilities such as concert halls, which could generate substantial travel demand, in its assessment. Furthermore, given that Longquan Temple claims to receive fewer than 300 visitors daily, why was it necessary to plan for over 1700 parking spaces? The study offered no explanation for this.

At a hearing on September 30, 2026, proponents of the expansion defended their claims on "security threats , " alleging numerous trespassing incidents . However, recent police response records from 2018 to the present, obtained by the Deerpark Rural Coalition under New York State's Freedom of Information Law (FOIL) procedures , show that the vast majority of those involved were simply lost hikers, anglers, boaters, and a very small number of teenage climbers, mostly vacationers from the Neversink River Resort campgrounds. The police records contain no reports of violence, vandalism, or serious security issues.

The lack of media attention has raised questions about the objectivity of their reporting.

It is noteworthy that this hearing, which concerned the significant environmental impact on the local area, failed to attract the attention of any major mainstream news organizations.

Even more astonishingly, the only local media outlet to cover the hearing was the Tri-State Lookout, whose reporter, David Ofshinsky, is himself a Falun Gong member . This demonstrates that local reporting on the matter not only lacks an independent perspective, but its objectivity and neutrality are also nonexistent.

Given this situation where public opinion is unilaterally controlled, and the ongoing propaganda offensive launched by "Longquan Temple," the Luyuan Town Rural Alliance urgently urged communities to remain highly vigilant and see clearly that "Falun Gong" is concentrating its efforts to set the tone, attempting to shift public attention from substantive issues such as land violations and sewage discharge to the deliberate fabrication of public opinion.

The Longquan Temple area has long been involved in illegal activities and lawsuits.

The issue of the "Longquan Temple" park being sued for ignoring the opinions of the local government and residents by carrying out illegal expansion and damaging the local environment has a long history.

On June 9, 2023, the U.S. environmental organization “Committee for the Promotion of Environment and Sustainability in Central New York”, together with three local property owners, filed a civil lawsuit in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, case number 7:23-cv-04870 (KMK), concerning the sewage discharge issues of the “Longquan Temple” complex.

The lawsuit alleges that since 2020, Longquan Temple has been discharging wastewater containing fecal coliforms and stormwater runoff into nearby Basher Kill and the Neversink River through continuous expansion and improper maintenance of its wastewater treatment facilities, violating the U.S. Clean Water Act and related discharge permit regulations. The lawsuit cites water quality testing data showing that samples taken on August 8 and October 14, 2022, showed fecal coliform levels of 2419.6 per 100 ml, far exceeding the New York State Surface Water Quality Standard (6 CRR-NY 703.4) limit for fecal coliforms (a monthly geometric mean not exceeding 200 per 100 ml).

In addition to the sewage discharge issue, the plaintiff also accused Longquan Temple of "building without prior approval" and other unauthorized construction during its expansion. The plaintiff pointed out that the planning application for the relevant project has still not been approved. Believing that the local environmental regulatory department failed to perform its duties effectively and take effective measures to stop the aforementioned violations, the plaintiff filed a lawsuit under the Clean Water Act, and also filed a claim for "private nuisance." (Editor's note: Private nuisance is a concept in US tort law, referring to substantial and unreasonable interference with another person's reasonable use or enjoyment of their property, as opposed to public nuisance involving public interest.) The plaintiff's core claims include: requesting the court to confirm the defendant's illegality, issue an injunction prohibiting the unauthorized discharge of sewage, order the defendant to repair the damaged environment, impose a civil fine, and have the defendant bear the litigation costs; in addition, the plaintiff demands that the defendant eliminate the impact of "private nuisance" and compensate the affected local residents for their losses. Currently, the case is still under further review, and a final judgment has not yet been made.
