text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
November 9, 2026

Conservative Action Network Launches Free Technology Tools to Expand Civic Participation and Reduce Barriers for Local Candidates

[Loudoun County, VA] — Conservative Action Network (CAN), a newly formed social welfare organization, today announced its launch to promote the common good by expanding civic engagement and reducing structural barriers that limit who can effectively participate in local and state elections. The organization will provide free software tools—where state law permits—that support direct voter contact and data-informed outreach, helping more community members run competitive races without the heavy intermediary costs that currently discourage participation.

CAN’s primary purpose is the promotion of social welfare through broader civic involvement. Any political activity is secondary and conducted in full compliance with federal and state law.

At a Glance

- Social welfare organization focused on expanded civic participation
- Free software tools for voter contact and data outreach (where state law allows)
- Goal: lower barriers so more community members can run and voters have more choices
- Seeking $5,000 in recurring monthly support to sustain the platform
- Website: https://t.co/mTWv0C9SRk

Why the 2026 Midterms Underscore the Need for Better Civic Infrastructure

The 2026 midterm elections follow repeated cycles in which high costs and limited tools have reduced competitive races and narrowed voter choice. In Virginia’s 2025 elections, Democrats swept every statewide office. Abigail Spanberger defeated Winsome Earle-Sears for Governor by roughly 57 percent to 42 percent. Ghazala Hashmi defeated John Reid for Lieutenant Governor by about 55 percent to 44 percent. Jay Jones defeated Jason Miyares for Attorney General by approximately 52 percent to 46 percent. Republicans failed to break 50 percent in any of those contests and underperformed both Donald Trump’s 2024 total and Glenn Youngkin’s 2021 total.

The same structural issues—uncontested seats, consultant-driven costs that consume half or more of contributions, and limited modern tools—have continued into the 2026 cycle. When local candidates face $10,000–$50,000 in service fees and statewide candidates face $50,000–$100,000 before they can effectively reach voters, fewer people run. When seats go uncontested, as 15 House of Delegates seats did in 2025 and 20 did in 2023, hundreds of thousands of voters lose the opportunity to choose. Midterms amplify these gaps because they depend heavily on local and state races where resources are thinner.

Aggressive modern technology can help reverse that pattern by lowering the cost of direct voter contact and data-informed outreach. Expanding the number of people who can participate as candidates increases competition, improves accountability, and gives voters more meaningful choices—core elements of stronger civic life.

A Twenty-Year Structural Imbalance Documented in The Blueprint

This effort is informed by the long-term structural reality documented in The Blueprint: How the Democrats Won Colorado (and Why Republicans Everywhere Should Care) by Adam Schrager and Rob Witwer. For roughly the last 20 years, progressive donors and organizations built coordinated infrastructure—beginning with the Colorado Democracy Alliance around 2004—that operates outside traditional party structures through nonprofits, data-driven targeting, and year-round operations. That model has been adapted across states, counties, and localities.

No comparable permanent civic infrastructure was built on the other side. The results in Virginia in 2025 and patterns visible in the 2026 midterms are consistent with one side operating sustained networks while the other continues to rely on high-cost consultants, incomplete recruitment, and tools that do not scale. Addressing that imbalance through practical technology that lowers barriers is one step toward restoring broader participation and meaningful voter choice. Time remains limited if communities want more competitive local races in the years ahead.

Ignored Approaches and Local Contrast

Four years ago, Scott Pio shared detailed approaches with then-Virginia GOP Chair on strengthening results in Virginia and expanding the House of Delegates majority. Last year he discussed comparable data and strategies with then Virginia GOP Chair focused on statewide competitiveness. Neither set of recommendations was adopted, and efforts were made to remove Pio as Loudoun County Republican Committee chair despite local gains. Also last year, Pio sat down with Senator Bryce Reeves and walked through data and voting mechanisms in Virginia along with what it would take to compete effectively for U.S. Senate. Within two weeks Reeves withdrew from the race.

Under Pio’s local leadership, the Loudoun County Republican Committee substantially increased membership and raised $1,200,000 —compared with roughly $20,000 annually before—while improving the county’s Republican position by 9 points. Those results showed that practical tools and consistent outreach can expand participation even in competitive areas. Broader application of data-driven and technology-supported approaches was largely not pursued at the state level.

“I am frustrated—deeply frustrated—with a system that lets consultants get rich while candidates and communities get shortchanged,” said founder Scott Pio. “We are done waiting for the same structures to fix themselves. Aggressive technology that puts tools directly in the hands of local candidates is how we expand real civic participation and give voters more choices.”

What Candidates Receive

CAN offers free software that supports direct voter contact, data-informed outreach, and efficient campaign operations to approved applicants in states that permit such assistance. In jurisdictions that restrict free software or in-kind support to candidates, the organization fully complies with applicable law and provides only legally permitted support. The tools are designed to reduce intermediary costs so candidates can focus resources on reaching voters. Application details and state-by-state compliance information are available on the organization’s website.

Call to Action

CAN is seeking $5,000 in recurring monthly support from individuals who share its commitment to expanded civic participation and more competitive local races. These funds will sustain the technology platform and related engagement efforts. These funds will FIRE many of the consultants we have grown to hate always getting paid while their candidates continue to lose.

Candidates and community groups preparing for the 2027 cycle and beyond can learn about the application process and available tools at https://t.co/29BtBh2m2v. Media inquiries and requests for founder availability or additional materials should be directed to the contact below.
For more information on the organization’s social welfare mission, priorities, or to contribute, visit https://t.co/29BtBh2m2v.

About Conservative Action Network

Conservative Action Network is a social welfare organization whose primary purpose is the promotion of the common good and general welfare of communities through expanded civic engagement, public education on constitutional republic participation, and aggressive modern technology that reduces barriers for candidates focused on local and state issues. It provides free software and support resources where permitted by law, with the aim of increasing the number of people who can effectively participate in the electoral process. Donations are not tax-deductible. More information is available at https://t.co/6gtzOUFLba.

Scott Pio 
Founder, Conservative Action Network

text:
The Architecture of the True Flock: The Forensic Indictment, the Sovereign Shepherd, and the Resurrected Assembly
The Jurisdiction: The Forensic Indictment and the Sovereign Assumption of Custody
The structural baseline of covenant stewardship rests upon a clear legal principle: an under-shepherd holds delegated authority, never proprietary ownership. Under Mosaic jurisprudence, a custodian was held strictly accountable for any loss or harm to the flock unless he could prove sacrificial defense (Exodus 22:10–13). If torn by wild beasts, the shepherd had to produce the mangled carcass as physical evidence to clear himself of liability.
In Ezekiel 34, the Sovereign Owner of the estate issues a formal covenant lawsuit against Israel's civic, royal, and spiritual rulers—explicitly indicted as "the shepherds of Israel" (Ezekiel 34:2). These custodians committed a catastrophic breach of fiduciary duty—consuming the fat, clothing themselves with the wool, slaughtering the healthy, and scattering the vulnerable flock through violent, self-serving negligence.
Furthermore, the divine indictment extends beyond the corrupt leaders to adjudicate horizontal tyranny within the fold itself. In Ezekiel 34:17–22, Yahweh intervenes to judge between sheep and sheep, specifically between the fat sheep and the lean sheep. The aggressive rams and he-goats used their horns to thrust aside the sick, fouled the clear drinking waters with their hooves, and trampled the rich pastures so the weak had to graze on ruined ground. Lest there be any doubt regarding the parties involved, Yahweh defines the legal entities at the conclusion of the audit: "You are My flock, the flock of My pasture; you are men, and I am your God" (Ezekiel 34:31). The sheep are the covenant people; the shepherds are their appointed magistrates and priests.
Because the delegated stewards defaulted on their trust and permitted the strong to exploit the afflicted, Yahweh revokes their commission and declares an extraordinary jurisdictional takeover:
"Behold, I am against the shepherds, and I will require My flock at their hand... I Myself will search for My sheep and look after them." (Ezekiel 34:10–11)
Yet within the identical judicial decree, He establishes that "My servant David" will be their singular prince and shepherd (34:23–24). This is not an administrative contradiction; it is the prophetic architecture of the Incarnation.
When Jesus steps into the Temple courts during the Feast of Dedication (Hanukkah)—the very festival commemorating the cleansing and re-consecration of corrupt temple institutions—and proclaims:
"I am the good shepherd" (Egō eimi ho poimēn ho kalos, John 10:11)
He does not offer a sentimental agrarian illustration. He uses kalos—the noble, authentic, legally qualified Shepherd—and claims the burning-bush identity (Egō eimi) to execute the Ezekiel 34 decree. This pronouncement immediately follows the events of John 9, where the religious authorities weaponized excommunication (aposynagōgos, John 9:22), acting as the brutal "fat sheep" who thrust with their horns and cast out (exebalon, John 9:34) the man born blind simply because he confessed Christ. Jesus seeks out the cast-off sheep, demonstrating that the True Shepherd lawfully extracts His own from an abusive holding pen. While Mosaic law permitted a bailee to present a slaughtered sheep to absolve himself of blame, the True Shepherd steps into the teeth of the wolf, offering His own flesh as the substitutionary purchase price for their deliverance.
The Test: The Scattering of the Bones and the Pretense of the Hireling
The adversary's enduring tactic is the dispersion and starvation of the covenant community, accompanied by the false claim that scattered, desiccated bones cannot be revived. Ezekiel 37 opens in a valley of extreme death—bones bleached dry, disjointed, and severed from any vital connection to the head. This reflects the outward reality of humanity under the curse of sin and broken covenant structures: divided tribes, dead religious formalism, and systemic helplessness under faithless oversight.
The test challenges the authority of the Sovereign Word: Can these bones live?
Counterfeit shepherds attempt to manage the outward appearance of the flock through human organization, ceremonial legalism, or political compromise, all while leaving the bones devoid of breath. Their contempt for the flock was foretold in Zechariah 11:12–13, where Israel's leaders criminally appraised the True Shepherd's labor at thirty pieces of silver—the statutory restitution price for a gored slave (Exodus 21:32).
In John 10, the hireling abandons the flock at the first sight of the wolf because his motivation is wages, not covenant fidelity; he has no skin in the estate. The test of the True Shepherd is whether He possesses the judicial authority to call His own sheep by name out of the grave, breathe the breath of life (Ruach) into their lungs, and break down the ancient dividing walls that fragment them into competing, defensive camps. In contrast to the hireling who flees in self-preservation, Christ exercises singular, sovereign prerogative over His own mortality:
"I lay down My life for the sheep [tēn psychēn mou tithēmi hyper tōn probatōn]... No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have authority [exousia] to lay it down, and I have authority to take it again." (John 10:15, 18)
The hireling’s life is taken by predatory force; the Good Shepherd makes a deliberate, voluntary judicial deposit of His own life to discharge the accumulated debt of the estate and secure absolute deliverance for the flock.
The Response: The Breath of the Ruach and the Binding of the Scepter
The divine countermeasure operates not by human institutional reformation, but through sovereign resurrection, legal security, and organic unification:
The Resurrection through the Word and Spirit: In Ezekiel 37, the prophet speaks the decreed Word to the dry bones, followed by the summoning of the four winds (Ruach). Bone knits to bone, sinew and flesh cover them, and the Spirit enters them until they stand as an exceedingly great army. Christ demonstrates this exact operational power in John 10. He acts as the prophetic "Breaker" (ha-Poretz, Micah 2:12–13) who calls His sheep by name and leads them out (exagei autous) of the sterile, institutional fold into living liberty. He declares Himself to be the Door (hē thura) who guards the fold with His own body. His sheep recognize His voice, He imparts eternal life that cannot be extinguished, and no hostile power can snatch them out of His or the Father's hand.
The Unification of the Sticks: Ezekiel is instructed to take two distinct sticks—one for Judah and one for Joseph (the house of Israel)—and join them into a single rod in his hand, establishing an irrevocable Covenant of Peace (b’rît shālôm) under one Davidic King (Ezekiel 37:16–26). This foreshadows the direct gathering work of Christ:
"And other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd." (John 10:16)
The Lamb as the Sovereign Shepherd: The culmination arrives in Revelation 7. Prior to the release of judgment winds, the angel seals the bondservants on their foreheads—the direct fulfillment of Ezekiel 9:4 and Ezekiel 20:37, where the flock passes under the Shepherd's rod to receive an indelible mark of protective immunity and sovereign ownership. The resulting multi-ethnic multitude—drawn from every tribe, tongue, and nation, having washed their robes white in the blood of the Lamb—stands gathered before the throne. In a stunning reversal of natural metaphors, the Lamb at the center of the throne becomes their Shepherd (Revelation 7:17). Fulfilling Ezekiel 37:27 ("My tabernacle also shall be with them"), the One seated on the throne tabernacles over them (skēnōsei ep’ autous), leading them directly to living fountains of water and wiping away every tear.
The Daily Walk: The Practice of the True Sheep
For the seeker of truth operating in the present age, this forensic reality establishes practical principles for daily fidelity:
Attuning the Ear Exclusively to the Master's Voice: The primary defense against modern hirelings and theological revisionists is an unwavering familiarity with the Shepherd's canonical voice. The sheep do not follow a stranger because they do not recognize the stranger's syntax. Every teaching, philosophy, and institutional demand must be audited against the plumb line of the written Word.
Refusing the Seduction of the Hireling: True disciples do not outsource their spiritual custody or family stewardship to hirelings who flee when cultural wolves attack. Whether in the home, the congregation, or the civil square, biblical stewardship demands personal risk, sacrificial defense of the weak, and an absolute refusal to compromise the flock for temporary self-preservation.
Resting in Sovereign Security: Fear is entirely eliminated by the legal finality of the Shepherd's purchase. The sheep do not keep themselves; they are kept by the grip of the Sovereign Shepherd who conquered the grave. No circumstance, accusation, or spiritual adversary can overturn the title deed executed at the Cross.
Living as Reunited, Resurrected Vessels: Having been brought from the valley of dry bones into the life of the Ruach, the believer actively pursues the unity of the true, historic flock across every cultural, ethnic, and denominational boundary. The true sheep refuse to enact the abusive bullying of the "fat sheep" or retreat into sectarian tribalism where the Chief Shepherd has decreed one unified fold under one eternal King.

text:
Watched Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana. 

It is a disappointment for me overall. 

But given that Bollywood churned out Adipurush before this it is to be seen as an incremental improvement? 

I couldn't watch Adipurush beyond 15mins. So this one is a shade better that way. 

Overall it is clear that the director and that Boddhisatva guy who is cited as research assistant for the film are both smitten by progressivism keeda. 

Add to that a good dash of Dravidoid style narrative on Ravana and you have a lethal combo. 

The entire character arc of Ravana is totally messed up. Yash does a good job with screen presence and acting but that doesn't mean we give a free pass to the script. 

The character arc is totally contrived. Unnecessary Oppressor-Oppressed narration. KGF style saviour complex. Totally uncalled for. 

Telugu audience will remember Sr NT Ramarao's excesses w.r.t Ravana simping. 

Script writers have made a deliberate attempt to not show the evil side of Ravana in many places. 

Shoorpanaka character arc is also totally messed up. Again it feels deliberate. If the script writers were innocent they would have followed Valmiki Ramayana and popular understanding of Shoorpanaka and Ravana. But they wanted to innovate and show some crazy progressive khichdi. 

Sita giving social justice gender justice gyan on this episode also felt out of place. 

Ravana-Sita encounter in the climax is such a huge let down. It is like both of them are not clear why this episode is happening. Just plain sister revenge? Ravana is shown as he is just some angry young man with zero love and lust for women. 

Sai Pallavi as Sita seems to be deliberately miscast so that she never ever appears beautiful. Live no one would consider her beautiful compared to Shoorpanaka, Mandodari et al. That's how deliberate the makeup and actor choices are. 

Also sword wielding Sita fighting orcs is another out of place intervention which messes up the character arc and narration. But then we have the progressivism gender justice itch that we tolerate 'Sita - Warrior of Mithila' style creative liberty. So this too shall pass. 

Rama's character arc also is messed up. Unnecessary scenes of self-doubt, random social justice dialogues. 

Visuals are good in parts. But there is also TV serial vibes in many places. 

Costumes are all over the place. No coherence with the times of Ramayana era. 

Lot of focus on VFX and Visual spectacle aspects. 

Hans Zimmer and ARR music is a big letdown. In some places it was too jarring. 

It's sad so much money and publicity went into this only to get this tasteless but colorful insta worthy khichdi out. 

But such are times. This is the best our film industry has to offer at the moment unless we want to point people back to older classics. 

Part-2 can be a shade or two better if they want to course correct. Otherwise it will follow Part-1. The character arcs are set up already.

text:
BLOG: Elvis: the King and I

I saw that ELVIS film from a few years back last night. The one with Austin Butler and Tom Hanks. It was just stunning! Easily one of the best performances in any film I’ve ever seen. I though the Michael Jackson one was spot on but this was on another level. The story-telling, the art direction, the acting- it was all incredible...

And I say this as someone who has something of a history with Elvis.

As a teenager, one of my summer jobs in Blackpool was as a spieler for an Elvis exhibition on the promenade.

For those who don't know, a 'spieler' is someone who stands outside the front of a place and calls people to come inside. It's the old 'roll up! roll up!' job from the days of travelling circuses but for me, in the 80’s in Blackpool, it meant standing on a box with a microphone connected to a speaker fixed to each corner of the Woolworths building (next to the Tower) so I could be heard across half a mile of seafront, talking non-stop, all day, about Elvis.
I gently declined the offer of a gold, ‘fake-lamé’ suit, citing the windy conditions on that section of prom.

I had to learn a ‘spiel’ that I would recite, verbatim, along with interactions with passing people, maybe a few songs (yes I was also a damn fine impersonator, and my Elvis impression was praised by Freddie Starr on one of his many visits).
After a few weeks, boredom took over and I did less of the spiel. It basically turned into my little Elvis tribute/stand-up act.

It was the 80’s. There were no rules, nobody got arrested for offending people, and I was a cocky teenager with infinite confidence and a fast mouth.

I quickly went from:

‘For the first time, anywhere in the world, The Graceland Estate is proud to present the life and times of Elvis Presley, here on Blackpool’s Golden Mile! Born January the 8th, 1935, in Tupelo Mississippi….’

To this:

‘Hello ladies! Are you fans of Elvis?... you are? Well, come on in! You can check out his famous jump suits- it’s the only jump some of you are gonna see this weekend!... [singing] ‘she’s everything a man could want, and you’re not her’!’

‘Ever been to Tennessee mate? No? didn’t think so, you look like you have to make a tenner see you through the week!’

‘Where’s Graceland? It’s just off the coast of Scotland, everyone’s called ‘Grace’!’

‘You booked your accommodation yet lads? I recommend the Heartbreak Hotel coz none of you could get your end away in a brothel with a twenty pound note in each ear! I hope you kept the receipt for those johnnies!’

‘A ‘waste of money’ madam? Didn’t stop you buying a bra did it?’

‘They called him ‘Elvis The Pelvis’, I hope your name’s not Mick Head!’

You get the idea. I got a lot of laughs but I also, rightly, got a lot of abuse. I was punched, dragged off my box, shouted at- a LOT, and had to run and hide inside a few times when I’d gone too far with  drunken stag-do’s.

The main problem was that it was in Blackpool, the home of loud noises and loose morals, flashing lights and kiss-me-quick hats. Where gobby young idiots like me were meant to be, along with invisible dogs on leads, glitter wigs, glow-in-the-dark necklaces and tee-shirts with a drawing of Roadrunner getting throttled, and shagged, by Wyle-E-Coyote and ‘meep-meep now you bastard!’ written underneath (all of which I have sold on the prom). It was the place where one expected the lowest quality and the cheapest tat, and nothing else.

Unfortunately for the Elvis Exhibition, it was totally legit.

Every single thing in it was 100% authentic, and the Elvis fans who knew about it, but couldn't afford a trip to Graceland, would come over at great expense from all across the country and even abroad.
It wasn't just Freddie Starr, there were lots of mid-to-low level celebrities who were fans.

We even had a cavalcade of 4 limousines containing the Graceland estate legal team who turned up, out of the blue, to check everything was going to plan.
They expected to find a respectful shrine to the most popular human who's ever lived, including Jesus (yes, that was in my script). And a museum-like, tastefully-presented collection of some of his most treasured possessions.

We had the bible he kept on his desk at Graceland, opened at the back page where he had written, in pencil, various combinations of drugs and how they affected him. Letters to his mother Gladys. The guitar he was playing on the day he died with his fingerprints still on it, and a collection of his jumpsuits including the infamous ‘pizza’ jumpsuit which he had made, at a low point, to mock himself when he gained weight.
There was even a video playing on a monitor, showing an interview with Priscilla Presley who was so unpopular with his legion of die-hard fans that every day the cleaner had to wipe the spit from the screen.

This was, at the time, the only collection of genuine Elvis artefacts, outside of Graceland, anywhere in the world, and my boss had somehow convinced them to put it on Blackpool promenade (I assumed it was because he had convinced them that Blackpool was the ‘Vegas of Britain’).

And the first thing they see, standing on a box with a microphone in his hand and a cocky little smile on his cocky little face, was a teenager with a quick wit, a slack mouth and an apparent death wish.
I greeted them, over the mic, with, ’look out! The Mafia’s arrived! I hope I don’t wake up with a donkey’s head in bed with me!... Although it wouldn’t be the first time!‘ [cheeky wink and an offered handshake to a man in a black suit who acted like I’d just fallen from the back end of a dog.]
There were complaints.

I also discovered that Elvis fans are insane.

The number of people who tried to get in by telling me they were related to him was incredible. Every other day I'd have some deadbeat from Rotherham trying to convince me they were his distant cousin. I even had somebody hold up one of the postcards that we sold in the shop, with their face cut from some old photograph and glued over the face of Elvis's dad, claiming that it was a picture of him and the king together.

They drove me so mad that eventually I did something that I wasn't proud of. On a rainy day, when standing outside wasn't an option, I did a stint selling merchandise in the shop.

We had, ‘for display purposes only’, a small plastic statue of Elvis, the base of which you could insert a small cassette tape into and then the statue would flash different colours and a very quiet, tinny recording of ‘Hound Dog’ would play.
That was the only song we had, the only song it played.
It wasn't for sale, it was just something the owners had grabbed from their travels to fill a gap on a shelf.

But then I was approached by one of his lunatic fans. Already drunk and walking around with no top on, just so the world could see his collection of Elvis tattoos. My heart had become wooden... I decided I was going to rip him off.

He was stood at the counter, looking for something to buy. I got the little plastic ornament down and pretended to be on the phone talking to the boss to see if they had any more of them or was it ‘just this one?’. I knew I had his attention. I put it back on the shelf, gave it a light dusting, inserted the tape and let his greedy little eyes take the wheel.

He asked about it, I told him it was a one off display piece from the Graceland estate and so not really for sale. Then I had the cheek to tell him he couldn’t afford it, like I was doing him a favour.

Eventually I told him he could have it for £150. He said he’d think about it and I sang, ‘It’s now or never!’ to show him who he was dealing with.
He nodded at me… I was speaking his language.
I even waited while he went out of the exhibition to the cashpoint to get the money, and then paid to get back in, just to buy this bit of plastic crap. He handed over £150 and walked away with about £1.50 worth of garbage.
In the 1980’s, £150 was a hell of a lot of money.

I still think about him now, from time to time. I know I ripped him off but I actually believe I made him happy. His life, his world, his sphere of existence, they were very small and they were filled with one obsession- Elvis. As far as he was concerned (and maybe still is unless he reads this), he was the only Elvis fan in the world who owned a unique piece of Elvis memorabilia, sent directly from Graceland. It will have been given pride of place on his home-made Elvis shrine. I picture him popping the little cassette in, closing his eyes, and imagining the King holding this little plastic thing and saying to Colonel Tom Parker, ‘We're only going to make one of these, right Colonel?’ while he does his much-rehearsed Elvis moves in the living room.
(I know he did this because he told me that they were ‘actually genuine kung-fu moves that Elvis learned off a monk to fight off mad fans and the FBI, who were trying to frame him for the JFK thing!’ I didn’t reply, ‘Elvis did Karate, you mad twat- call yourself a fan?’ Because I felt it might have reopened an already closed deal.)
He may have been in Blackpool, where everything you can see is cheap tat, but he knew he was in a small oasis of authenticity, sanctioned by The king himself, where everything was genuine, and where the nice young man behind the counter was kind enough to allow him to take home a unique, not for sale, one-of-a-kind piece of genuine Elvis history.

Bit of a bargain really....

text:
YOU WILL SMILE AGAIN

There are seasons in life when the pain is so loud, it drowns out the sound of hope. You wake up every day carrying the weight of yesterday, wondering if the future has anything better to offer. You go to bed tired, not just from the day’s work, but from fighting invisible battles in your mind and heart.

People see you outside and think you’re fine because you’ve mastered the art of hiding your scars. You laugh in public so no one will ask too many questions. You keep yourself busy so your thoughts don’t catch up with you. But when the noise fades, and it’s just you alone in the quiet, the tears you’ve been holding back finally break free.

Child of God, hear me: God has not forgotten you. Every tear you’ve cried has been counted. Every sleepless night has been noticed. Every prayer you whispered when you didn’t even have the strength to say it out loud — Heaven heard it. And the God who sees in secret is about to reward you openly.

The valley you’re walking through is not permanent. David said, “Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death…” he didn’t say he would stay there, he said he would walk through. That means there is an exit. There is an end. And beyond this valley, there’s a table prepared for you, in the presence of those who thought you wouldn’t make it.

You may not feel it now, but there is a version of you in the future who will look back at this very moment and smile, not because the pain was easy, but because the pain produced something priceless in you. Strength. Depth. Faith that cannot be shaken.

So hold on a little longer. Keep praying, even when your voice trembles. Keep standing, even when your knees feel weak. The One who promised is faithful. And when He turns your mourning into dancing, you won’t just smile,b you will laugh the laugh of someone who has seen the goodness of God in the land of the living.

Your night will not last forever. Morning is on its way. And when it comes, you will smile again.

text:
After weighing acquisition cost, safety, quality of life, market momentum, lifestyle appeal and long-term livability, these are my three strongest recommendations for 2025–2026:

1. Portugal
Portugal currently offers one of the most attractive combinations on the continent. Housing remains more affordable than in Northern or Central Europe (despite strong recent price growth), while safety scores are solid and quality of life is high — especially in terms of climate, healthcare access, outdoor lifestyle and international connectivity. Cities such as Porto and the Algarve, along with the greater Lisbon area (outside the most premium zones), still deliver genuine value. The market has momentum, yet it has not fully priced out quality of life the way some Northern markets have.

2. Spain
Spain ranks very close to Portugal. Strong quality-of-life scores (climate, culture, food, healthcare), improving safety perceptions in many regions, and housing costs that, while rising, remain more accessible than in Germany, the Netherlands or Scandinavia. Coastal and secondary cities often provide better value than Madrid or Barcelona proper. Spain combines lifestyle advantages with a large, liquid property market and good infrastructure — a practical and enjoyable place to live or invest for the medium term.

3. Slovenia (or Croatia as a close alternative)
For those seeking a quieter, high-safety environment with excellent nature access and still-reasonable prices, Slovenia stands out. It scores very well on safety and quality of life while remaining cheaper than Western European peers.

(Croatia offers a similar profile with the added appeal of the Adriatic coastline. Both markets are smaller and less liquid than Iberia, but they deliver a strong quality-of-life-to-cost ratio and have been among the better performers in Central and Southern Europe).

These three destinations currently strike the best overall balance between what you pay for a home and what you receive in daily safety, liveability and long-term appeal. Markets further north (Netherlands, Denmark, Switzerland, Austria) deliver outstanding quality of life and safety but at a significantly higher entry cost. Eastern markets remain cheaper but generally lag on the combined safety + quality-of-life metrics.

Good morning to The Believers, to the ones who know humility, to the ones whose hearts are found in The Lord, good morning. 🌞

This morning, I woke with my favorite male human on my mind - the one who marches to his own drumbeat, the one whose named is chanted , in the thousands, by children... the one whose heart is made of gold - the one who is a my lamppost,  anchored in The Ceadars of Lebanon. 🌲

I feel grateful for this, as I recall the light found in his eyes which mirrored my own. I immediately go into prayer as I pray for restoration of the hearts who know the depth of my soul; please remember me. 💛

Visions of Christmases past scroll through my mind, as I recall a tradition established with my daughter. We made hand-painted, salt dough ornaments to give to family and friends - a reminder each year as they adorned their own trees, we loved them. 🎄

In my prayers, I pray to put up a Christmas tree this year, remembering the 12 ft tree I put up each year, dressed as a candy land of Hope. I pray to bake again, another way to bless others with Love - a tin of assorted, homemade treats of sweetness and comfort. 🍭

I have simple desires as I pray to The Lord, all asked through His Will and Plan for my Life. Whatever he wishes or asks of me, I eagerly beg to serve.

text:
## 13. WHY PROPHECY MATTERS: THE GOD WHO KNOWS THE FUTURE
**Isaiah 46:9–10** describes God as the One who declares the end from the beginning.
That is one of the extraordinary claims of biblical faith.
God is not merely observing history as it unfolds.
He knows its beginning, its end, and everything in between.
Human beings can make forecasts using mathematics, science, experience, and probability.
Sometimes our predictions are remarkably accurate.
But we cannot independently demonstrate perfect knowledge of the future.
If biblical prophecies were demonstrably written centuries before specific events and accurately described those events in ways beyond reasonable human foresight, that would be powerful evidence deserving an explanation.
And if divine revelation is the best explanation, then the implications are enormous.
It would mean that the Bible deserves to be taken seriously not merely as ancient literature, but as a revelation from God.
Of course, an apparent fulfillment must survive careful examination.
Not every claimed fulfillment will.
And I do not believe our faith should be based upon exaggerated facts, inaccurate history, or claims that cannot withstand scrutiny.
**Truth does not need exaggeration to remain true.**
That is why I welcome informed disagreement.
## 14. THE MOST IMPORTANT MESSAGE: GOD LOVES YOU
Ultimately, my interest in biblical prophecy is not driven by a fascination with catastrophe or fear of the future.
It comes from my belief that the Bible reveals a God who loves His creation.
Christianity makes an extraordinary claim.
The Creator of the universe entered His own creation in the person of Jesus Christ.
He lived without sin.
He willingly gave His life for humanity.
And He rose again.
**John 3:16** tells us that God loved the world and gave His only Son so that those who believe in Him may have everlasting life.
**Romans 5:8** tells us that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.
**Ephesians 2:8–9** teaches that salvation comes by grace through faith, not through works that earn God's favor.
**Philippians 2:6–8** describes Christ humbling Himself and becoming obedient to death on the cross.
**1 Corinthians 15:3–4** describes the central message of the gospel: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again.
Think about what Christianity is actually claiming.
**The Creator of everything loves His creation so deeply that He entered it and sacrificed Himself to reconcile us to Him.**
We cannot make ourselves perfect enough to earn salvation.
We cannot undo every mistake we have made.
We cannot purchase God's love with good deeds.
But the Christian gospel says we do not have to.
God offers salvation through Jesus Christ.
That is the message I hope everyone understands, regardless of whether they agree with my interpretation of end-times prophecy.
The Bible's central message is not simply that judgment is coming.
It is that forgiveness, redemption, and eternal life are available through Jesus Christ.
## FINAL THOUGHTS: PROPHECY PROVES GOD
So where does all of this leave us?
I believe Israel's historical restoration is significant.
I believe the conditions Jesus described deserve serious attention.
I believe modern technologies make certain future prophetic scenarios far easier to understand.
I believe geopolitical developments, discussions surrounding a future Temple, and other biblical passages present an increasingly interesting prophetic picture.
And I believe Jesus Christ is coming soon.
But I will make an important distinction.
**I am not claiming that every modern event I've discussed constitutes completed prophecy.**
Some passages may have historical fulfillments.
Some may have future fulfillments.
Some may have both, depending upon their proper interpretation.
And some modern correspondences may simply be interesting parallels rather than evidence of fulfillment.
My belief is that, when carefully evaluated together, these passages present a prophetic framework worthy of serious consideration.
I believe the Bible contains genuine prophecy.
I believe genuine fulfilled prophecy provides powerful evidence of God.
And I believe the future described in Scripture is approaching.
**PROPHECY PROVES GOD.**
That is my conviction.
Now I invite anyone who disagrees to challenge it.
Bring historical records.
Bring biblical scholarship.
Bring scientific data.
Bring competing interpretations.
Let's distinguish facts from assumptions, examine competing explanations, and consider what the evidence actually demonstrates.
And let's do it respectfully.
Because if these prophecies are true, the implications are far greater than winning an argument on Facebook.
They concern the existence of God, the identity of Jesus Christ, the future of humanity, and the possibility of eternal life.
**The God who knows the future is the same God who created you, loves you, and gave His life for you.**
And if Jesus Christ truly is coming again, I believe the most important question is not whether we can identify every prophetic detail correctly.
It is whether we know Him.
God bless you all, and have a wonderful day.
**The invitation is open to everyone.**

text:
Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization : https://t.co/qJh5PnEXEn

"arXiv:2611.09846v1 [https://t.co/gQRNwvACTl] 06 Nov 2026
Ensemble Methodology for Reference-Free Confidence Estimation in LLM-based Code Summarization
Marco Colombomcolom4@illinois.eduUniversity of Illinois Urbana-ChampaignSumit Tokkarstokkar@illinois.eduUniversity of Illinois Urbana-ChampaignBalaji A JBalaji_Jayaram@infosys.comInfosysSowmyakumari Selvarajsowmyakumari.s@infosys.comInfosysAnimesh Kumaranimesh.kumar14@infosys.comInfosysRavishankar ShettyRavishankarS@infosys.comInfosysAravinda Prasad Sistlasistla@uic.eduUniversity of Illinois ChicagoRigel Gjomemorgjome1@uic.eduUniversity of Illinois ChicagoAbstract.
This paper describes an approach and use case to estimate the correctness of LLM-generated COBOL summaries without access to human-authored references. The core intuition is that inter-model agreement on semantics is informative about truth, and that an LLM-as-judge can provide higher-fidelity pairwise assessments than traditional string- or embedding-based metrics (Wu et al., 2024; Robinson and Kummerfeld, 2025). We operationalise this intuition with (i) controlled summary generation from diverse models; (ii) a LLM evaluator that compares pairs of summaries and emits structured judgments; and (iii) a calibrated aggregation rule that combines supportive evidence while penalising only corroborated contradictions.
1.Introduction
COBOL (Common Business-Oriented Language) remains deeply entrenched in enterprise computing, with billions of lines of code in production across financial services, insurance, government, and healthcare sectors (Britton, 2024). These legacy systems, developed over several decades, manage mission-critical operations including transaction processing platforms (IBM TPF), core banking systems, claims processing, and regulatory compliance frameworks. The technical complexity of these codebases stems from decades of incremental modifications, vendor-specific extensions, and business logic that evolved without adequate documentation, creating significant knowledge management challenges for organizations maintaining these systems.The imperative for COBOL modernization stems from multiple converging factors. First, the steep decline in COBOL-proficient developers—with a significant portion of existing practitioners approaching retirement age and limited new talent entering the field—creates a critical sustainability risk. Second, integration challenges between legacy COBOL platforms and modern cloud-native architectures, microservices, and API ecosystems impede digital transformation initiatives. Third, maintaining aging mainframe infrastructure incurs substantial costs. These factors have given rise to multiple initiatives aimed to transform COBOL codebases into modern languages and platforms (Gandhi et al., 2024; Chakravarthy et al., 2026). Some of these initiatives include direct translation of COBOL codebases into a modern language (Chakaravarthy et al., 2026; Froimovich et al., 2025; Challa et al., 2025) while others are focused on extracting specifications and the business logic, which can then be used to recreate that business logic in a modern language and architecture (Bhattacharyya et al., 2025; Kalohia, 2026).In this paper, we are focused on the latter approach, business logic extraction from COBOL codebases. The main challenge in this approach is that the vast majority of legacy COBOL programs lack adequate inline comments, external documentation, or design specifications—original developers have often retired, taking institutional knowledge with them. This creates a fundamental documentation gap: to safely migrate, refactor, or rewrite these systems, engineers need accurate descriptions of what each program does, yet manual documentation at scale is prohibitively expensive given the extensive codebases requiring analysis.Recent advances in Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated promising capabilities in code understanding and documentation generation. Multiple frontier models, including GPT-4, Claude, LLaMA, and specialized code models, can generate human-readable summaries of code functionality. This creates an opportunity to automatically document legacy COBOL codebases at scale. However, a fundamental question remains: How do we evaluate the quality, accuracy, and reliability of AI-generated documentation when no ground truth exists? Traditional code summarization research relies on reference-based metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) that measure similarity against human-authored reference summaries. These metrics are inapplicable to legacy COBOL scenarios where no reference documentation exists.LLM-based approaches. Existing approaches to assessing LLM output quality offer partial solutions but are insufficient in isolation. Reference-based metrics (BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002)), ROUGE ( (Lin, 2004)), CodeBLEU ( (Ren et al., 2020)), BERTScore ( (Zhang et al., 2019)) require human-authored ground truth summaries—fundamentally inapplicable when no reference documentation exists. Model-internal confidence signals such as perplexity and logit probabilities provide valuable indicators of generation uncertainty and can flag when models are uncertain about their predictions. However, these token-level signals cannot reliably detect when a model is confidently wrong about semantic interpretation—a model may generate a fluent, high-probability summary that completely misinterprets business logic. Single-model LLM-as-judge approaches where one model evaluates another’s output show promise but face validity concerns: evaluators may have systematic biases or blind spots, lack deep understanding of COBOL-specific constructs and mainframe paradigms, have no ground truth for calibration, and can themselves produce inconsistent assessments. No single metric adequately addresses the multifaceted challenge of reference-free evaluation for domain-specific legacy code.Challenge: No human-authored references. In the absence of human-authored references, how can we quantitatively estimate confidence in LLM-generated COBOL documentation to determine which outputs are reliable enough for operational use and which require human expert review? This requires evaluation metrics that are: reference-free (operable without ground truth comparisons); quantifiable (producing numerical confidence scores supporting prioritization and quality gating); interpretable (providing actionable signals explaining why outputs are flagged as low-confidence); multi-dimensional (assessing correctness, completeness, and consistency across multiple quality axes); robust (resistant to single-model biases and prompt engineering artifacts); and scalable (applicable to millions of lines of code requiring documentation). For enterprise adoption, organizations need confidence metrics that indicate: “This summary has high inter-model agreement and complete code coverage—safe for downstream use” versus “This summary has contradictions and potential omissions—requires expert review.”Our approach: overview. We propose a multi-metric ensemble framework that combines complementary evaluation mechanisms:
(1)Inter-model agreement via LLM-as-judge: generating summaries from multiple diverse models and employing structured pairwise comparisons;
(2)Calibrated aggregation: combining judgments through linear pooling with conjunctive penalty for corroborated contradictions;
(3)Token-level confidence scores: measuring generation certainty through perplexity and logit probability analysis;
(4)Code coverage assessment: employing G-Eval metrics to quantify documentation completeness.This reference-free framework enables automatic triage of AI-generated documentation.Our approach has been implemented inside Infosys to deal with summarization of large code bases and extraction of business rules from those code bases for developers. This paper is organized as follows. Section 2 contains backgroun and related work. Section 3 describes our approach in detail. Section 4 describes the evaluation of our approach and results, and Section 5 concludes the paper.
2.Background and Related Work
CODE-NN (Iyer et al., 2016) introduced the first fully data-driven, end-to-end neural approach to code summarization, using LSTM networks with an attention mechanism to generate natural language descriptions of C# code snippets and SQL queries. The model was trained on a corpus automatically mined from StackOverflow, sidestepping the need for hand-labeled data. Building on this attentional encoder-decoder paradigm, code2vec (Alon et al., 2019) took a different angle, representing code as a fixed-length vector by decomposing it into paths through its abstract syntax tree (AST) and learning to aggregate those paths; trained on roughly 14 million methods, it was shown to predict method names accurately even on previously unseen code and to capture meaningful semantic relationships between code snippets. Code2seq (Alon et al., 2018) extended this AST-path idea into a full sequence-generation setting, using attention over the same compositional AST paths to decode natural language sequences rather than single labels, and it outperformed prior token-sequence-based neural machine translation models across multiple languages and tasks, including code summarization and code captioning.DeepCom (Hu et al., 2018) approached the problem as a structure-aware machine translation task, applying NLP techniques together with structural information extracted from Java methods to automatically generate descriptive comments, and it demonstrated clear gains in BLEU-4 scores over earlier baselines like CODE-NN by better capturing the semantics of source code rather than just its token sequence. Finally, the Transformer-based approach of Ahmad et al. (Ahmad et al., 2020) replaced recurrent architectures with a self-attention Transformer model for encoding code, finding that relative position encoding of code tokens (rather than the absolute encoding used in standard Transformers) substantially improved performance; combined with copy attention, this simple adaptation outperformed prior state-of-the-art techniques by a significant margin and has since become a common baseline architecture in the field. Together, these five papers trace the field’s progression from RNN/LSTM-based sequence models, through AST-path-based structural representations, to Transformer architectures explicitly adapted to the syntactic properties of code.Code summarization models are commonly evaluated using a combination of lexical overlap, syntactic awareness, and semantic similarity metrics. BLEU (Papineni et al., 2002) measures the n-gram overlap between a generated summary and one or more reference summaries, emphasizing precision by rewarding exact word sequence matches. ROUGE (Lin, 2004) focuses on recall and evaluates how much of the reference summary is captured by the generated text, with variants such as ROUGE-N and ROUGE-L measuring n-gram and longest common subsequence overlap, respectively. To better assess code-related text generation, CodeBLEU (Ren et al., 2020) extends BLEU by incorporating programming-language-specific features, including weighted n-gram matching, abstract syntax tree (AST) similarity, and data-flow consistency, providing a more comprehensive evaluation of code understanding and generation quality. In contrast, BERTScore (Zhang et al., 2019) leverages contextual embeddings from pre-trained transformer models to measure semantic similarity between generated and reference summaries, allowing it to capture meaning even when different words or phrasing are used. Together, these metrics provide complementary perspectives on code summarization quality, ranging from surface-level lexical agreement to deeper semantic and structural correctness.
3.Approach
A high level view of our approach is depicted in Figure 1. The first step of the approach includes parsing and static analysis of the COBOL code to understand dependencies among paragraphs, build a call graph, and extract other types of information. The output of this step is a set of code chunks, each of which is summarized as a unit in the next steps. Determining the correct granularity of this step is an important aspect of our approach. At one end, chunks at the level of single instructions create verbose descriptions that are not useful. At another extreme, chunks that include whole programs create summaries that hide important details and are not useful. After experimenting with different granularities, we settle for chunks at the paragraph and function level.Let C denote a COBOL code chunk dedicated to a single functionality. Importantly, the chunking policy is not under our control: the segmentation into summarisation units is predetermined by the Infosys pipeline. Our method therefore treats the Infosys chunking as fixed and operates downstream. This constraint reflects realistic deployment conditions, where third-party enterprise tooling governs preprocessing.We assume a set of auxiliary descriptions for called paragraphs or programs, 𝒟={(ni,di)}i=1m, where ni is a callee name and di is a fixed, vetted English description. These include descriptions of called paragraphs/functions. These dependency descriptions are injected into prompts and not reconstructed per run, both to reduce variance and to keep the evaluation focused on the behaviour of C. In addition, the prompt is also augmented with a list of criteria L={L1,…,Ln} specifying the task to the LLM and the outputs (See Appendix for the list used in the evaluation). Specifically, the list L contains the criteria decided by Infosys in their prompt.We consider three summarisation systems:M0=Infosys (OpenAI-based),M1=LLaMA 3.3-70B,M2=Grok-3.Given a prompt template aligned with Infosys’ style (to control granularity), each model produces a summary:S0←M0​(C,𝒟),S1←M1​(C,𝒟),S2←M2​(C,𝒟).Model diversity is desirable but the method is agnostic to the specific choices so long as the models are competent summarizers and not identically trained; the ensemble logic extends to k>3 models.Figure 1.Overview of the ensemble-based confidence estimation pipeline. A COBOL code chunk and its dependencies are summarised by three models (Infosys, LLaMA 3.3–70B, Grok–3). Pairwise comparisons with an LLM-as-judge yield structured scores, which are then aggregated into a final confidence estimate.

3.1.Pairwise Evaluation via LLM-as-Judge
Traditional reference-based metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore) correlate imperfectly with human judgments for code summarisation and are sensitive to surface form and identifier overlap—a poor fit for reference-free settings. Prompted LLM judges, by contrast, have shown strong correlation with human ratings on code tasks (Wu et al., 2024; Robinson and Kummerfeld, 2025). We therefore instantiate a dedicated OpenAI model 𝒥 as an evaluator that compares pairs of summaries following a list of criteria L={L1,…,Ln} specifying the task to the LLM and the outputs (See Appendix for the list used in the evaluation).
Anchored, pairwise comparisons.
We conduct two comparisons anchored on the Infosys output:E1=𝒥⁡(S1,S0),E2=𝒥⁡(S2,S0).Each evaluation returns a structured JSON record
Ei=(agreementi,scorei,missing_detailsi,contradictionsi,rationalei).The agreement label is one of Agree/Mostly Agree/Disagree; the score is a continuous confidence on [0,10] tied to a list of criteria that emphasises functional equivalence (purpose, logic, inputs, outputs) and discounts mere wording differences. The missing-details and contradictions fields enumerate omissions and logical conflicts, respectively, and the rationale gives a concise justification. These fields serve both downstream explainability and manual auditability.
Granularity control.
A common failure mode in pairwise judging is spurious disagreement caused by mismatched levels of detail. To mitigate this, all generators use prompts that mirror Infosys’ template, and evaluators are instructed to: (i) ignore stylistic paraphrase; (ii) treat minor omissions as Mostly Agree if they do not alter semantics; and (iii) reserve Disagree for contradictions or omissions that change behaviour. This alignment makes disagreements diagnostic rather than an artefact of verbosity mismatches.
3.2.Aggregation: Linear Pooling with Conjunctive Penalty
Let ai∈{Agree,Mostly Agree,Disagree} and si∈[0,10] denote the label and confidence produced by Ei. Define the support contributed by each judge asui={si,ai∈{Agree,Mostly Agree},0,ai=Disagree,and the base support as the linear opinion poolu¯=12​(u1+u2).This is the equal-weight linear pool, preserving interpretability (two 10s average to 10) and reflecting the standard practice of combining expert scores via averaging.We then apply a conjunctive penalty to encode corroborated negative evidence. Let 𝟏​[⋅] be the indicator and define the disagreement strength for a judge asdi={5−si5∈[0,1],ai=Disagree,0,otherwise.Intuitively, a Disagree accompanied by si≈5 is weak (di≈0), whereas si≈0 is strong (di≈1). Let Pmax∈[0,5] be a hyperparameter. The final score isConf=clamp(u¯− 1[a1=Disagree∧a2=Disagree]⋅Pmax⋅d1+d22, 0, 10)That is, we subtract a penalty only if both judges disagree, and we scale that penalty by the average strength of their disagreement. When only one judge disagrees, its support is already zero; we do not double-penalise, which improves robustness to single-rater noise.The rule combines two standard ideas: equal-weight linear opinion pooling for supportive evidence and a k-of-n (conjunctive) decision fusion for negative evidence. If a false Disagree occurs with probability α per judge, the chance that both are false is α2, so penalising only the 2-of-2 case reduces the expected false penalty from α to α2 under approximate independence. Empirically, this yields cleaner separation for triage: cases with two emphatic Disagrees are pushed decisively low, while “contested” cases (e.g., 10 vs. 5-Disagree) remain in the middle for human review.
Illustrative outcomes.
With Pmax=3.5:
•(10,Agree) and (5,Disagree) ⇒u¯=5.0, no penalty ⇒Conf=5.0.
•(3,Disagree) and (2,Disagree) ⇒u¯=0.0; mean d=0.5; penalty 1.75 ⇒Conf=0.0 after clamp.
•(5,Disagree) and (5,Disagree) ⇒u¯=0.0; mean d=0; penalty 0 ⇒Conf=0.0.
3.3.Token-Level Confidence via Perplexity
While inter-model agreement provides evidence of semantic consistency, it does not capture the generation certainty of individual summaries. A model may produce a fluent output that agrees with others yet internally exhibit high uncertainty during generation. To address this, we incorporate token-level confidence scores derived from the model’s output probability distribution.
Logit probabilities and perplexity.
Modern LLM APIs support returning log-probabilities for generated tokens when the logprobs parameter is enabled. For each token ti in a generated summary S={t1,t2,…,tn}, the model provides log⁡P⁡(ti∣t<i,C), representing the log-probability of token ti given the preceding context and COBOL input C. We compute the perplexity of a generated summary as(1)PPL(S)=exp(−1n∑i=1nlogP(ti∣t<i,C)).Perplexity measures how “surprised” the model is by its own generation: lower perplexity indicates higher confidence, while higher perplexity suggests the model struggled to predict subsequent tokens. For enterprise applications, perplexity provides a reference-free signal identifying generations where the model exhibited uncertainty—even if the output appears superficially fluent.
Confidence score normalization.
Raw perplexity values are model-specific and domain-dependent. We normalize scores to [0,10] using(2)Confppl​(S)=10×clamp⁡(1−PPL⁡(S)−PPLminPPLmax−PPLmin, 0, 1),where PPLmin and PPLmax are calibrated thresholds from a held-out validation set of COBOL summaries (Figure 2). This yields an interpretable score where 10 indicates maximum certainty and 0 indicates the model was highly uncertain during generation.
Threshold calibration.
Because perplexity is unbounded on [1,∞) and its absolute scale varies across models and domains, raw values are neither directly interpretable nor comparable with the other [0,10] metrics. The thresholds PPLmin and PPLmax anchor the mapping of Equation (2): PPLmin marks the “confident” end (mapped to confidence 10) and PPLmax the “uncertain” end (mapped to confidence 0), with linear interpolation in between and clamping outside. Both are estimated from the perplexity distribution over a held-out set of COBOL summaries, keeping the metric reference-free yet calibrated to the deployment model and corpus.PPLmin=1.2PPLmax=8.50246810Perplexity PPL⁡(S)Confppl​(S)Figure 2.Perplexity-to-confidence normalization (Equation (2)). Summaries with PPL≤PPLmin saturate at maximum score 10; score decreases linearly to 0 at PPLmax and is clamped beyond. The plot shows: constant score of 10 for PPL≤1.2; linear decrease from 10 to 0 over interval [1.2,8.5]; constant score of 0 for PPL≥8.5.

Integration with ensemble scores.
Perplexity complements the inter-model agreement framework:
•A summary with high inter-model agreement and low perplexity (high Confppl) is strongly validated.
•A summary with high inter-model agreement but high perplexity may indicate convergence on a challenging interpretation that warrants additional review.
•A summary with low inter-model agreement and high perplexity clearly signals unreliability.We combine these signals through weighted averaging:(3)Confbase=α⋅Conf+(1−α)⋅Confppl,α∈[0.6,0.8],where Conf is the aggregated confidence and α weights ensemble agreement more heavily (as it captures semantic correctness), while perplexity provides a complementary generation-quality signal.
3.4.Code Coverage Assessment via G-Eval
A critical failure mode unaddressed by pairwise comparison and perplexity is omission: a model may generate a confident, internally consistent summary that simply fails to document significant portions of the input code. Reference-based metrics like BLEU cannot detect omissions without ground-truth coverage annotations. We therefore introduce a coverage-aware metric adapted from G-Eval (Liu et al., 2023)—a framework that uses LLMs as evaluators with chain-of-thought reasoning.
G-Eval for summarization coverage.
Given a COBOL code chunk C and a generated summary S, we prompt an LLM evaluator ℰ to assess coverage:
“You are an expert code reviewer. Given the following COBOL code and its summary, evaluate the code coverage of the summary. Code coverage measures whether the summary accounts for all significant logic: procedure divisions, conditional branches, file I/O operations, data transformations, and control flow. Identify any code segments omitted by the summary. Rate coverage on a scale of 1–5: 5: All significant code paths documented; 4: Minor omissions (e.g., edge cases); 3: Moderate omissions; 2: Significant portions undocumented; 1: Summary misses critical logic. Provide a brief rationale explaining your rating.”The evaluator returns a structured response consisting of a coverage score, identified missing segments, and justification rationale.
Aggregated coverage score.
To ensure robustness, we query the evaluator k times (temperature >0 for diversity) and aggregate:(4)Cov⁡(S,C)=2k​∑i=1kcoverage​_​scorei∈[2,10].We use k=3 for cost-efficiency while achieving stable estimates (empirically, variance stabilizes beyond k=3). Because each run returns an integer rubric score in {1,…,5}, with k=3 the aggregate takes values in {2.0,2.67,…,9.33,10.0}; the factor of 2 rescales the 1–5 scale to [2,10] for consistency with the other confidence metrics, where higher values indicate better coverage.COBOL chunk C   +   summary SG-Eval coverage prompt(1–5 rubric + criteria)Eval run 2Eval run 1Eval run kCov⁡(S,C)=2k​∑i=1kcovi∈[2,10]Conffinal=Confbase×Cov⁡(S,C)10Figure 3.Coverage assessment via G-Eval. The (chunk, summary) pair is scored k times (τ>0) on a 1–5 rubric; scores are averaged and rescaled to [2,10] (Equation (4)), then applied as multiplicative penalty to base confidence (Equation (5)).

Detection of systematic omissions.
Beyond numerical scores, G-Eval’s rationale field enables qualitative analysis. If multiple evaluations identify the same missing segments (e.g., “file error handling not mentioned”), this provides actionable feedback for human reviewers or model fine-tuning.
Why G-Eval over heuristics?
Naive coverage metrics might count lines of code mentioned or perform keyword matching (e.g., checking if all COBOL verbs appear in the summary). However, such heuristics fail to capture semantic coverage: a summary might mention “file operations” without explaining what those operations do. G-Eval’s LLM-based evaluation reasons about semantic ..."

Training Your Service Dog, Part 33: Riding Calmly on a City Bus
Monday, Nov 9, 2026

Part 32 covered the restaurant table. Next up: the city bus, where your dog boards, settles out of the aisle and steps off calmly.
Guide Dogs for the Blind advises waiting a couple of steps back from the curb, since buses pull in close. Board with a short leash and the dog right behind you, then keep the dog's body and tail out of the aisle so no one steps on them.
Start at home. Line up two chairs like a bus bench, cue a wait, sit down, then invite your dog into a tucked down at your feet. Pay with food while the dog is relaxed. Food stays the daily training paycheck.
Then try one short ride on a quiet PSTA route in Pinellas at an off hour. The front seats are reserved for seniors and riders with disabilities, which gives you more floor room. Guide Dogs for the Blind also suggests stepping a few feet away from the bus after exiting so the engine noise fades. Mark calm and pay. Never yell the dog's name. No loud NO. Keep dogs on our schedule.
PSTA also offers free one on one travel training for riders who want help learning the system.
How to measure progress: aim for 8 of 10 calm rides across 2 routes this month, with the dog tucked in a down within a minute of sitting and nothing in the aisle. Here in Tampa Bay, Odin is an 8 1/2 year old golden who started functional tasks at 6 months with Ski.
Watch Dogs of Service from Iowa PBS on YouTube

Sources: Guide Dogs for the Blind travel lecture, Pinellas Suncoast Transit Authority rider guide, photos of Odin by DigitalAssetsUS.

text:
Scientists Engineer Rice That Fights Back Against a Devastating Crop Disease | University & Colin Collins, SciTechDaily

An AI-designed gene-editing tool is opening new possibilities for protecting essential food crops.

An artificial intelligence-designed gene-editing tool has helped scientists develop rice plants resistant to bacterial blight, a destructive disease that threatens harvests across Asia and Africa. Researchers at the University of Missouri achieved the result using a technology previously tested in animal cells, opening a potential new route to protecting one of the world’s most important food crops.

The breakthrough centers on OpenCRISPR-1, a gene-editing system developed by California biotechnology company Profluent. Led by Bing Yang, a Curators’ Distinguished Professor in the College of Agriculture, Food and Natural Resources, the Missouri team adapted the technology for use in rice.

An AI-Designed Tool for Stronger Crops

Gene editing allows scientists to make targeted changes to DNA, including modifications to genes that influence a plant’s vulnerability to disease. By studying how bacterial pathogens interact with rice at the genetic level, researchers can identify opportunities to strengthen the crop’s defenses.

OpenCRISPR-1 also offers an advantage over some existing gene-editing systems: it is freely available for research and commercial crop development.

“Unlike proprietary gene-editing tools that may require licensing agreements for commercial use, OpenCRISPR-1 is open source and free for research and commercialization of crop genome editing,” Yang said. “That accessibility gives researchers and companies greater flexibility to explore new genetic solutions and develop crop varieties with valuable agricultural traits.”

Protecting Rice From a Devastating Disease

Bacterial blight can severely reduce both the quantity and quality of rice harvests. In regions where rice farming supports millions of livelihoods, outbreaks can have serious economic consequences and threaten a vital food supply.

“Bacterial blight can wreak havoc on rice crops, reducing both yield and quality, which creates serious challenges for farmers who depend on the staple grain,” Yang said. “Our lab investigates how bacterial blight interacts with rice at the genetic level — knowledge that helps us identify ways to strengthen the plant’s natural defenses.”

Although the researchers have successfully developed resistant plants, the work remains at the laboratory stage. The next challenge is transferring the findings into commercially grown rice varieties, followed by additional testing, regulatory review, and partnerships with companies capable of bringing the crops to market.

Could the Technology Protect Other Crops?

Farmers may have to wait several years before rice varieties developed through this research become available. Meanwhile, Yang’s team sees potential applications beyond bacterial blight, including improving resistance to other diseases and helping crops withstand environmental stresses.

Corn and soybeans are among the crops that could eventually benefit from similar genetic approaches, although such applications would require further research.

“Our recent breakthrough paves the way to explore genetic solutions to a range of challenges that farmers face across Missouri and nationwide, from devastating plant diseases to drought and extreme temperatures,” Yang, an investigator in the Bond Life Sciences Center, said. “By developing crops that are better equipped to withstand these stresses, we can help farmers protect yields, strengthen agricultural resilience and prepare for an increasingly challenging growing environment.”

text:
I was at The Palestra for Pitt vs. Penn State last night. Here are my main takeaways for each squad:

Pitt: 

1. This is Jeff Capel’s most talented roster since 23-24. The individual talent is VERY apparent, the question is whether or not Capel can get his guys to operate as a unit. Jonathan Powell, A’lahn Sumler, Jalil Bethea and Baye Ndongo are really good players that should be able to combine to create at the VERY least a top-10 ACC team. Oh, and Chase Foster, despite a down game, has the potential to have his name called in the draft at some point. At 6’9, he’s silky, patient, strong and has great mechanics + feel.  

2. Pitt actually trailed for a decent part of the first half and it was almost frustrating to watch because there was such a large gap in talent between the two squads and how severely it felt like they were underperforming — that is early November college basketball to be fair. That being said, Penn State was playing with discipline, taking good shots, getting 50/50 balls and playing as a cohesive unit. Pitt had 5 guys out there playing for seemingly 5 separate teams. 

3. Pitt’s size, or lack thereof, really, will be a huge limiting factor. Outside of Ndongo — who, to be fair, is scary good when he’s locked in — they are in trouble in the front court. Akir Souare is a tall/long body out there but offers next to nothing on the offensive end and isn’t a needle-mover on defense. Off the bench, i actually feel like Mighty is a decent option but has a pretty herky-jerky play style and still kind of needs to grow into his body despite being a senior. All this is to say, if Ndongo, who could very-well wind up on an All-ACC team, gets into foul trouble — like he did last night — Pitt is going to have a very hard time beating good teams. 

4. It’s early in the season which bodes well for the Panthers. Talent-wise, this team can absolutely make an NCAA Tournament. I know it’s early, and it’s crazy to already have a strong opinion like this, but with the construction of this roster, the trajectory and path to success feels relatively clear. Pitt needs to play as ONE and keep Ndongo out of foul trouble best as possible. If they do that, they could be dancing for the first time since 2023. 

Penn State: 

1. I really like Mike Rhoades as a coach but he has been dealt another tough hand. The funds just aren’t not there for the basketball program — which the AD made clear. It’s unfortunate because they could absolutely be competitive, maybe even a bubble-ish team, if Rhoades had access to more resources. That being said, he has a few nice pieces. 

2. Dasonte Bowen is a solid, experienced anchor in the backcourt who plays under control and can score when Penn State needs a bucket. Ivan Juric is REALLY good and will be a problem for a lot of B1G opponents. He gets to the line whenever he wants with his physicality, timing and positioning around the rim — and converts too (9-10 last night). I imagine he will be a hot commodity in the portal after this year. Brant Byers hasn’t connected from deep efficiently yet this year but this feels like inevitable. They need to find more ways to get him open, it felt like every look he got was off of a broken play or individual creation rather than a set. 

3. Penn State’s trajectory and/or path to success is not as clear. One thing was for certain: they do not have the raw talent that Pitt has. And they likely do not have the raw talent that the rest of the B1G has. Penn State’s path to conference wins will be attempting to control the pace and play in the half court while also making the best decision and taking the best shot EVERY TIME. It feels like there will be little room for error with this team. The Nittany Lions may have another long season ahead of them, but one thing they will do is compete.

Good morning, Camarillo!  Warm, dry weather and sunny skies will continue across Ventura County through at least the middle of the week as high pressure maintains a weak offshore wind pattern over Southern California.

Temperatures topped 90° in Camarillo yesterday, coming within just a few degrees of the daily record. We should cool off slightly today, but temperatures will remain well above normal for early November.

Our attention now turns to a developing pattern change later this week. Beginning Thursday, the high-pressure system responsible for our recent warmth will be pushed eastward as low pressure approaches from the Pacific. Whether that system arrives as a sharp trough or develops into a separate, cut-off low remains uncertain, but either way, a cooling trend is expected.

Temperatures will gradually fall heading into the weekend, returning to near-seasonal levels by Saturday before dipping below normal as rain chances begin increasing.

Forecast models are still struggling with the finer details of the approaching storm, particularly its timing and track. Recent guidance has trended toward a slower arrival and a more southerly path, which could limit the potential for heavier rainfall across Ventura County.

At the moment, rain chances sit around 30% to 40% on both Sunday and Monday. Those daily probabilities reflect considerable uncertainty in the storm's timing, rather than suggesting that rain is unlikely throughout the entire period. The overall forecast continues to favor at least some rainfall during that window.

As for amounts, it's still too early to offer reliable estimates. We'll need to see better agreement among the forecast models before putting numbers on the board.

For now, enjoy the sunshine and unseasonably warm afternoons. A much cooler, potentially wetter pattern appears to be taking shape for the weekend and early next week.

Today: Mostly sunny, with a high near 86. North northeast wind 5 to 15 mph.

Tonight: Partly cloudy, with a low around 62. North wind 5 to 10 mph.
