text:
Podcast Summary | Huberman Lab: Overcome Addictions & Obsessions of All Kinds | Dr. Anna Lembke

Overview
Addiction is not simply a chemical or behavioral problem but a disorder of attachment, control, and the brain's reward circuitry. Dr. Anna Lembke argues that severe addiction often becomes an addiction to control itself, where the substance or behavior provides a reliable lever to manage feeling states in a narrowed "world within a world." Recovery therefore requires more than abstinence: it demands restoring homeostasis, confronting consequences, and in many cases a spiritual pivot of radical surrender that acknowledges the limits of will.

Key Themes
- Addiction is defined by the four C's—out-of-control use, compulsive use, craving, and continued use despite consequences—plus tolerance and withdrawal, and it operates through a shared dopamine pathway regardless of the substance or behavior.
- Repeated use enlarges the pain side of the reward balance, lowering the joy set point so people need more just to feel normal; withdrawal symptoms explain why relapse happens even when life is visibly better.
- The modern environment is "drugified," with digital media, gambling, and pornography making everyone more vulnerable; individual agency matters but so do guardrails from governments, schools, and corporations.
- Severe addiction often requires consequences before recovery begins, because the addicted brain minimizes harm; "hitting rock bottom" is the point where denial collapses, and the threshold varies by person.
- Addiction to control underlies much modern distress, including anxiety, self-loathing, and despair among young people; the antidote is surrender rather than more optimization.
- Surrender has a neurobiological correlate: when strategies fail, serotonin-linked and periaqueductal gray mechanisms activate, quieting rigid predictions and creating openness to new ways of being.
- Codependency is its own form of addiction, where people manage others' behavior to regulate their own emotions; letting go often prompts the addicted loved one to seek recovery.
- Restoring healthy experiences of lost control—rites of passage, time off screens, doing things one is bad at—counters a culture of validation, uncertainty avoidance, and constant sharing.

Detailed Summary
Lembke, director of the dual diagnosis addiction clinic at Stanford University School of Medicine, describes addiction as continued compulsive use of a substance or behavior despite harm to self or others. The core markers are the four C's: out-of-control use, compulsive use, craving, and continued use despite consequences, alongside tolerance and withdrawal.

All reinforcing substances and behaviors converge on the same final common pathway, releasing dopamine in the nucleus accumbens. Dopamine is framed as a common currency for addictive potential, with faster and larger release meaning more reinforcement. Rodent data cited show increases above baseline of roughly 55 percent for chocolate, 100 percent for sex, 150 percent for nicotine, and about 1,000 percent for methamphetamine; the general principle is said to hold in humans even though absolute levels are harder to measure.

The mechanism is homeostasis. Pleasure and pain sit on opposite sides of a balance in the reward pathway, and the brain works to restore neutrality after any deviation. Repeated use causes neuro adaptation that enlarges the pain side and lowers the joy set point, so people need more of the substance just to feel normal rather than to get high.

Withdrawal produces universal symptoms—anxiety, irritability, insomnia, depression, and craving—which helps explain relapse even when life is visibly better without the substance. By weeks three to four, about 80 percent of people report starting to feel significantly better. Abstinence is framed as a 30-day experiment rather than a lifetime commitment, since that is on average how long it takes to begin resetting reward pathways.

Treatment aims at restoring homeostasis, either through abstinence long enough for adaptation to reverse or through long-acting medication on the pleasure side, such as buprenorphine or methadone for opioid addiction. The clinical approach begins with a therapeutic alliance and an assessment of motivation and confidence, not an immediate demand to abstain. Patients who have repeatedly failed to quit on their own may be referred to higher levels of care.

Pairs matter clinically. Giving up alcohol and nicotine together can yield better outcomes, and if coffee reliably triggers cigarette craving, both may be temporarily removed. The "whack-a-mole" problem of substituting one addiction for another is acknowledged as common.

Digital and social media addiction is framed as a collective problem rather than purely individual. In some adolescent clinic referrals, about half are now for digital media addiction in some form. Opting out is hard when social life and connection are mediated by the same platforms, so individual agency must be paired with top-down guardrails. The "enshittification" of technology is cited: products first add value, then are engineered to exploit value from users as companies profit. Awareness of harms has grown, yet the medium has become even more compulsively reinforcing.

Recovery is more than abstinence. Someone can be abstinent yet still enact narcissistic pathology and not be in recovery. The 12-step view holds that without a values-based life, abstinence alone is a dry drunk, and the aspiration is to escape the addiction vortex rather than swap one addiction for another. The modern environment, with more access to gambling, pornography, and social media, is called the modern plague; with more leisure and disposable income ahead, the question becomes what people do with themselves.

Consequences are often the gateway to recovery because the addicted brain is masterful at minimizing or denying them. Hitting rock bottom is where denial collapses, and the threshold varies—"high bottoms" and "low bottoms." A rat trained to press a lever for cocaine will press to exhaustion; when the drug is removed the behavior extinguishes, but after a painful foot shock the rat returns to lever-pressing, suggesting stress can reactivate dormant addiction networks.

Childhood trauma is a significant risk factor but not the sole cause; genetic and access risk factors matter, and addiction does not discriminate. Having a biological parent or grandparent with alcohol use disorder raises risk even without being raised in an alcohol-using home, and simply having access to a drug increases the likelihood of use, brain change, and addiction. Lembke argues that digging for the "reason" behind addiction is unproductive initially; trauma work should come after early recovery, homeostasis, and prefrontal function return. Victim narratives are described as unproductive, while 12-step character inventory forces examination of what a person contributed, even if only repeating maladaptive childhood patterns.

In severe cases, the attachment may be to control rather than the substance. The addictive behavior creates a simplified world within a world where a single reliable lever changes how one feels. Humans evolved to reduce uncertainty and assert control, but modern life offers so many levers that people become addicted to control itself—optimizing relationships, careers, looks, steps, sleep, and calories. Clinically, young people appear highly anxious and self-loathing, driven by fear of choosing wrong, FOMO, and the belief that they must engineer a perfect life.

Gambling is cited as addiction to the game, not money, which explains loss chasing: gamblers partly want to lose to justify staying in the game longer. As addiction progresses, the drug stops working and may make the person feel worse, but it still provides a sense of control.

The proposed antidote is a spiritual pivot: radical surrender, acknowledging the limits of control, and merging with life as it unfolds rather than engineering future perfection. A key tension is that reducing uncertainty was adaptive in a chaotic world but becomes maladaptive in a paved-over, controlled world. When control removes uncertainty, people may engineer it through social media, slot machines, and sports betting.

Spirituality and control may be opposing networks: the control network can inhibit the spirituality network, so surrender requires shutting down control. A neuroimaging example: prefrontal control centers light up when the Pac-Man enemy is far away, while the periaqueductal gray lights up when the Pac-Man is about to die. Lesion studies reportedly show spirituality is a circuit with the PAG as a probable hub. The PAG is rich in mu-opioid receptors and oxytocin receptors, and activating these stimulates serotonin receptors important for neuroplasticity.

Dopamine and serotonin are framed as opposites: dopamine drives "get more of it," while serotonin signals retreat, re-evaluation, and finding a new way when existing strategies fail. Repeated frustration and inability to predict or solve problems are associated with proliferation of 5HT2A serotonin receptors—the brain preparing for a transformative moment when mental maps fail.

Surrender quiets executive function and planning, activating serotonin and down-regulating rigid precision predictions. Lembke questions whether the potency of surrender comes from adopting an external rule system in place of one's own failed strategizing. Surrender narrows scope: letting all balls drop, doing the next right thing, taking it one day at a time. The 12-step idea of giving it over to God is linked to acknowledging the limits of control and rightsizing the ego.

Psilocybin's main plasticity mechanism engages the serotonergic pathway and these receptors; SSRIs and psilocybin both increase serotonin tone, and SSRI work reopened critical-period plasticity in rat studies. Lembke voices reservations about psychedelics: risks, unpredictability, and misuse seen in clinic, including psilocybin. Psychedelic use is no easy ride and requires therapy before, during, and after; it may help some and be the worst option for others. Early claims of low harm were attributed to low usage rates, and a published paper found emergency department visits and hospitalizations from hallucinogens rise as use rises, with reported harms including psychosis, suicide, persistent hallucinosis, and severe mood effects.

Lembke describes being addicted to control, achievement, and optimization before her son's diagnosis with and death from leukemia. Many hours of psychotherapy and reading every paper on the relevant translocation and congenital leukemia felt empty. The pivot came from acknowledging "I'm not in control," surrendering attempts to overmanage, and showing up for life—profoundly spiritual but also physiologic, like her brain got reset. The book is described as the first time she has written publicly about her son's death.

Many Stanford faculty spoke of secret spiritual lives, reluctant to admit them in scientific circles, and many patients are never asked about spirituality despite it being core to handling mental illness. Great scientists historically had faith at the core of their science; the spirit of science is open curiosity, which overlaps with spiritual surrender. A William James analogy compares humans to dogs and cats in a library—seeing books without understanding them. A Stoic idea is cited: to live in accordance with God, live in accordance with nature; to live in accordance with nature, pursue virtue—values largely absent from psychotherapy. Acceptance and commitment therapy addresses acceptance and values-based living in secular terms.

Fear of death and lack of control may be at the root of addictions; avoidance makes existential fear worse, while confronting it reduces suffering. The modern crisis is framed as a crisis of the will: even minor uncertainty triggers crisis because of over-reliance on control, and the narcissistic defense is rage, denial, and doubling down. Prayer is recommended even without belief—defined as admitting limits of control and asking for help outside oneself. Positive change accumulates through doing the next right thing daily, stringing good days into weeks, months, and years.

Codependency is described as its own form of addiction, where people try to control others' behavior and use others to manage their own emotions. It originated in early Alcoholics Anonymous in the 1930s, when wives of AA members formed meetings that became Al-Anon, and it appears today in many forms including Codependents Anonymous. The old stereotype of the enabling partner is described as inaccurate and outdated. The rope metaphor applies: pulling on opposite ends of the same rope gets nowhere, while dropping one end prompts the other person to drop theirs and seek recovery. Clinically, when the codependent person lets go and focuses on self-care, the addicted loved one often moves into recovery, described as happening like clockwork.

A recovery saying holds that when the addict gets sober, the sick get angry—family members may become angry because their codependency no longer has a place to go. When one person's substance use is kept in check by another's addiction, the sobering person's improvement can allow the other's disorder to blossom. Mind-reading others' thoughts is presented as a major relational error; assuming you know what someone feels is a disaster. Monitoring technology intensifies reactivity—checking a dog camera on vacation created anxious checking, and the conclusion was that it is better not to know.

Winnicott's good enough mother is invoked: initially meeting every need, then gradually restraining herself so the child can differentiate and act autonomously. Parenting benefits from surrender—accepting children have their own lives and decisions, and only bearing witness or helping when asked. Rites of passage are described as healthy experiences of giving up control, since participants do not decide when a ritual starts or ends, teaching young people they can survive loss of control.

Digital life is argued to have shaped a generation's reward circuitry around validation and scrolling, reducing tolerance for uncertainty and imperfection, partly because search and AI hold out the promise of an exact right answer if you keep looking. Suggested practices include spending part of every day off screens, going outside, looking at the sky, talking to a human, making a mistake and apologizing, and doing something you are bad at. Examples of offline gathering include Gen Zers playing music together without aiming to become pop stars, and people in South Korea meeting to crochet. Dating apps are criticized for fostering a "maybe there's somebody better" mindset; the alternative offered is openness to a person who does not fit one's checklist.

On faith, a colleague is cited for the idea that language lacks a verb for "faithing" and that there is a tradition of faith without belief or with enormous doubt. Faith is distinguished from belief: one can have faith with doubt, and prayer can be an affective practice of humble surrender that does not require belief. Evidence is cited that praying for others changes one's mindset and promotes pro-social behavior. Serotonin and spirituality are linked: persevering in doing the right thing without getting the needed response is a type of suffering that leads to proliferation of serotonin receptors, laying the foundation for letting go of rigid models and being open to something new.

ET randomly listed 5 of 16 qualified bidders, not the final 5.

Domestic tech still lacks proven continuous low-defect sintered production, mainly jet milling, alignment, GBD. Ashvini has BARC's upstream TOT; and while MAM/Midwest has NFTDC's TOT of molten-salt electrolysis, the mid/downstream is largely blueprint. MAM is progressing but 500TPA to 1200MTPA scale up won't be easy, while also maintaining yield for EV grade. ARCI/DMRL offer pilot-scale process till sintering & magnetic alignment but lack commercial viability. Def R&D labs operate under a cost-is-no-bar, low-volume framework.

Only Proterial & NEO bring proven process. SIs & big balance-sheet bidders will run hybrids — local upstream/process + imported IP/equip for the hard steps.

GOOGLE $GOOGL EXPANDS ITS AI CHIP LINEUP WITH AMD $AMD. THE BATTLE FOR AI COMPUTE IS BECOMING MORE SPECIALISED.
I've been following Google's TPU strategy closely, and this latest development reinforces why I'm bullish on Alphabet's long-term AI infrastructure opportunity.
Google is introducing two new TPU variants, 8tx and 8i Max, designed to address different requirements as AI workloads become more complex.
WHAT'S CHANGING
🔹 TPU 8tx: Combines Google's AI accelerators with AMD EPYC CPUs to support confidential computing and protect sensitive AI workloads.
🔹 TPU 8i Max: Combines two TPU chips in one package, increasing memory capacity and computing resources for long-context AI applications.
🔹 Target Applications: AI agents, coding, scientific research, drug discovery and regulated industries.
🔹 Availability: The new variants are expected to become available in 2027.
WHY THIS MATTERS
The AI semiconductor market is moving beyond a competition over raw processing power.
Memory bandwidth, power efficiency, security and the cost of running increasingly complex AI models are becoming just as important.
For Google, custom TPUs offer an opportunity to improve the economics of Google Cloud while reducing dependence on third-party accelerators.
For AMD, the collaboration demonstrates that its EPYC CPUs can benefit from AI infrastructure growth even when customers choose custom accelerators rather than AMD GPUs.
And for NVIDIA, it reinforces the growing competitive pressure from hyperscaler-designed silicon.
MY TAKE
I'm bullish on $GOOGL and $AMD, and I see this as another important development in the AI infrastructure buildout.
But I wouldn't interpret it as an immediate threat to NVIDIA's dominance.
NVIDIA still benefits from its software ecosystem, networking capabilities and broad customer adoption.
The bigger opportunity for Google is turning its custom silicon advantage into stronger cloud margins, higher utilisation and sustainable free cash flow.
The next phase of AI infrastructure won't be won by processing power alone. It will increasingly come down to performance per dollar, memory efficiency, energy consumption and the economics of running AI at scale.

text:
When someone in Japan tells a couple お二人とも、仲睦まじいですね (you two are so close), it is pure praise, but look at the middle kanji, 睦 (mutsu): its left half is an eye, 目, sitting inside a word for getting along.

The first recorded use of that kanji, as it turns out, was on a hunting scorecard.

Sunday breakfast, a couple married for thirty years. He gives her one glance and she silently slides the soy sauce across the table. Now try that same look three days into a marriage. She panics: "What? Are you mad at me?" Eye-talk skill: level 1.

The debut of 睦 is bizarre. On Shang oracle bones from over 3,000 years ago, it had nothing to do with harmony. It was the name of a royal hunting ground. One specific bone lists the day's carnage: eleven foxes, four deer and five fawns.

Kiko our fox has been warned to stay far away.

Take it apart. The eye 目 carries the meaning. The right half 坴 (riku) is there for sound only, though its oldest forms depicted hands next to a crop. You have already seen this part.

Add the hill radical 阝 and you get 陸 (riku), land, as in 着陸 (chakuriku), touchdown, and 大陸 (tairiku), continent. Old account books even wrote 陸 instead of 六, six, because a plain 六 is too easy to forge with a few extra strokes. Anti-fraud tech.

In modern life you encounter 睦 in 親睦会 (shinbokukai), the party at work or in a club that is designed for bonding. In reality, this means two hours of the boss doing karaoke. You also find it in 睦月 (mutsuki), the old name for January, and BanG Dream!

fans know it from 若葉睦, Mutsumi Wakaba.

So why the eye? The 六書故, a Chinese dictionary from over 700 years ago, offers an explanation: joy and anger always show on your face, in your eyes. That is why getting along is written 睦 and being at odds is written 睽 (kei), both featuring the eye on the left.

Even in its oldest form, the eye represents a gentle, friendly look. Japanese even has a proverb for this: 目は口ほどに物を言う, meaning the eyes say as much as the mouth. After thirty years of marriage, you get soy sauce by eye. After three days, you get a screaming match by eye.

That is not 睦. That is 睽.

text:
The 2026 midterm election results have been hailed across bourgeois media as a sweeping triumph for the Democratic establishment. Wall Street networks and corporate outlets like CBS New York and MS NOW celebrate a historic political realignment, broadcasting glowing segments on Representative Hakeem Jeffries’ ascent toward becoming the first Black Speaker of the House and Senator Chuck Schumer’s reclaim of the Senate Majority Leader’s gavel.

Yet beneath the triumphalist liberal theater of a "Blue Wave" lies a fundamental contradiction that exposes the rotting core of the two-party dictatorship. Millions of working-class voters turned out not out of devotion to the Democratic Party leadership, but to deliver a scathing repudiation of economic brutality and authoritarian escalation. However, the reward offered by the Democratic apparatus is not structural transformation or a pivot toward human liberation; it is the continued rule of two Brooklyn machine politicians whose loyalty belongs entirely to Wall Street capital, private equity trade groups, and the military-industrial apparatus powering the Israeli settler-colonial project.

For anti-capitalists, anti-imperialists, and anti-Zionists, the post-election maneuverings offer an essential lesson in state power: the Democratic Party is not an instrument for reform, but a protective shield for elite consensus, designed explicitly to blunt popular demands and safeguard the empire.

The Wall Street and AIPAC Mandate
To understand why the Democratic establishment remains immune to popular outrage, one must look directly at the economic and geopolitical interests Jeffries and Schumer represent. Their elevation is not a reflection of democratic will, but the logical outcome of a political system driven by oligarchic capital.

As detailed by independent media analyses on Breakthrough News, both Jeffries and Schumer serve as the chief legislative custodians for two primary power centers: the private equity class and the Zionist lobby. Far from opposing the expansion of corporate power, Schumer’s Capitol Hill apparatus has long functioned as a revolving door for private equity giants like Blackstone and Apollo. Jeffries’ leadership campaign, meanwhile, was underwritten by venture capitalists, executives from defense-tech monopolies like Palantir and Anduril, and massive injections of capital from AIPAC.

This financial backing dictates their legislative trajectory. When the working class demands universal healthcare, functional public infrastructure, inflation relief, and an end to billionaire tax exemptions, the leadership responds with technocratic corporate giveaways.

Simultaneously, their commitment to foreign imperialism remains absolute. Both leaders joined hands across the aisle to invite Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to address a joint session of Congress, providing dozens of standing ovations while funding the systematic destruction of Gaza. As highlighted by international reporting on Indisputable, this bipartisan consensus demonstrates that no matter how drastically public opinion shifts against imperialism—with vast majorities of the Democratic base rejecting unconditional aid to Israel—the party apparatus remains structural security for military-industrial capital.

Mass Rejection and the Illusion of Reform
The grassroots response to this entrenched leadership has been immediate and fierce. Following the midterms, an online petition demanding that incoming House Democrats reject Jeffries for Speaker surged past half a million signatures, eventually climbing past one million signatories as high-profile figures waded into the debate.

Yet the establishment’s response to this mass petition drive demonstrates their total contempt for rank-and-file dissent. On popular independent media outlets like The Jimmy Dore Show, commentators have pointed out the grotesque comedy of liberal voters expecting corporate-funded leadership to voluntarily step down simply because millions of working-class people demand it:

"The idea that Chuck Schumer or Hakeem Jeffries gives a single damn about a million signatures on a petition shows how deep the liberal delusion goes. They don't work for voters; they work for their donors. You can sign all the petitions you want, but until you threaten their actual control over capital and state power, they will just laugh their way to the podium."
This sentiment echoes across the left media ecosystem. On Due Dissidence, analysts dissected how the Democratic leadership leverages identity politics to sanitize imperialist violence and corporate governance:

"Jeffries taking the gavel is celebrated by corporate media as historic progress, but for the working class and the victims of U.S. foreign policy, it’s just a new face on the same old empire. They use representation as a cloak for austerity and war, expecting the left to fall in line out of political exhaustion."
While MS NOW and traditional outlets emphasize Jeffries' promises of "affordability" and legislative oversight, their coverage deliberately obscures the reality of governance under capitalist hegemony. "Affordability" within a neoliberal framework means protecting private profit margins while offering workers marginal scraps. Oversight within a bipartisan imperial frame means holding hearings for televised spectacle while quietly passing multi-billion-dollar military budgets.

Why the Democratic Party Will Never Yield
The delusion persistent among progressive reformers is that the Democratic Party can be captured from within through incremental electoral pressure or moral appeals. But the post-election consolidation of power by Jeffries and Schumer reveals a structural reality: the Democratic Party is functioning precisely as it was engineered to perform.

Its primary role in American political life is to serve as a graveyard for social movements. When populist anger erupts against conservative reaction or economic collapse, the Democratic machine captures that energy, channels it into vote extraction, and neutralizes it within committee rooms co-chaired by private equity lobbyists.

text:
Agilix Labs Receives AWS Grant for Sierra Leone’s Finder Program

Agilix Labs has received support through the AWS Education Equity Initiative for Sierra Leone’s Finder Program, bringing AI and cloud technology into the program’s work. The announcement identifies the grant’s purpose but gives no monetary value, so its size cannot be compared with other funding. It describes support for an existing program rather than setting out a separate initiative. The grant connects Agilix Labs, the program’s operator, and AWS services in the learners’ work. The Future Learning Institute, or FLI, runs Finder. Agilix Labs established FLI in 2025 under an agreement with Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Technical and Higher Education. The institute’s role is to train young Sierra Leoneans to become Finders. The grant therefore supports work carried out through an institute created by Agilix Labs under that government agreement. The program’s central idea is to prepare young people to respond to questions raised in their communities. A Finder is someone local people approach for answers, and the role combines AI-assisted checking with personal judgment before practical guidance is returned. This definition makes clear that the technology is part of a human process, not the sole source of an answer. The grant supports the AI and cloud elements of that work. The program is structured around a year of learning and applied work. During that period, participants use AI to address questions from local businesses and community groups. Those tasks give the training a community-facing focus, while the Finder role describes how answers are checked and shared. The available information does not state how many learners participate or how many questions they handle.

The grant changes where the learners’ AI work is to run: it is slated to use AWS through Amazon Bedrock. That describes the cloud service intended for the AI work, not a reported change to the lessons themselves. Lessons use Agilix Dawn, a platform that keeps functioning if an internet connection is interrupted. The two tools therefore have distinct stated roles: Dawn supports lessons, while Bedrock is where the AI work is to run. The information does not say that every part of the program requires a continuous internet connection. It says specifically that Dawn continues working when the signal drops, which matters in settings where connectivity is unreliable. No further details are supplied about how learners connect to Bedrock or what happens to AI tasks during an outage. The grant’s stated technical effect should therefore be limited to running learners’ AI work on AWS through Bedrock. The intended participants include young people in Sierra Leone who earned university eligibility but were unable to secure a place. The program also names young women, learners with disabilities, and people from rural communities or low-income households among those it is intended to serve. These categories describe the program’s intended reach, not a count of enrolled participants. No figures are provided for how many people in any group have joined. The learners’ work is tied to requests from businesses and community groups, while the Finder definition emphasizes answering questions from the surrounding community. Together, those details describe the kinds of people the program aims to serve and the practical nature of the tasks. They do not establish how many organizations submit questions or how the quality of answers is measured. The stated unit of learning is a year-long program, not a reported number of completed tasks.

The program has developed through centers in Kono and Freetown. Mustapha Turay, president of FLI Centers in Sierra Leone, said the work began in Kono and that the capital now has a center of its own. FLI’s Kono District center opened in March 2026. A separate center at Freetown Polytechnic was scheduled to open in November 2026. The Freetown Polytechnic center was also set for a formal launch of the Finder Program on Nov. 10. The announcement places that launch and the center opening on the same scheduled date, but it does not establish that either event had already taken place. This distinction matters because the stated dates describe plans, while the Kono center is reported as having opened. The two locations therefore have different statuses in the account. The planned Freetown center is FLI’s second Community Learning Center, according to the announcement of the scheduled launch. The separate description of the centers identifies Kono as the first location in the program’s reported expansion and Freetown as a new center. No details are given about the facilities’ capacity, staffing, or the number of learners at either site. The center count describes locations, not participants or outcomes. Turay also spoke about young people’s knowledge of their communities and described returning home with an education gained in the United States. His account links the program’s local focus to the experience of its leadership, without supplying figures on staff or learner backgrounds. The role of local judgment in the Finder process is consistent with that emphasis on community knowledge. The announcement does not say that every learner has the same educational experience as Turay.

Agilix Labs co-founder, chairman and chief executive Curt Allen described FLI as an effort to help young people find jobs, beginning with those prepared to learn but lacking a place to do so. That explanation connects the institute’s purpose to the access barriers identified among the intended learners. It does not report how many participants have found work or whether job placement is guaranteed. The program details instead describe a year of learning and community-directed AI tasks. Allen also said that learners at the centers use AI in service of their communities and are being trained for Finder work. This account places the technology inside a community task rather than presenting AI use as an end in itself. It aligns with the program’s description of practical answers checked with local judgment. No outcome data are given to show the effect of that work on learners or the people who submit questions. The program’s intended beneficiaries include both learners seeking an opportunity after qualifying for university and the local groups whose questions they answer. Businesses and community organizations are specifically named as sources of those questions. That gives the training a defined service context, but the available facts do not quantify demand or describe how requests are selected. It also provides no measure of whether the work leads to employment. The announcement thus offers descriptions of purpose, participants, tools, and planned locations, but not a numerical evaluation of the program. It does not state the grant amount, enrollment, completion, employment results, or a count of answered questions. The reported opening dates and the year-long duration are operational details, not evidence of outcomes. Readers can distinguish those stated plans and structures from results that have not been reported.

Based in Lehi, Utah, Agilix Labs is an education technology company. Its Buzz platform has supported more than 55 million course enrollments, and its users span more than 200 countries and territories. Those figures describe Buzz’s reach, not participation in the Finder Program. They provide company context without showing how many people in Sierra Leone use Agilix products. The enrollment total counts course enrollments, rather than a stated number of unique individuals. The geographic measure counts countries and territories where Buzz has users, not learners at FLI centers. Neither figure measures the grant’s value, the reach of the Finder Program, or its results. Keeping those measures separate avoids treating the company’s wider platform history as evidence about this particular program. The grant announcement brings together Agilix’s education technology role and FLI’s local training model. Its specific technical commitment is that learners’ AI work is to use AWS through Amazon Bedrock, while lessons continue to use Dawn. The program’s stated design combines AI with community knowledge and judgment, over a year of work on questions from local groups and businesses. The facts establish that structure and intent, but do not report measured effects. The planned Freetown Polytechnic opening and formal launch were set for Nov. 10, following the reported opening of the Kono District center in March 2026. The account identifies the people the program seeks to reach and the kinds of questions learners are expected to answer. It also names the services intended for lessons and AI work, without specifying the grant’s amount. The clearest reported change is therefore support for the program’s AI and cloud work, alongside its ongoing training and center plans.

text:
You misunderstand Christianity.  The Altar and Satisfaction in the New Covenant are Superabundant and Eternal.

It’s not a “past event” that merely passes away but Infinite and Eternal.

(1) Magisterium

1992 CCC 1085

In the liturgy of the Church, it is principally his own Paschal mystery that Christ signifies and makes present. During his earthly life Jesus announced his Paschal mystery by his teaching and anticipated it by his actions. When his Hour comes, he lives out the unique event of history which does not pass away: Jesus dies, is buried, rises from the dead, and is seated at the right hand of the Father "once for all."

His Paschal mystery is a real event that occurred in our history, but it is unique: all other historical events happen once, and then they pass away, swallowed up in the past. the Paschal mystery of Christ, by contrast, cannot remain only in the past, because by his death he destroyed death, and all that Christ is - all that he did and suffered for all men - participates in the divine eternity, and so transcends all times while being made present in them all. the event of the Cross and Resurrection abides and draws everything toward life. . . . from the time of the Church of the Apostles . . .

(2) Scripture

Hebrews 9:11-15 “But when Christ came as high priest of the good things that have come to be,[j] passing through the greater and more perfect tabernacle not made by hands, that is, not belonging to this creation, he entered once for all into the sanctuary, not with the blood of goats and calves but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption. For if the blood of goats and bulls and the sprinkling of a heifer’s ashes[k] can sanctify those who are defiled so that their flesh is cleansed, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal spirit offered himself unblemished to God, cleanse our consciences from dead works to worship the living God.  For this reason he is mediator of a new covenant: since a death has taken place for deliverance from transgressions under the first covenant, those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance.”

Hebrews 9:24-26 “For Christ did not enter into a sanctuary made by hands, a copy of the true one, but heaven itself, that he might now appear before God on our behalf. 25 Not that he might offer himself repeatedly, as the high priest enters each year into the sanctuary with blood that is not his own; 26 if that were so, he would have had to suffer repeatedly from the foundation of the world. But now once for all he has appeared at the end of the ages[s] to take away sin by his sacrifice.

Romans 12:1-2 “I urge you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your spiritual worship. 2 Do not conform yourselves to this age but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, that you may discern what is the will of God, what is good and pleasing and perfect.”

Hebrews 10:11-14 “Every priest stands daily at his ministry, offering frequently those same sacrifices that can never take away sins. But this one offered one sacrifice for sins, and took his seat forever at the right hand of God; [f]now he waits until his enemies are made his footstool.  For by one offering he has made perfect forever those who are being consecrated.”

text:
We are familiar with the idiom "Its a dog's life". It means a very hard, unpleasant, or miserable existence filled with constant work, struggle and even mistreatment.

Not so, at least for the dogs in Nepal..🐕😍

Nepal has a very heartwarming and amusing tradition of honoring dogs during the 'Kukur Tihar'. It is a special festival dedicated to thanking dogs for their loyalty, protection, and companionship.
It was celebrated on 8th November.

In Hinduism, dogs (shvana) are deeply revered as sacred companions, divine messengers, guardians of the realms, and symbols of loyalty, dharma (righteousness), and detachment

The roots of the tradition trace back to the epic Mahabharata, where Yudhishthira refuses to enter heaven without his faithful dog.

Dogs are seen as close companions of three very significant divine manifestations:

🔴Kal Bhairava: The dog (Shvan) is the sacred vahana (vehicle/mount) of Kal Bhairava, the fierce, time-governing manifestation of Lord Shiva

🟠Dattatreya: The syncretic sage-god Dattatreya (an avatar combining Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva) is frequently depicted accompanied by four dogs symbolizing the four Vedas (Rig, Yajur, Sama, Atharva),

⚫️Yama's Watchdogs: Yama, the God of Death, is described as owning two four-eyed watchdogs who guard the gates of the netherworld/afterlife, tracking souls and ensuring cosmic order

Kukur Tihar is celebrated by...

🐕..Draping the dogs with bright, colorful marigold flower garlands around their necks as a sign of respect and blessing

🐕..Applying a 'Red Sacred Tika', which is a mark made of vermilion powder, rice, and yogurt is applied to the dog's forehead to honor them.

🐕..Offering them feasts and treats. Dogs are offered rich traditional meals, meat, milk, eggs, and specialized treats.

text:
How to Market Your Online Business Successfully in Nigeria: A Practical, Long-Term Guide
Marketing an online business in Nigeria is not about posting randomly and hoping for the best. It is about showing up consistently where your customers already spend their time, building trust quickly, and making it easy for them to buy from you. With more than 100 million internet users and WhatsApp on the majority of smartphones, the opportunity is real—but so is the competition. The businesses that grow are the ones that treat marketing as a daily system, not a one-off activity.
Here’s a clear, practical breakdown of what actually works for online sellers and small businesses in Nigeria right now.
Start by Knowing Exactly Who You’re Talking To
Before you create any content or run any promotion, get specific about your customer. “Everyone” is not a target. Think about their daily life: Where do they live? What time do they usually check their phone? What problem are they trying to solve when they look for your product? How much can they comfortably spend?
For example, if you sell food items like garri, rice, or household groceries online, your customer might be a busy working parent in Lagos or Abuja who wants quality products delivered without the stress of market runs. They care about freshness, clear pricing, reliable delivery, and proof that other people have bought from you successfully. Speak directly to that person in everything you post.
The clearer you are about this, the easier every other part of marketing becomes.
WhatsApp Is Still the Most Powerful Sales Tool You Have
In Nigeria, many purchases start on Instagram or TikTok but finish on WhatsApp. People trust the chat more than a website checkout in many cases. Set up WhatsApp Business (not the regular app) and use it properly:
•Complete your business profile with your name, what you sell, location or delivery areas, and a clear description.
•Use the catalogue feature so customers can browse products and prices inside the chat.
•Post on your Status daily or every other day. Show real products, packing process, customer feedback, and current prices. Status only reaches people who have saved your number, so it is a warm audience.
•Reply fast. Nigerian buyers often message several sellers at once. The first clear, professional response usually wins the sale. Always state the price confidently and add any current offer or delivery information.
Build your broadcast list carefully. Only message people who have chosen to hear from you (customers who bought before, people who messaged you first, or those who scanned a QR code or clicked a link you shared). Mix useful updates with promotions. Too many hard-sell messages and people will start ignoring or blocking you. A good mix is tips or behind-the-scenes content, customer testimonials, and occasional offers.
Social Media: Show the Product, Build Familiarity
Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook remain strong for discovery. Short videos perform better than static photos in most cases. You do not need expensive equipment. Use your phone, natural light, and show the product in real life.
What to post regularly:
•Clear product photos or short videos with the price and key details in the caption.
•Unboxing or packing videos so people see how carefully you handle orders.
•Customer testimonials (screenshots of chats with permission, or short video reviews).
•Simple tips related to your product (for example, how to store garri properly, quick meal ideas, or how to choose quality items).
•Behind-the-scenes of your process.
Post consistently. Many successful Nigerian sellers post almost every day during peak times (roughly 7–9am, 12–2pm, and 7–10pm). Quality matters, but showing up regularly matters more. Use relevant hashtags and always include a clear next step: “Send a DM”, “Click the WhatsApp link in bio”, or “Reply for current price and delivery”.

text:
Kheel Batasha..

Why Kheel? for those who do not know this name, this is Laja.. puffed paddy actually.

Take a raw paddy seed & put it in the soil.. it will grow again.

In Vedanta, a raw seed represents Vasanas & pending karma.. the seeds which still have the capacity to fructify and create another cycle

But when that same paddy touches agni, it bursts open & becomes white kheel.

If you sow Kheel in the ground, it never sprouts again.. yet it becomes light and nourishing.

This is the old <Dagdha Bija> principle.. the burnt seed.

Laja itself is not an ordinary grain. We even have the Laja Homa, where puffed paddy is offered into Agni.

Diwali comes around the paddy harvest and traditionally Kheel was made from the new crop & offered before we consumed it ourselves.

Astrologically also, Rice carries a strong Moon connection.. while Kheel brings in Dhanya & abundance and Batasha brings sweetness & rasa.. both naturally connecting with Lakshmi and Venus tattva.

Batasha is sweetness and rasa.. very venus.. Batasha too comes to the puja thali only after passing through agni.

So Kheel-Batasha carries three things together.. Dhanya, Agni Samskara and Samriddhi.

In fact, one should offer Kheel-Batasha to Maa Lakshmi every Friday, if possible.. as naivedya.

text:
Scientists Say This Medication Could Be the Next “Wonder Drug” | Michigan Medicine - University of Michigan, SciTechDaily

A diabetes medication may protect against heart attacks and strokes through an unexpected biological mechanism.

Two medications used in people with type 2 diabetes produced dramatically different results when scientists tested their ability to prevent dangerous blood clots. In mice with injured blood vessels, sotagliflozin reduced clot formation by approximately 60%, compared with just 5% to 10% for the widely prescribed drug empagliflozin.

Researchers at Michigan Medicine also found that sotagliflozin suppresses excessive platelet activity, a process that can block blood flow to the heart or brain. Published in the Journal of Clinical Investigation, the findings suggest a possible explanation for the drug’s ability to reduce heart attack and stroke risk beyond its effects on blood sugar.

Why Sotagliflozin Works Differently

Sotagliflozin, marketed as Inpefa, belongs to a group of medications called sodium-glucose cotransporter (SGLT) inhibitors. These drugs interfere with proteins that transport glucose through the body. Common treatments such as empagliflozin (Jardiance) and dapagliflozin (Farxiga) primarily block SGLT2, a protein that helps the kidneys reabsorb glucose. Sotagliflozin acts on both SGLT2 and SGLT1, which is also present in other tissues.

Although SGLT2 inhibitors have established cardiovascular benefits, clinical trials have shown that sotagliflozin can also reduce ischemic events, including heart attacks and strokes. These occur when blood clots or other blockages restrict circulation. The researchers investigated whether the drug’s broader action on glucose transport proteins might help explain this protection.

“A drug that can both decrease the risk for diabetes along with the risk for having a heart attack or stroke could be a turning point in our ability safely treat this growing population in the US and abroad,” said Michael A. Holinstat, Ph.D., M.S., co-senior author and professor of pharmacology, internal medicine, and surgery at the University of Michigan Medical School.

A Powerful Effect on Blood Platelets

Scientists compared sotagliflozin and empagliflozin using blood samples from healthy volunteers and people with type 2 diabetes. Sotagliflozin significantly reduced platelet activation and made platelets less likely to clump together. Empagliflozin produced little or no comparable effect.

Platelets normally help stop bleeding by gathering at damaged blood vessels. However, excessive activation can produce clots inside arteries, potentially triggering a heart attack or stroke. Sotagliflozin’s ability to suppress this activity may contribute to its cardiovascular benefits.

“These experiments showed that sotagliflozin has a unique effect, and blocking SGLT2 alone is not enough to inhibit platelet aggregation,” said Eugene Chen, M.D., Ph.D., co-senior author and Frederick G. L. Huetwell Professor of Cardiovascular Medicine at the University of Michigan Medical School.

“Sotagliflozin may offer additional protection against blood clots, potentially lowering the risk of heart attack and stroke.”

Blocking SGLT1 Explains Only Part of the Effect

The researchers next investigated whether inhibiting SGLT1 alone could account for sotagliflozin’s effects. When they genetically removed SGLT1 from mouse platelets, blood clot formation decreased by approximately 40%. However, neither this genetic approach nor treatment with mizagliflozin, a drug that selectively blocks SGLT1, fully reproduced sotagliflozin’s results.

This suggests that other biological mechanisms contribute to the drug’s ability to prevent clot formation. One possibility involves SGLT1 in endothelial cells, which form the inner lining of blood vessels and interact with circulating platelets. Researchers have not yet established whether these cells contribute to sotagliflozin’s anti-clotting effects.

“Sotagliflozin appears to be in the sweet spot because compounds that have higher levels of SGLT1-selective inhibitors can cause gastrointestinal issues,” said Bertram Pitt, M.D., co-author and professor emeritus of internal medicine at the University of Michigan Medical School.

“We think this could be a wonder drug with potential to offer benefit for many conditions.”

Could the Benefits Extend Beyond Diabetes?

Sotagliflozin is FDA-approved to reduce certain cardiovascular risks in adults with heart failure and in adults with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease, and additional cardiovascular risk factors. The researchers hope to investigate whether its effects on clotting could benefit patients with other conditions, including chronic kidney disease and atrial fibrillation, an irregular heart rhythm associated with increased stroke risk.

The laboratory and animal findings provide evidence that sotagliflozin affects clotting through mechanisms beyond conventional SGLT2 inhibition. However, further clinical research is needed to determine how much this platelet effect contributes to preventing cardiovascular events in humans and whether it can do so without increasing bleeding complications.

“The search for medications that reduce the risk of life-threatening blood clots without increasing the risk of bleeding has continued for decades,” Holinstat said.

“Sotagliflozin has now been demonstrated to serve both functions and may represent the next advancement in prevention of blood clots, heart failure and stroke in patients with and without diabetes.”

Randell Clifford Means is a logistics and supply chain professional from Detroit, Michigan, who has worked contractually for Biobest, a global leader in biological control and crop pollination headquartered in Belgium with North American operations based out of Waterloo, Canada.

Biobest Group (rebranded as part of the BioFirst Group) is a world-leading Belgian sustainable agriculture company specializing in biological pest control (biocontrol) and natural pollination.
Founded in 1987 by veterinarian Roland De Jonghe—who initially began breeding bumblebees in his garage to organically pollinate tomatoes—the company has expanded into a global powerhouse operating in over 70 countries with more than 2,800 employees.
Core Offerings & Solutions
Biobest focuses on Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategies to minimize chemical pesticide use, combat pest resistance, and maximize crop yields safely. Their portfolio includes:
• Natural Pollination: Industry-leading bumblebee hives used extensively across greenhouse vegetables (such as tomatoes and peppers) and soft fruits. They also offer specialized delivery systems like the Flying Doctor System for precision biopesticide distribution via bees.
• Biological Control (Biocontrol): Production and commercialization of over 30 species of beneficial insects, predatory mites, and beneficial nematodes to naturally hunt and manage plant pests.
• Biopesticides & Biostimulants: Naturally derived micro-organisms, pheromones, and natural substances that boost plant immune systems and disrupt pest reproduction.

Belgium 🇧🇪 & Waterloo Canada 🇨🇦 & Toronto Canada 🇨🇦 & The Means 

Biobest Career & Role
At Biobest, Means worked out of the Metro Airport Center Industrial Space in Romulus, Michigan. His experience with the company includes:
• Logistics & Supply Chain Management: Serving as a Logistics Coordinator and Logistics Analyst, he managed the supply chain of company products (beneficial insects, mites, bees, and nematodes) imported from the manufacturer in Belgium for distribution to crop growers across North America and Mexico.
• Compliance & Technical Systems: He handled product life cycle analysis, FDA storage regulations, and hazardous materials shipping systems, holding certifications or proficiency in the DGIS Label Master System, Lion Technology DOT & IATA hazardous materials shipping, and Sage accounting software.

His Excellency delivered a presentation titled "In Silico Clinical Trials" during the session on "Global Trends and Practical Strategies for Using AI in Drug Regulation." He highlighted the role of AI and computer simulation in transforming drug development by accelerating clinical trials, generating stronger scientific evidence to back regulatory decisions, and reducing burdens on patients, all while maintaining rigorous standards of quality, safety, and efficacy.
He emphasized the importance of utilizing these technologies in developing treatments for rare diseases, which often face challenges in conducting traditional clinical trials due to limited patient populations and recruitment difficulties. He noted that computer simulation offers opportunities to complement and improve the design of traditional trials, and even substitute certain parts when appropriate, thereby speeding up the development of therapies and making them available to patients sooner.
Furthermore, he explained that the SFDA is working to build a supportive regulatory environment for this transformation through initiatives such as the "Nader" program for rare disease medications, guidelines on the use of AI in clinical development, and the establishment of the "CELL" AI Laboratory to support the testing and evaluation of applications in regulatory science. He stressed that leveraging these technologies depends on the reliability and validity of the generated evidence to support regulatory decision-making, which requires high data quality, model validation, transparency, human oversight, as well as fostering international collaboration and knowledge sharing.
The session also addressed the experiences and strategic directions of several international regulatory bodies in employing AI within drug and biological product regulation, supporting decision-making, improving communication strategies, and drawing regulatory lessons from healthcare AI applications. Participants included representatives from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the European Medicines Agency (EMA), the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), the Spanish Agency of Medicines and Medical Devices (AEMPS), and Brazil's National Health Surveillance Agency (Anvisa).
The SFDA's participation reflects its role in advancing international regulatory practices and keeping pace with technological shifts in the pharmaceutical sector, as it is the first regulatory authority from the Middle East and North Africa region to gain full membership in the Coalition (ICMRA). This allows the SFDA to contribute to shaping policies and decisions, boosting the efficiency of regulatory frameworks, and accelerating patient access to safe and effective therapies globally.
The Coalition (ICMRA) is an international executive-level alliance comprising heads of drug regulatory authorities from around the world. It aims to strengthen cooperation, coordination, information exchange, and joint efforts in addressing global health crises, thereby ensuring the safety, quality, and efficacy of medicines and vaccines while supporting innovation and expediting the delivery of new treatments under strict safety standards.

text:
$TLS Q3 2026 earnings: Telos wins $58 million in orders, while profit beats plan

Telos Corporation, a cybersecurity and identity contractor for the US government, broke a six-quarter drought in new contract awards while posting its highest profit since going public. Third-quarter revenue rose 7% to $55 million, beating the company's plan for a seventh straight quarter on expanding identity programs and TSA PreCheck airport enrollments. Management raised its full-year sales and profit outlook, and its new fourth-quarter forecast sits well above what the prior full-year plan pointed to by our math.

• Revenue: $𝟓𝟓.𝟐𝐌 (+7.3% from a year ago (~16% underlying by our math))
• Net new cyber risk orders: $𝟓𝟖𝐌 (expected to bring ~$20M of 2027 revenue)
• Adjusted EBITDA: $𝟏𝟎.𝟔𝐌 (19.2% of sales; beat $6.0–6.8M plan)
• Full-year revenue outlook: 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐝 $𝟖.𝟓𝐌 (middle of the range: 21% growth)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢 Bullish

The story got better because Telos won $58 million of new orders for its Xacta cyber risk software and services, which management forecasts will bring in about $20 million of revenue in 2027. That single win replaces nearly two-thirds of the $33 million in low-margin software resales the company is phasing out starting next quarter. One caution: employee stock grants still outpaced share buybacks, pushing the diluted share count up 1% from a year ago and keeping profit per share excluding one-offs unchanged.

The question now is whether Telos can win enough of its remaining proposal pipeline to replace the last $13 million of exiting software sales and return to underlying growth in 2027. Either the third-quarter orders mark the start of delayed federal contracts finally converting, or the company still faces a smaller revenue drop next year alongside higher margins. Fourth-quarter award announcements and the initial 2027 outlook next quarter will settle it.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢🟢 𝐍𝐞𝐰 𝐂𝐲𝐛𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤 𝐎𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐂𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐄𝐱𝐢𝐭
Telos plans to stop reselling low-margin software from other vendors starting in the fourth quarter, a move that will remove about $33 million of annual sales after 2026. Investors needed to see new contract awards replace those lost sales after federal procurement delays pushed decisions back for six straight quarters.

The federal security contractor broke that drought this quarter. Telos announced that its "Information Assurance business has secured $58 million of net new Xacta and professional services orders that are forecasted to generate approximately $20 million of Revenue in 2027." Xacta is the company's software platform for managing cyber risk and compliance.

These orders matter because they replace nearly two-thirds of the exiting software resale stream before 2027 begins, and they carry higher software and service margins. The win also revives growth in the Xacta product line after flat performance earlier this year. However, one quarter of orders only eases the concern around award delays rather than ending it, because about $13 million of the 2027 revenue exit still needs backfilling from the remaining proposal pipeline.

What to watch: fourth-quarter contract award announcements and the initial 2027 revenue outlook next quarter. Another $25 million to $30 million of multi-year awards would fully cover the remaining revenue gap.

🟢🟢 𝐈𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐏𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐂𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐮𝐬 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧𝐬
Telos sells identity and biometric services through Telos ID, which includes TSA PreCheck airport security enrollment. Management had planned for third-quarter cash gross margin—gross profit before non-cash depreciation and stock pay—to drop to between 37.5% and 38.5% because of reserves for fixed-price contracts.

Instead, cash gross margin reached 43.1%, beating the middle of the company's plan by 5.1 percentage points. GAAP gross margin fell 2.0 percentage points from a year ago to 37.9% as cost of sales in Security Solutions rose 7.5 percentage points of revenue, lapping one-time program start-up revenue from last year. Lower selling, general and administrative expenses—down 13.2 percentage points of revenue on falling stock pay—more than offset that dip.

• Q3 revenue: $55.2 million, up 7.3% from a year ago (up about 16% on an underlying basis by our math)
• Q3 Adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, amortization and stock pay): $10.6 million, vs $6.0–6.8 million planned
• Q4 Adjusted EBITDA outlook: $7.0–8.8 million, vs $2.9–7.1 million implied by the prior full-year plan by our math

The company credited the beat and full-year raise to "strength in TSA PreCheck ® volumes, and margin outperformance on large programs". Beating its own plan for a seventh straight quarter shows management sets conservative targets, and the higher fourth-quarter outlook confirms margins are holding up as the low-margin software exit begins.

What to watch: fourth-quarter cash gross margin against the third quarter's 43.1% reading. A rise toward the mid-40s would show the software resale phase-out is lifting profitability as planned.

🟢 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰 𝐓𝐨𝐩𝐬 𝟏𝟐% 𝐨𝐟 𝐒𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐚 𝐒𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐡 𝐐𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫
Telos has shifted from burning cash two years ago to generating steady cash from its security programs. Third-quarter operating cash flow reached $9.4 million, and free cash flow—operating cash minus equipment purchases and capitalized software development—rose 11.9% from a year ago to $7.4 million. That represents 13.4% of revenue, marking a seventh straight quarter above 12%.

The Virginia-based contractor used that cash to step up share buybacks, spending $5.7 million in the quarter to repurchase more than 1.2 million shares at an average price of $4.59. Over the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow totaled $20.4 million, up from $15.0 million a year earlier, giving the business funding to buy back shares while keeping cash above $51 million.

What to watch: fourth-quarter free cash flow conversion as accounts receivable—which absorbed $5.7 million of cash this quarter—are collected. Collecting those bills should keep the full-year free cash flow margin above 13%.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐄𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐲𝐞𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐆𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐒𝐭𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐞 𝐒𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐲𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐬
Telos celebrated its "Highest Quarterly Profit Since IPO" and highlighted its accelerated share repurchases in the earnings release. GAAP net income swung to $4.4 million from a $2.1 million loss a year ago because stock-based compensation fell from $9.4 million to $3.0 million.

Beneath that headline, share buybacks are still not shrinking the share count for shareholders. Over the first nine months of 2026, the company spent $12.6 million buying back stock and another $7.6 million paying employee taxes on vesting shares, consuming nearly all $20.4 million of its free cash flow. Yet diluted shares used to calculate profit per share excluding one-offs still rose 1.2% from a year ago to 76.5 million.

• Basic share count: 74.2 million, up 2.3% from 72.6 million a year ago
• Diluted share count (excluding one-offs): 76.5 million, up from 75.6 million a year ago
• Profit per share (excluding one-offs): $0.09, unchanged from $0.09 a year ago despite 7.3% revenue growth

Because the share count grew while Adjusted EBITDA rose only 4.7%, profit per share excluding one-offs did not grow at all from a year ago. In addition, Telos includes $0.7 million of accrued bonuses in its stock-pay add-back that it can still choose to pay in cash.

What to watch: diluted share count in the fourth quarter. A drop below last year's 75.6 million level would prove buybacks are finally reducing dilution rather than just offsetting employee stock grants.

🔴 𝐒𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐍𝐞𝐭𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬 𝐒𝐡𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐤𝐬 𝟖𝟎% 𝐚𝐬 𝐋𝐞𝐠𝐚𝐜𝐲 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐠𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐬 𝐄𝐧𝐝
Telos operates two reporting segments: Security Solutions, which houses cyber compliance and identity services, and Secure Networks, which builds secure communications infrastructure. While Security Solutions grew 16.6% from a year ago "primarily due to the expansion of large programs in Telos ID", Secure Networks is nearly gone.

Secure Networks sales fell 79.6% from a year ago to $1.0 million, down from $5.0 million in the third quarter of 2025, as older government contracts wrapped up without replacement wins. That contraction cut 7.7 percentage points from total company revenue growth this quarter by our math, and left Security Solutions generating 98.2% of total sales. The business now depends almost entirely on one segment.

What to watch: whether Secure Networks stabilizes near $1 million per quarter or winds down completely in 2027. Once it reaches zero, the drag on company growth stops, but Telos loses all business diversification.

🔴 𝐑𝐢𝐬𝐤𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬 𝐪𝐮𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐝𝐢𝐝𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐬𝐰𝐞𝐫
The third-quarter earnings release left four standing risks and watch items without new data.

• Remaining 2027 revenue gap: the $58 million Xacta win provides about $20 million in 2027, leaving roughly $13 million of the $33 million software resale exit still to be won from the broader proposal pipeline; fourth-quarter award disclosures will test this.
• Concentration in large Telos ID programs: the release again grouped all growth into large Telos ID programs without sizing the Defense Manpower Data Center contract or confidential security work; the quarterly Form 10-Q filing may offer customer concentration percentages.
• Chief executive succession: chief executive John Wood has been on medical leave since April 2026 with no update in the release on a permanent appointment; board announcements will settle this.
• 2025 restructuring completion: the release showed zero restructuring charges, but the remaining cash severance balance (which stood at $0.7 million in June) is only readable in Note 2 of the upcoming Form 10-Q filing.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐭 𝐥𝐢𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟕.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Total contract liabilities—cash customers have paid upfront for services Telos has not yet delivered—rose 24.6% from $13.7 million a year ago by our math, outpacing 7.3% revenue growth. The balance dipped $1.0 million from the second quarter's $18.1 million as the company recognized revenue from earlier billings.

𝐀𝐜𝐜𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐭𝐬 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐞𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞, 𝐧𝐞𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟑.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Uncollected customer bills rose 16.2% from $20.4 million a year ago and climbed $5.7 million from the second quarter's $18.0 million. That build in receivables grew more than twice as fast as third-quarter sales and reduced operating cash flow by $5.7 million during the period.

𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐞𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐯𝐚𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐬 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟓𝟏.𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇒ stable
Cash on the balance sheet increased by $1.1 million from the second quarter's $50.6 million, even after the security group spent $5.7 million on share buybacks and $0.5 million on finance leases. Total finance lease debt fell to $6.1 million from $6.6 million three months earlier.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐐𝟒 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟒𝟕.𝟓–𝟓𝟎.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $42.3–48.9 million (implied by prior FY26 outlook)
Raised against the prior implied range. The plan calls for 2% to 7% growth from a year ago (4.2% at the middle of the range), slowing from 7.3% in Q3 as low-margin software resales begin phasing out. By our math, that is 6.9% above what the old full-year plan implied. Telos has beaten its quarterly sales midpoint by an average of 9.5% over the last four quarters; if the pattern holds, Q4 revenue would reach $53.4 million.

𝐅𝐘 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞: $𝟏𝟗𝟖.𝟐–𝟐𝟎𝟎.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $187.0–195.0 million
Raised. Management lifted the middle of the full-year range by $8.45 million to 21.0% growth (20% to 22% stated), more than reversing last quarter's $2.5 million trim. Across four quarters of updates, the middle of the range moved by $0.0 million, -$2.5 million, and now +$8.45 million. With $150.7 million already booked in the first nine months, the target is well within reach.

𝐐𝟒 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟕.𝟎–𝟖.𝟖 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from $2.9–7.1 million (implied by prior FY26 outlook)
Raised against the prior implied range. The forecast points to $7.9 million at the middle of the range, up 8.3% from a year ago but down 25.3% from the third quarter's seasonal peak. By our math, the new midpoint is 58.8% higher than the $5.0 million implied by the prior full-year plan. Over the last four quarters, the company beat its profit midpoint by 51.5% on average; if the pattern holds, Q4 would reach $12.0 million.

𝐅𝐘 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $𝟑𝟐.𝟑–𝟑𝟒.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $23.6–28.6 million
Raised. The middle of the range jumped $7.1 million to $33.2 million, representing 83.1% growth from 2025. It is the second raise this year and much larger than the first: $0.0 million in Q1, +$1.8 million in Q2, and +$7.1 million in Q3. Because the group has already earned $25.3 million through September, the full-year outlook looks achievable.

text:
We Americans need to have a positive vision for the future of our people. Americans. Not foreigners, not corporations.

Democrats promise socialism and the old and young eat it up. We know it's a lie.

But what Republicans have been promising for decades has also been a lie. Maybe not here in New Hampshire, but we've been powerless to stop it. The nation now controls our local politics through elections, immigration, money printing and more.

If you want to win an election ever again focus on the youth, not as a side project, but as the focal point of everything we do.

Promise them a world that is better than the one you grew up in, and deliver.

How?

1) Stop pandering to foreigners and immigrants. America is for Americans. Promise them that.

For the moment, New Hampshire is still one of the few states that is majority Americans. I don't mean US Citizens, I mean real heritage Americans who have deep roots here. Both the left and the right have allowed legal immigration and illegal immigration, giving away our country to foreigners instead of keeping it for our own children. Nobody feels empowered when their country is invaded by foreigners. Socialism feels comforting in the face of an invasion - it feels more stable. Offer the next generation the stability you grew up with.

It doesn't matter if we can't legally do anything about it right now - we have to make fighting for Americans the #1 issue for Republicans going forward and we have to actively sell this to the youth of all ages.

We need bold policy here and real community building. Once the youth feel empowered, this message will spread via peer pressure and eventually even their hippie grandparents will be voting Republican again to save the country for their grandkids.

Then all we have to do is follow through.

2) Stop pandering to corporations, especially big out-of-state ones. New Hampshire if for people, not corporations.

No Granite Stater feels empowered when the Governor and Mayor praise a California developer for building apartments here.

No Granite Stater feels empowered when our own Business and Economic Affairs office actively works to sell our land to Chinese corporations.

We need a renaissance of American young men working together, for themselves and their friend and their families. Stop selling our land, start buying American and start hiring American.

3) Support healthy Christian family life. Be the American Christian role model this next generation needs.

Bring your family to Church. Pray regularly. Eat well. Stay focused.

Put God first. This will be a tough one, because a return to the Gospel means a big change for our way of life personally and politically. He has a way of doing things, and America has strayed from that.

This part is new for me. I grew up in the Church but never heard a call, never felt God, until my 40th year of life. I won't look back.

I also grew up in liberal California and watched it fall to foreign invasion. Now, I have returned my family to where we started in 1623 when my ancestors first set foot in New England, and the more I read about how they organized political life in early New England the more I realize... they were right. We have strayed from the Bible, from God, and from the system of early America that made us strong.

4) Teach our history. Teach it as good. Teach it as moral. Teach it as the Providence it was.

Stop pandering to foreign cultures and foreign religions. Stop supporting them, stop funding them, stop respecting them.

Believe that American culture is the best culture. Believe the Christian God is the only God. Apologize for nothing.

Practice our culture. Practice our history. Practice our religion. Instill into this next generation a stronger sense of Americanism than you had. Learn it and pass it on. If it's not alive, then it's dead. Don't let America die with you.  Keep it alive and well for the next generation to enjoy.

5) Protect American institutions. Reserve them for Americans. Nobody feels empowered when foreigners rule over them.

Don't let our country be invaded. Don't let our government be invaded.

We can use soft policies such as defunding foreign-owned endeavors, ending loans for foreigners, taxing remittances, charging foreigners more to use our state parks, charging foreigners to send their children to our schools, removing any welfare or benefits to foreigners or foreigner-headed households, having no pathways to citizenship, ending birth-right citizenship, prosecuting those who hire illegals, and most of all, protecting our government from foreigners by requiring natural born citizenship and residency requirements for employment or office at any and every level of government including all government funded projects.

Ultimately, we need to support remigration.

Foreigners have their own nations they came from. They can go home, whereas American youth have nowhere to run - this is their home.

------------

Ultimately, country, language, culture, and religion are all gifts from God, given to our ancestors who passed them down to us and it is our duty to cherish them and pass them on, in good condition, to the next generation.

This is the American family heirloom.

America is your inheritance, not just the land, but the American ethnicity... our people, our language, our culture, our government, our religion...

Know we are beautiful; cherish this and pass it on.

text:
RIP and respect for Rube Wright who passed away on this day in Pro Wrestling History, November 9th, 1983 at the age of 76. Known as “The Preacher’s Son,” he was a legitimate tough guy and skilled catch wrestler who rose through the Southern California club circuit in the 1930s (after winning the 1932 Southern Pacific AAU heavyweight title). In 1942, during a California State Athletic Commission-sanctioned tournament at the Olympic Auditorium in Los Angeles (promoted amid the chaotic world title scene involving figures like Jimmy Londos, Toots Mondt, and others), he defeated the Swedish Angel (Phil Olafsson) with his signature step-over toe hold to claim recognition as world heavyweight champion. He briefly shared that contested status with several other claimants of the era (including Wild Bill Longson and Orville Brown) before the title was effectively reduced to a California state title.

Later in his career (from the early 1950s into the mid-1960s), he worked under the gimmick of Lu Kim (or Mongol), billed as a Manchurian seafarer who combined jiu-jitsu with catch-as-catch-can style and offered challenges such as $1,000 to anyone who could pin him. Peers including Stu Hart and Karl Gotch spoke highly of his toughness (Hart reportedly felt Wright could have handled Lou Thesz in a legitimate shoot). He also had a brother, Big Jim Wright (who wrestled as Kolo Stasiak), and remained active in various territories including the South and West Coast.
