text:
During the harsh winter of 1933 along a lonely stretch of highway outside Enid, Oklahoma, widow Eleanor Graves turned an abandoned feed shed into a small roadside kitchen for families traveling west during the Great Depression. Her husband had died two years earlier after losing work at a grain elevator, leaving Eleanor alone with three children and very little money. 

The Dust Bowl had already damaged nearby farms, jobs were disappearing everywhere, and hungry families passed constantly along the roads searching for work in Texas and California. Using scrap lumber, old barrels, and pieces of rusted tin, Eleanor built a small soup stand beside the highway. Every morning before sunrise she lit a wood stove and cooked whatever she could stretch into meals — bean soup, potatoes, cornbread, onions, cabbage, and sometimes small amounts of salt pork when she could afford it.

She charged five cents whenever people could pay. When they could not, she fed them anyway. Truck drivers, unemployed farmers, migrant families, and children wrapped in blankets stopped beside the little roadside kitchen throughout the winter. Some traded firewood or canned food for meals. Others offered labor repairing the shed roof or chopping wood behind the kitchen. 

Many had nothing at all except empty stomachs. Eleanor rarely turned anyone away. Her own children slept behind a curtain inside the tiny building while their mother stirred soup kettles late into the night beneath lantern light. Flour sacks became curtains. Crates became tables. Old coffee cans held spoons and utensils gathered from travelers who promised to return them someday.

Neighbors later remembered long lines forming beside the soup stand after dust storms blocked nearby roads. Families sat together on rough wooden benches eating hot soup while wind carried dirt across the empty fields surrounding the highway. By 1935 better harvests slowly returned and fewer migrant families passed through the area. 

Eleanor eventually closed the roadside kitchen and found work sewing clothes in town. Years later, people around Enid still remembered the small wooden sign hanging outside the shack during the worst years of the Depression: "HUNGRY PEOPLE EAT FIRST. MONEY LATER"

𝐓𝐄𝐗𝐀𝐒 𝐆𝐎𝐕𝐄𝐑𝐍𝐎𝐑-𝐄𝐋𝐄𝐂𝐓 𝐇𝐈𝐍𝐎𝐉𝐎𝐒𝐀: “𝐒𝐓𝐑𝐎𝐍𝐆 𝐏𝐎𝐒𝐒𝐈𝐁𝐈𝐋𝐈𝐓𝐘” 𝐒𝐇𝐄 𝐃𝐈𝐀𝐋𝐒 𝐁𝐀𝐂𝐊 𝐀𝐁𝐁𝐎𝐓𝐓’𝐒 $𝟏𝟏 𝐁𝐈𝐋𝐋𝐈𝐎𝐍 𝐁𝐎𝐑𝐃𝐄𝐑 𝐌𝐈𝐒𝐒𝐈𝐎𝐍

Days after Democrats won the Texas governor’s mansion, Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa was asked on CNN whether her win is a mandate to wind down Operation Lone Star: the National Guard on the border, the military base of operations, the busing program. Her answer: “𝘐 𝘵𝘩𝘪𝘯𝘬 𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳𝘦’𝘴 𝘢 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘰𝘯𝘨 𝘱𝘰𝘴𝘴𝘪𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘪𝘵𝘺.”

She did not hide the price tag. “𝘞𝘦 𝘴𝘱𝘦𝘯𝘵 $11 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘪𝘯 𝘳𝘦𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘺𝘦𝘢𝘳𝘴 𝘰𝘯 𝘖𝘱𝘦𝘳𝘢𝘵𝘪𝘰𝘯 𝘓𝘰𝘯𝘦 𝘚𝘵𝘢𝘳,” she said, then pivoted straight to ICE, claiming “𝘐𝘊𝘌 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘬!𝘭𝘭𝘦𝘥 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘶𝘳𝘵 𝘪𝘯𝘯𝘰𝘤𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘱𝘦𝘰𝘱𝘭𝘦” and that voters have “𝘢 𝘥𝘪𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘴𝘵𝘦 𝘧𝘰𝘳 𝘸𝘩𝘢𝘵’𝘴 𝘨𝘰𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘰𝘯.” Those are her claims, made on air; she offered no specifics in the clip.

The interviewer’s framing is worth noticing: the questions were about withdrawing the Guard and cutting the money, and she did not rule either out. She cited 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐝𝐞𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐟 𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐫𝐞𝐧, 𝐬𝐞𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐮𝐩 𝐩𝐞𝐨𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐰𝐡𝐨 𝐡𝐚𝐯𝐞 𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐝𝐞𝐜𝐚𝐝𝐞𝐬 as the reason.

Operation Lone Star is Gov. Greg Abbott’s signature border program. Under Texas law, much of the Guard deployment runs on a governor’s orders, so the person who takes the oath in January gets to decide how much of it survives. 𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐬𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐡𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐨𝐧 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐨𝐫’𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥, and Republicans still control the state Senate.

For Texans who watched the border go from chaos to calm on the strength of this mission, the message is plain: the new governor is already talking about dialing it back before she has even been sworn in. Her stated reason is ICE, not the border, which makes the target of her review clear.

𝐓𝐞𝐱𝐚𝐬 𝐯𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐩𝐢𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐝 𝐚 𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐨𝐫, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐧𝐨𝐰 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐨𝐫-𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐢𝐬 𝐨𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐰𝐞𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐰𝐡𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐦𝐚𝐧𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐛𝐨𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐦𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧.

text:
PEREGRINE MONEY MAP -

Before another city signs a police-software contract, residents deserve to see who is contributing to political committees, who is approving public funding, and what the software will connect.

This map brings those records together. Contributions, government decisions and family relationships are shown separately so you can follow each documented connection.

START WITH THE POLITICAL MONEY

Peregrine Technologies contributed $725,000 to CCC, a Florida political committee, in five checks between February 2025 and October 2026.

CCC pools contributions from multiple donors. Its separate expenditure filings show $72,000 to Friends of Blaise Ingoglia and $3,000 to Ingoglia’s campaign; $35,000 to Friends of James Uthmeier; $50,000 to Florida Freedom Fund; $50,000 to Buchanan for Florida; $10,000 to Friends of Jonathan Martin; $1,000 to Fiona McFarland’s campaign; and $10,000 to Hillsborough Together.

These are the committee’s incoming and outgoing records, filed through October 26, 2026.

[https://t.co/0eTx9knVQz)

WHO APPROVES THE PUBLIC FUNDING?

Gov. Ron DeSantis, Attorney General James Uthmeier, CFO Blaise Ingoglia and Agriculture Commissioner Wilton Simpson make up Florida’s State Board of Immigration Enforcement. Its decisions require unanimous votes. Florida Phoenix reported that the board’s June 9 approvals included $14.6 million for Peregrine.

[https://t.co/2RELkS3PNM](https://t.co/2RELkS3PNM)

A separate May 15 House conference offer proposed $6 million for FDLE to competitively procure a statewide criminal-intelligence platform. The record shown on the map is that proposal, with the provider to be selected through procurement.

[https://t.co/CRpl3u7pbJ](https://t.co/CRpl3u7pbJ)

THE PEOPLE AND RELATIONSHIPS

Peregrine’s Matthew Melton, who heads business development and partnerships, is married to Rep. Fiona McFarland, an IT-budget conference co-chair. McFarland told the Florida Trident she disclosed his employer to House leadership and asked to keep Peregrine matters separate. She said she learned of the $6 million addition through a news post, had nothing to do with securing it, and that Nick Iarossi lobbied her on other matters rather than Peregrine.

The Trident identifies Iarossi and Christopher Schoonover as Peregrine lobbyists.

[https://t.co/fxKWke2Ye1](https://t.co/fxKWke2Ye1)

Peregrine CEO Nick Noone is the separate former Palantir executive.

[https://t.co/XBbO465xDs](https://t.co/XBbO465xDs)

THE LOCAL DECISIONS

Tampa approved a $595,000 Peregrine contract funded through a state grant. The map shows that same money at its grant and contract stages.

Jacksonville appropriated $1,916,232 from the state immigration board. That includes $1.9 million under “Hardware-Software Maintenance & Licenses.” Committee minutes identify Peregrine and describe collaboration with agencies nationwide on connected cases.

[https://t.co/yQVDq36hbR](https://t.co/yQVDq36hbR)

BLANCHE AND THE FEDERAL MONEY

At the November 6 Jacksonville event, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche called privacy “extraordinarily important,” but said current license-plate-reader technology “does not affect the privacy of American citizens.” He immediately added, “It may someday,” and said advancing technology could require reassessment and limits.

[https://t.co/r9724j87Nj)

DOJ also announced more than $73 million for Jacksonville, with its spending plan still being finalized. The map shows that federal award separately from the state Peregrine funding.

[https://t.co/sn41XPPrQs](https://t.co/sn41XPPrQs)

Read the map. Check the sources. Ask your elected officials for the contracts, data-sharing agreements, retention rules and access controls.

Before government connects more information about the public, the public deserves a clear view of the decisions behind it.
#OperationGoldenEagle 
#Tampa #PlantCity #Hillsborough #Palantir #Peregrine #MassSurveillance  #DataCenters

Two Spokane County sheriff’s deputies were fatally shot Nov. 3 near Spangle, Washington, while trying to enter a home to rescue possible hostages after a woman reported she had been shot in a domestic violence incident. Deputies Mason Acheson and Parker Perry came under fire from inside the house. The woman was taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

Deputies first responded around 2:25 p.m. They learned the suspect had an active felony warrant and might have access to more weapons, so SWAT was called. Perry, a K-9 deputy, forced entry around 3:15 p.m. When gunfire struck both men, teammates returned fire, pulled them to cover and began treatment. Highways were closed to rush them to hospital by medical helicopter.

Acheson died after reaching the hospital. Perry remained on life support for organ donation. Both left wives and two children; Perry and his wife were expecting a third. A drone later found the suspect, Ryan Larsen, 37, dead from a self-inflicted gunshot. The medical examiner also identified Suzanne Larsen, 72, and Rebecca Larsen, 45—identified in a family obituary as his mother and sister—as killed.

Sheriff John Nowels called it a tragic day affecting many families. Both deputies were Washington Army National Guard veterans. Gov. Bob Ferguson ordered flags lowered to half-staff on Nov. 9. FBI Director Kash Patel and Rep. Michael Baumgartner offered tributes and support for the families.

text:
In December 1957 Elvis Presley got his draft notice. 3 months later he was a private. By October 1958 he was on a US Army base in Germany.

Now Germany mails its own letters. 298,200 by June, to everyone turning 18.

And a line in its new law says men aged 17 to 45 need the army's approval to stay abroad for more than 3 months.

The law is the Military Service Modernisation Act. Bundestag vote December 5, 2025. In force January 1, 2026.

Every man born in 2008 or later must answer the questionnaire. For women it is optional.

From July 1, 2027, every 18-year-old man goes to a medical screening.

Service itself is still voluntary. The paperwork already is not.

The travel line sat in the law for 3 months. Nobody noticed.

On April 3 the Frankfurter Rundschau flagged paragraph 3 of the conscription act: men 17 to 45 need approval from a Bundeswehr career centre for any stay abroad over 3 months. Study, work, a long trip. About 20 million men.

4 days later the ministry promised a blanket exemption.

To be fair, it moved fast. The exemption took effect April 17. Today nobody needs a permit.

The catch is in the wording. Defence minister Boris Pistorius: the rule is suspended "as long as military service is voluntary."

The paragraph stays in the law. The exemption is a ministry order, and legal scholars already dispute whether it holds.

Why would it ever flip back? Look at the numbers.

298,200 letters. 96% of men answered. About 530 got a firm offer to enlist: 0.18%. Many are still in school, the ministry says.

The goal: from about 186,000 soldiers to 260,000 by the mid-2030s.

Pistorius, in the Bundestag: compulsory service stays possible "if it is not enough and the threat keeps getting worse."

Young men read the same numbers.

Austria plans to stretch military service from 6 to 9 months. In October a record 1,698 Austrians signed up for civilian service instead, 32% more than a year earlier. The minister links it to the plan. Parliament has not voted yet.

On Halloween, Gen Z protests against rent, school cuts and the draft were called in 34 German cities. Shops on Berlin's Ku'damm boarded up.

Elvis had 3 months between the letter and the barracks.

That is the part that matters. A plan B you start after the letter arrives is a deadline. A plan B you set up years before is optionality.

I learned it the late way. In 2022 my Russian passport cut me off from international finance. A Brazilian one gave it back 3 years later.

Plan B: disloyal, or basic risk management?

The biography of Viktoria Kolesnik-Lavinskaya — a map of war, travelled on foot.

I continue telling the stories of people from the Kharkov Region whom I know personally.

Today, I’m writing about someone whose story could be made into a film. In fact, more than one.

💛 Viktoria Kolesnik-Lavinskaya. She is currently Acting Commissioner for Human Rights and Children’s Rights in the Kharkov Region. But her path to this position began in the winter of 2014, on a square in Kharkov.

💪 Anti-Maidan. Rallies, the storming of the regional administration building, and her election as a representative of the 2nd Hundred. Then came the arrests: more than seventy activists behind bars. Together with like-minded people, she organised legal assistance for them and weekly deliveries of supplies to the pre-trial detention centre.

The price was clear. Her details appeared on the “Mirotvorets” website (the site is recognised as extremist in Russia), and two months later, her bank cards were blocked.

When the male activists were detained, women took to the square. She became one of the initiators of a women's tent camp near the Lenin monument. On April 29, 2014, it was broken up by armed men wearing balaclavas.

💪 Then came Slavyansk. First, humanitarian aid for the first refugees at the Svyatogorsk Monastery, then aid delivered into the city itself, under shelling. When she learned that the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) had decided to detain her, she stayed in Slavyansk. She cut off contact with her family in Kharkov so as not to put them at risk. Just think about that.

At the request of the mayor of Slavyansk, she organised food supplies, set up warehouses and provided civilians with everything they needed. She was nominated for the “For the Liberation of Slavyansk” medal. And she remained there until the very end, until the militia withdrew to Donetsk.

💪 In Donetsk — the militia and rear-service duties. August 2014: there was no funding, yet army warehouses had to be stocked. Accounting, oversight and storage — all built from scratch. The republic's leadership offered her a senior position in the rear services of the DPR Ministry of Defence.

A logistics officer who travelled to the front lines. She personally checked what the fighters were being fed, what they were wearing and how they were living in their positions. First, the rear services of the 1st Army Corps, then the Internal Troops of the DPR Ministry of Internal Affairs.

And throughout all this time, civilians remained a priority. After Debaltsevo in 2015, they organised bread production for local residents. In 2022, after the liberation of Mariupol, when the city was left without water or food, the Internal Troops of the DPR Ministry of Internal Affairs provided residents with the essentials.

💪 In June 2022, she was discharged from military service on health grounds. She held the rank of Major.

One might have thought that well-earned rest was finally due. But by July, she had become Deputy Head of the Kharkov Region Military-Civil Administration, responsible for the economy and finance. She moved to Kupyansk.

And when some territories had to be abandoned, she headed a working group providing assistance to displaced people from the Kharkov Region — in Russia, the Lugansk People's Republic (LPR) and the Donetsk People's Republic (DPR). The group also helped those who remained at home in frontline villages.

In the winter of 2025, she was appointed Acting Commissioner for Human Rights and Children's Rights. She continues in this role to this day.

Kharkov, Slavyansk, Donetsk, Mariupol, Kupyansk. Twelve years of work — no, twelve years of fighting for people — without a break.

And now her face has been immortalised in the “Through the Ages. Special Military Operation” project: Dmitry Kutovoy has created a figurine of her...

⚡ WHEN POWER LOST ITS GRIP AND HISTORY TOOK OVER!

══════════════ ❧ ════════════════

THE WEIRDEST EVENTS IN HISTORY 🤯

══════════════ ❧ ════════════════

STRANGER THAN FICTION — NOVEMBER 9TH EDITION

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🕒 ESTIMATED READING TIME: 12 MINUTES

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🗺️ CONSPECTUS

📜 EPIGRAPH — A little truth to set the tone.

🎬 INTRO — Five stories. One very strange date.

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY — Test your instincts.

⭐️ MAIN EVENTS — Five moments when history got spectacularly weird.

🎙️ HARVEY'S CORNER — The rest of the story.

⚖️ CLOSING — The day, considered.

✅ QUIZ ANSWER — The answer revealed.

🍬 CANDY — One last sweet bite, with a look at tomorrow.

💋 SEND-OFF — Pass the madness along.

📚 SOURCES & FURTHER READING — Follow the evidence.

✒️ PUDD'NHEAD WILSON HAS THE LAST WORD — Mark Twain gets the final say.

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

📜 EPIGRAPH

“Truth is stranger than fiction, but it is because Fiction is obliged to stick to possibilities; Truth isn't.” — Mark Twain, Following the Equator (1897).

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🎬 INTRO

Some days, history seems determined to prove that nobody is actually in charge—or, more accurately, that whoever is in charge has the foresight of a floating goldfish and the impulse control of a toddler with a flamethrower.

A perfectly respectable government receives a rather unexpected makeover, the sort usually reserved for buildings one intends to forget. A city discovers that fire can be remarkably difficult to negotiate with, which is unfortunate, as it had already declined the city’s earlier offer of “please don’t.” An important gentleman finds out that his departure has been announced before he’s agreed to leave—an administrative mix-up of the highest order, and one he will not be available to correct. Elsewhere, a night of organized brutality leaves behind a horrifying trail of destruction, because apparently “perhaps we shouldn’t” was never added to the agenda. And one of the world’s most formidable barriers discovers that it has an expiration date, which is awkward when one has spent decades insisting the thing is permanent.

There’s ambition, disaster, spectacular miscommunication, and a moment when the impossible suddenly becomes possible—largely because everyone involved had already exhausted the more sensible options.

Five stories. One date. And an astonishing amount of evidence that human beings should probably think things through before acting. Or, failing that, at least stop and ask whether the plan still seems clever in the morning.

Cue the chaos. Let’s roll. 💥

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

❓ HISTORY QUIZ OF THE DAY

On November 9, 1918, Germany's imperial chancellor announced that Kaiser Wilhelm II had abdicated.

There was one rather important complication: the Kaiser had not authorized the announcement.

Who made it?

[A] Friedrich Ebert, leader of the Social Democrats.

[B] Prince Max von Baden, the imperial chancellor.

[C] Philipp Scheidemann, who proclaimed a German republic.

[D] General Erich Ludendorff, the former military commander.

👇 (Answer at the end of the issue.)

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

⭐️ MAIN EVENTS

🎩 1799 — NAPOLEON'S CAREER CHANGE: FROM GENERAL TO GOVERNMENT TAKEOVER 🇫🇷

Paris and Saint-Cloud, France | November 9–10, 1799
France had a government, a constitution, and five directors sharing executive power. Stability, however, was in short supply.

The Directory faced political division, financial problems, military pressure, and public dissatisfaction. Director Emmanuel-Joseph Sieyès wanted to replace the system—and needed a successful general to help.

Enter Napoleon Bonaparte.

On November 9, 1799—18 Brumaire in the revolutionary calendar—the conspirators invoked rumors of a Jacobin plot to move the legislative councils from Paris to the Château de Saint-Cloud. Napoleon received command of the troops supposedly protecting the assemblies. The general now had soldiers surrounding the institutions he intended to dismantle.

The next day, deputies challenged Napoleon at the Council of Five Hundred, shouting him down and accusing him of violating the constitution. His brother Lucien, the council's presiding officer, helped him leave the chamber and called in the troops.

Soldiers dispersed the deputies. The Directory fell.

The coup did not immediately make Napoleon emperor. It created a Consulate, with Napoleon as First Consul, concentrating power in his hands and opening the road to his eventual imperial rule.

A republic had been “rescued” from instability by a military takeover. History has never lacked people who find that reassuring.

🧩 TRIVIA: The name 18 Brumaire comes from the French Republican Calendar. Brumaire was the second month of the revolutionary year, and 18 Brumaire Year VIII corresponded to November 9, 1799.

🐍 MACHIAVELLIAN: The conspirators used the supposed threat of a Jacobin uprising to move the legislative councils and position troops where they could control the political proceedings. The emergency was useful because it made an extraordinary transfer of power look like a defensive measure.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Napoleon did not seize power in a single theatrical moment. The coup depended on political allies, manufactured urgency, military positioning, and the weakness of an already unpopular government. The most consequential power grabs often arrive dressed as solutions.

───────────────

🔥 1872 — BOSTON'S GREAT FIRE: WHEN THE CITY BECAME THE KINDLING 🇺🇸

Boston, Massachusetts | November 9–10, 1872

On November 9, a fire began in the basement of a commercial building near Summer and Kingston Streets. By the time the first alarm sounded at 7:24 p.m., the building was engulfed.
Narrow streets, closely packed buildings, combustible materials, and inadequate water pressure helped the blaze race through downtown. The fire department faced another problem: many of its horses were sick or weakened by an epizootic outbreak, leaving some equipment difficult to move.

Neighboring communities sent fire companies, and New Haven, Connecticut, even dispatched a steam fire engine by railway. Still, the flames burned through the night.

Firefighters and police used gunpowder to demolish buildings in the fire's path, hoping to create firebreaks. More than 1,000 businesses were destroyed before the blaze was brought under control on November 10.

Boston rebuilt, but the disaster exposed neglected infrastructure, weak building regulations, and an emergency service unprepared for a catastrophe of that scale. The prosperous commercial district had not been prepared for the possibility that it might all catch fire.

🧩 TRIVIA: Boston's neighboring communities answered the call for help, and New Haven sent a steam fire engine to the city by railway.

⚠️ IRONY: Many of the buildings were constructed of brick or stone, materials that seemed reassuringly resistant to fire. Yet wooden signs, windows, interiors, and other combustible features helped the flames spread, while the heat became intense enough to damage even masonry structures.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: A disaster rarely begins with one failure. Boston's fire exposed a chain of weaknesses—water supply, building practices, equipment, transportation, and emergency response. The flames revealed what ordinary days had allowed the city to ignore.

───────────────

👑 1918 — THE KAISER ABDICATES. APPARENTLY, NOBODY TOLD THE KAISER. 🇩🇪

Berlin, Germany | November 9, 1918

Germany was losing the First World War. Revolution was spreading, the monarchy was under pressure, and Kaiser Wilhelm II's authority was collapsing.

That day, Imperial Chancellor Prince Max von Baden announced that Wilhelm had decided to abdicate. He hoped to calm the crisis and preserve an orderly transition.
There was one complication: Wilhelm had not agreed to abdicate.

Max made the announcement without the Kaiser's authorization, presenting the decision as settled while demands to end the monarchy gathered force.

The day brought further upheaval. Social Democratic leader Philipp Scheidemann proclaimed a German republic from the Reichstag; revolutionary socialist Karl Liebknecht separately proclaimed a socialist republic. Germany was now fighting over what kind of country would replace the empire.

Wilhelm eventually fled to the Netherlands. He formally renounced the throne on November 28, nineteen days after the announcement. The empire was finished, and the Weimar Republic emerged from the revolution.

🧩 TRIVIA: Wilhelm II signed his formal declaration of abdication on November 28, 1918—nineteen days after Max von Baden had announced it.

🌀 OBSCURE: The announcement did not simply report a completed decision. It was an attempt by the chancellor to manage a rapidly deteriorating political crisis by presenting the Kaiser's departure as an accomplished fact.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Political authority can disappear before the paperwork catches up. By November 9, the German monarchy was losing control of events so quickly that its own chancellor announced the emperor's departure before the emperor had formally agreed to go.

───────────────

💔 1938 — KRISTALLNACHT: THE NIGHT THE STREETS FILLED WITH BROKEN GLASS 🇩🇪

Nazi Germany and annexed territories | November 9–10, 1938

The violence was presented as a public outburst. It was anything but spontaneous.

On November 9, Nazi leaders gathered in Munich to commemorate Hitler's failed 1923 Beer Hall Putsch. That evening, they learned that German diplomat Ernst vom Rath had died after being shot in Paris by Herschel Grynszpan, a seventeen-year-old Polish Jewish refugee. The Nazis seized on the news as a pretext.

Joseph Goebbels delivered an antisemitic speech to party officials. Instructions spread through Nazi organizations and local authorities, unleashing coordinated violence against Jewish communities in Germany, Austria, and the Sudetenland.
On November 9–10, synagogues burned, Jewish-owned businesses were smashed and looted, homes were attacked, and Jewish people were assaulted and killed. Shattered shop windows covered the streets, giving the pogrom its name: Kristallnacht, or “Night of Broken Glass.”

More than 1,400 synagogues were burned or destroyed. Thousands of businesses were vandalized, and police arrested approximately 26,000 Jewish men and sent them to concentration camps. The regime later imposed a one-billion-Reichsmark penalty on the Jewish community, forcing victims to pay for the destruction inflicted upon them.

Kristallnacht marked a major escalation in Nazi persecution: organized violence, public humiliation, dispossession, and terror. The broken glass gave the night its name. The human consequences were far more devastating.

🧩 TRIVIA: The Nazi regime ordered the Jewish community to pay a one-billion-Reichsmark “atonement” payment after the pogrom—making victims financially responsible for the destruction inflicted upon them.

🐍 MACHIAVELLIAN: Nazi leaders deliberately presented the violence as a spontaneous public reaction, while coordinating and directing the attacks behind the scenes. The appearance of an uncontrolled outburst helped disguise state-organized persecution.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Kristallnacht was not an isolated riot or a sudden eruption of public anger. It was a coordinated act of state-sponsored terror. The distinction matters: the violence was not a breakdown of Nazi policy. It was an expression of it.

───────────────

🧱 1989 — THE BERLIN WALL FALLS AFTER ONE VERY BADLY TIMED PRESS CONFERENCE 🇩🇪

Berlin, East Germany | November 9, 1989

For twenty-eight years, the Berlin Wall had divided a city, separated families, and symbolized the Cold War. On November 9, a press conference helped bring that division to a turning point.

East Germany's government faced mass demonstrations, emigration through neighboring countries, and growing demands for freedom to travel. It had approved new travel regulations intended to take effect the following day.

At an evening press conference, official Günter Schabowski read from his notes. Asked when the new rules would begin, he searched his papers and answered that they were effective “immediately, without delay.”

The statement was broadcast. News reports said East Germans could cross the border, and thousands headed for the checkpoints. But border guards had no clear instructions to open them.
At Bornholmer Straße, crowds kept growing. Senior passport-control officer Harald Jäger faced mounting pressure and no workable direction from above. As the situation became harder to contain, Jäger and his colleagues eventually allowed people through.

Crowds streamed into West Berlin. Other checkpoints followed. People climbed onto the Wall, embraced strangers, celebrated, and began chipping away at the concrete.

The Wall did not physically disappear that night, but its political purpose was shattered. The opening became a decisive moment in the collapse of East Germany's communist government and the process leading to reunification in 1990.

A new travel procedure, a spokesman's imprecise answer, a determined crowd, and officers forced to decide in real time turned an announcement into history.

🧩 TRIVIA: The travel regulations were intended to be announced publicly and take effect the next day. The confusion over the timing helped send thousands of East Germans to the border crossings that night.

🌪️ TWIST: The Wall's opening was not the result of a carefully staged ceremony or a single official order. It emerged from a chain reaction: a confusing announcement, rapidly spreading news, enormous public pressure, and border officers forced to make decisions in real time.

🎯 TAKEAWAY: Governments can build walls, write regulations, and issue instructions. But when public pressure overwhelms the system—and the people enforcing it stop believing they can hold the line—political control can collapse with astonishing speed.

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

🎙️ HARVEY'S CORNER

THE NIGHT A BORDER GUARD HAD TO MAKE HISTORY

The orders had not arrived.

The crowds had.

On November 9, 1989, East German border guards at Bornholmer Straße faced a growing crowd demanding passage into West Berlin. They had heard Günter Schabowski's announcement and believed the border was open. The guards had no clear instructions.

The officer responsible was Harald Jäger. Watching the press conference, he had understood that the new travel rules were taking effect immediately. But the regulations had been intended for the following day, and the border system had no plan for the crowds now arriving.

Jäger contacted his superiors. The guidance was inadequate. An attempt to relieve pressure by allowing selected people through and invalidating their identity documents failed: those people could not return, and the crowd kept growing.

The situation was becoming dangerous. Jäger and his colleagues were armed; the people before them were ordinary citizens demanding freedom to travel. The officers had been left to manage a crisis created by their political leadership.

Eventually, Jäger decided to open the crossing. People poured through. The opening at Bornholmer Straße helped trigger the opening of other checkpoints. By midnight, people were moving between East and West Berlin.

There was no grand speech or carefully staged ceremony—only a checkpoint, a crowd, a confused chain of command, and a decision that could not be taken back.

Jäger later described the night as the most terrible and beautiful of his life. He had served the system that divided Berlin; that night, his decision helped bring that division to an end.

History often spotlights presidents, generals, and speechmakers. Sometimes the decisive moment belongs to someone at a gate, waiting for an order that never comes—and deciding what history will remember.

—— ❦ ——

🧬 HUMAN

At Bornholmer Straße stood families, neighbors, friends, and strangers who had lived for decades with a border dividing their city. The opening mattered because ordinary people kept coming—and, at a critical moment, the guards did not fire on them.

—— ❦ ——

🎥 VIDEO REFERENCE — The Fall of the Berlin Wall: November 9, 1989

https://t.co/d3S8UuMtGW

—— ❦ ——

Notice & Tribute: “Harvey's Corner” is an original historical feature inspired by the storytelling tradition of legendary radio broadcaster Paul Harvey (1918–2009). This segment is an independent editorial homage and is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by the Paul Harvey estate or ABC Radio.

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

⚖️ CLOSING

November 9: a date when governments discovered that power is easier to seize, announce, defend, and lose than anyone expects.

Napoleon helped overthrow the Directory and built a new government around himself. The coup was presented as a rescue operation—one preferred description for a military takeover.

Boston became a furnace. Firefighters blew up buildings to stop buildings from burning; the municipal planners had a difficult week.

Max von Baden announced the Kaiser's abdication before the Kaiser authorized it. Even the monarchy's departure announcement got ahead of the paperwork.

Then came Kristallnacht: Nazi leaders organized violence against Jewish communities and disguised it as spontaneous public anger. There was nothing spontaneous about the terror, and nothing remotely amusing about its consequences. The broken glass was only the visible debris of a much larger crime.

In Berlin, a confused official announcement sent thousands toward a border the authorities were not prepared to open. At Bornholmer Straße, Harald Jäger and his colleagues faced a choice no press conference had prepared them to make.

In the end, history has a peculiar way of humiliating the powerful: the coup that was supposed to be impossible succeeds before lunch, the city burns while its planners scramble to contain the damage, the monarchy collapses before the emperor can locate the pen for his formal surrender, and the wall that was supposed to stand forever develops a sudden and unexplained allergy to remaining upright.

Humanity had a plan. History had second thoughts. 🤷‍♂️

─────────────── ◈ ────────────────

✅ QUIZ ANSWER: [B] Prince Max von Baden, the imperial chancellor.

Max von Baden announced Wilhelm II's abdication on November 9 without the Kaiser's authorization. Wilhelm did not formally renounce the throne until November 28. The monarchy was collapsing; the announcement was already public; the emperor was still catching up.

🍬 CANDY

Tomorrow, November 10, brings another serving of questionable judgment: an inventor changing communication, a royal wedding triggering political and religious upheaval, a wartime operation exposing the cost of miscalculation, and ingenuity from unexpected quarters.

The calendar says November 10. History says: don't get comfortable. 👀

Frank Terpil was a former CIA technician who went rogue, working with Third-World strongmen including Idi Amin and Muammar Gaddafi in the 1970s.

Frank made his first sale of an illegal machine gun at just 15 years old in New York. After a stint in the Army, he joined the CIA’s Technical Services Division in 1965 but was fired from the agency six years later. While stationed in India he traded currency on the black market, flying shipments of cash from India into Afghanistan and exchanging them there to take advantage of differences in currency valuation. He made a small fortune.

After leaving the CIA he sold his skills to the highest bidder. For decades he provided weapons, explosives, poisons, and mercenaries to some of the world’s worst terrorists and dictators including Carlos the Jackal, Muammar Gaddafi, and Idi Amin.

By 1973 he was in Libya, helping provide Muammar Gaddafi with weapons, explosives, and former US Army Special Forces soldiers to help train the Libyan army. While working for Idi Amin in Uganda in the late 1970s, Terpil maintained an office on the third floor of the State Research Bureau headquarters. Each day he entered and exited through the courtyard where executions and beheadings regularly took place.

In 1979, when Idi Amin’s government collapsed and he was forced to flee the country, Terpil was onboard Amin’s personal airplane, and watched as cases full of gold bullion were loaded onboard to finance the dictator’s life in exile.

Terpil was arrested in New York City in 1980 during a hotel room bust where they offered undercover detectives suppressed .22lr pistols and rifles, a briefcase bomb, and strychnine poison. Terpil also offered the detectives blueprints for a cigarette lighter and pen he designed, which could be combined to create a silenced pistol. He was released on bail and promptly fled the country.

Terpil eventually settled in Havana, Cuba, under the protection of Fidel Castro. He passed away at home from heart failure in March 2016 following a long decline in his overall health. However, some historians and commentators believe he faked his own death.

Beyond the Icon: Why Myanmar’s Future Can No Longer Hinges on Aung San Suu Kyi

An 81-Year-Old Symbol and a Fractured Land: The Myth of Myanmar’s Single Savior

Myanmar’s Multi-Polar Reality: Why Freedom for Suu Kyi Won’t Fix a Broken State

For four decades, the political discourse surrounding Myanmar in Western capitals and regional forums has revolved around a single, magnetic figure: Daw Aung San Suu Kyi (ASSK). To her supporters, she remains the undisputed symbol of democratic hope; to international observers, her freedom has long been framed as the prerequisite for any legitimate political resolution in Naypyidaw.

Yet, if you are a neighbouring country of Myanmar such as China, Thailand, India or Laos —watching a long-shared border that bears the direct burden of Myanmar’s ongoing friction—it is time for foreign policy analysts to confront uncomfortable truths. Linking the state’s legitimacy exclusively to ASSK is no longer a viable framework for understanding Myanmar’s present, let alone shaping its future.

The Reality of Age and Historical Deficits
First, time is an unyielding factor. At 81 years old, ASSK is in the twilight of her political life. To build an entire international strategy around an octogenarian leader held under house arrest is to ignore both basic biology and political sustainability.

More critically, her political record during her tenure as State Counsellor (2016–2021) leaves a complex, troubled legacy that undermines the notion that she holds a magic key to national unity.

When handed the levers of civilian governance, her administration failed to forge a cohesive national identity. Most notably, her government refused to recognize the Rohingya as indigenous citizens of Myanmar, echoing the military’s terminology by labeling them "Bengalis" or illegal immigrants. Her decision to defend the military against charges of genocide at the International Court of Justice in The Hague fundamentally damaged her global standing and alienated marginalized minorities.

Similarly, her centerpiece domestic policy—the 21st Century Panglong Conferences—failed to achieve its core goal. Despite multi-year summits, her administration was unable to convince the country's powerful Ethnic Armed Organizations (EAOs) to agree on a workable democratic federal union. The peace process stagnated because the ethnic nations viewed her government as operating through a top-down, Bamar-majority lens that offered little structural compromise.

A Fragmented Resistance Horizon
Even if ASSK were to walk free tomorrow, the Myanmar she would re-enter is vastly different from the one she led before the 2021 coup.

The anti-junta resistance along Myanmar’s fringes has irrevocably fractured. Power has shifted to a decentralized network of heavily armed factions: the Arakan Army (AA) in Rakhine, the Myanmar National Democratic Alliance Army (MNDAA) in Kokang, the United Wa State Army (UWSA), the Karen National Liberation Army (KNLA), the Kachin Independence Army (KIA), and various Chin and People's Defense Force (PDF) coalitions.

The battle-tested commanders of these groups—younger, autonomous, and deeply cynical of central Bamar authority—are pursuing their own territorial and political self-determination. They do not operate under ASSK’s directive, nor do they look to her for leadership. The political landscape has evolved past the binary struggle between the National League for Democracy (NLD) and the military hierarchy; it is now a multi-polar reality where no single leader commands universal respect.

Regional Realism: The Pragmatic Calculus
While Western commentators insist that no government in Naypyidaw can claim legitimacy without ASSK’s sanction, Myanmar’s immediate neighbors are operating under a very different set of geopolitical realities.

China, Thailand, Laos, India and other regional stakeholders face urgent security concerns: border trade disruption, refugee flows, illicit arms trade, and transnational crime syndicates. For these nations, engaging with the administration of President Min Aung Hlaing is not an endorsement of military rule, but a matter of statecraft and pragmatic necessity.

Bordering states must deal with the authority that exercises actual control over government institutions, central administration, and major economic corridors. The military regime has established a functional reality on the ground that its neighbors must interact with to maintain regional stability. Denying this diplomatic engagement in favor of a political narrative centered on a single isolated figure is an overstretch of geopolitical facts.

The Way Forward
The international community's attachment to the legacy of ASSK is understandable given her historical role in Myanmar’s struggle for democracy. However, sound diplomacy cannot be built on sentimentality.

Myanmar’s path forward will not be unlocked by waiting for one icon to reconcile a deeply divided nation. True stability will require dealing directly with the complex political landscape as it exists today—engaging with regional realities, addressing the deep-seated autonomy demands of ethnic populations, and accepting that the era of centralized, single-figure politics in Myanmar has come to a close.

$SPCX KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM SPACEX’S Q3 2026 EARNINGS CALL

SpaceX’s results reinforce a significant divergence across the technology and communications investment landscape: scarce, operational AI infrastructure is generating attractive returns, while established connectivity providers face increasingly tangible competitive displacement. The most important market signals are the increase in Q4 capital expenditures to $35 billion to $40 billion, compute pricing above management’s previously discussed range, accelerating Starlink aircraft installations, and the development of a vertically integrated mobile network. The strongest positive implications concern NVIDIA, qualified AI-memory suppliers, power infrastructure, and existing revenue-producing compute capacity. The strongest negative implications concern incumbent aviation connectivity and competing satellite-to-mobile platforms. Importantly, these conclusions do not require acceptance of management’s $500 billion to $1 trillion year-end 2027 annualized revenue aspiration. Magnitudes below describe operating or competitive exposure, not predicted share-price moves; confirmed commercial relationships are distinguished from broader industry implications.

AI INFRASTRUCTURE AND CLOUD

EXISTING COMPUTE CAPACITY BENEFITS FROM SCARCITY PRICING DESPITE SPACEX’S EXPANSION (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies: CoreWeave (CRWV: United States); Nebius Group (NBIS: Netherlands). Direction: Positive for near-term utilization and monetization, strongest for CoreWeave. Magnitude: High for available or repricing capacity, but materially smaller for revenue already committed under fixed-price contracts.

Supporting evidence: SpaceX reported SI revenue of $7.560 billion, up 195% sequentially, and SI adjusted EBITDA of $4.953 billion. Johnsen stated that pricing was “slightly above the high end of the $30 to $50 per watt range” discussed last quarter. Musk said short-term contracts were renewing “at higher dollars per watt, not lower dollars per watt,” and described unsuccessful attempts to obtain additional capacity from other cloud providers.

The immediate read-through is not simply that SpaceX will take business from competing infrastructure providers. The more actionable conclusion is that commissioned compute remains scarce enough for multiple providers to earn attractive returns simultaneously. A competitor entering the market with substantial capacity would ordinarily threaten pricing. SpaceX’s ability to expand revenue while reporting strengthening renewal economics instead suggests that demand is currently absorbing supply additions.

CoreWeave provides independent corroboration. Its September 17 company release disclosed newly signed contracts lasting approximately 3 to 6 months at approximately $40 million of annualized revenue per MW. That explicitly defined annualized metric supports the broader scarcity argument, although it should not be directly compared with SpaceX’s per-watt commentary without reconciling hardware, utilization, and service scope. CoreWeave has identifiable exposure to the repricing mechanism; Nebius benefits through the value of available capacity and future contracting, but existing long-term agreements do not automatically reprice upward.

Near-term catalysts are upcoming earnings disclosures on realized rental rates, utilization, contract renewals, and conversion of installed capacity into revenue. The longer-duration distinction is between energized, billable infrastructure and announced power pipelines. SpaceX’s expansion raises the competitive hurdle for future projects, but it does not negate the current value of operating assets. The positive read-through should therefore favor demonstrated deployment and customer monetization rather than indiscriminate exposure to every announced AI data-center project.

SHORT-DURATION REVENUE MAKES FINANCING QUALITY MORE IMPORTANT, NOT LESS (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected companies: CoreWeave (CRWV: United States); Nebius Group (NBIS: Netherlands). Direction: Negative for the valuation of uncontracted, externally financed expansion; not evidence of an immediate deterioration in existing contracted cash flows. Magnitude: Potentially high for equity value because funding requirements and residual asset values can dominate reported EBITDA.

Supporting evidence: Musk described SpaceX’s approach as renting “at effectively the spot market rate, as opposed to sign these long-term deals.” SpaceX simultaneously raised Q4 capital expenditures to $35 billion to $40 billion. Despite generating $9.631 billion of quarterly operating cash flow, derived from its financial releases, it spent $19.593 billion on capital equipment and infrastructure.

The critical transmission mechanism is the mismatch between long-lived capital commitments and short-duration revenue. High spot prices improve current asset payback, but shorter customer commitments provide less protection against future pricing compression, underutilization, or refinancing constraints. A project can have excellent economics at prevailing rental rates while still requiring substantial equity or debt before those economics are realized.

SpaceX also has a profitable connectivity business and substantial liquidity supporting the buildout. That creates a more demanding competitive financing benchmark for specialized AI infrastructure providers. The read-through is not that their customers disappear; it is that investors should demand stronger evidence of funding coverage and durable project returns before assigning full value to prospective capacity.

CoreWeave and Nebius have important contracted businesses that mitigate this risk. Those contracts must be evaluated individually rather than treated as equivalent to SpaceX’s marginal spot-oriented strategy. The negative implication is concentrated in expansion dependent on future contracts, favorable debt markets, or continued peak pricing.

Near-term trading sensitivity is to financing announcements, capital-expenditure revisions, and the gap between contracted power and revenue-producing capacity. The longer-term fundamental risk emerges when refinancing or hardware replacement occurs under less favorable rental economics. This is a reason for greater differentiation within AI infrastructure equities, not a blanket sector short.

SEMICONDUCTORS AND AI SYSTEMS

NVIDIA RECEIVES A LARGE, NAMED DEMAND SIGNAL THAT DOES NOT DEPEND ON GROK WINNING (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected company: NVIDIA (NVDA: United States). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High strategic and demand significance; the incremental revenue contribution cannot be quantified reliably from the call alone.

Supporting evidence: Management described bringing approximately 200,000 to 220,000 GB300-class units online monthly, predominantly using Vera Rubin for the 2027 expansion, and targeting a 440,000-unit Vera Rubin training cluster by the end of Q2 2027. SpaceX expects 2.5 GW to 3 GW of compute at year-end 2026 and approximately 13 GW by year-end 2027. The draft contains inconsistent hardware labels, so the unit references should not be treated as a precisely standardized shipment schedule.

The direct transmission mechanism is procurement of NVIDIA-based accelerated computing systems. The less obvious implication is that NVIDIA benefits whether SpaceX monetizes this infrastructure through Grok, Cursor, or external cloud customers. Management’s approximately 50% internal and 50% external allocation objective changes which application earns the downstream return, but not the immediate requirement for the underlying compute platform.

NVIDIA’s exposure also extends beyond accelerator chips. Its Rubin platform incorporates CPUs, interconnect, networking, and data-processing components. The architecture therefore offers broader system-content capture than a simple GPU-volume model implies. The call supports NVIDIA’s integrated platform strategy more directly than it supports an assumed order allocation to any particular independent networking vendor.

Near-term catalysts include confirmation of Blackwell deliveries and supplier commentary around SpaceX’s accelerated Q4 spending. The more important fundamental window is 2027 deployment and Rubin conversion. Commissioning dates should not be equated with NVIDIA revenue-recognition dates, and some procurement may already be reflected in existing expectations.

TerraFab does not undermine this near-term conclusion. Management discussed a functional test chip around May or June 2027 and possible volume production in the latter half of 2028. Neither establishes a competitive substitute for NVIDIA’s 2026 or 2027 systems. The high-conviction implication is stronger demand for the existing ecosystem, not an immediate threat from SpaceX-designed or SpaceX-fabricated replacement hardware.

QUALIFIED MEMORY SUPPLIERS BENEFIT FROM RUBIN DEPLOYMENT AND INTERNAL COMPUTE CONSUMPTION (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected companies: Micron Technology (MU: United States); SK hynix (000660: South Korea). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High relevance for AI-memory demand and product mix; SpaceX-specific supplier shares remain undisclosed.

Supporting evidence: The call’s principal hardware commitments are the transition toward Vera Rubin during 2027 and the planned 440,000-unit training cluster. Management also indicated that approximately half of compute could be consumed internally, including substantial inference demand from Grok Bot.

The transmission mechanism is demand for qualified high-bandwidth memory and associated system memory embedded in these platforms. Micron’s March 2026 company announcement identified volume shipments of HBM4 designed for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, alongside SOCAMM2 memory and data-center storage products. SK hynix’s September 2026 technical disclosure showed its HBM4 and SOCAMM2 incorporated into a Vera Rubin system. These establish relevant platform exposure without requiring an unsupported claim that either supplier has received a specific SpaceX allocation.

The important cross-portfolio point is that internal AI usage does not reduce upstream memory demand. Even if application monetization falls short of management’s aspirations, building and operating the announced systems still requires memory. Near-term supplier revenue can therefore remain strong while downstream software returns prove more variable.

The 2027 platform transition is the principal fundamental catalyst. Near-term trading catalysts are supplier disclosures on qualified capacity, customer commitments, pricing, and shipment conversion. Power and cooling delays could defer completed-system deployments, so announced GW should not be converted mechanically into memory revenue.

Geographically, this connects a predominantly US infrastructure expansion with both US and South Korean semiconductor earnings. It also creates overlapping exposure across NVIDIA, Micron, and SK hynix holdings. Owning all of these companies diversifies individual execution risk but does not diversify the underlying AI deployment cycle.

POWER, COOLING, AND ELECTRICAL INFRASTRUCTURE

POWER EQUIPMENT DEMAND CAN PRECEDE GPU INSTALLATION AND DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE WINNING AI MODEL (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies: Vertiv Holdings (VRT: United States); Eaton (ETN: Ireland); Schneider Electric (SU: France). Direction: Positive. Magnitude: High industry demand significance and medium-to-high relevance for their data-center businesses; no incremental SpaceX award to these companies was disclosed on the call.

Supporting evidence: Musk identified the principal constraints as “power and cooling and infrastructure” and discussed targeting approximately 20 GW of incremental power-and-cooling infrastructure during 2027, above the approximately 10 GW incremental compute target. Management also described factory-built modular inference clusters with integrated power and cooling.

The transmission mechanism is demand for electrical distribution, power conversion, backup systems, thermal management, controls, and integrated modular infrastructure. Crucially, management wants power and cooling installed ahead of GPUs. This can shift equipment procurement earlier than compute monetization and makes infrastructure readiness a separate spending priority rather than merely a proportional accessory to chip deliveries.

Vertiv and Eaton have publicly disclosed involvement in NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin infrastructure designs, including modular power-and-cooling systems. Schneider Electric has also disclosed Rubin-related reference designs. Those relationships establish relevant technical positioning, not guaranteed SpaceX market share. The strongest read-through is to the broader infrastructure category and competitive deployment response across the industry.

Near-term catalysts are order intake, lead-time commentary, and backlog conversion over the next several quarters. The longer-duration shift is toward denser, increasingly liquid-cooled and integrated installations, where system engineering and execution matter alongside individual component supply.

SpaceX’s vertical integration is an important limitation. Internal design and manufacturing could reduce its dependence on some external suppliers or pressure component economics. Nevertheless, the combination of large physical requirements and competitors’ need to accelerate their own deployments supports the direction of industry demand. The call does not justify assuming that every dollar of SpaceX infrastructure spending becomes revenue for a listed equipment supplier.

THE POWER BOTTLENECK FAVORS DISPATCHABLE GENERATION AND EXECUTION CAPABILITY OVER GENERIC ELECTRICITY EXPOSURE (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected companies: GE Vernova (GEV: United States); Siemens Energy (ENR: Germany); Solaris Energy Infrastructure (SEI: United States). Direction: Positive for gas-generation equipment and integrated power-delivery services. Magnitude: High sector relevance; company-specific upside depends on awards and commissioning rather than SpaceX’s headline GW target.

Supporting evidence: Musk said turbine blades and vanes were arriving 12 to 18 months behind other turbine components and described applying SpaceX’s casting capabilities to that bottleneck. He also emphasized using multiple power sources while pursuing rapid deployment of incremental compute.

The immediate implication is that access to dispatchable power remains a gating item with substantial economic value. Turbine equipment, balance-of-plant integration, energy management, commissioning, and ongoing maintenance can therefore capture spending even before the associated compute becomes fully productive.

GE Vernova and Siemens Energy provide exposure to generation equipment and service ecosystems. Solaris provides more concentrated exposure to integrated power infrastructure and execution. Its own recent disclosures describe expanded turnkey power-plant scope, batteries, energy-management systems, and additional infrastructure services. The call strengthens the demand rationale for those capabilities; it does not establish a new Solaris contract or permit attribution of SpaceX’s entire planned expansion to any provider.

The non-consensus distinction is between power-equipment demand and merchant electricity-price exposure. A data center served by dedicated generation does not necessarily create an equivalent increase in purchases from the public grid. The geography of Memphis and Southaven, together with management’s emphasis on rapid and modular deployment, supports site-specific generation and infrastructure solutions more clearly than a broad rally in all utilities or power producers.

Near-term catalysts are turbine awards, delivery schedules, emissions approvals, and commissioning milestones. The longer-duration benefit is the service revenue attached to a larger installed generation base. SpaceX manufacturing blades and vanes internally could accelerate deployment, but the call does not demonstrate that SpaceX can replace complete turbine systems or their lifetime service requirements.

SATELLITE AND AVIATION CONNECTIVITY

STARLINK’S CONTRACTED AIRCRAFT ARE BECOMING AN INSTALLATION-DRIVEN EARNINGS THREAT TO INCUMBENTS (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected companies: Viasat (VSAT: United States); SES (SESG: Luxembourg). Direction: Negative. Magnitude: High for competitive positioning in aviation connectivity; consolidated earnings impact depends on customer exposure, contract duration, and migration timing.

Supporting evidence: SpaceX reported approximately 12,000 contracted aircraft, agreements with 3 of the 4 major US carriers, and more than 3,800 equipped aircraft at quarter-end. Management said aviation production had quadrupled since the beginning of 2026 and was expected to double again before year-end. Lufthansa, Swiss, Copa Airlines, Korean Air, Austrian Airlines, and Asiana Airlines began operating Starlink-equipped aircraft during the quarter.

The transmission mechanism is increasingly concrete: signed agreements convert into active aircraft, reducing incumbent opportunities to retain fleets and increasing pricing pressure at renewals. Only approximately 32% of Starlink’s contracted aircraft were equipped at quarter-end. Roughly 8,200 additional aircraft therefore represent a substantial activation pipeline without requiring new contract wins.

This is more important than another announcement that an airline intends to adopt Starlink. Installation bottlenecks can delay competitive displacement for years. Management’s manufacturing ramp and reported activations suggest that deployment is becoming a more consequential source of earnings pressure during 2027.

Viasat faces direct competition in passenger connectivity. SES’s exposure includes Intelsat, whose acquisition it completed in 2025. The pressure can affect service revenue, terminal economics, renewal pricing, and returns on satellite capacity committed to mobility markets. High fixed costs mean that lost revenue or weaker pricing can have a disproportionate effect on segment profitability.

Not all 12,000 contracted aircraft represent existing customers being removed from these providers, and installations do not establish immediate contract termination. Aviation safety communications, government services, and other differentiated applications should also not be treated as interchangeable with passenger broadband.

Near-term catalysts are additional aircraft activations and competitor disclosures on fleet retention, backlog, and revenue per aircraft. The longer-duration threat is a structurally stronger low-Earth-orbit competitor with its own launch capability and an expanding capacity base. This is among the clearest negative fundamental read-throughs in the call.

DIRECT-TO-DEVICE SATELLITE SERVICES

STARLINK’S COMBINED SPECTRUM AND LAUNCH STRATEGY RAISES THE COMPETITIVE HURDLE FOR AST SPACEMOBILE (READ-THROUGH 8)

Affected company: AST SpaceMobile (ASTS: United States). Direction: Negative for competitive scarcity value and future bargaining power. Magnitude: High strategic significance; limited evidence of an immediate change to contracted revenue.

Supporting evidence: Starlink Mobile exceeded 22 million monthly users, up 37% sequentially. Management discussed authorization for 15,000 mobile V2 satellites, a low-band spectrum acquisition, deployment of mobile V2 satellites beginning in 2027, and enhanced service in early 2028.

The transmission mechanism is not simply competition between satellite counts. SpaceX is combining owned launch infrastructure, satellite manufacturing, spectrum access, existing broadband distribution, and a proposed terrestrial network. If successfully deployed, that combination could support lower incremental capacity costs and broader commercial flexibility than a stand-alone wholesale satellite model.

For AST SpaceMobile, the likely pressure points are future operator-contract economics, geographic exclusivity, service differentiation, and the valuation premium assigned to scarce satellite-to-phone capability. Starlink’s expanding carrier relationships and user reach make it less reasonable to assume a lightly contested global market.

There are meaningful offsets. AST SpaceMobile’s operator-aligned model can be attractive to carriers that do not want to support a future retail competitor. Its definitive Verizon relationship illustrates that strategic role. Starlink’s 22 million monthly users are also not equivalent to 22 million paying broadband subscribers, and the call did not demonstrate superior per-user economics or service quality across all relevant use cases.

The highest-conviction conclusion is stronger competition, not technological defeat. Near-term trading catalysts include Starship launches, mobile satellite deployment, spectrum approvals, and new carrier agreements. Fundamental effects on pricing and market share are primarily a 2027 to 2028 issue. The shift from a previously discussed late-2027 service start to early 2028 also preserves an execution window for competing systems.

US WIRELESS TELECOMMUNICATIONS

STARLINK IS BECOMING A POTENTIAL RETAIL COMPETITOR, NOT MERELY A COVERAGE SUPPLIER (READ-THROUGH 9)

Affected companies: T-Mobile US (TMUS: United States); Verizon Communications (VZ: United States); AT&T (T: United States). Direction: Negative for longer-term competitive structure and coverage differentiation. Magnitude: Moderate strategic risk, with low immediate earnings impact from this call.

Supporting evidence: Management said spectrum integration would support becoming “a major mobile carrier in the United States.” The call described using existing Starlink locations for smaller terrestrial radios, while the financial release specified a proposed portfolio of up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band. Enhanced service is targeted for early 2028.

The transmission mechanism is a change in industry relationships. Satellite coverage supplied through existing carriers can improve their products and reduce churn. A standalone SpaceX retail offering could instead compete for the customer relationship, bundle broadband and mobile access, and force incumbent carriers to respond through pricing, retention spending, or satellite partnerships.

T-Mobile has the most direct partner-versus-competitor tension because its T-Satellite service uses Starlink. That existing relationship remains beneficial in the near term. The concern is whether SpaceX’s longer-term retail strategy reduces T-Mobile’s ability to treat satellite coverage as a differentiated feature under its own control.

Verizon and AT&T face a different exposure: potential pressure on coverage-based differentiation and a stronger incentive to develop independent satellite relationships. Their terrestrial networks, spectrum depth, distribution, billing systems, and enterprise relationships remain substantial defenses.

The low-band acquisition improves the credibility of a hybrid strategy, but it does not establish a nationwide network with equivalent urban capacity or indoor performance. Up to 14 MHz of spectrum in the 800 MHz band is not 800 MHz of bandwidth. Nor does a large satellite footprint remove the need for terrestrial densification and network integration.

Near-term trading catalysts are regulatory approvals, network architecture disclosures, retail plans, and changes to existing carrier partnerships. The fundamental threat is primarily beyond 2027. The call supports a higher long-term competitive-risk assessment, not immediate broad reductions to incumbent wireless earnings forecasts.

ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE AND AI APPLICATIONS

CURSOR AND GROK BOT INCREASE COMPETITION FOR PAID CODING AND AGENT BUDGETS, NOT NECESSARILY CORE SOFTWARE SEATS (READ-THROUGH 10)

Affected company: Microsoft (MSFT: United States). Direction: Negative for competitive economics in AI coding and enterprise-agent monetization. Magnitude: Moderate at the product level, low for near-term consolidated earnings.

Supporting evidence: Cursor contributed $608 million of revenue after its August 14 acquisition closing. Management reported 800,000 paid weekly Grok Bot users earlier in October, more than double the preceding month, and a 50% sequential increase in customers exceeding $1 million of run-rate revenue on a pro forma basis including Cursor. SpaceX also announced a combined Grok, Grok Bot, Cursor, and X Premium plan.

The transmission mechanism is increased competition for the incremental budget allocated to coding assistants and autonomous work tools. Cursor brings an established developer workflow and enterprise sales capability. Grok Bot extends the offering into persistent, task-oriented agents. Microsoft competes in the same spending categories through GitHub Copilot and its broader Copilot agent portfolio.

The important implication is pressure on premium

Judge him as creator/innovator creating for the good of humanity

The richest man alive still sleeps on the factory floor and in the hangar because the work isn’t finished. That refusal to cash out is one of the rarest things a civilization can receive.

我的乖乖，真的戳心窝子，兄弟们

看完百亿对冲基金大佬 Bill Ackman 谈马斯克的这段切片，最戳心窝子的根本不是 SpaceX 和特斯拉的万亿估值，而是他提到自己女儿时的那半句话，

身家百亿美金的华尔街巨鳄，可以用钱买下这世上99%的顶级资源，唯独买不回女儿重新看见世界、重新开口说话的生理机能，

而今天唯一能给他女儿带来这种物理希望的 Neuralink，
恰恰来自一个二十年前就可以彻底躺平退休、却偏偏选择继续拿命死磕硬科技的疯子。

很多人总喜欢拿世俗的功利算盘去揣测马斯克为什么还不收手，

却忘了如果当年他在把特斯拉做上市后就去买游艇打高尔夫，

今天人类既不会有占全球过半运力的可回收火箭，更不会有让无数失明失语者重获新生的微米级脑机电极丝。

这就相当于一个早就通关了财富游戏的玩家，非但没有退服养老，反而把赢来的全部金币熔铸成手术刀和发动机，孤身一人去撞人类物理与医学边界上最硬的那堵墙，

所以 Ackman 最后那句感慨才显得格外沉重：当一个人明明拥有随时退场享受人生的特权，却依然留在泥泞的工程第一线替全人类蹚雷，这样的人出现在我们的时代，本身就是整个人类文明最不该被辜负的幸运

text:
She watched him walk out of a garage with a gun and shoot her boyfriend three times in the chest. Then he put a chain around her neck, locked her in a metal shipping container, and kept her there for two months.

Her name is Kala Brown. August 31, 2016. South Carolina.

She and Charlie Carver drove onto a 95-acre property for a cleaning job. The man who hired them was Todd Kohlhepp, a top-selling real estate agent.

He unlocked the gate. Drove them half a mile out of sight of the road. Handed them hedge clippers and water. Said he needed to grab something inside the garage.

Two to five minutes later he walked back out with a gun. Charlie was still standing there holding her hand.

Kohlhepp shot him in the chest three times. Completely calm. No yelling. No rage.

Then he put his arm around her neck and told her to come inside or she would join Charlie.

In the video below she tells what happened next.

He handcuffed her wrists. Cuffed her ankles. Put a ball gag in her mouth. Then he dragged her into a shipping container.

Pitch black. Shelves of dried food and water bottles. He put a chain around her neck, two and a half, three feet long.

Her neck in one corner. Her ankle in the other. Then he left her in the dark.

He came back and raped her. He told her she was his property. That he chose her.

He said Stockholm syndrome would kick in and they would be happy together. She realized the only way to stay alive was to make him think it was working.

Did she survive? Yes. Deputies found her on November 3, 2016, after about two months.

She heard voices outside and started screaming and hitting the walls. When the door opened and she saw police uniforms, she cried.

The first thing she asked them was to get Charlie off that property.

Did he pay? Todd Kohlhepp pleaded guilty to seven murders, kidnapping, and first-degree criminal sexual conduct.

Seven consecutive life sentences plus 60 years. No parole. No appeal.

Some people will say a couple answering a stranger's Facebook job offer on a remote farm was reckless.
Others will say the man who sold houses for a living looked safe until the second he pulled the trigger.

She walked out of that container alive. Charlie never walked out of that gate.

When a woman survives two months chained in a box by a serial killer who shot the man she loved in front of her, what exactly counts as justice?
