Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, is seen at 0.2%, less than September's 0.3%. There won't be a year-over-year CPI number because of last year's government shutdown. Beyond CPI, Fed speeches and Treasury auctions pepper the week, with several Fed speakers today. A 10-year Treasury note auction Tuesday and a 30-year auction Thursday might be watched for demand signals, with yields lower than the last time these durations were auctioned. "Generally speaking, if you get a weak demand, that can be a little bit concerning," said Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at SCFR. "But demand has generally held up, and I think that should continue given the relative attractiveness of where yields are today." On Friday, the University of Michigan's preliminary November Consumer Sentiment report exceeded expectations. It was the second recent survey that showed consumers' mood improving.
 
Technical stumble assessed: Even before Thursday's selloff, the market had suffered immense technical damage since the tech-dominated Nasdaq hit an all-time high in early October. Thursday's move suggests technical weakness might have pushed selling into overdrive as investors sought perceived safety outside equities. "A lot of key technical levels were violated," including 7,600 in the S&P 500 Index that had been long-term support, noted Nathan Peterson, director of derivatives research and strategy at SCFR. Other levels violated included the 200-day moving averages for the Nasdaq and Nasdaq 100. Liquidation by hedge funds appeared to be a factor. If selling continues, Peterson will look for possible capitulation in the Relative Strength Indexes (RSI) of the major indexes, a momentum indicator. The RSI of both the Nasdaq 100 and the PHLX Semiconductor Index (SOX) dropped under 30 on Thursday, a traditional oversold hallmark, though being under 30 doesn't guarantee a quick reversal. A move back above 30 for the RSI in either index is among possible signs that capitulation was reached.

The conglomerate's operating profit totaled $12.7 billion, down 5.8% from the previous year. Net earnings also declined amid weakness in Berkshire's insurance operations. Buybacks accelerated dramatically, however. The firm repurchased $9.6 billion of its shares during the period, versus $4.5 billion in the second quarter. text:
Public venture capital (VC) can equalize the playing field for Smart City as a Service (SCaaS) projects by mitigating market failures that favor only massive tech conglomerates or hyper-wealthy municipalities.
Traditional venture capital demands rapid, high-margin, software-centric scalability, while public procurement favors massive, established contractors who can absorb long sales cycles and dense regulatory overhead. This leaves smaller, innovative SCaaS startups and mid-to-lower-tier cities priced out of the ecosystem.
Public venture capital directly corrects these imbalances in five key ways:

1. Absorbing the "First-Loss" Risk for Early-Stage Projects

Infrastructure development often fails at inception because the timeline is long, upfront capital is heavy, and outcomes are highly uncertain. Public VC funds act as patient capital or "first-loss absorbers". By providing early-stage mezzanine finance or concept development equity, they absorb structural risks that scare off purely profit-driven investors. This allows small, specialized SCaaS startups to build out their core technologies without needing an immediate 10x commercial return.

2. Shifting Metrics from Financial ROI to Civic Value

Traditional private equity prioritizes direct revenue-producing metrics. However, the most critical smart city components—like flood prevention, predictive road maintenance, and civic GovTech platforms—offer complex returns measured in quality of life, citizen satisfaction, and long-term cost efficiency rather than immediate cash flow. Public VC explicitly invests based on social and civic return on investment (ROI), funding vital public services that private capital typically ignores.

3. Funding Regulatory Compliance and Procurement Hurdles

One of the steepest barriers for independent SCaaS providers is navigating fragmented stakeholder ecosystems, public procurement laws, and localized zoning policies. Large tech firms have massive legal and lobbying budgets to survive these multi-year processes. Public VC provides startups with the prolonged financial runway and institutional alignment necessary to withstand public sector sales cycles, successfully transforming policy awareness into policy integration.

4. Creating Regulatory Sandboxes and De-Risking Partnerships

When a public or municipal venture fund backs an SCaaS project, they bring more than money—they bring the city itself as an innovation platform. Public VC inherently facilitates municipal partnerships, opening doors to data integration, public physical assets, and regulatory sandboxes. This de-risks adoption for conservative local governments, giving smaller SCaaS providers a legitimate mechanism to pilot, refine, and prove their interoperability with legacy city infrastructure.

5. Democratizing Technology Across Smaller Cities

Without public intervention, cutting-edge smart city developments remain concentrated in wealthy, tier-one global hubs. By creating state, regional, or federally backed public venture funds, governments can pool regional SCaaS projects and aggregate demand. This reduces transaction costs, creates localized ecosystems, and allows mid-sized or underfunded municipalities to lease advanced digital solutions on a subscription (SCaaS) basis, rather than being forced to build multi-million dollar tech frameworks from scratch.

text:
Seiberling Mansion, Historic Indiana
"In the 1880s and ‘90s, eastern Indiana experienced massive economic growth after the discovery of abundant natural gas, which the state offered for free to manufacturers willing to relocate to Indiana. The Gas Boom ended in the early twentieth century, but its architectural legacy endures.

Built for Monroe Seiberling in 1891, the imposing Neo-Jacobean and Romanesque Revival mansion at 1200 West Sycamore Street served as the Seiberling family home until 1901. Formerly of Akron, Ohio and uncle to Goodyear Tire and Rubber founder Frank Seiberling, Monroe Seiberling came to the city to found the Kokomo Strawboard Company. He subsequently sold the business and opened the Diamond Plate Glass Company — another Gas Boom manufacturer.

For much of the early twentieth century the house belonged to George Kingston, inventor of the Kingston Carburetor. The mansion later served as the original home of Indiana University-Kokomo; the Historical Society assumed stewardship in 1971 and restored the house as a museum."

text:
James Gunn's official statement:

"Oh, boy. What a four years.

Thanks to all of you who have supported me and Peter in our time as the heads of DC Studios.

When I was a kid growing up in Manchester, Missouri, I used to write and draw my own comics with a mix of DC Comics characters and my own characters. Having full access to these characters to do whatever we wanted has been a dream come true. I didn’t know if I wanted this job when it was offered to me, but I just couldn’t pass up the unique opportunity. I’m glad I took the job.

But what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least. I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I’m always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I’ve stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years (Jenn, I love you and I’m sorry and you don’t need to feel guilty for being the happiest of all people that I’m no longer doing this job). And the thing my ADHD hyperfocus has had the most difficulty with has been dividing my time between projects I’m incredibly passionate about and the ones I’m not so much and all the things I have to do as a studio head.

There have been so many highs along the way – releasing Superman and Clayface, making Peacemaker, reading the scripts to The People Vs, the entire process of Man of Tomorrow, which thus far has been the best filmmaking experience of my life, and numerous other moments.

The highest of the highs have been all the talented and wonderful people I’ve worked with and grown to love: the DC Studios crew, our talented collaborators, our casts and crews, and the boisterous and hilarious fans. And the best part of all has been working with Peter Safran, the smartest and most competent person I know. You’ve been the best partner a person could ask for, and, more so, a truly good friend.

So, yes, I will miss the people around me, and I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I’m also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking.

That’s not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we’ve just been engaged on another DC project which I’m writing, and we’ll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we set up will live on.

Thank you so very, very much for embracing the characters and stories we’ve put on screen.

Love and gratitude,

James Gunn"

Via: @JamesGunn on Threads

🩷 I Don’t Want to Waste This Life I’ve Been Given. 🩷

I’ve been thinking a lot about life lately. How precious it is, how quickly it passes, and how easy it can be to get caught up in things that really don’t matter.

I’ve lived long enough to know that tomorrow isn’t promised to any of us. I’ve experienced difficult days, frightening moments, heartbreak, and loss. But I’ve also experienced incredible kindness, love, laughter, and the simple beauty of being alive.

And one thing I know for certain is this:

I don’t want to waste this life I’ve been given.

I want to wake up excited about the possibilities of a new day. I want to keep learning, exploring, growing, and discovering things I’ve never experienced before.

I want to love people while they’re here to receive that love. I want to offer kindness without expecting anything in return. I want to laugh more, worry less, and appreciate the little things that make life so extraordinary.

And I want to remind others that it’s never too late to begin again, try something new, or find a reason to smile.

We don’t have to accomplish something extraordinary every day to live an extraordinary life.

Sometimes it’s planting a seed. Sometimes it’s watching a sunrise. Sometimes it’s reaching out to someone who needs a little encouragement. And sometimes it’s simply sitting quietly, grateful for another beautiful day.

None of those moments are wasted.

There is still so much life to live, so much beauty to discover, and so much good we can bring into this world.

Whatever season of life you’re in, I hope you remember that your story isn’t finished. There are still chapters waiting to be written, memories waiting to be made, and possibilities you haven’t even imagined yet.

Don’t let the noise of the world steal the joy of being here.

Be kind. Be curious. Love deeply. Find your peace. And never stop looking for the beauty in this life.

I don’t want to simply count my days. I want to make my days count. 🩷

There is always something to discover, if we never stop looking.

REAGAN GAVE 2.7 MILLION ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS AMNESTY. WHAT HAPPENED NEXT SHOULD BE REQUIRED READING BY POTUS and CONGRESS.

Washington is discussing legalization again. Before anyone promises that another immigration deal will finally solve the problem, consider what happened in 1986.

Be aware granting amnesty creates a lifelong benefit loving, welfare dependent, Democrat voter. Every time.

President Ronald Reagan signed the Immigration Reform and Control Act, granting legal status to approximately 2.7 million unauthorized immigrants.

The deal was supposed to combine legalization with enforcement against employers hiring unauthorized workers.

Here is what happened to the estimated unauthorized population afterward:

1986: 3.2 million 

1988: 1.9 million

2000: 8.5 million

2007: 12.4 million

2023: 14 million

The initial reduction was a small dip, but what followed was substantial growth. 

Understand more didn't accept it than did. They knew they would lose their jobs if FLSA, OSHA, and taxes were suddenly applied they also would be required to renounce their existing citizenship.

Legalization did not permanently eliminate unauthorized immigration as promised. And the employer sanctions included in the 1986 law did not prevent millions more from entering or remaining unlawfully.

Source: Congressional Research Service, RL33874; Migration Policy Institute, Immigration Laws Since 1986; Pew Research Center, 2025.

BUT THERE IS ANOTHER CONSEQUENCE THAT DESERVES ATTENTION: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN MILLIONS OF PEOPLE EVENTUALLY BECOME VOTERS?

Reagan's amnesty provided a route to permanent residence and citizenship.

And the political effects have actually been studied.

Research examining the 1986 legalization found that counties with larger concentrations of legalized immigrants subsequently experienced increases in Democratic presidential vote share.

Now look at Pew Research's validated voter data.

Among naturalized American citizens:

2020: Biden 59%, Trump 38%.

2024: Harris 51%, Trump 47%.

That's a 21-point Democratic advantage in 2020, shrinking to four points in 2024.

The political preferences of naturalized citizens clearly aren't fixed. But legalization can eventually change the electorate, and the effects can be substantial when millions of people are involved.

Source: Pew Research Center, June 26, 2025; CESifo Working Paper 10554.

NOW ENTER REPRESENTATIVE MARÍA ELVIRA SALAZAR AND THE DIGNITY ACT.

Salazar's proposal would allow qualifying unauthorized immigrants to obtain renewable legal status, work authorization, and protection from deportation.

Her principal Dignity Program is the first step to provide a path to citizenship.

The economic question remains.

What prevents another unauthorized workforce from developing after the current one receives legal status?

Employers still need labor and aren't going to pay them full price.

Some industries argue they cannot find enough Americans willing to accept the wages and conditions offered. Wages are the key and exactly what is harming our workforce.

When businesses depend on access to vulnerable workers, legalization alone does not eliminate the incentives that can encourage future unauthorized hiring.

And Americans should ask whether expanding the labor supply will reduce pressure on employers to raise wages, improve working conditions, and invest in productivity.

THEN THERE IS THE SAVE AMERICA ACT.

The SAVE America Act would require documentary proof of citizenship for federal voter registration and photo identification for voting.

It is also a clear sign that most Americans recognize the threat and might be unwilling to directly tell a pollster to deport them, but willing to say our vote needs to be protected from illegals. 

But there is a distinction Congress should make absolutely clear.

Verifying citizenship today does not answer who may become a citizen tomorrow.

Those are separate policy decisions.

And when Congress debates immigration legalization, Americans deserve to understand the eventual consequences for employment, public finances, and the electorate.

HERE IS WHAT I WANT CONGRESS TO ANSWER.

How many people would qualify for legalization?

How many could eventually become citizens?

What protections would prevent another unauthorized workforce from developing?

Pretty much the same questions that Ronald Reagan put to congress and was naive enough to accept.

Would employers face meaningful consequences for knowingly hiring unauthorized workers?

And what measurable improvement in American wages and employment should voters expect?

Reagan's 1986 legislation legalized millions. Yet the unauthorized population eventually grew to several times its immediate post-amnesty level.

In no way did California benefit from this action. Grades slid, crime soared, and the 'California Dreamin' culture was overridden with flags from Mexico.

Before Washington repeats any part of that experiment, Americans deserve the numbers, the enforcement plan, and an explanation of what will actually be different this time.

text:
It’s one of the earliest and most important baseball cards of all time: the 1869 Cincinnati Red Stockings Peck & Snyder trade card. Led by Harry and George Wright, the Red Stockings - baseball’s first all-professional team - toured the nation and went undefeated for ninety-two consecutive games. Because of their dominance, the team was a legend in its own day, though at the time, of course, no one could have imagined the impact it would have on the game. Just two years later, the National Association, baseball’s first all-professional league, was formed in large part because of the success of the Red Stockings. Shortly thereafter, in 1876, the National Association gave way to the National League, and baseball officially became big business. By any definition, the 1869 Cincinnati Red Stockings trade card is one of the earliest of all baseball cards and one of the few collecting icons representing the birth of both professional baseball and the “baseball card.” Several known varieties of cards feature this classic team pose of the 1869 Red Stockings. The smaller CDV style is known with several different backs; most known examples are blank-backed. The larger Peck & Snyder trade card is recognized as the most desirable of the several card styles featuring this image of the 1869 Reds, both because the players are identified on the front of the card and because this style features advertising for Peck & Snyder’s “Base Ball and Sportsman’s Emporium” (“126 Nassau Street, New York”) on the reverse. The offered example is the most desirable style, with red printing on the mount and with the classic Peck & Snyder advertising on the reverse.

It will be part of our Fall Catalog Auction opening on November 20.

text:
Democrat Operative ADMITS: We’ve Been Committing MASSIVE Mail-in Vote Fraud for Decades

bySelwyn Duke

“There is no race in New Jersey — from city council to United States Senate — that we haven’t worked on,” states the Democrat operative. He also reveals that such efforts, which extend far beyond New Jersey, “could be enough to flip states.”

The operative is talking about what mainstream media assure us is no problem: vote fraud. In fact, the operative’s specialty is fraud effected via mail-in ballots — a voting method Democrats want to implement nationwide for the presidential election using COVID-19 concerns as a pretext.

The man, described as a “top Democratic operative” by the New York Post, has been committing mail-in vote fraud “on a grand scale, for decades,” writes the paper. The Post spoke to him under the condition of anonymity, but confirmed his identity and reveals that he’s a Bernie Sanders partisan indifferent to both major-party candidates on the ballot. He has a warning, too.

There “is going to be a f–king war coming November 3rd over this stuff,” he told the Post. But if “they knew how the sausage was made,” he added, “they could fix it.”

The operative sure knows — and he explained, in detail, how mail-in vote fraudsters have been stealing elections for years.

The Democrat admits to not only altering ballots himself, but to having led vote-fraud teams and to training at least “20 operatives in New Jersey, New York and Pennsylvania — a critical 2020 swing state,” writes the Post. And how many have those trainees trained, as this mushrooms?

We don’t know. What is certain is that in an “election that is swayed by 500 votes, 1,000 votes — it can make a difference,” the paper related the tipster as warning. “It could be enough to flip states.”

The Architecture of Electoral Artifice
Relating the fraud’s mechanics, the Post informs that in New Jersey, for example, voters receive a mail-in ballot and “certificate of mail in voter” (which the voter must sign) in a large envelope. Unbelievably, however, the ballot has no “specific” security features; thus, the operative explains, he’d just replicate them using a copying machine.
But the envelopes are more secure and can’t easily be recreated. So the Democrat said that he and his team would go to residences and offer to mail in voters’ ballots as a public service. They’d then go home and use an old-fashioned method:

Over boiling water, they’d “steam it [the envelope] to loosen the glue,” the insider told the Post.

“He then would remove the real ballot, place the counterfeit ballot inside the signed certificate, and reseal the envelope,” the paper continued.

“‘Five minutes per ballot tops,’ said the insider.”

Here’s what scary: I recently reported on how mail-in vote fraud was so bad in Patterson, New Jersey, during a May 12 special election that a judge ordered that a new election be held. Yet, points out the insider, that vote-fraud operation was only uncovered because it was amateurish: 900 ballots were found in just a few mailboxes.

“‘If they had spread them in all different mailboxes, nothing would have happened,’ the insider said,” the Post further tells us. Of course, this raises a question:

How many elections are stolen so professionally that the fraud is never exposed?

Why the Democrats Love the Post Office
The operative also revealed that anti-Trump/Republican postal workers help facilitate the fraud. Sometimes, for instance, they’ll simply throw away ballots coming from GOP strongholds. In other cases, “mail carriers were members of his [the insider’s] ‘work crew,’ and would sift ballots from the mail and hand them over to the operative,” writes the Post.

Conning the Elderly
Another “gold mine” for votes is nursing homes. In some facilities “‘the nurse is actually a paid operative. And they go room by room by room to these old people who still want to feel like they’re relevant,’ said the whistleblower,’” the Post relates. “[They] literally fill it [the ballot] out for them.”
When You Can’t Fake the Ballot, Fake the Voter
Yet another trick is voter impersonation. Remember when United Nations observers monitored our 2012 election — for fear of “vote suppression” by Republicans — but instead registered shock at how many states require no voter identification?

This not-a-bug-but-a-feature defect allows fraudsters to vote under someone else’s name. “The best targets were registered voters who routinely skip presidential or municipal elections — information which is publicly available,” the Post tells us.
Actually, though, the best targets may be voters who’ve recently moved from their districts, who are great in number in inner cities. Note that their identities are often known by Democrat operatives called “apartment captains” or “block captains,” as I reported in 2005. This is one reason why inner cities are vote-fraud hotbeds.

Whomever is being impersonated, the con is the same. “You fill out these index cards with that person’s name and district and you go around the city and say, ‘You’re going to be him, you’re going to be him,’ the insider said of how he dispatched his teams of dirty-tricksters,” the Post also relates.
Note that after I left the Bronx, anyone who knew I’d departed could have voted in my name. All they had to do was show up, say “I’m Selwyn Duke” and sign my name.

The operative also related how he and his crew would bribe susceptible voters, such as vagrants — who come cheap.

Summing up, the Post writes that organizationally, “the tipster said, his voter-fraud schemes in the Garden State and elsewhere resembled Mafia organizations, with a boss (usually the campaign manager) handing off the day-to-day managing of the mob soldiers to the underboss (him). The actual candidate was usually kept in the dark deliberately so they could maintain ‘plausible deniability.’”

           ❗️❗️THE COSMIC SIGNIFICANCE❗️❗️

Govardhan Puja falls on Kartik Shukla Pratipada, the first tithi of the waxing lunar fortnight.

Traditionally, Shukla Paksha represents increasing light, renewal and the movement towards fullness. Pratipada carries the symbolism of a fresh beginning.

In 2026, the observance falls on Tuesday, 10 November, according to the stated Udaya Tithi convention.

🔴Tuesday is associated with Mangal (Mars) in Vedic astrology.

🚩Mars symbolises courage, initiative, land, strength, protection and decisive action.

🚩The Govardhan story offers a meaningful reflection on the higher expression of strength: not aggression, but the courage to protect.

🪐PLANETARY SYMBOLISM THROUGH DEVOTION

These are reflective associations within devotional and astrological interpretation not guaranteed planetary remedies or compulsory rules.

🌅 Surya: Wheat and nourishing preparations can symbolically represent vitality, confidence and life-giving energy.

🌙 Chandra: Milk, rice and kheer evoke nourishment, emotional steadiness and peace of mind.

🔴 Mangal: Red lentils and acts of protection symbolise courage, discipline and constructive action.

🌿 Budh: Green vegetables and thoughtful learning represent intelligence, communication and discernment.

📚 Guru: Yellow foods, knowledge-sharing and book donations reflect wisdom, dharma and generosity.

🤍 Shukra: Milk-based sweets and kheer symbolise harmony, refinement, relationships and comforts.

⚫ Shani: Black sesame and service to the disadvantaged invite humility, responsibility and compassion.

☊ Rahu: Unusual or diverse food offerings may be used as a contemporary symbolic reflection on desire, diversity and attachment.

☋ Ketu: Simple offerings and spiritual contemplation can represent detachment, introspection and inner awakening.

Some contemporary astrological interpretations also connect Govardhan with Ketu's themes of detachment and spiritual insight. This is an interpretive association, not a universally established classical rule.

🌆INDIA'S REGIONAL EXPRESSIONS

The post-Diwali period carries several beautiful traditions across India. Their names and rituals are connected through the festive calendar, but they are not all identical observances.

▫️ Braj, Uttar Pradesh and parts of North India: Govardhan Puja, symbolic hillocks made from cow dung, flowers, parikrama and worship of cows and bulls.

▫️ Mathura and Vrindavan: Govardhan Parikrama, approximately 21 km, temple celebrations, bhajans and Annakut offerings.

▫️ Nathdwara, Rajasthan: Special Shrinathji darshan and the celebrated Annakut tradition.

▫️ Gujarat: Bestu Varas, the Gujarati New Year, with Chopda Puja and the beginning of new business account books.

▫️ Maharashtra and other regions: Bali Pratipada or Padwa, associated with King Bali and the Vamana Avatar, alongside regional family traditions.

▫️ Some communities: Vishwakarma worship, honouring tools, instruments, craftsmanship and the dignity of labour.

Different traditions. Different expressions. One beautiful civilisational spirit of gratitude, devotion and renewal.

3/5 | ANNAKUT: WHEN GRATITUDE TAKES THE FORM OF FOOD

Annakut literally means a mountain of food.

It is an offering of gratitude to Shri Krishna for the nourishment provided by nature and the abundance that sustains life.

Temples and households prepare a variety of cooked dishes, sweets, fruits, grains and other offerings.

Some traditions offer Chhappan Bhog : 56 preparations; others may offer 108 or a different number according to family and temple customs.

A popular devotional explanation connects 56 Bhog with Krishna's seven days beneath Govardhan: eight meals a day multiplied by seven days.

The number is a traditional devotional explanation, not a compulsory rule for every household.

🪔 HOME PUJA | SAMAGRI

Keep the arrangements simple and devotional:
▫️ Roli and akshat (unbroken rice) 
▫️ Fresh flowers and Tulsi 
▫️ Ghee diya and incense 
▫️ Water, fruits and sweets 
▫️ Krishna's idol or picture 
▫️ Cooked food for Annakut 
▫️ Cow dung, clean clay, rice or grains for a symbolic Govardhan mound

🕉️TRADITIONAL GOVARDHAN PUJA VIDHI

🪷 1. Preparation and Purification
Clean the home and place of worship. Sprinkle Ganga Jal according to family tradition.

🌿 2. Creation of Govardhan
Prepare a symbolic Govardhan hill using cow dung, traditionally decorated with flowers, leaves and natural elements.

🪔 3. Worship of Govardhan Maharaj
Offer flowers, Kumkum, Akshata, sweets and prayers. Perform Parikrama around the symbolic Govardhan.

🐄 4. Gau Puja

Bathe and decorate cows and bulls where customary. Offer appropriate fodder, fresh water and loving care.

🦚 5. Shri Krishna Abhishek and Shringar

In temples and households following this tradition, the Krishna deity is ceremonially bathed with milk and adorned with beautiful garments and ornaments.

🍲 6. Annakut Bhog

Prepare 56 Bhog (Chhappan Bhog), 108 preparations or a variety of traditional vegetarian dishes according to family and temple customs.

🪷 7. Aarti and Prasad Distribution

Offer Bhog, perform Aarti and distribute Prasad among family, friends and the community.

🍇THE SIGNIFICANCE OF ANNAKUT

• Food is a divine blessing, not something to waste.

• Nature is the foundation of nourishment.

• Sharing food is an expression of compassion.

• Gratitude is the foundation of true abundance.

In some household and temple traditions, Krishna's deity is also ceremonially bathed with milk and adorned with fresh clothes and ornaments.

Where cow and bull worship is customary, animals may be respectfully bathed and decorated. Their comfort, safety and suitable food must always come first.

👉🏻Remember: The deepest offering is not the size of the feast. It is the willingness to share it.

Let no celebration remain confined to our own homes. Let someone in need also experience its blessings.

text:
Yes. Carolina Gold Rice was grown in Texas, although it is most strongly associated with the coastal regions of South Carolina and Georgia where it became famous in the 1700s and 1800s.

When commercial rice production expanded in the United States during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, some Carolina Gold seed stock was brought west and planted in Texas and Louisiana. Over time, however, growers largely switched to newer rice varieties that offered higher yields and better disease resistance, and Carolina Gold Rice nearly disappeared as a commercial crop.

Today, the variety is primarily grown as a specialty heirloom rice by preservation-minded farmers such as Tidewater Grain Co., which identifies itself as a major grower of Carolina Gold Rice. [https://t.co/IxRpw7CGxR]

An interesting Texas connection is that the modern Texas rice industry began in the coastal prairie region around Beaumont, Orange, Eagle Lake, and the Gulf Coast, and some of the earliest rice varieties planted there were derived from rice grown in the Carolinas before newer strains took over.

So the short answer is:

Yes, Carolina Gold Rice was grown in Texas.
It originated and became famous in South Carolina and Georgia.
It was later planted in Texas and Louisiana as rice cultivation moved westward.
It eventually declined and was replaced by modern commercial varieties.
It has been revived in recent years as a heritage crop. [https://t.co/IxRpw7CGxR]

If you're interested, I can also trace whether Carolina Gold was grown in the Eagle Lake / Colorado County area of Texas, where much of Texas' early rice history is centered.

Help, from the government is not coming. We are on our own.

So be your brother‘s keeper look out for your neighbors. Think of sending your kids to school with an extra sandwich if that you can to offer a child who does not have food that day.

For those wealthy people, consider calling your local schools to see how many children have accounts at school for food and pay that off. 
Consider starting a program at these schools for the weekend where you can provide them with bags of groceries to get them through the weekend beans, rice, potatoes, milk, eggs, and yes, put that in a refrigerated bag that they can take home after school on Fridays to help them get through the weekend with their families.

Make sure you are enrolling your kids in food assistance programs at school so they can eat there usually breakfast and lunch.
Some local churches also offer a really great meal once a week that you can go and pay for usually no more than $20 for the entire family, and they also offer food support. It doesn’t hurt to call.

Streamline you’re driving to places you need to go so you minimize using the gas that’s so expensive.

These politicians are going to spend months arguing in committee about the current administration and what they can do to terrorize them, nothing said about us and our kids who are hungry, nothing said about us, at all. 
Nothing said about us that we can afford to go to the doctor because we can’t.
Stay alive, stay healthy, and survive. We are in this together.

THEY LAUGHED WHEN SHE STARTED SELLING FOOD BY THE ROADSIDE. YEARS LATER, THEY WERE APPLYING TO WORK FOR HER.

When Beatrice lost her job, she had two options.

She could spend months searching for another job or find a way to earn an income immediately.

She chose the second option.

With her little savings, she bought cooking equipment and started selling rice and stew beside a busy road.

Some former colleagues mocked her.

One even asked whether she had abandoned her education to become a roadside food seller.

Beatrice pretended not to hear.

She focused on improving the quality of her food and treating customers well.

She woke up early every morning, purchased fresh ingredients and ensured her customers received good value.

Initially, she sold only a few plates.

But people started recommending her food.

Within a year, she had enough customers to employ two assistants.

Three years later, she opened her first restaurant.

Five years later, she had three outlets.

One afternoon, a former colleague who had mocked her walked into the restaurant looking for a job.

Beatrice recognised him immediately.

She didn't insult him.

She simply asked him to submit his CV and attend the interview like every other applicant.

After the interview, she offered him a position.

When someone asked why she had hired a person who once ridiculed her, she replied:

"My business is built on food and opportunity. I don't need to turn someone's past mistakes into my future behaviour."

LESSON: Never despise humble beginnings. Honest work is never shameful. What matters is the value you create, not how impressive your starting point looks to others.

Madueke has benefitted from playing regularly. And it’s high time Arsenal fans totally backed him. He’s going to be very present this season. 

The whole of last season, he didn’t finish a single Premier League game but he has played every minute of four of Arsenal’s last five league matches. 

Why that has happened is because he had a good break the last time and Arteta said he worked the hardest during that period. His hard work has been rewarded with game time, but that’s also been helped by the fact that Saka is injured. 

Madueke has become a legitimate rival to Saka on the right wing, and it’s a rivalry both players will relish. 

Unknown to many, Saka and Madueke are very close friends. They’ve been close since their childhood and their fathers are longtime friends too. It’s a friendly rivalry. 

Before Arsenal signed Madueke, Saka and Rice gave recommendations for him. 

Saka’s body has been through it. Before he turned 22, he’d played 139 Premier League games. Only six players have played more at the same age in the history of the Premier League. 

Remember when he started 87 consecutive games for Arsenal? That’s a longstanding Arsenal record he broke. He paid for it with his body. 

His body is shot. 

Since October 2023, Saka has suffered 9 separate injuries. He’s not as explosive, and you can tell in how Arsenal are evolving his game. 

He played a total of 49 games last season but suffered three different injuries to his hamstring, hip and Achilles. 

Madueke, at the same time is beginning to offer the required directness and work rate, with the end product slightly better too. His game is also evolving in his movement and reading of space. His timing is better. He’s been Arsenal’s most improved player over the last month. 

When Saka gets back, both players have to share those minutes as much as possible, to preserve the physical condition of one, and keep the other positive and in continuation of his improvement journey. 

They’re both promising footballers who can become even better.

text:
Trump Makes His Moves to Position Marco Rubio for 2028! Immigration Reform Changes the Game, DeSantis Distances Himself, and Ted Cruz Bets on Winning Back Texas

Trump is changing the rules of the political game while much of the Republican leadership remains trapped in the rhetoric that has just led the party to a devastating electoral defeat.

Donald Trump's unexpected willingness to negotiate immigration reform with Democrats is much more than a change in rhetoric. In my analysis, we are witnessing a political maneuver designed to turn the Republican Party's 2026 electoral defeat into an opportunity to regain Hispanic support and prepare for the 2028 presidential succession.

Trump is changing the rules of the game while much of the Republican leadership remains trapped in the rhetoric that has just led the party to a devastating electoral defeat.

And there is one figure I consider central to this strategy: Marco Rubio.

After Republicans lost control of both chambers of Congress, Trump publicly acknowledged that his deportation policies had been too harsh. He admitted that his administration had ended up hurting people who had spent 10 to 15 years working in the United States, paying taxes, and contributing to the economy.

Then he did something few expected: he expressed his willingness to negotiate immigration reform with Democrats.

This is no minor development.

For years, immigration was one of the main sources of confrontation between Republicans and Democrats. Now Trump has introduced a possibility capable of reshaping relations between the two parties and altering electoral calculations ahead of 2028.

My thesis is that Trump is trying to recover lost ground, rebuild his relationship with Hispanic voters, and open a political path that could benefit Marco Rubio as his eventual presidential successor.

Immigration Reform: The Move That Puts Democrats in a Difficult Position

For years, Democrats have advocated immigration reform that would provide solutions for millions of undocumented immigrants.

Now they face an opportunity they could hardly have imagined: negotiating that reform with the very president who made mass deportations one of his central campaign promises.

Beginning January 3, 2027, Democrats will control both chambers of Congress.

But that majority also means they will have to make decisions and assume responsibility.

What will they do if Trump introduces a proposal allowing immigrant workers who have lived in the United States for years to obtain legal status?

Will they refuse to negotiate a reform they have demanded for so long?

Or will they accept the conditions of a Republican president to achieve a historic agreement?

This is the political maneuver: Trump is placing Democrats in a position where either response could carry electoral consequences.

If Democrats reject the proposal, Trump will attempt to blame them for blocking a solution for millions of immigrants.

If they agree to negotiate and ultimately approve a reform, Trump will be able to present himself as the president who achieved an immigration agreement that previous administrations failed to deliver.

That does not mean Democrats lack the power to negotiate their own terms. Nor does it mean Trump can impose whatever proposal he wants.

But the president has just regained the political initiative on one of the most sensitive issues for Hispanic voters.

And that initiative could ultimately become a defining part of his legacy.

Marco Rubio: The Piece Trump Wants to Position on the Presidential Chessboard

This is where Marco Rubio enters the picture.

The secretary of state possesses several characteristics that make him an important figure in the Republican succession: he is the son of Cuban immigrants, speaks Spanish, has a long political career in Florida, and understands major issues involving Latin America.

Trump has mentioned him among the leaders who could play an important role in the Republican Party's future.

He has also mentioned JD Vance, meaning no official successor has yet been designated.

Nevertheless, my interpretation goes beyond Trump's public statements.

I see the immigration opening as a political opportunity for Trump to rebuild Republican support among Hispanic voters and facilitate Marco Rubio's positioning for the presidency.

Successful immigration reform would allow Trump to change his relationship with communities that began distancing themselves from him after the deportations.

And Rubio could benefit from this new political environment without having been the principal public face of the deportation policy.

There is another interesting detail.

Rubio has concentrated much of his public activity on his diplomatic responsibilities and international affairs.

That does not eliminate the State Department's involvement in certain immigration-related actions. But it does highlight a distinction between Rubio's public profile and that of officials directly associated with deportation operations.

While Trump bears the political cost of deportations and now proposes discussing reform, Rubio maintains a public image more closely associated with diplomacy and foreign policy.

In my analysis, that distinction will matter if a contest for the 2028 Republican presidential nomination develops.

Stephen Miller: A Contradiction That Reveals the Complexity of the Maneuver

But one of Trump's decisions deserves particular attention.

Following the electoral defeats, the president elevated Stephen Miller to White House chief of staff.

Miller is one of the principal architects of the administration's most restrictive immigration policies.

That creates an obvious contradiction.

How can Trump place Stephen Miller in charge of his White House staff while almost simultaneously acknowledging that deportations were too harsh and expressing a willingness to negotiate immigration reform?

My interpretation is that Trump is attempting to keep two political positions open.

On one hand, he keeps close to him a figure who represents the toughest immigration stance and enjoys support within the MAGA movement.

On the other, he introduces a message of negotiation aimed at those who oppose indiscriminate deportations.

It is a complex maneuver.

Trump is attempting to change the immigration debate without completely breaking with the political base that returned him to the White House.

But he is also taking a risk.

If his reform never materializes, his statements could be interpreted as an electoral maneuver with no real consequences.

And if he achieves a broad agreement, he will have to explain to the Republican Party's most restrictive factions why he decided to modify a policy he defended for years.

The question is no longer simply what Democrats want. It is also how far Trump is willing to go and how much of his own political base will follow him.

Ron DeSantis Distances Himself From Immigration Legalization

In this scenario, Ron DeSantis represents a different position.

The governor of Florida has maintained an especially restrictive stance toward illegal immigration.

In March 2026, when several law enforcement officials proposed mechanisms to allow certain undocumented immigrants to obtain legal status, DeSantis publicly rejected the idea.

His words were forceful:

"This idea that unless you're an axe murderer you should be able to stay is not consistent with our laws and it's also not good policy."

He also questioned the idea that someone could enter the United States illegally and remain in the country as long as they did not commit a violent crime.

Those remarks preceded Trump's recent interview, but they demonstrate the distance between their respective approaches.

While Trump is opening the possibility of an agreement for longtime immigrant workers, DeSantis has defended a much more restrictive interpretation of immigration law.

And this is where a problem begins for the Republican Party.

If Trump introduces immigration reform that includes legalization mechanisms, Republican leaders who reject such measures will have to decide whether to support the president or maintain their positions.

DeSantis is an important figure in this debate because of his record as Florida governor and his previous presidential ambitions.

Immigration reform could become one of the issues that define the differences among future Republican leaders.

Ted Cruz and His Bet on Winning Back Texas

Another leader who deserves particular attention is Senator Ted Cruz.

Following the Republican defeats in Texas, Cruz insisted that his state would return to Republican control and that Texans' fundamental values had not changed.

But his explanation of the results was very different from the opening Trump is now proposing.

Cruz argues that Democrats will ultimately overreach while exercising power.

He accuses them of being dominated by radical, Marxist, and Islamist factions and believes they will pursue an ideological agenda that will cause voters to regret their decisions.

He has also defended free-market policies and insisted that Republicans must offer economic solutions for working Americans.

Ted Cruz is betting on winning back Texas through Democratic failures. Trump, by contrast, is opening the door to negotiating with Democrats.

That difference is fundamental.

One strategy depends on the opponent making mistakes, while the other attempts to change the political conditions that caused voters to withdraw their support.

And this brings me to my main criticism of Cruz's reasoning.

Republicans cannot simply sit back and wait for Democrats to fail.

They also need to understand why millions of voters decided to stop supporting them.

In Texas, shifts in voting patterns among Hispanic communities were among the most significant signals of the 2026 elections.

The party lost ground in areas where it had made substantial gains during the 2024 presidential election.

That should force some serious reflection.

Calling your opponents socialists is not enough when part of the electorate is demanding concrete solutions to immigration, economic, and family concerns.

My impression is that Trump has begun to understand this reality and has decided to introduce a new variable into the political contest.

Democrats Must Also Prepare for Their Presidential Succession

But Republicans are not the only ones who need to rethink their strategies.

If Trump succeeds in advancing immigration reform, Democrats will have to decide how to respond to a new political reality in which a Republican president could claim part of the credit for a historic agreement.

And this is where James Talarico enters the picture.

His victory over Ken Paxton in Texas represents one of the most significant developments of the 2026 midterm elections.

Talarico became the first Democrat elected to the U.S. Senate from Texas since 1988.

But what makes him particularly interesting is his political profile.

Talarico incorporates his religious convictions into his public message, focuses on economic inequality, and has challenged the ideological polarization that dominates much of American political debate.

In my opinion, his emergence deserves special attention when examining the Democratic Party's future.

While Trump seeks to reshape the immigration debate and Marco Rubio emerges among the figures discussed in the Republican succession, Talarico represents a new generation of Democratic leaders who defeated Republicans in a state that had long been difficult territory for their party.

That does not mean Talarico has announced a presidential campaign.

But his political trajectory and victory in Texas make him a figure worth examining in the context of 2028.

There are also other Democratic leaders, such as Jon Ossoff, whose political experience will form part of the discussion about the party's future.

The selection of candidates will be closely connected to the issues that ultimately dominate the national debate.

And immigration reform could occupy a central place.

The Hispanic Vote Is the Key to This New Political Battle

In my analysis, the significance of immigration reform goes far beyond undocumented immigrants.

It also affects millions of Hispanic voters who are U.S. citizens, have immigrant relatives, or maintain close ties to communities affected by deportations.

Many supported Trump because they shared his positions on the economy, security, religion, or opposition to socialism.

However, immigration policies created new tensions within those communities.

The Venezuelan case is particularly interesting.

For years, many Venezuelans admired Trump for his confrontation with Nicolás Maduro and his anti-communist rhetoric.

But when deportations began affecting members of their own community, some started questioning a president they had previously supported enthusiastically.

And that produced a political contradiction: conservative Venezuelans, deeply opposed to Chavismo, began moving closer to Democrats without necessarily abandoning their ideological convictions.

They did not become socialists.

They simply began placing their immigration situation and their families' safety above their previous political identification with Trump.

That is a reality both Republicans and Democrats must understand.

And it is precisely why the president's immigration opening carries such significance.

A Maneuver That Changes the Political Game

My final interpretation is that Trump is attempting to turn his electoral defeat into an opportunity for political recovery.

Immigration reform allows him to open a dialogue with Democrats, regain the attention of Hispanic communities, and begin building a new political scenario for the 2028 presidential succession.

Marco Rubio emerges as a figure who could benefit from that realignment.

Ron DeSantis represents a restrictive position that could come into conflict with immigration legalization.

Ted Cruz is betting on winning back Texas by capitalizing on what he sees as Democratic mistakes.

Meanwhile, Democrats will have to decide whether to negotiate with Trump and how to defend their own proposals before millions of immigrants waiting for a solution.

Trump's major political move is to shift the discussion away from mass deportations and toward the possibility of immigration reform, forcing both his opponents and his allies to take a position.

But one fundamental step is still missing: the president must present a concrete legislative proposal.

Until then, the situation remains open.

What is already clear is that Trump has introduced a new issue into the political contest following the elections.

Republicans will have to decide whether to continue defending their previous policies without changes or accept a discussion about a new immigration strategy. Democrats will have to demonstrate what they are willing to negotiate to achieve reform.

And the potential protagonists of 2028 will have to develop their own positions on the issue.

My conclusion is that Trump has moved beyond simply defending deportations and has begun positioning the pieces for a new political game.

A game that could define his presidential legacy, reshape the Republican Party's relationship with Hispanic voters, and trigger new struggles for leadership within both parties.

Trump has already made his first move. Now it is up to Marco Rubio, Ron DeSantis, Ted Cruz, and the Democrats to respond.

We don't need foreign hospitality workers. We don't need any of it. They want it. The left. text:
$TXO Q3 2026 earnings: TXO's oil prices rose 34%, but hedges erased the gain

Buyers paid TXO far more for its oil this quarter, but its own hedging contracts handed the gain back. Sales to customers grew by a quarter, while hedging losses of $57.9 million pushed the partnership into a net loss. Co-chief executive and finance chief Brent Clum still declared $0.44 per unit, the fourth rise in a row.

• Sales to customers, before hedging: $𝟏𝟏𝟑.𝟎𝐌 (+25% from a year ago)
• Total revenue, after hedging losses: $𝟓𝟓.𝟏𝐌 (-45% from a year ago)
• Loss per common unit: -$𝟎.𝟓𝟖 ($0.08 profit a year ago)
• Quarterly distribution declared: $𝟎.𝟒𝟒 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭 (raised from $0.40)

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🔴 Bearish

The case got worse, because the cash behind the payout disappeared. Cash available for distribution, the partnership's own measure of what it can hand out, fell below zero, and drilling spending almost doubled. One positive: lifting costs came down and cash earnings grew 26%.

The question now is who gains when the hedges expire. TXO has locked in only about a quarter of its oil output for early 2028, by our math, against most of it today. Either unitholders collect the market price, or a cheaper barrel leaves them unprotected. February's hedge table will show which way management leaned.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🟢 𝐂𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐏𝐚𝐢𝐝 𝐅𝐚𝐫 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐄𝐚𝐜𝐡 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐥
TXO Partners pumps oil, gas and natural gas liquids from long-lived conventional fields in Texas, New Mexico, Colorado, Montana and North Dakota. It sells at the wellhead, so monthly commodity prices set what it earns. Buyers paid $113.0 million for that output, up a quarter from a year earlier.

Oil fetched $84.20 a barrel before hedging, against $62.80 last year. Liquids prices climbed 42%, the partnership said. This mattered because the fields TXO bought in Montana and North Dakota pump mostly oil, so crude now drives its revenue more than gas does.

What to watch: the oil price after hedging that TXO reports in the annual report due in February. If that figure closes the gap with the unhedged price, more of each barrel will reach unitholders.

🟢 𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐧 𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐖𝐞𝐥𝐥 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬
Elm Coulee, in the Williston Basin of Montana and North Dakota, takes most of TXO's drilling money. Crews now push laterals, the horizontal part of a well that contacts the rock, toward 14,000 feet, against about 10,000 feet in 2025.

Co-chief executive Gary Simpson said: "Our development teams did a stellar job extending laterals in our Williston Basin wells and delivering production rates in excess of 1,000 BOE per day on average." Drilling times improved and total costs landed on budget, he added.

What to watch: the depletion charge per barrel in February's annual report. It reached $10.39 this quarter against $9.02 a year ago, because Williston barrels carry "a higher rate than the historical properties". A flat charge would show the longer wells pay for themselves.

🟢 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 𝐆𝐫𝐞𝐰 𝐚𝐬 𝐋𝐢𝐟𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐨𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐅𝐞𝐥𝐥
Cash earnings tell a different story from the loss. Adjusted EBITDAX, which measures profit before interest, tax, depreciation, exploration costs and paper hedging losses, reached $41.3 million, a rise of 26%. Cash from operations climbed to $33.7 million.

Production expenses fell 9% in dollars, because the joint-venture sale removed $10.9 million of them. Measured against sales to customers, they dropped 14.2 percentage points. Overhead shrank 19% on lower professional fees, the partnership said.

Each barrel still costs slightly more to lift, though: production expense reached $18.73 per barrel of oil equivalent against $18.23, since the fields TXO sold were cheap to run.

What to watch: production expense per barrel in February's annual report. A reading near $18 would show the Williston wells absorb the extra maintenance work the partnership has taken on.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞

🔴🔴 𝐇𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐬 𝐓𝐨𝐨𝐤 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐖𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐞 𝐎𝐢𝐥 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐆𝐚𝐢𝐧
TXO sells oil at market prices but has promised counterparties a fixed price on most of its barrels. When the market sits above that fixed level, TXO pays the difference in cash. Oil averaged $84.20 a barrel this quarter, far above the levels it locked in during 2025.

So the gain never arrived. After cash settlements, the oil price TXO actually collected came to $63.62 a barrel, against $62.73 a year earlier. Hedging swallowed 18% of everything customers paid.

• Cash paid to counterparties: $20.6 million, against $3.1 million received a year ago
• Paper loss on contracts not yet settled: $37.3 million
• Hedging liability: $65.7 million, of which $54.5 million falls due within a year

That liability matters because TXO settles it in cash as each month passes, and those bills compete with the payout. Lenders granted "a waiver of all hedge requirements for months 19 through 24" for the June and September quarters, so coverage of 2028 can thin out.

What to watch: the hedge table in February's annual report, which lists volumes and prices for 2027 and 2028. Coverage near this quarter's level would mean a firm oil market again bypasses unitholders.

🔴🔴 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐏𝐚𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐑𝐚𝐧 𝐏𝐚𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐈𝐭 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐝
TXO calls itself a production and distribution business, "driven by dynamic capital allocation", and its partnership agreement tells it to hand out all available cash. Co-chief executive and finance chief Brent Clum says the team will "closely manage distributions, leverage and growth capital with a focus on long-term value".

This quarter produced no such cash. Cash available for distribution, the partnership's own measure, starts from cash earnings and subtracts interest and drilling spend; it came to minus $2.7 million, against $7.5 million a year ago. Clum still declared $0.44 per unit, a fourth straight increase.

By our math that payout costs about $24.4 million, which TXO must fund from its bank line or from the money its joint venture returned. Drilling spending explains the squeeze, because it rose 85% from a year ago and exceeded cash from operations.

What to watch: cash available for distribution for the fourth quarter, when the full-year plan leaves only about $13 million of spending by our math. A positive reading would show the shortfall came from heavy summer drilling rather than from the payout itself.

🔴 𝐆𝐚𝐬 𝐎𝐮𝐭𝐩𝐮𝐭 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐆𝐚𝐬 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐁𝐨𝐭𝐡 𝐃𝐫𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐝
The San Juan Basin in New Mexico and Colorado supplies most of TXO's natural gas, and that output keeps draining away. Gas volumes fell 27% from a year ago, which the partnership attributes to the Cross Timbers sale and "natural decline in the San Juan Basin".

Prices offered no help. Customers paid $2.14 per thousand cubic feet before hedging, a tenth below last year, so gas sales to customers slipped to $11.2 million. Gas still makes up more than a third of production, so its decline caps how far oil growth can lift total volumes.

What to watch: whether TXO funds Mancos shale drilling or finds a partner for it. The partnership holds 58,500 net acres there and says today's 2027 forward prices do not justify the capital, which leaves its gas business shrinking.

👓 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐉𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐕𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐈𝐬 𝐀𝐥𝐦𝐨𝐬𝐭 𝐖𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐔𝐩
TXO's half-owned joint venture, Cross Timbers Energy, sold its wells for about $200 million gross this year and sent TXO $95.0 million in July. Management used $70.0 million of that to settle the deferred bill for the Montana purchase and cut bank debt with the rest. Fees from the venture dropped to $0.1 million, and TXO expects no more.

— • — • —

💲 𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐃𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐲 𝐨𝐢𝐥 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐠𝐫𝐨𝐰𝐭𝐡, 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): 𝟐𝟕% 𝐚𝐛𝐨𝐯𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟓 𝐚𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞  ⇘ decelerating
Oil output keeps growing, but at a slower clip than last year. Daily oil production runs 27% above the 2025 average, after a 30% reading at midyear. The 2025 year itself gained 54%. Quarterly oil volumes reached 1,088 thousand barrels against 1,053, as new Williston wells offset the fields TXO sold.

𝐋𝐨𝐧𝐠-𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐦 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟐𝟕𝟏.𝟏 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
Borrowings fell to $271.1 million from $291.1 million at the end of 2025. TXO repaid more than it drew over nine months, helped by the cash its joint venture returned. Room left on the bank line now stands at $146.0 million, and the rate on it was 7.4%.

𝐀𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐫𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐨𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟔𝟏.𝟐 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
This is the money TXO must spend to plug and clean up wells at the end of their lives. It fell to $161.2 million from $221.1 million in January, because buyers of the joint venture's wells took on $68.4 million of it. Unwinding the discount added $11.0 million back.

𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞 (𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑): $𝟏𝟏.𝟕 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇗ accelerating
Earnings from outside the wellhead more than doubled, to $11.7 million. TXO credits its gas plant and CO2 assets, which earned $4.1 million more "due to the absence of third-party pipeline disruptions", plus a $2.0 million bonus on a lease assignment. This income now covers overhead and most of the interest bill.

— • — • —

🔮 𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝟐𝟔𝐐𝟑 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐢𝐛𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐨𝐧 𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭: $𝟎.𝟒𝟒  ⇗ accelerating
🠅 raised from $0.40
Raised. The board lifted the quarterly payout to $0.44 per unit, its fourth increase in a row. By our math it costs about $24.4 million, more cash than the quarter itself generated. Clum promises another programme for 2027 but has not named a figure for it.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐝𝐫𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐟𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠: $𝟗𝟎.𝟎-𝟗𝟓.𝟎 𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧  ⇘ decelerating
🠅 raised from ~$80 million
Raised. TXO expects to spend $90-95 million this year, after $79.2 million in the first nine months. By our math that leaves roughly $13 million for the fourth quarter, about half the quarterly pace so far. It is the third step up from the original $70 million budget, a rise of about a third in a year.

𝐓𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐥𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞: 𝐧𝐞𝐭 𝐝𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐭𝐨 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀𝐗: 𝟏.𝟎𝐱-𝟐.𝟎𝐱  ⇒ stable
🠆 unchanged from 1.0x-2.0x
Unchanged. TXO still aims to keep debt between one and two times its annual cash earnings. By our math it sits near 1.45 times, using borrowings of $271.1 million and nine-month cash earnings annualised. Lenders also require current assets above current liabilities, a test TXO met in September.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟔 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀𝐗 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 (𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐡𝐢𝐩 𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐞): 𝟒𝟑%  ⇒ stable
New. TXO reckons 43% of this year's revenue will reach cash earnings, using actual results through September and its own forecast for the rest. The estimate counts gas plant and CO2 earnings as revenue, and it assumes oil prices hold near the late-October forward curve.

— • — • —

❓ 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐗𝐎 𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐧 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟕?
Clum says the partnership is designing another programme for 2027 and gave no figure. The 2026 plan has already moved from about $70 million to $90-95 million, and spending drives the cash left for unitholders.

𝐖𝐡𝐲 𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐩𝐚𝐲𝐨𝐮𝐭 𝐰𝐢𝐭𝐡 𝐧𝐨 𝐬𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐜𝐚𝐬𝐡?
Cash available for distribution fell below zero this quarter, yet the board lifted the distribution for a fourth time. Unitholders need to know which source funds the next one: the bank line, asset sales or operating cash.

𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐦𝐮𝐜𝐡 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖 𝐨𝐢𝐥 𝐰𝐢𝐥𝐥 𝐓𝐗𝐎 𝐡𝐞𝐝𝐠𝐞?
Lenders waived the hedge requirement for months 19 to 24 for two quarters only. If they restore it, TXO may add contracts well below the price its customers now pay, repeating this quarter's drag.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐜𝐞 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝟐𝟎𝟐𝟖 𝐬𝐰𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐲?
In October TXO sold counterparties the option to put it into 2028 oil swaps at $80 a barrel for 3,880 barrels a day. The partnership has not said what premium it received or when the option expires.

𝐖𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐫𝐞𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐜𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐣𝐨𝐢𝐧𝐭 𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞'𝐬 𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐞?
Cross Timbers Energy contributed $1.0 million of property income this quarter and fees that have now stopped. Investors need the size of the gap in next year's cash flow once the wind-up completes.

text:
I paid $36,000 this year to fill 4 swimming pools with dirt

2 of them were fully functional.

In Florida, Arizona or Texas a pool sells the house

But in Ohio it's 3 months of swimming and 9 months of staring at a muddy tarp

And on the houses I buy, the dirt makes the house worth more than the pool did.

The people buying my houses are first time buyers paying $160,000 to $230,000, usually on an FHA or VA loan with 3.5% down and almost nothing left in the bank after closing

To that buyer a pool is 5 problems:

1. The loan. FHA and VA appraisers have to write up a pool that's green, cracked, torn or unfenced. Now it's a required repair, and the bank won't fund the loan until somebody fixes it

2. The insurance. It costs more every year, and a lot of companies won't write the policy without a 4 foot fence that latches. No fence means $6,000 the buyer doesn't have

3. The upkeep. Chemicals, the pump's electric bill, opening it in May and closing it in September run $2,000 to $3,000 a year. The liner rips every 8 to 10 years for about $5,000, and the pipes crack when the ground freezes

4. Little kids. Drowning is the number one cause of death for kids 1 to 4. A lot of young parents won't even book the showing

5. The appraiser barely counts it. A pool that cost somebody $40,000 usually adds $5,000 to $10,000 to the appraisal around here, if anything

One of the 2 that worked was a 3 bed outside Columbus. Blue water, new pump, the owner kept it perfect

It sat on Zillow for 74 days at $185,000.

Two FHA buyers got it under contract and both fell apart, one over the appraiser's pool write up and one over a $6,000 fence his insurance company wanted

The seller sold it to me for $128,000 so she could stop paying for a pool nobody wanted

I filled it for $9,200. Sod was $1,400. Paint and floors inside were $11,000

Relisted at $204,900 with a flat grass yard. 4 offers in 6 days, and it closed at $207,000 with a clean appraisal

If you're about to fill one in, the cheap way costs more. A guy with a tractor dumps dirt into the bowl for $3,000, the rain has nowhere to go, and 2 winters later there's a sunken rectangle of mud in the yard.

The next buyer's inspector sees the old pool on the satellite photos, asks for the permit, and the deal stalls

Done right it's $8,000 to $12,000, and these go in the contract:

1. A city permit, so the removal is on record and you have paperwork to hand the next buyer

2. Holes jackhammered through the floor, plus a layer of gravel, so rainwater drains into the ground

3. The top 2 to 3 feet of wall knocked in, and the liner, pipes and pump hauled out

4. Dirt packed in 12 inch layers with a compactor, with a compaction report you keep with the house papers

5. The pool circuit cut at the panel, and the gas line capped if there was a heater

After it passes, ask your county to take the pool off your property tax record. Most people keep paying tax on a pool that's been grass for years

Buying a house with a pool you don't want? Get a fill quote before you make an offer and take it off your price. A seller who just got quoted $20,000 to fix a cracked shell usually says yes

The fill, the sod and the paint all have to be paid the month I close, before the house is worth a dollar more. I keep that on 0% introductory business credit so my cash is ready for the next one

If you've got 700+ credit, my team helps qualifying investors line up 0% introductory business funding for repairs like these

I built a free calculator to estimate how much funding you could qualify for

Tap the link in my bio and see how much capital you could have ready before you find a seller willing to knock $20,000 off a house over a pool you can bury for $9,000

In 1966 Texas sentenced a 20-year-old to the electric chair for killing three teenagers. In 1989 the state let him walk out the front gate. He had once tried to bribe the parole board with $10,000. Within months, women started disappearing:

His name was Kenneth McDuff, from the small town of Rosebud, Texas. In 1972 the Supreme Court struck down the death penalty, and his sentence became life with the possibility of parole. In 1981 he offered the parole board $10,000 and was convicted of bribery. In 1989, with Texas prisons badly overcrowded, the board paroled him anyway. He was one of 20 former death-row inmates and 127 murderers let out.

Between 1989 and 1992 he killed at least six women. Among them were Colleen Reed, taken from an Austin car wash, and Melissa Northrup, a convenience store clerk in Waco. Then he vanished.

He turned up in Kansas City, working for a garbage company under the name Richard Fowler. On May 1, 1992, a coworker was watching America's Most Wanted and realized the man on the screen was the new guy at work. Three days later, U.S. Marshals arrested him on his way to a landfill.

In the video below, the Marshals fly him back to Texas. He steps off the plane in handcuffs and a white T-shirt, and a crowd of officers walks him to a caged patrol car. At 0:20 a reporter shouts, "Did you kill anyone, Mr. McDuff?" Then: "Did you know Melissa Northrup?" He sits in the back seat and says nothing.

He became the only man in Texas history to be sentenced to death, released, and sentenced to death again. On November 17, 1998, he was executed in Huntsville. His last words: "I'm ready to be released. Release me."

The state had him on death row once and let him go. How many women would still be alive if "life" had meant life?

On The First Day Of Bill Prefiling For The 90th Texas Legislature, Democratic Lawmakers Introduced Measures That Would More Than Double The State Minimum Wage, Restrict Firearm Transfers To Adults Under 21, Establish A Temporary Guest Worker Program With Mexico, Provide Across-The-Board Raises For State Employees & Repeal The Education Savings Account Program That Funds Private School & Homeschool Options For Families.

House Bill 110 By Rep. Ana-María Rodríguez Ramos Relates To The Minimum Wage. Texas Currently Follows The Federal Rate Of $7.25 Per Hour. Prior Democratic Proposals In Recent Sessions, Including Those By Rodríguez Ramos, Sought To Set A Floor Of $15 Or Higher, Which Would Represent More Than A Doubling Of The Existing Rate. Similar Bills Have Been Filed In Past Sessions But Have Not Advanced Under Republican Control.

House Bill 173 By Rep. Joe Moody Would Prohibit The Transfer Of Certain Semiautomatic Rifles To Persons Younger Than 21 Years Of Age. The Official Bill Text Amends The Penal Code To Make It An Offense To Intentionally Or Knowingly Sell, Rent, Lease, Give Or Offer Certain Semiautomatic Rifles Capable Of Accepting A Detachable Magazine & Chambered In A Caliber Greater Than .22 To Anyone Under 21. Violations Would Be A State Jail Felony. Exceptions Exist For Peace Officers, Current Or Honorably Discharged Members Of The U.S. Armed Forces & Certain Temporary Loans For Hunting, Sporting Or Recreational Activities In Specific Settings. The Measure Would Take Effect September 1, 2027.

House Bill 294 By Rep. Garcia Of Bexar Relates To The Establishment Of A Temporary Guest Worker Program. The Bill Directs The Governor To Seek Federal Authorization & Then Negotiate A Memorandum Of Understanding With A Mexican State. Under The Program, Texas Businesses Could Obtain Legal Temporary Guest Workers From Mexico Through U.S. Nonimmigrant Visas To Fill Jobs Identified By The Texas Workforce Commission As Most In Need Of Skilled & Unskilled Migrant Labor. Participating Businesses Must Certify That Sufficient Local Workers Are Unavailable & That The Employment Will Not Adversely Affect The Wages Or Working Conditions Of Similarly Employed Texas Workers.

House Bill 219 By Rep. John Bucy Relates To A Pay Raise For Certain State Employees. Previous Versions Of Similar Legislation Proposed By Bucy Sought Uniform Annual Increases, Such As $10,000 For Full-Time Employees, Applied Across State Agencies & Institutions Of Higher Education.

House Bill 164 By Rep. Bucy Relates To The Repeal Of The Education Savings Account Program. This Program, Established In The Prior Session, Provides State-Funded Accounts That Families May Use For Private School Tuition (Approximately $10,500 Per Student), Homeschool Expenses ($2,000) Or Higher Amounts For Students With Disabilities. Gov.-Elect Gina Hinojosa Has Publicly Pledged To End The Program & Redirect Funding Toward Public Schools.

These Filings Occurred On November 9, 2026, The Opening Day For Prefiling Ahead Of The Regular Session That Convenes January 12, 2027. Democrats Will Control The Governor’s Office & The Texas House For The First Time In Decades, While Republicans Retain A Majority In The Senate. Official Bill Texts Are Available On The Texas Legislature Online Site.

Just 13 days after reporting her cancer, management fired her. The filing includes a call recording where Vitalik acknowledged fears that conceding to staff organizing would invite future pushback. text:
Twelve Hasselblad cameras are still sitting on the moon.

The Hasselblad 500C was a boxy medium-format camera made by Victor Hasselblad's company in Gothenburg, Sweden, and it came out in 1957. By 1962 it sold for about $500 in the US, with interchangeable Zeiss lenses and removable film magazines.

In the summer of 1962, astronaut Wally Schirra walked into a Houston photo shop and bought a 500C on the advice of photographers from Life and National Geographic. John Glenn had taken pictures from orbit earlier that year with a $40 camera from a Florida drugstore. Schirra stripped his Hasselblad and painted it black to cut reflections, then flew it on Sigma 7 that October, and NASA flew modified 500Cs on several more missions before Hasselblad even noticed and offered to build cameras for space. By the Apollo moon landings, every pound counted on the trip home, so astronauts brought back the film and left the camera bodies behind.

🎧 $EVGO EARNINGS CALL RECAP

// EVgo $EVGO goes quiet on LS Power's $2.00 bid and spends its Q3 call cutting the build

Management opened the third quarter call with the bid hanging over everything and refused to touch it. CEO Badar Khan said the special committee of independent directors is working with its own legal and financial advisers, that no decisions have been made, and that the company would not comment further on LS Power's unsolicited offer to take EVgo private at $2.00 a share. The rest of the call was retrenchment: slower deployment, lower spending, and a charging business carrying a shrinking construction arm.

• Guidance: full year revenue held at $375M to $400M with an adjusted EBITDA loss of $15M to $30M, adjusted G&A now seen near $145M against initial guidance of $150M to $155M, and stall adds of 1,075 to 1,275 for 2026, split 600 to 750 public and autonomous vehicle stalls and 475 to 525 eXtend stalls
• Capital spending: gross capex in 2026 is now expected to run about $100M below the prior target as some construction slips into 2027 and certain sites return to the development pipeline, one 50 stall autonomous vehicle site due in late December could slip into early 2027, 2027 adjusted G&A is targeted at least 15% under the prior implied view of $173M to $178M, and liquidity stood near $787M at September 30 including about $620M of capacity across two debt facilities
• Segment color: charging network revenue rose 29% to $72M in a 19th straight quarter of double digit growth and network gross margin reached 39%, up 380 basis points; eXtend revenue fell by half to $16M and CFO Keefer Lehner guided it down to a $5M to $10M annual level by 2028; network throughput rose 8% to 103 GWh while daily throughput per stall fell 4% to 283 kWh on expiring automaker credits, and rose 7% excluding automaker charging programs
• The network push: over 290 NACS stalls are live with about 400 expected by year end, NACS drivers took 9% of public throughput at a charging rate 35% higher than CCS, the first EVgo branded Supercharger site opened in the Chicago area under the Tesla $TSLA agreement with EVgo owning the chargers and setting prices while Tesla builds and runs them, a second site outside Houston is due this quarter, Brixmor $BRX and Regency Centers $REG partnerships add over 900 chargers, and a new 750 kW charging architecture starts deploying in 2027

THE CATCH

The bid is the stock now, and management gave it nothing: no timeline, no price talk, no rejection either, just a committee and silence. Underneath, the plan is shrinking to fit a slower EV tape, and the growth math leans harder on a charging segment whose per stall output fell this quarter once automaker credits rolled off.

THE TAKEAWAY

EVgo is running two clocks at once: a cost reset built to stretch $787M of liquidity toward self funding, and a $2.00 cash bid from its majority holder that turns every quarter of patience into a negotiation. The charging engine is genuinely strong, up 29% with margin expanding, but it now has to outrun a construction arm in managed decline.

Does the special committee take LS Power's $2.00, or does the leaner EVgo earn the right to refuse it? 👇 NFA
