London – Szilvia Berki (31), a Hungarian masseuse living in England, has accused Jemima Khan (40) and Russell Brand (39) of sexual assault and false imprisonment.

August 3, 2014, 8:10 PM

A few days ago, *The Telegraph* briefly reported on events that took place two months prior; on Sunday, the *Daily Mail* published a detailed account of the incident. Szilvia had been hired as a birthday surprise for the partner of the businesswoman—who also serves as a UN ambassador—but the intended massage never took place. According to the masseuse, the couple had a different vision for the afternoon than what had been agreed upon.

“Jemima reached out to me in early June. We made arrangements via text message and then email. She wanted a massage for Russell Brand’s birthday. I was surprised they didn’t hire someone local, but since she offered to compensate me for my travel time and send a car to pick me up, I agreed. We settled on a fee of £500 (190,000 HUF), as it involved a four-hour journey, and it was a weekend,” recounted Szilvia, who was asked to travel to the woman’s estate in Oxfordshire. “Jemima welcomed me and led me to a guest room upstairs, where a massage table had been set up next to a double bed. She told me to get changed at my leisure, then stepped out for ten minutes. When she returned, she was in her underwear. At that point, I assumed I was supposed to massage her, but she simply lay down on the double bed, saying she would just watch. Russell then entered the room, locked the door, and turned off the lights, leaving only a faint glow. I asked him to lie on the massage table, but he insisted on using the double bed. As I approached, he began touching me, and it became clear that their intentions were completely different from what we had discussed. If I had known, I never would have gone there!” declared Szilvia, adding that it took quite a while before she finally managed to get out of the building.

“I told them I wanted to leave, at which point they went into another room and started screaming at each other. Khan then came back in and asked me to stay, but I refused. At first, they wouldn’t let me go; then Brand started shoving me toward the exit, taking my bag in the process. I finally reached the front door, but it was locked—and to make matters worse, a large white shepherd dog was standing right there, facing me.” Eventually, Russell opened the door, but the dog jumped on me. I was terrified. The same driver who had picked me up then took me home from the house. He tried to calm me down, but since he also works for the Khans, there wasn’t much he could do,” recounted Szilvia, who wants nothing more than to see justice served. She believes that serious crimes were committed—specifically, that she was not only sexually harassed but also had her personal liberty restricted.

Lawyers for the celebrities denied Szilvia’s allegations to the *Daily Mail*, noting that Jemima Khan even emailed her the following day to apologize for any misunderstandings. Furthermore, the agreed-upon sum of £500 was paid. Despite this, the Hungarian woman turned to the police and filed a complaint.

However, on July 25, the Thames Valley Police responded that they would not be pursuing the matter, citing a lack of independent evidence or witnesses.

Szilvia claims that it was at this luxury estate in Oxfordshire that Russell Brand attacked her, and that the couple subsequently kept her confined behind locked doors for a period of time.

text:
🇺🇲 Trump told 60 Minutes his fortune grew because of stocks. The Forbes journalist who calculated his wealth says the money came from somewhere else.

When Donald Trump was asked on 60 Minutes how his personal fortune had increased by nearly $3 billion, he offered a simple explanation: everyone had become wealthier. When interviewer Ross Douthat pointed out that his own net worth had not risen by anything approaching that amount, the president replied, “Well, you should have had stock.” Trump then insisted that he devoted almost no attention to his finances, that his sons managed his businesses and that he barely knew how much money he had accumulated. The exchange might have passed as another familiar Trump boast. Instead, it prompted an extraordinary 41-part examination by Dan Alexander, the Forbes senior editor responsible for calculating the president's wealth, documenting how political influence, cryptocurrency ventures, foreign investment and overseas licensing agreements helped transform Trump's financial position.

Alexander's central finding is that the stock market explains almost none of the extraordinary increase Trump invoked during the interview. According to Forbes, Trump's estimated net worth rose from $4.3 billion in the autumn of 2024 to $7.3 billion in September 2025. The magazine's more recent estimate, published in September 2026, places his fortune at approximately $7 billion, still $2.7 billion above its level when he won the presidential election. These figures represent estimates of net worth, which include the market value of assets and liabilities rather than simply cash received. Nevertheless, the underlying transactions offer a revealing account of how Trump's political comeback coincided with a transformation of his business model.

The story begins before Trump returned to the White House. In March 2024, Forbes estimated his fortune at $2.3 billion. By the autumn, it had risen to $4.3 billion, largely because Trump Media & Technology Group, the parent company of Truth Social, had entered the public markets. Alexander estimates that approximately $1.8 billion of that initial $2 billion increase came from Trump Media. The company's valuation depended heavily on investor enthusiasm surrounding Trump's political prospects rather than conventional measures of profitability. His electoral appeal had become an asset capable of generating billions in estimated personal wealth.

The next phase was more consequential. Shortly before the 2024 election, Trump and his family launched World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency venture that offered investors digital tokens while promising a transformation of financial services. Its ownership and revenue-sharing arrangements were unusually favorable to the president and his relatives. According to Alexander's examination of the original structure, after an initial $30 million threshold, 52.5% of certain proceeds were allocated to Trump, another 22.5% to family members and 12.5% to an affiliate of the family of Steve Witkoff, Trump's longtime associate who subsequently became a central figure in his administration's foreign-policy negotiations. These figures describe the arrangement Alexander examined, rather than the distribution of every dollar earned by the venture.

The business initially struggled to attract investors. That changed after Trump's election victory. Cryptocurrency entrepreneur Justin Sun, who had faced a civil fraud case brought by the Securities and Exchange Commission, announced a $30 million investment in November 2024 and an additional $45 million shortly before Trump's inauguration. His total commitment reached $75 million. Alexander argues that the investment helped establish the commercial momentum of World Liberty Financial at precisely the moment its principal political beneficiary was preparing to assume the presidency. Around the same period, Trump launched his own memecoin, adding another highly speculative asset tied directly to his public identity and political following.

The scale of the resulting business is striking. Alexander estimates that World Liberty Financial generated approximately $789 million in earnings during 2025, while the Trump memecoin contributed another $636 million. The president also retained substantial holdings of digital tokens, whose estimated value rose as the ventures expanded. In Alexander's breakdown of the $3 billion increase between autumn 2024 and autumn 2025, cryptocurrency earnings contributed more than $1 billion, while retained cryptocurrency holdings accounted for roughly another $1 billion. These categories involve different kinds of wealth: proceeds generated by business activity are not interchangeable with the estimated value of tokens that may remain restricted, volatile or difficult to sell at their quoted prices.

The foreign-investment dimension raises questions beyond personal enrichment. Alexander identifies substantial purchases associated with the United Arab Emirates, including a $25 million token acquisition by a company that had recently relocated there and a separate $100 million purchase by an Abu Dhabi-linked nonprofit. A further transaction, subsequently reported by The Wall Street Journal, involved associates of an Abu Dhabi royal who agreed to purchase a 49% stake in the Trump family's cryptocurrency venture for $500 million. Such transactions are particularly sensitive because the investors are connected to a region where Washington exercises considerable influence over security guarantees, advanced technology, financial regulation and diplomatic relationships.

The existence of these investments does not, by itself, establish an illegal exchange of political favors. It does, however, create an identifiable conflict-of-interest problem: foreign investors and politically connected business figures can establish substantial financial relationships with enterprises benefiting the sitting president while simultaneously having interests affected by his administration's decisions. The question is whether the financial incentives and governmental decisions can be meaningfully separated when the president retains an economic interest in the underlying businesses.

Cryptocurrency was only one component of the expansion. Trump's overseas licensing operations also accelerated, particularly across the Middle East. Alexander traces part of that development through Ziad El Chaar, a businessman who had previously worked with Dubai billionaire Hussain Sajwani before moving into Saudi-linked property development. As Trump's return to power became more likely, new agreements multiplied across the region, often involving developments associated with Gulf ruling establishments. Forbes estimates that Trump's annual licensing income rose from approximately $6 million in 2023 to $46 million in 2024 and $61 million in 2025. The estimated value of the broader licensing business increased from roughly $100 million in autumn 2024 to $500 million a year later.

Another significant component of Trump's reported wealth increase came from a courtroom rather than a commercial transaction. In August 2025, a New York appeals court eliminated the massive financial penalty imposed in the civil fraud case brought by the state's attorney general, while leaving important findings against Trump intact. Removing a liability of approximately half a billion dollars improved his estimated net worth without requiring him to generate an equivalent amount in new business income. Alexander includes that change in his accounting, alongside approximately $400 million in additional value attributed to the expansion of Trump's licensing business.

Taken together, Alexander's rounded figures identify more than $1 billion in cryptocurrency earnings, approximately $1 billion in retained crypto assets, $400 million in additional licensing-business value and roughly $500 million associated with the eliminated civil penalty. The categories explain the broad increase, although they should not be interpreted as a precise cash-flow statement. They also expose the weakness in Trump's suggestion that ordinary stock-market appreciation was responsible for his extraordinary financial gains.

Alexander examined that claim directly. Based on Forbes estimates, Trump's liquid assets in autumn 2024 totaled approximately $415 million, with only about 10% invested in conventional stocks. During the subsequent year, the S&P 500 gained approximately 14%, implying a gain of only around $6 million on that estimated portfolio. Meanwhile, Trump Media shares declined by roughly 10% over the comparable measurement period, reducing the value of his holdings by an estimated $226 million. On Alexander's calculations, the combined stock-market effect was negative by approximately $220 million. The market Trump credited for making him billions had, by this measure, reduced his estimated wealth.

Trump's other defense during the 60 Minutes interview was that he pays little attention to his finances and leaves the business to his sons. Alexander challenges that assertion using years of reporting on the Trump Organization. In a 2017 interview, Eric Trump acknowledged that his father received financial and profitability updates, potentially on a quarterly basis. Alexander also points to more recent reporting describing Trump's involvement in specific business decisions, including details of property operations and branding. None of this proves that Trump personally negotiated every cryptocurrency transaction or foreign licensing agreement. It does undermine the impression that his business interests have been placed entirely beyond his attention.

The broader institutional question is whether the presidency has become inseparable from the commercial value of the Trump name. Investors in his cryptocurrency projects are not merely purchasing conventional financial assets. They are participating in enterprises whose visibility, perceived influence and commercial prospects are closely associated with the president of the United States. Foreign developers licensing his brand are likewise entering business relationships with a family whose patriarch controls American foreign policy. The financial arrangements may be formally private, but the political circumstances surrounding them are impossible to ignore.

Trump ended the interview by pointing out that he does not take the presidential salary, which is set at $400,000 annually. Alexander's response was to compare that amount with the billions added to Trump's estimated fortune. The comparison is rhetorically powerful, although the distinction between annual income and an increase in estimated net worth matters. A billionaire can experience an enormous increase in paper wealth without receiving that amount in cash. The relevant issue is the financial benefit derived from businesses operating alongside the presidency, not whether a presidential salary is collected.

The timing adds a new political dimension. Trump's interview came immediately after Republicans suffered devastating midterm losses, with voters expressing dissatisfaction over the Iran war, economic conditions and the administration's priorities. As Democrats prepare to exercise greater congressional oversight, the president's foreign business interests, cryptocurrency transactions and financial relationships with politically connected investors are likely to face renewed scrutiny. Congressional investigations could examine ownership arrangements, financial disclosures, foreign counterparties and the relationship between private transactions and public decisions. Such scrutiny would need to establish evidence of improper conduct rather than presume that every profitable transaction constituted corruption.

Alexander's investigation leaves a question that Trump's answer to 60 Minutes did little to resolve: how should Americans assess a presidency in which the officeholder's political power and personal business interests have become so closely intertwined? The available financial evidence points overwhelmingly toward cryptocurrency ventures, overseas commercial agreements and changes in legal liabilities as the principal drivers of Trump's extraordinary wealth increase. His explanation that stock ownership made the difference does not withstand the numbers published by the very magazine whose estimates prompted the question.

Sources: @DanAlexander21 's November 8 investigation and Forbes wealth assessments published in September 2025 and September 2026; CBS News/60 Minutes, November 8, 2026; reporting by The Wall Street Journal on the Abu Dhabi-linked investment in World Liberty Financial. https://t.co/vxNeWjXBT4

text:
The General Who Ended the French Revolution

On November 9, 1799, a 30-year-old French general began a political operation that would bring the French Revolution’s republican government to an end. His name was Napoleon Bonaparte.

France had endured a decade of revolution, political violence, foreign wars, and repeated changes of government. By 1799, the Directory, the five-man executive governing the republic, had lost much of its authority. Military victories had preserved France from its enemies, but the government struggled with corruption, financial instability, and deep political divisions.

Napoleon returned from his Egyptian expedition to find influential politicians searching for a way to replace the existing regime. Among them was Emmanuel-Joseph Sieyès, who believed a new constitutional structure was necessary. Napoleon offered something the conspirators lacked: enormous public prestige and the loyalty of soldiers.

On 18 Brumaire, Year VIII of the revolutionary calendar—November 9, 1799—the conspirators arranged for France’s legislative councils to relocate to Saint-Cloud, supposedly because of a security threat. Napoleon was placed in command of troops responsible for their protection.

The following day, the operation nearly collapsed when legislators resisted the proposed changes. Napoleon’s brother Lucien helped rally the soldiers, who dispersed the Council of Five Hundred. The Directory was replaced by a provisional consular government.

Napoleon would soon emerge as First Consul, concentrating power in his own hands. Five years later, he crowned himself emperor.

The Revolution had overthrown a monarchy in the name of liberty. A decade later, its political institutions were dismantled by a general whose authority rested increasingly upon military power.

The most important tasks any Christian should tend to is their relationship with God. To that end I suggest getting on your knees every morning and evening. Pray these AM & PM prayers for 30 days and see how your life changes. Do this in the position of humility…on your knees.

Morning: "Let the morning bring me word of your unfailing love, for I have put my trust in you. Show me the way I should go, for to you I entrust my life." 
~ Psalm 143: 8

I offer myself to Thee- To build with me and to do with me as Thou wilt. Relieve me of the bondage of self, that I may better do Thy will. Take away my difficulties, that victory over them may bear witness to those I would help of Thy Power, Thy Love, and Thy Way of life. May I do Thy will always!

Evening: O my God, I am heartily sorry for having offended Thee, and I detest all my sins, because I dread the loss of Heaven and the pains of Hell, but most of all because they offend Thee, my God, who art all good and deserving of all my love. I firmly resolve, with the help of Thy grace, to confess my sins, to do penance, and to amend my life.

Merciful God, as I reflect on this day, I confess my sinfulness. I ask for Your forgiveness and the cleansing power of Your grace. Have mercy on me, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. In Jesus' name, I humbly pray. Amen.

National Louisiana Day! 

Joining the USA as the 18th state in the Union, Louisiana was added as a state in 1812, less than a decade after the famous Louisiana purchase. Louisiana has roots that are extremely French, but its culture has also been strongly influenced by Africans as well as Spanish culture. It’s a hotbed for Creole and Cajun cultures that have their own unique foods, music and experiences!

With Baton Rouge as the capitol, Louisiana offers a whole lot of unique and interesting experiences, the first celebration of National Louisiana Day took place in 2017.

text:
Coffee with Emerson, Whitman, and Thoreau on the Age of Abundance. 
 
The table's round this time. No head. 

Emerson's notebook's open again. Whitman's got a cigar he hasn't lit, rolling it between his fingers like a baton. I'm between them, closer to the middle than I sat with Emerson alone.

"Nature," Emerson says. "The woods were my first church."

Whitman leans forward. "The woods were my body. I didn't worship them. I was them."

Emerson's pen stops. "That's the difference. 

You made yourself the subject. I made myself the witness."

"A witness who never got wet," Whitman says.

I tap the table. "He's asking whether nature's a temple or a skin. Which is it?"

Emerson doesn't look at me. He looks at Whitman. "It's a text. You read it."

"It's a muscle," Whitman says. "You use it."

The cigar finally gets lit. He doesn't inhale. Just lets it burn.

"Abundance," I say. "Machines making everything. Food, power, houses. What happens to nature when scarcity dies?"

Emerson's quiet for a while. The radiator's the only sound.

"Then nature stops being a resource," he says. "It becomes what it always was. A presence. The question was never whether we'd have enough. It's whether we'd still know how to stand in it."

Whitman laughs. Low. Not mocking. Almost tender.

"You sound like a man who's never had to work for dinner."

"I grew up poor," Emerson says. "My father died when I was eight. I know what not having looks like."

"Then you know abundance isn't the point," Whitman says. "The point is whether the man who has everything can still feel the grass under his feet. Most can't. They build walls around the grass."

I look at Emerson. "Is that what you did?"
He doesn't answer right away. He writes one line in the notebook. Shows me this time.
It says: "I built a wall and called it a study."

Whitman reads it over my shoulder. Nods once.

"At least you admitted it," he says. "Most men die inside the wall and call it a home."

I push my chair back. Stand up between them.

"Here's what I think. You're both right and you're both wrong. Emerson, you made nature sacred by keeping it at arm's length. Whitman, you made it holy by getting inside it. But neither of you asked the question that matters now. What happens when the wall comes down and there's no grass left to stand in? When abundance means the forest's gone and the machine's doing the breathing?"

Emerson closes the notebook. Whitman puts out the cigar. Neither one answers.

They don't have to. The silence is the answer.

Chapter Four. Emerson and Thoreau. 
 
Different room. Smaller. No radiator. A window open to actual trees — not through glass, through the frame itself. Thoreau's already there, sitting on the floor against the wall, boots still on. Emerson takes the chair like it was built for him.

"You lived in a cabin for two years," Emerson says.

"I lived in the woods," Thoreau says. "The cabin was just where I slept."

"You could have stayed at my house. I offered."

"I know. That's why I left."

I sit between them on a crate. "He means the house had too many rooms."

Thoreau almost smiles. "It had opinions."

Emerson opens his notebook. Doesn't write. Just holds the pen.

"Self-reliance," he says. "I wrote that a man should be ashamed to repeat yesterday. You spent two years doing the same thing every day. Chopping wood. Hauling water. Watching the pond."

"I wasn't repeating," Thoreau says. "I was arriving. Every morning was the first morning. That's not consistency. That's renewal."

"Same result."

"Different man."

I lean in. "Here's where I get stuck. Emerson, you told me the wall was your study.  Thoreau, you tore the wall down and built a hut. But the hut's still a structure. Still a boundary. What's the difference?"

Thoreau looks at Emerson. Not hostile. Almost pitying.

"The difference is he built the wall to keep nature out. I built the hut to keep me in. One's a fortress. The other's a door."

Emerson's pen moves. One line. He doesn't show it this time.

"Abundance," I say. "Machines making food, power, shelter. No scarcity. What does a man do with two years when nothing's required of him?"

Thoreau stands up. Walks to the open window. The trees are right there, close enough to touch.

"He finally has time to notice he's been asleep," he says. "Most men never get that. They die inside the wall and call it a home."

Emerson doesn't move. The pen's still in his hand.

"I built the wall," he says. "You built the door. But the door only works if somebody walks through it."

Thoreau turns around.

"I did."

"I know," Emerson says. "That's the part that still hurts."

I stand up. The crate scrapes the floor.

"Last question. If the machines take everything — the chopping, the hauling, the work itself — what's left that's worth doing by hand?"

Thoreau's already at the door. He doesn't turn around.

"Everything," he says. "That's the whole point."

He leaves. Boots on the wood. The trees swallow him.

Emerson sits alone for a long time. Then he writes in the notebook. Shows me.

It says: "He was the better student. I was the better teacher. Neither of us was the better man."

Outside, the same dog. Barking at nothing.

text:
The Biological Layer Beneath Power
Human history is usually explained in terms of power, ideology, economics, or occult networks. These analyses are often sharp, but they almost always miss one fundamental layer: the biological. Not as a side issue or metaphor, but as a structural steering mechanism that has existed for thousands of years and continues to be actively used today. Life never emerged in the form of isolated individuals. From the very beginning, life has been a continuous process of cooperation, competition, and reorganization between organisms. Humans are no exception.
We are holobionts — complex ecosystems in which billions of organisms coexist. Bacteria, fungi, viruses/exosomes, and parasites are an integral part of our functioning. They influence not only our digestion and immune system, but also our behavior, emotions, and decision-making.Within this biological ecosystem, there exists a specific group of parasites that exerts a remarkably strong influence on human behavior and social structures. This group, referred to here as the quintet, consists of five organisms, each affecting the host’s internal environment in its own way:

--- Parasite
- Key vectors
- Effect on the individual. Effect on larger power structures

--- Toxoplasma gondii
- Cats, raw/undercooked meat
- Reduces anxiety and inhibitions, increases risk-taking, status-seeking and ideological receptiveness. Makes populations more compliant with authoritarian and high-risk systems

--- Treponema pallidum
- Sexual contact
- Moral disruption, reduced empathy, increased lust and grandiosity. Weakens moral cohesion and makes corruption and exploitation easier to accept

--- Borrelia (Lyme etc.)
- Tick bites
- Chronic fatigue, brain fog, inflammation and cognitive decline. Keeps large parts of the population in a state of reduced clarity and initiative

--- Helicobacter pylori
- Contaminated water and food
- Weakens energy metabolism and increases stress and anxiety sensitivity. Increases dependence on medical systems and medication

---Taenia solium
- Contaminated pork
- Can cause neurological symptoms and personality changes in severe cases. Can contribute to reduced cognitive sharpness in key positions

From Natural Phenomenon to Deliberate Weaponry ...
These parasites have existed in nature for a long time and influence behavior as part of evolutionary processes. That, in itself, is a biological reality. The critical distinction lies between the natural effect of these organisms and the conscious use of their effects as a means of control. The legends surrounding King Solomon describe how he was able to externally command demonic, parasitic forces to build the Temple. What is less emphasized in these stories is that he ultimately lost internal control over these same forces. He became morally corrupted, and the Temple he had built became contaminated. This reflects a structural pattern: whoever attempts to use these internal forces as a weapon, without structurally limiting them within themselves and within the system they are building, will eventually be affected by them themselves.
Biological Warfare Against One’s Own Population ...
In modern times, this biological layer is not merely endured but actively supported and strengthened in multiple ways. This occurs through both the targeted dissemination of these parasites and the systematic weakening of the population’s internal environment (terrain).
Concrete methods include:
• Lowering of sexual morality: The deliberate erosion of sexual boundaries facilitates the spread of Treponema pallidum (syphilis), leading to greater moral disruption and reduced empathy across society.
• Promotion of tick populations: There are indications that certain laboratories have worked on breeding and releasing ticks, thereby increasing the spread of Borrelia and keeping parts of the population chronically fatigued and cognitively impaired.
• Promotion of cats and cat ownership: Cats are the definitive host of Toxoplasma gondii. Intensive promotion of cat ownership increases infection rates and strengthens the parasite’s effect on fear, inhibition, and risk assessment.
• High sugar and seed oil consumption: The widespread promotion of sugar and industrial seed oils creates a chronic inflammatory environment that weakens overall energy metabolism and supports organisms such as Helicobacter pylori.
• Electromagnetic and chemical exposure: Large-scale deployment of electromagnetic fields (EMF), combined with chronic exposure to endocrine disruptors and other chemicals, further degrades cellular and mitochondrial function.
• Pharmaceutical and molecular interventions: Certain medical interventions, particularly injectable technologies, directly interfere with immune regulation and cellular signaling.
• Psychological and perceptual manipulation: Through media and digital systems, perception is systematically shaped, reducing the population’s ability to recognize the real causes of declining health and autonomy.
Historically, similar methods have been used more crudely, such as the deliberate contamination of water sources with dead bodies during the Black Death, which not only spread disease but also further weakened the general condition of the population.

Power Structures and the Biological Layer ...
This biological weakening functions as a silent amplifier of existing power structures. While money and media steer behavior from the outside, the quintet works from within. It lowers the threshold for the acceptance of corruption, authority, and dependency.
• The Vatican (spiritual/moral power) benefits primarily from moral disruption and reduced inner inhibitions.
• The City of London (financial power) benefits from increased risk appetite and reduced moral scruples.
• Washington DC (military and geopolitical power) benefits from a population that is chronically fatigued and less inclined toward deep resistance.
In all cases, the biological layer functions as a structural facilitator of centralized control. Ultimately, we are waging a war against unbalanced, harmful parasites. Nature offers an abundance of effective means to keep them in balance, so there should be no limits to controlling these and their poisoned accomplices. Unfortunately, we have been stuck in an anti-isomorphic society for a very long time, so a great deal will need to be done to get out of this for good.

Conclusion
The biological layer beneath power is not incidental. It is a structural component of how power consolidates and maintains itself. As long as analyses of power structures ignore this layer or reduce it to purely spiritual or psychological phenomena, they remain incomplete. The pattern of Solomon repeats itself whenever groups attempt to use internal forces that lower moral and behavioral boundaries as instruments of control, without structurally limiting these forces within themselves and within the systems they build. Ultimately, this corrupts not only the population, but also the rulers themselves and the structures they have created. text:
Water trickled from the southern side of the temple.

It emptied into the polluted sea and made the waters fresh.

Living creatures multiplied and abundant fish filled the flow.

Fruit trees bore fresh fruit each month and leaves for medicine.

This is the vision of Ezekiel, the healing river from the sanctuary.

The Temple Stream in Ezekiel 47 Can Refresh a Life That Keeps Trying

A Holy Life Grows Where Grace Keeps Flowing

Many Catholics want a holy life and also know the familiar gap between desire and follow-through. A kind plan unravels. A prayer gets postponed. A habit you hoped to leave still knocks. Ezekiel 47 meets that gap with a bright image. Holiness looks like water leaving God's house and traveling toward thirsty ground. The stream does not demand a perfect traveler before it starts. It flows, and life appears along its path.

Where Does Holiness Quietly Begin?

The vision opens at the temple entrance. Water rises from beneath the threshold and runs toward the east. A guide then leads the prophet outside, around the long way, to the outer gate that faces east. There the stream shows itself again. That path is good news for anyone who tries and sometimes misses the mark. The source is not private strain. The source is God's dwelling. Catholics meet that dwelling in the Church, in Scripture, in the sacraments, and in honest prayer. A holy life begins with a return to the threshold, not with a lonely project of self-perfection. The walk around the outside matters too. Growth is guided. You can take the longer road, lose a step, and still find the water where God promised it. Small acts already belong to the stream. A sincere confession, a gentler reply, a few faithful minutes of prayer, these are real beginnings. They look modest. They carry the same water.

What If the Dry Place Is Exactly Where the Water Goes?

The guide describes the stream moving east and down into the dry valley. It reaches a bitter sea that cannot support life. There the water turns fresh. Living creatures thrive. Fish become many. Everything lives where the river arrives. This is a deeply hopeful word for people who know their tender spots. Sin can feel like water that sits still. The same reaction returns. The same worry pools. A hard thought says the place is beyond help. Ezekiel offers a brighter reading. The stream does not skip the lifeless sea. It enters it. Freshness comes from upstream as a gift. That picture can soften the work of avoiding sin. The aim is not a tighter jaw. The aim is to stay near the water that makes bitter water sweet. When anger, envy, lust, or neglect appears again, the holy next step is a return. Come back to Mass. Come back to mercy in Reconciliation. Come back to a friend who speaks truth with kindness. The reading promises life rather than a scolding. Old patterns can loosen. A heart can become a place where living things gather again. Slow change is still life, and life is the point of the river.

How Can Fruit and Healing Keep Coming Back?

Trees for food grow on both banks. Their leaves stay green. Their fruit does not run out. Fresh fruit appears month after month because the trees drink water from God's holy place. The fruit feeds. The leaves heal. Here the vision turns outward, and that turn is a relief. A holy life is not a private prize. It nourishes people. It helps people mend. You do not have to force a dramatic bloom on your own calendar. Water from the sanctuary keeps the trees in season. Fruit every month suggests a rhythm. One strong stretch does not have to cancel a hard stretch. The next stretch can still bear fruit. Healing leaves also speak to the times you fall short. Holiness includes repair. A sincere apology, a quiet act of care, a choice not to pass on gossip, these tend a wound without denying it. Catholics who want to avoid sin can look for this double gift. Seek fruit that feeds your own fidelity. Offer something that helps another person recover. Both grow from the same source.

What Does This Reading Give Your Next Good Step?

Ezekiel 47 is gentle with real effort. It shows a temple stream, a guided walk, a lifeless sea made fresh, and trees that keep giving. You do not have to become the river. You only have to remain near it. When you do good and then stumble, the vision still holds. Water flows from God's dwelling. Life follows that water. Food and healing grow on the banks. That is a holy life within reach. Begin again at the threshold. Let grace enter the place that feels stuck. Trust that fruit can return in its season, and that imperfect faithfulness can still become food and healing for someone nearby.

text:
The American Conservative: The Ukraine Conflict Could Have Been Prevented — Kiev and the West Missed Several Chances for Peace

New details about diplomacy between Russia and the West suggest the war in Ukraine was not inevitable. The publication traces a series of missed opportunities — from the Minsk agreements to the talks in Istanbul.

Minsk was used as a breather. Petro Poroshenko’s admission is recalled: the arrangements were «never meant to be implemented.» Kiev’s goal was to «delay the war — to secure eight years to restore economic growth and build powerful armed forces.» The «great diplomatic achievement,» as Poroshenko told the Financial Times, was that Ukraine, even «without having an armed forces at all,» managed to «keep Russia away from a full-sized war.»

Angela Merkel and François Hollande confirmed this: Minsk gave Ukraine the time and space to strengthen its military.

The Istanbul process came close to an agreement. Former MP Vadym Novinsky said that in the first days of the war, on Zelensky’s instructions, he organized negotiations. Russia demanded that neutrality and a rejection of NATO be enshrined in the constitution, along with a special status for Crimea and Donbass. Novinsky claims: «I coordinated every point with Zelensky, and at that time he agreed to everything.» But the process fell apart — according to him, «our leadership was to blame.»

The back channel didn’t work either. According to the Financial Times, lawyer Richard Conn and banker Bob Foresman reached Putin through Matthias Warnig. Putin replied that he was «very open to negotiations»: a pullback to prewar positions, de facto recognition of Crimea, the return of the ZNPP, and $300 billion for reconstruction. However, according to Warnig, Kiev barely looked at the offer, and Sullivan said Washington had not «approved» the channel.

At key moments, it was Kiev and its Western partners who walked away from diplomacy, not Moscow.

It was basically a threat from the US Tariff Commission and not inevitable if Washington had been willing to engage constructively in de-colonisation, as it was supposed to be doing.

Another threat made a few years later was that war veterans would lose their pensions if Puerto Rico became independent.

The newspaper I framed was the Puerto Rico World Journal, dated April 28, 1945. The main headline was about a surrender offer from Nazi Germany being rejected by the US and Britain because it didn't include Russia.

Some 65,000 Puerto Ricans fought for the US in that war believing they'd be rewarded with freedom, but instead they were told they'd be punished if they pushed for it.
 
The newspaper was among my father's Puerto Rican papers, most of which I'm donating to the archives @CentroPR in New York.

text:
GQ, who is not a scholar or scientist, claims that "science proves that Adam and Eve couldn't exist.”But, as usual, he is working from outdated assumptions, and not the latest science. His claim has been thoroughly debunked by actual secular, mainstream population genetics.

The breakthrough came from Dr. S. Joshua Swamidass, a computational biologist at Washington University in St. Louis. Swamidass is not a fringe creationist; he is a mainstream scientist who fully affirms evolutionary science and common descent. His crucial point: his mathematical and genetic findings have not been refuted by the scientific community. In fact, prominent evolutionary biologists who previously claimed science ruled out Adam and Eve have publicly admitted they were wrong and corrected their stances after reviewing the math. 

GQ’s claim completely falls apart because it confuses genetic ancestry with genealogicalancestry.  Even if genetics were to show that we didn't bottleneck down to just two people as the sole source of all our modern DNA, science doesn't track ancestry purely through DNA.  

Science tracks it through family trees. 

Dr. Swamidass demonstrates that because of how quickly family lines cross and overlap over time, standard population models prove that a single couple living in the past would inevitably become the universal ancestors of every single person on Earth. And because DNA dilutes so rapidly over generations, those ancestors would leave absolutely no genetic footprint today. They would be "genetic ghosts," completely invisible to modern DNA testing. Science literally cannot disprove their existence.

And, GQ’s original claim assumes this requires defending a rigid 6,000-year-old timeline. It doesn't. Dr. Swamidass’s work explicitly demonstrates that the math works whether you place this couple recently or much further back in deep time. The framework easily accommodates an ancient Adam and Eve or a more recent one, all while leaving the entire timeline of human evolution completely intact. 

So, like every other argument GC has made on X, this one attacks a strawman. A mainstream scientist used rigorous, unrefuted population genetics to prove that evolution outside a Garden and a literal couple inside a Garden can coexist without a single scientific contradiction.

But it would be “game on” even without GQ had some science to offer.

His claim is that  without a literal Adam, there is no "Original Sin," and thus no need for Jesus. This relies on the false notion that Jesus had to die because we inherited a "sin gene" or a guilty nature from Adam. But because GQ has never read the Bible, he’s also ignorant that of what is bad theology. The Bible doesn't teach that Jesus died to fix an inherited biological defect. Jesus died to redeem human beings from their actual, observable sins—the real greed, violence, and selfishness that we actively choose to commit every single day. 

As the Apostle Paul famously argued in 1 Corinthians 15, the single condition upon which the entire Christian faith turns is not an inheritance from Adam—it is the historical fact of the resurrection of Jesus. Paul explicitly writes, "If Christ has not been raised, your faith is futile and you are still in your sins." 

The hinge of Christianity is an empty tomb, not a bloodline.

🎄🇺🇸 CHRISTMAS THROUGH THE YEARS Christmas 1780: Betrayal, Hardship, and a Glimmer of Hope
By Christmas 1780, the American Revolution had entered its sixth year. The Continental Army was exhausted, supplies were scarce, and independence was still far from certain.

Yet even in one of the darkest years of the Revolution, there were reasons to hope.

❄️ Three glimpses of Christmas 1780:

🇺🇸 Another Winter Away From Home: George Washington's army settled into winter quarters around New Windsor, New York, and neighboring areas. After years of war, soldiers continued to face shortages, cold weather, and separation from their families.

🕯️ A Shocking Betrayal: Just three months earlier, General Benedict Arnold had been exposed for plotting to surrender West Point to the British. His betrayal shook the American cause and reminded Washington how fragile the fight for independence remained.

⭐ Hope in the South: Charleston had fallen to the British in May, and the American defeat at Camden followed in August. But the Patriot victory at Kings Mountain in October showed that the struggle was far from lost.

🎄 CHRISTMAS TRADITIONS IN 1780:

Christmas in colonial and Revolutionary America was quite different from our celebrations today. In communities that observed the holiday, families might decorate with fresh holly, ivy, and evergreens, gather for special meals, attend church services, or enjoy seasonal music. But Christmas was not celebrated across the colonies. Some religious communities discouraged or rejected the holiday altogether.

Decorated Christmas trees were already known in German-speaking Europe, but they had not yet become a widespread American tradition. The familiar Santa Claus, Christmas cards, and mass-produced glass ornaments would come much later.

❤️ The Spirit of Christmas 1780
For soldiers far from home, Christmas offered little relief from the uncertainty of war. Yet the hope of independence endured.
In 1776, America found hope. In 1777, it learned perseverance. In 1778, it gained strength. In 1779, it endured a brutal winter. And in 1780, even betrayal could not extinguish its determination.

❤️ From Yesterday's Mom, where it's always Christmas!

text:
April 2012. A rusted Harley washes ashore in North America after drifting 4,000 miles from the Japanese tsunami.

Harley Davidson offered to make it brand new for free, and a 29 year old man who had nothing left turned them down.

His name was Ikuo Yokoyama.

Before the March 2011 earthquake, that black 2004 Night Train was everything to Yokoyama. Then the tsunami hit Miyagi Prefecture, killing 15,000 people, including three members of his own family.

For over a year, Yokoyama slept on the floor of a tiny temporary shelter. Everything he had ever owned was at the bottom of the Pacific.

Or so he thought.

When Peter Mark discovered the salt crusted bike inside a broken storage box on Graham Island, Harley executives in Milwaukee stepped up. They offered to restore every bolt and fly the gleaming machine home to Japan.

Yokoyama shook his head.

He could not bear the thought of riding a shiny motorcycle past grieving neighbors who had lost their spouses and kids.

Instead, he gave up the last surviving piece of his old life. He asked Harley to display the bike untouched in Wisconsin, still crying ocean salt and red rust, as a voice for the 15,000 people who could no longer speak.

It stands there untouched to this day.

A man who lost everything refused a brand new dream so 15,000 strangers would never be erased from memory.

P Diddy was j*rking off in front of a hundred guests. A girl would walk up. Stay for a minute. Walk away. Then another. He’d go inside. Come back. Start again. A hundred women at his party and he was still sitting there doing it alone on a couch in full view of everyone.

She was twenty feet away when he leaned over to the man next to him and whispered four words. “I want her.”

Her name is Tanea. A singer from South Central. Never famous. She got flown to Miami by a man she calls the Prince who spent three weeks promising her a music career. The career meeting turned out to be a party on Star Island. The party turned out to be a freak off.

In the video below she walks through what she saw the way a paramedic would describe a scene they showed up to too late. No emotion. Just the sequence.

Phones went into sealed bubble cases at the door. His son Christian hand-picked who got in. She got white robe slippers. That was the pass. Inside, people were passed out on furniture. Others having sex with strangers in every room. House music shaking the walls at sunrise.

He called her over. Offered his photo booth. Ice cream. “Everything is free,” he said. Then he turned to the Prince and started whispering about her like she wasn’t standing right there.

“I want her. Like, I want her.”

Before she could ask what that meant, three people hit her with the same question. The Prince. A girl too far gone to stand straight. Then Diddy himself. “You’re going to Cuba with us, right?”

She said yes and walked straight to the front door.

She called the police on the Prince, got a printed plane ticket handed to her on the way out, and flew back to LA that night. She later learned that Cuba is the one place where they don’t always stamp your passport. And where people disappear.

In 2022, she told this story on camera. The internet called her a liar. Two years later the FBI kicked down that same front door.

Did P Diddy let her walk out because he had a hundred other girls that night, or because he already knew she’d never be able to prove a single thing she saw?

text:
A Decision Is Not the Same as the Capability to Act

Two households receive the same energy-price shock and make the same rational response: they cut consumption. One absorbs it — savings buffer it, an efficient home limits it, remote work removes its worst edge. The other cannot: savings deplete, retraining is deferred, work ends early. Identical behaviour. Different economy.

Economics sees the decision very well. It is largely blind to the structural conditions that determined which decisions were available in the first place.

On the 31st October, The Global Structure Network publishes the expanded institutional edition of The Household Affordability Frontier. It defines the structural threshold at which the combined financial, temporal, physical and participation costs of household life begin to restrict the capacity to accumulate and deploy productive capability — and connects three domains usually examined separately: household structural conditions, monetary transmission and heterogeneous-agent dynamics, and the allocation of long-duration capital.

The opportunity is structural: by shifting households from survival optimisation to capability investment, the Frontier converts economic participation from a trap into a mobility escalator — unlocking sustainable macroeconomic throughput and offering a route out of the inflation-stagnation loop.

For central banks, institutional investors, infrastructure capital and economic strategy teams, the practical question is straightforward: which structural costs are currently preventing existing capability from becoming productive capacity, and which forms of investment can measurably expand the residual space in which households can adapt?

The framework does not claim empirical superiority over existing approaches. It is offered as a proposed analytical architecture, not a finished model — with explicit measurement requirements, testable hypotheses and clear falsification conditions published in full. If threshold position and duration below it carry no predictive power beyond income and balance sheets, the framework fails.

What is stated here can be tested — by design.

text:
RAWA Statement on the Proposed Tyne–Wear Derby Bubble

A bubble match means away fans cannot get their ticket unless they travel on the official, police‑escorted coaches. No choice of transport, no freedom to plan your day. It places blanket restrictions on thousands of ordinary supporters. This would be the first bubble in the history of the Tyne–Wear derby, imposed after a fixture with only three arrests and described by police as “largely without incident.” There has been no consultation with supporters at any point in the seven months since that game.

Red and White Army is extremely concerned that such a drastic and restrictive measure has been pushed through without proper evidence, without meaningful engagement, and without any attempt to work with supporters on a proportionate plan.

The SAG minutes released this week raise serious questions. They show that concerns from the March derby were discussed, but they do not show any detailed evidence pack, incident data, intelligence summary or formal risk assessment being shared. The meeting appears to have centred almost entirely on a managed coach operation, with no alternative options formally presented, tested or compared. Supporter consultation didn’t happen before the recommendation was made, and “engagement” was only mentioned as something to do afterwards.

There is no sign of a balanced assessment of risk. Issues linked to independent travel were noted, but there is nothing to show these were weighed against the risks introduced by a compulsory coach operation. There is no distinction between different types of supporters, despite acknowledging that the vast majority behave responsibly. And there is nothing to show that targeted, less restrictive measures were even considered before deciding a bubble was the only answer.

Prior to receiving the SAG minutes (obtained via a Freedom of Information request), RAWA, the clubs, NUST and the FSA produced a detailed mitigation document. It sets out practical, proportionate steps covering behaviour, travel, stadium operations and policing. These include enhanced voluntary coach travel, managed rail options, alternative walking routes with larger buffer zones, targeted deployment at known congregation points, and strong fan‑led communications. Together, these measures offer a workable, collaborative approach that tackles the risks identified without removing supporter choice.

We have asked Northumbria Police to reassess the decision in light of these mitigations and the clear gaps in the SAG process. So far, they have refused to do so.

David Rose, Vice Chair of RAWA and Deputy CEO of the Football Supporters’ Association, said:

“A bubble is a backwards step for football policing. It strips away supporter freedoms, applies blanket restrictions to thousands of law‑abiding fans, and ignores a decade of progress in how high‑risk fixtures are managed. Supporters deserve better.”

Based on the information released to date, RAWA does not believe the case has been made that a compulsory bubble is necessary, proportionate or justified. We continue to urge Northumbria Police and partner agencies to revisit the decision and work with supporters and clubs on a safer, more balanced plan that respects both safety and supporter rights.

Supporters remain ready to work constructively with all stakeholders. What we need now is a willingness from Northumbria Police to do the same.

Supporters can read the full detail in the two documents linked below:

Joint Mitigation Proposal (RAWA, SAFC, NUFC, NUST, FSA)

RAWA Summary of SAG Minutes and Key Concerns

Please head over to our website for the full set of documents relating to the Safety Advisory Group Meeting.

text:
Do you struggle with money and sacrificial giving with faith being mentioned in church? 

In 2 Samuel ,  David said “I will not offer to the Lord my God burnt offerings that cost me nothing”

It's sad that people have become so cynical and jaded by those who have abused their authority, that even a good church; a church making real change in the local community can't talk about money without some people feeling uncomfortable, or taking to social media to write a review like it's all about them.

"I didn't like the lighting. They didn't play my preferred worship songs. They just want my money! 2 out of 5 stars. ⭐️⭐️✴️✴️✴️ "

My church, which is a larger church with locations in Massachusetts (where I go), DC, NY, TN, Santiago Chile, Florence Italy, Johannesburg South Africa, and very soon Nairobi Kenya, celebrated its 30th birthday this past Sunday. The actual anniversary is tomorrow.

Each location has what is called a 'Vision' offering each year- that people who call that church location-their home can give to, on Vision Sunday, and/or in installments from November to November. 
This is an Offering, so it is in addition to the tithe and treated accordingly.

In the case of the location I attend, the Vision for 2025-2026 was paying off our new building (our first permanent location for Massachusetts) in addition to creating a better ministry for grades 6-12, an autism-friendly room for Sunday mornings, and community outreach (meals, school supplies, helping individuals in difficult situations). 

Real lives being impacted, and none of it comes without a cost.

The Vision for 2026-2027 includes rolling over the remaining balance of the building (not yet paid off) and doubling the amount of outreach in the local community for 2027.

So unfortunately, if it was your first time coming to My church this past Sunday, with all the talk about the Vision offering and 'sacrificial giving', 
if you either didn't grasp the context, or already struggle with conversations about money- it probably made you squirm. I know this to be true because my wife saw a 'review' on Facebook to this end.

If you ever find yourself in such a scenario, I pray you'll do a heart check when it comes to money and the church. 
I'm not talking about opulence and fancy cars.
I'm talking about people putting their money where their mouth is, equipping the church to be the church, and not getting all bent out of shape when a pastor dares to teach on the tithe, or raise an impactful offering to do things like buy baby furniture for a pregnant mother, or school bags, turkey dinners, or Christmas gifts for the poorest among us.

Jesus didn't say, 'pay more taxes and let Caesar take care of the widow and orphan'; He told us to do it.

If your church needs to hold a bake sale to get anything done, it probably means that people aren't tithing or going above and beyond, or they are not being good stewards of the resources.
We as Christians shouldn't need to sell cookies or wash cars to make it possible to bless others. We should be stretching ourselves in this area, and making sure our priorities are where they need to be.

Give like you really believe our God owns it all, and will replenish.
Be the church.

text: Harvard econ prof Mankiw calculated his marginal tax rate at 90% back in 2010 (New York Times article). That's counting corporate income, capital gains, estate tax, etc. Excerpt: Suppose that some editor offered me $1,000 to write an article. If there were no taxes of any kind, this $1,000 of income would translate into $1,000 in extra saving. If I invested it in the stock of a company that earned, say, 8 percent a year on its capital, then 30 years from now, when I pass on, my children would inherit about $10,000. ... First, assuming that the Bush tax cuts expire, I would pay 39.6 percent in federal income taxes on that extra income. Beyond that, the phaseout of deductions adds 1.2 percentage points to my effective marginal tax rate. I also pay Medicare tax, which the recent health care bill is raising to 3.8 percent, starting in 2013. And in Massachusetts, I pay 5.3 percent in state income taxes, part of which I get back as a federal deduction. Putting all those taxes together, that $1,000 of pretax income becomes only $523 of saving. And that saving no longer earns 8 percent. First, the corporation in which I have invested pays a 35 percent corporate tax on its earnings. So I get only 5.2 percent in dividends and capital gains. Then, on that income, I pay taxes at the federal and state level. As a result, I earn about 4 percent after taxes, and the $523 in saving grows to $1,700 after 30 years. Then, when my children inherit the money, the estate tax will kick in. The marginal estate tax rate is scheduled to go as high as 55 percent next year, but Congress may reduce it a bit. Most likely, when that $1,700 enters my estate, my kids will get, at most, $1,000 of it. Without any taxes, accepting that editor’s assignment would have yielded my children an extra $10,000. With taxes, it yields only $1,000. In effect, once the entire tax system is taken into account, my family’s marginal tax rate is about 90 percent.

text:
“I kept my festivals indoors.” - I have seen this statement generate quite a bit of criticism. Let me offer my two cents on how I interpret it (ofcourse at the risk of being called a brown sepoy)

To me, keeping our festivals indoors does not mean confining our culture to the four walls of our homes or avoiding public celebrations altogether. It means celebrating responsibly and within the boundaries of local laws and community norms.

Here in the US, we celebrate festivals in our homes and backyards, at temples, in rented conference halls, and through organized community gatherings. I have Diwali fireworks and Holi celebrations in my own backyard where kids, from different demographics, from the neighborhood participate. Our children learn traditional dances, vocal music, and languages, often through temples and cultural organizations, and perform at organized events. 

They also get invited to perform at schools and other public gatherings, and we happily participate.

But here is what I have observed over the past 10 years. Let me share two incidents I know firsthand.

1. Diwali fireworks on a public ground in Morisville -  A group celebrated Diwali with fireworks on a ground without authorization, damaging the facility. For context, the City of Morrisville in North Carolina, had prepared this ground in record time as a cricket venue to host Major League Cricket (IPL equivalent in US) featuring international players. The police eventually had to issue a directive addressing this unauthorized activity.

2. A Ganesh Chaturthi procession in a neighboring community - A group of Indians took their cars out in a procession without obtaining the necessary permissions. They simply went around as though being the dominant demographic in that community gave them the right to do so.

These are just two examples of what some people might describe as expressing their religion and culture. Such incidents get discussed in my private circles, but rarely do we speak out publicly.

My question is simple -  Why not seek permission from the city or county and organize these celebrations properly? Why engage in unauthorized activities in the name of culture or religion when local authorities are often willing to grant permits, facilitate the event, and provide the necessary security?

There is another important consideration -  This is a two-way street. If we expect the freedom to express our own religious and cultural practices in public spaces, we must be prepared to extend the same principle to others. We cannot object, for instance, when another religious group gathers to pray in Times Square if we believe our own public religious expressions should be unquestionable.

Cultural preservation and religious expression are rights worth protecting. But they come with responsibilities. Respecting local laws, obtaining permits, and being considerate of the wider community do not dilute our culture. They demonstrate that we can preserve our traditions while respecting the society we are part of.

I’m a South Indian born & raised as a fourth-generation Delhi girl. I assimilated to such an extent that I looked like a Delhi girl—my Hindi was very fluent, I dressed like a North Indian & celebrated their festivals. I did the same in the US: changed my English, & dressed conforming to the American society.  I kept my festivals indoors. Now, recent arrivals from India—who just stepped off the plane into a path my generation and the ones before us spent decades paving—have the arrogance to call me and my ilk "brown sepoys." Instead of integrating, they are building parallel worlds, cut off from mainstream society. Other Asian groups understand a low profile. Blending in is resilience, not a betrayal. I haven’t lost my identity, I just don’t display it loud.

text:
I have an interesting counterproposal. 

A good friend of mine is thoroughly representative of the Rust Belt working class faction that broke away from the Dems and made Trump's election possible. He is not a man of statistics. He's not going to quote figures to me. But he does provide a reliable insight into the day to day goings on of the class he embodies, and through that he has been able to offer a kind of folksy anecdotal "truth" of the on the ground reality in a place like Michigan.

He was right when he predicted that based on what he was seeing in his local area Michigan was going to flip for Trump, to the shock and horror of the Liberals in our social circle. He was also right that El-Sayed was going to win. From the start of the Iran War he had reliably been informing me that his area felt betrayed and that they could not feed their families as gas and grocery prices rose. He said this war was going to cost us the state and he was right.

But he painted a picture for me of something still in the future, something "distant," but a sentiment starting to get some "ironic" discussion. It went something like this:

As the MAGA coalition appears to implode as a consequence of losing the midterms, and particularly as Trump now starts to make conciliatory statements that abandon his base, he described a sense of disillusionment with the capability of the American Traditional Right (not the neo-cons, but those who would appeal to older conceptions of America) to meaningfully deliver answers to the needs young American men, and that this failure represents a kind of surrender. 

In other words, the MAGA coalition feels like it squandered the last chance to save what America was, and so in failing to do that young men are looking to something else that will grant them the ability to express a kind of masculine excellence.

text:
Stanford CS230, Agents, Prompts, and RAG, Lecture 8 (Part 2) continued: prompt chaining

Chaining is the most popular technique covered so far, and it is different from chain of thought. Chain of thought asks for step-by-step reasoning inside one prompt. Chaining splits a complex task across separate prompts.

The example: read a customer review and write a professional response that acknowledges the concern, explains the issue, and offers a resolution. The review says a laptop arrived three days late with damaged packaging, and the customer needed it urgently for work. As a single prompt, this may work, but every step is mixed together, so you can't tell which one is weak.

Chained version. Prompt 1: identify the key concerns in the review. Prompt 2: using those issues, draft an outline that acknowledges concerns, explains possible reasons, and offers a resolution. Prompt 3: using the outline, write the full response.

Now each prompt can be tested on its own, so you can find where optimization pays off most. A better outline might raise open rate or user satisfaction. Chaining improves performance, and its bigger value is control over the workflow and easier debugging.
