text:
FLP CHAPBOOK OF THE DAY: Breaking Through Broken by Saitharn Im-Iam
 
On SALE:  https://t.co/lZT2cANLxI
    
In this debut chapbook, Breaking Through Broken, is a collection of poems portraying a Thai immigrant’s imperfect and incomplete journey. Through vivid fragments, this collection delves into the unflinching and uncompromising reality of a once-broken poet’s autobiography, tracing her journey from childhood immigration to a tumultuous adolescence. Words, stories, and emotions are interwoven to offer a poignant exploration of the journey of an unyielding young immigrant who carries within her the essence of a fluctuating cultural connection, childhood dreams, brutal realities, and the yearnings of the universe. #poetry #ThaiAmerican #BIPOC #memory #childhood
 
Saitharn Im-Iam is a first-generation Thai American poet, writer, English instructor, and life-long dreamer. She received her MA from Emporia State University, and received her BA from Pittsburg State University where she graduated Summa Cum Laude. She loves all things nerdy–specifically anime, video games, comic books, and magic in every essence. She has been published in the Cow Creek Review, The Blue Route, Coelacanth, Runestone, Mockingheart Review, Flint Hills Review, and Midwest Quarterly. Breaking Through Broken is her debut chapbook.
PRAISE:
.
In Sai Im-Iam’s heartbreaking debut collection, we’re introduced to a speaker born as cataclysm. Fragmentation, rebirth, regeneration, and creation haunt these poems strong enough to converse with such great poetic voices as Lucille Clifton in her “Shapeshifter” poems, and as Gwendolyn Brooks, to whom she responds, “We / learn white.” Sai Im-Iam is a woman who deserves to be recognized, and I mean that quite literally—because as an immigrant child in America with “a ‘Valid for Work Only’” card, her community failed her in all the most important ways a child can be failed. “I was an immigrant daughter with a middle school education,” she writes in the collection’s third poem as the narrative body of this book builds a complex backstory for a poet whose lyrical voice (Thank goodness, she is now voiced!) will move the reader to tears. Evocative details of personal experience unspool in such skilled and beautiful poetic lines as “My mom was there with light earthen eyes, / a gentle smile, and a large pot of jok / to cure illness of the body or heart,” and:
A kid, with nowhere to go, standing in an open,
grassy plain of nowhere Kansas
with only one match.”
Sai Im-Iam, a woman who has had to go out with “lanterns looking for [her]self”; who has created toys of stars—rocking horse, flowers and pearls—“in the night sky where the stars did more than survive,” has written poems to transform a violent obscene world. In these poems she claims her place amongst American letters.”
–Laura Lee Washburn, author of Arteries, The Book of Stolen Images, This Good Warm Place, and Watching the Contortionists
.
With the care she uses to describe how one of her poem’s characters prepares traditional Thai rice, this whole collection is seasoned with precision along with a keen eye for important, representative, cultural detail. This whole collection wafts with that enticing aroma and ushers in a new strong voice—like a searchlight’s strong cone of light up through the clouds, a signal from a new, promising, illuminated strain in American poetry.
–Kevin Rabas, Poet Laureate of Kansas, 2017-2019

text:
Richard Bernard "Red" Skelton (1913–1997) was one of America’s most beloved physical comedians, vaudevilians, and entertainers...

Raised by a single mother, Ida Mae, Skelton began working around age seven—selling newspapers and doing odd jobs. By age 10, he performed on street corners to help support his family. At age 15, he left home to join traveling medicine shows and vaudeville acts, learning silent timing, facial expressions, and physical comedy from veteran performers.

In 1930, Skelton met Edna Stillwell in Kansas City. Impressed by her candid feedback on his comedy, they married. Edna became his manager and chief writer, helping craft their breakout "Doughnut Dunkers" pantomime sketch inspired by people in a diner. The act led to major theatre bookings, radio shows starting in 1937, and a contract with MGM in the 1940s, where he starred in over 30 films. He achieved his greatest fame hosting The Red Skelton Show (later The Red Skelton Hour) on NBC and CBS from 1951 to 1971, pulling in nearly 40 million weekly viewers at its peak and winning multiple Emmy Awards.

. . . 

Red Skelton was one of America's biggest entertainment stars long before television became mainstream. After finding success in radio, films, and live vaudeville, he launched The Red Skelton Show on television in 1951. His gentle, family-friendly comedy and beloved characters made him a household name. For nearly two decades, the show consistently ranked among television's most-watched programs, drawing millions of viewers each week.

By the late 1960s, however, television networks had become obsessed with attracting younger audiences. Even though The Red Skelton Show was still performing well in the ratings, CBS executives believed its viewers were too old to appeal to advertisers. In 1970, the network canceled the show as part of what became known as the "rural purge," a sweeping effort that removed many popular but older-skewing programs from the schedule. Skelton was reportedly offered opportunities to modernize his act, but he refused to abandon the wholesome style that had made him famous.

Losing his television show did not end his career. Instead, Skelton returned to what he loved most: performing live. He spent the next 22 years touring the United States, filling theaters and casino showrooms with loyal fans who continued to support him. He also devoted more time to painting, another lifelong passion. When he retired in 1992, he had outlasted countless television trends, proving that while networks chase demographics, genuine audience loyalty can endure for generations.

His remarkable success as a painter. While most people remember him as a comedian, he spent decades creating artwork, especially clown paintings that reflected both humor and melancholy. Skelton took painting seriously, often working for hours after performances, and eventually sold thousands of pieces through galleries and television specials. 

By the later years of his life, his artwork had become so popular that it generated millions in sales, giving him a second creative legacy beyond entertainment. Many fans who knew him only from television were surprised to learn that he considered painting one of his greatest passions.

The scenario described is not some fringe speculation, but rather a verifiable account of internal debates in Washington in early November 2026. On November 7, Joe Kent, the former director of the National Counterterrorism Center (NCTC), publicly accused U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) of "bypassing the White House" and "inviting Iranian escalation" by expanding a naval blockade into a land-based one—dubbed Task Force "Iron Gate"—at a time when Vice President Vance was leading indirect negotiations with Iran. Kent’s exact words were: "This is CENTCOM inviting Iranian escalation while the Vice President is attempting to negotiate with the Iranians." He characterized this as "policy by CONOP" (concept of operations)—a situation where the military takes actions that ensure the escalation or continuation of a conflict, all without explicitly defying the President. Regarding the incident on October 19–20—just one week before the election—when Israel flew dozens of combat aircraft to the Iranian border before turning back, U.S. officials told *Axios* that some speculated Israel might have been attempting to goad Iran into opening fire, thereby providing a pretext for an Israeli strike.

Kent’s Allegations: The Verifiable Details

Joe Kent resigned from his position as director of the National Counterterrorism Center in March 2026, citing his assessment that Iran did not pose an imminent threat. On November 7, he posted on X regarding a new task force announced by CENTCOM, codenamed "Iron Gate." Comprising approximately 20 military and civilian personnel and based in Tampa, Florida, the unit’s mission is to "disrupt" Iran’s overland supply routes. Kent’s characterization is as follows:

“This is CENTCOM inviting an escalation with Iran at the very moment the Vice President is attempting to negotiate with them. It is an example of what CENTCOM calls ‘policy dictated by operational concepts’—where the military finds a way to subvert the White House without openly defying the President, by taking actions that ensure war escalates or persists.” He added, “This strategy has been employed time and again throughout the wars on terror in Iraq, Syria, and Afghanistan. Many Americans have died needlessly.”

Kent describes the continuation of the blockade as an “illusion of choice,” noting that enforcing it “puts our troops in harm’s way and risks them being shot down, which would inevitably drag us back into kinetic warfare.” He urged Trump to “install a new national security team—one not wedded to waging war, but capable of ending it.”

Vance’s Negotiations and CENTCOM’s Actions: Parallel Realities

The factual basis for Kent’s allegations lies in the fact that two separate tracks were unfolding in parallel during the same period.

Over the past two weeks, Vance has been directly involved in indirect consultations with Iran. He sent a letter to the Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, Rezaei, proposing a resumption of direct negotiations, and has been in near-daily communication with the Prime Minister of Qatar and the Chief of Army Staff of Pakistan. These mediation efforts have shown “progress, albeit very slow.” Within Trump’s inner circle, Vance is the most prominent opponent of war; on November 4, he stated publicly, “The reason we are losing is because of the wars themselves.”

Meanwhile, on November 7, CENTCOM announced the formation of Task Force “Iron Gate,” which expanded the blockade from maritime routes to include overland supply lines. On the same day, CENTCOM disclosed that its forces had disabled a St. Kitts-registered cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman that was attempting to breach the blockade. On November 6, Trump himself confirmed a “small-scale strike” that destroyed an Iranian air-defense installation—an action on which CENTCOM had offered no comment prior to the President’s confirmation. Israeli Border Flights: Documented, but Intent Remains a Matter of Inference

On the night of October 19–20, dozens of Israeli fighter jets and refueling aircraft flew through the airspace of Syria and Iraq, following a flight path similar to one that would be used for an actual strike. They reached the vicinity of the Iranian border before turning back, without ever entering Iranian airspace. The operation covered a distance of over 800 miles and involved dozens of combat aircraft. Israel notified the United States in advance, characterizing the operation as a "deterrence exercise."

However, U.S. officials told Axios and Israel’s Channel 12 that some suspected Israel might have been attempting to goad Iranian air defenses into opening fire—thereby providing a pretext for an Israeli strike on Iran. One U.S. official remarked, "The impression we got was that Israel wanted Iran to fire on the jets, which could then be used to justify a strike on Iran." The flights took place one week before Israel’s October 27 election, a time when Benjamin Netanyahu was seeking reelection.

Interpreting the Situation

Kent’s allegations represent the political judgment of a former official rather than verified institutional fact. His interpretation—that U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) was "undermining the White House"—rests on the premise that Donald Trump himself was either unaware of or had not authorized the expansion of the "Iron Gate" initiative. The White House, however, has not clarified whether Trump approved the expansion. What can be verified is that CENTCOM announced the task force, Vance was engaged in negotiations during the same period, and Trump—speaking publicly—both acknowledged "small-scale strikes" and stated that "we are in talks with Iran."

What Kent describes as an "illusion of choice"—a false dichotomy between "maintaining a blockade" and "resuming large-scale strikes," both of which lead to the same outcome—points to a genuine structural issue: when a military establishment simultaneously enforces a blockade and prepares for strikes, while diplomatic channels operate on a separate track, who controls the pace of escalation? It is a verified fact that both tracks existed concurrently in early November, with no public mechanism for coordination between them. Kent’s assessment is that this parallel operation, in itself, constituted an act of "subversion." Whether this assessment holds true depends on whether Trump was aware of and authorized the action—a point that cannot be determined from currently available public information.

Good morning India !
#HappyBhaiDooj2026 

Tomorrow Wednesday, November 11 , 2026 most of the Hindus in India will be celebrating #BhaiDooj. Let me tell you, all you need to know about this great #hindufestival .

 The #Legends

According to the legends, Lord #Yamraj, the God of Death, visited his sister #Yamuna on the second day after Diwali. He was given a hearty welcome by his sister, when he visited her home. On his arrival, she performed #aarti, applied #tilak on his forehead and adorned his neck with a beautiful garland. She cooked delicious dishes and prepared sweets for him. Touched by her heartfelt welcome, Yamraj bestowed presents upon her and showered blessings on her.

He gave her a boon that every time a brother visits his sister on this day, he would be prospered with health and wealth. This is why Bhai Dooj is also known as #YamDwitiya. 

Another version states that Lord #Krishna, after killing Narakasur, the demon king day before Diwali, went to meet his sister #Subhadra. Subhadra welcomed Him in the traditional way by Aarti and putting on His forehead a tilak of her sisterly protection.

Another story behind the origin of Bhai Dooj says that when #BhagwanMahavir, the founder of #Jainism, attained #Nirvana, his brother King #Nandivardhan was distressed because he missed him and was comforted by his sister #Sudarshana. Since then, women have been revered during Bhai Dooj.Thus, Bhai Dooj has also become an important festival for the followers of #Jainism.

👉Bhai Dooj Celebrations
 
On the auspicious day of 'Yam-Dwitiya' the people of #Kayastha community of Hindus celebrate the holy function of worshipping Lord #Chitragupta who, it is believed maintains the records of life and death of the human beings. The Kayastha community also worships the pen, paper and ink on this day in the honor of Lord Chitragupta. 

In #Bengal Bhai Dooj is called #BhaiPhota and is celebrated with a lot of grandeur . Sisters religiously fast until she applies a #phota or mark with sandal wood paste on her brother's forehead, offers him sweets and gifts and prays for his long and healthy life. An Aarti is also performed. 

In #Punjab this day is known as #Tikka. Sisters make a paste with saffron and rice and place an auspicious mark on their brothers’ foreheads as a symbolic gesture to ward off all harm.
 
In #UttarPradesh, the brother is gifted with an #aabf, a length of flax, knotted into a circular shape and dotted with sugar #batashas. After performing all the rituals that include the sister applying a #tilak of roli and rice on her brother's forehead and praying for him with an aarti to shed off all the evil effects, the story of Bhai Dooj ( #BhaiDoojKatha) is narrated.

👉The essence of the Bhai dooj festival is that it is celebrated to strengthen the love between brothers and sisters. It is a day of food-sharing, gift-giving and reaching out to the inner most depths of their hearts.

text:
Megan Thee Stallion was riding home from a party at Kylie Jenner's house when rapper Tory Lanez told her best friend, right there in the car, that he was sleeping with Megan. Then it came out he was sleeping with the friend too.
A fight broke out. As Megan walked away from the car, Tory yelled "Dance, bitch" and shot her in the feet.
Afterwards he offered her $1 million to stay quiet. She didn't. And the whole world started talking not about the shooting, but about who she was sleeping with.
Then someone pushed a fake AI porn video of her across the internet.

Megan and Tory got close because they had both lost their mothers. They slept together now and then, but Megan saw him as a friend. Her best friend and assistant, Kelsey Harris, had a crush on him.

July 12, 2020, around 4 a.m. The three of them left Kylie Jenner's house in the same Escalade. In the car, Tory told Kelsey he was sleeping with Megan. Then it came out he had slept with Kelsey too.

Megan said she didn't want any part of it and got out. Tory held a gun out the window, yelled "Dance, bitch" and fired at her feet.
At 4:27 a.m. Kelsey texted a friend: "Help. Tory shot Meg. 911."

When police arrived, Megan sat handcuffed in the ambulance, crying, her feet covered in blood. She told officers she'd stepped on glass. Protests against police brutality were sweeping America, and she was afraid they'd shoot first and ask later.

According to testimony, Tory then offered Megan and Kelsey $1 million each to stay quiet. Megan said no.
Two months later he put out an album claiming he hadn't shot anyone and was being framed.

The trial began in December 2022. Megan was 27, and she had to testify under oath, in front of everyone, about when and with whom she'd had sex. Tory's lawyer told the jury Kelsey was the one who really fired, out of jealousy.

"I'm not on trial!" Megan said on the stand. "This whole story has not been about the shooting. It's only been about who I been having sex with."
She said she sometimes wishes he had killed her. She still has nerve damage and can't feel part of her left foot.

The jury found Tory guilty on all three counts. In August 2023 he was sentenced to 10 years.

Even after the verdict, it didn't stop. Blogger Milagro Gramz pushed her followers to watch an AI-made porn video of Megan. Megan sued, saying the blogger was a paid mouthpiece for Tory and his father.

On December 1, 2025, a Miami jury found the blogger liable for promoting the deepfake and for coordinating with Tory. They awarded Megan $75,000.
Then the judge cut it to $59,000 on a technicality: the jury had ruled the blogger a "media defendant," and Florida law says those must be warned before they're sued.
The blogger also has to pay Megan's legal fees. Her lawyer said he was grateful the jury didn't award seven figures.

$1 million to stay quiet. 10 years for the bullets. $59,000 for the fake porn.

What should spreading a deepfake of someone actually cost?

text:
A note before you read: we are talking about the killing of 13-year-old Mary Phagan and the man convicted of it.

From the Georgia Supreme Court appeal record, Slides 0979 to 0981: a second copy of Judge Leonard S. Roan's charge to the jury, signed "Examined and approved as my charge in this case, Nov. 1, 1913" (printed on the slide). The charge was read to the jury on Monday, August 25, 1913 (trial record).

Mary Anne Phagan, 13, was murdered at the National Pencil Company in Atlanta on Saturday, April 26, 1913. A Fulton County jury convicted Leo Max Frank, the factory superintendent, on Monday, August 25, 1913. Judge Leonard Strickland Roan of the Fulton County Superior Court denied him a new trial on Friday, October 31, 1913, and the Georgia Supreme Court affirmed the conviction on Tuesday, February 17, 1914.

A judge's charge is his instruction to the jury on the law. Roan told them that once a killing is proven to be the act of the defendant, "the law presumes malice," and that they were "the sole judges of the credibility of the witnesses." He cautioned that the Solicitor General's questions to character witnesses were not themselves evidence. He told them Frank's statement was "not made under oath" and that they could believe as much or as little as they chose.

The defense version, 1913 and modern: the jury was swept along by the crowd.

The prosecution's answer at the time: the jury was told, in writing, to give Frank every reasonable doubt.

Our modern rebuttal: they had that instruction and they still convicted. The charge is fair on its face.

Forever 13 and Never forgotten.

#MaryPhagan #LeoFrank

Appendix: Full slide transcripts

Slide 0979

When a homicide is proven, if it is proven to be the act of the defendant, the law presumes malice, and unless the evidence should relieve the slayer he may-be found guilty of murder. The presumption of innocence is removed by proof of the killing by the defendant. When the killing is shown to be the act of the defendant, it is then on the defendant to justify or mitigate the homicide.

The proof to do that may come from either side, either from the evidence offered by the State to make out its case, or from the evidence offered by the defendant, or the defendant's statement.Gentlemen of the jury, you are now the sole judges of the credibility of the witnesses and the weight of the testimony of each and every witness.

It is for you to take this testimony as you have heard it, in connection with the defendant's statement, and arrive at what you believe to be the truth.Gentlemen, the object of all legal investigation is the discovery of truth. That is the reason of you being selected and sworn in this case--to discover what is the truth on this issue formed on this bill of indictment.

Is Leo M. Frank guilty? Are you satisfied that beyond a reasonable doubt from the evidence in this case? Or is his plea of not guilty the truth? The rules of evidence are framed with a view to this prominent end--seeking always for pure sources and the highest https://t.co/tviKNGvXiR evidence is that which immediately points to the question at issue.

Indirect or circumstantial evidence is that which only tends to establish the issue by proof of various facts sustaining, by their consistency, the hypothesis claimed. To warrant a conviction on circumstantial evidence, the proven facts must not only be consistent with the hypothesis of guilt, but must exclude every other reasonable hypothesis save that of the guilt of the accused.

The defendant has introduced testimony as to his good character. On this subject, I charge you that evidence of good character when offered by the defendant in a criminal case is always relevant and material, and should be considered by the jury, along with all the other evidence introduced, where the facts of the case.

It should be considered by the jury, not merely where the balance of the testimony in the case makes it doubtful whether the defendant is guilty or not, but also where such evidence of good character may of itself generate a doubt as to the defendant's guilt. Good character in a substantial fact, like any other fact tending to establish the defendant's innocence, and ought to be so regarded by the jury.

If, after all other facts are proved in the case, it should be weighed and estimated by the jury, for it may render that doubtful which would otherwise be clear. However, if the guilt of the accused is plainly proved to the satisfaction of the jury beyond a reasonable doubt, notwithstanding the proof of good character, it is their duty to convict.

But the jury may consider the good character of the defendant, whether the rest of the testimony leaves the question of his guilt doubtful or not, and if a consideration of the proof of his good character, considered along with the evidence, creates a reasonable doubt in the minds of the jury as to the defendant's guilt, then it would be the duty of the jury to give the defendant the benefit of the doubt thus raised by his good character, and to acquit him.

(Stephens case, 81 Ga. 589).The word "character" as used in this connection, means that general reputation which he bore among the people who knew him prior to the time of the death of Mary Phagan. Therefore, when the witnesses by which a defendant seeks to prove his good character are put upon the stand, and testify that his character is good, the effect of the testimony is to say that the people who knew him spoke well of him, and that his general reputation was otherwise good. When a defendant has put his character in issue, the State is157

Slide 0980

allowed to attack it by proving that his general reputation is not good, or by showing that the witnesses who have stated that his character is good, have untruly reported it. Hence, the Solicitor-General has been allowed to cross-examine the witnesses for the defense who were introduced to testify to his good character.

In the cross-examination of these witnesses, he was allowed to ask them if they had not heard of various acts of misconduct on the defendant's part. The Solicitor-General had the right to ask any questions along this line he pleased, in order thoroughly to sift the witnesses, and to see if anything derogatory to the defendant's reputation could be proved by them.

The Court now wishes to caution you that, although the Solicitor-General was allowed to ask the defendant's character witnesses these questions as to their having heard of various acts of alleged misconduct on the defendant's part, the jury is not to consider this as evidence that the defendant has been guilty of any such misconduct as may have been indicated in the questions of the Solicitor-General, or any of them, unless the alleged witnesses testify to it.

Furthermore, where a man's character is put in evidence, and in the course of the investigation any specific act of misconduct is shown, this does not go before the jury for the purpose of showing affirmatively that his character is bad or that he is guilty of the offense with which he stands charged, but is to be considered by the jury only in determining the credibility and the degree of information possessed by those witnesses who have testified to his good character.

(Henderson's case, 5 Ga. App. 495 (3)).When the defendant has put his character in issue, the State is allowed to bring witnesses to prove that his general character is bad, and thereby to disprove the testimony of those who have stated that it is good. The jury is allowed to take this testimony, and have the right to consider it along with all the other evidence introduced on the subject of the general character of the defendant, and it is for the jury finally to determine from all character evidence whether his character was good or bad.

But a defendant is not evidence of the crime with which he stands charged, even though, upon the consideration of all the evidence, as to his character, the jury believes that a character is bad, unless from all the other testimony in the case they believe he is guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.

You will, therefore, observe that this is the rule you will be guided in determining the effect to be given to the evidence on the subject of the defendant's character: If, after considering all the evidence pro and con, on the subject of the defendant's character, you believe that prior to the time of Mary Phagan's death he bore a good reputation among those who knew him, that his general character was good, you will consider that as one of the facts in the case, and it may be sufficient to create a reasonable doubt of the defendant's guilt, if it so impresses your minds and consciences, after considering it along with all the other evidence in the case; and if, after consideration, you should believe the benefit of the doubt and acquit him it does you should give the defendant the benefit of the doubt and acquit him.

If, however, though you should believe his general character was good, still, after giving due weight to it as one of the facts in the case, you believe from the evidence as a whole that he is guilty beyond a reasonable doubt, you would be authorized to convict him.If you believe beyond a reasonable doubt from the evidence in this case that this defendant is guilty of murder, then you would be authorized in that event to say "We, the jury, find the defendant guilty."

Should you go no further, gentlemen, and say nothing else in your verdict, the Court would have to sentence the defendant to the extreme penalty for murder, to-wit: to be hanged by the neck until he is dead. But should you see fit to do so, in the event you arrive at the conclusion and belief beyond a reasonable doubt from158

Slide 0981

the evidence that this defendant is guilty, then, gentlemen, you would be authorized in that event, if you saw fit, to do so, to say: "We, the jury, find the defendant guilty, and we recommend that he be imprisoned in the penitentiary for life." In the event you should make such a verdict as that, then the Court, under the law, would have to sentence the defendant to the penitentiary for life.

You have heard the defendant make his statement. He had the right to make it under the law. It is not made under oath and he is not subject to examination or cross-examination. It is with you as to how much of it you will believe, or how little of it. You may go to the extent, if you see fit, of believing it in preference to the sworn testimony in the case.

In the event, gentlemen, you have a reasonable doubt from the evidence, or the evidence and the statement together, or either as to the defendant's guilt as charged, then give the prisoner the benefit of that doubt, and acquit him; and in the event you do acquit him, the form of your verdict would be: "We, the jury, find the defendant not guilty."

As honest jurors do your utmost to reach the truth from the evidence and statement as you have heard it here, then let your verdict speak it.Examined and approved as my charge in this case, Nov. 1, 1913.(Signed) L. S. ROAN,J. S. C., St. Mt. Ct.

References

text:
Stellantis has officially confirmed the sale of its long idled Brampton Assembly Plant to Canadian defence technology company Roshel
The automotive giant announced the deal on Monday evening, concluding months of speculation and a tense standoff with its workforce union, Unifor.
The sale transfers ownership of the world class auto plant to Roshel, a major Brampton based manufacturer of armoured and tactical vehicles. Roshel’s CEO, Roman Shimonov, previously outlined plans to establish a "Canadian Centre of Excellence for Defence Manufacturing" at the massive facility. The total purchase price and specific conditions of the transaction have not yet been publicly disclosed. Prior to the official confirmation, Unifor leaders publically stated they were treating Stellantis's initial refusal to deny the transaction as a confirmation. The union has demanded that the contract's conditions be made entirely public. The permanent pivot away from traditional automotive assembly marks a critical economic shift for the region. Industry experts note that Roshel’s smaller production runs of light utility and armoured vehicles will not replicate the extensive employment levels or heavy supply chain demand of a major car manufacturer. 
To mitigate the blow, Roshel has indicated they are prepared to offer "letters of commitment for first consideration" to the laid off automotive employees. The facility has been inactive since late 2023, a shutdown that initially left over 2,200 hourly union members out of work. Stellantis had originally promised to build the next generation Jeep Compass there, but ultimately redirected that $2.8 billion investment to an Illinois plant following policy and EV tariff uncertainties.

(Roshel’s CEO, Roman Shimonov pictured below.)

**The main sources for the court orders and judgments in *Schiff v Nine Network Australia Pty Ltd* (Federal Court of Australia, file NSD 1086 of 2021) are the official public court portals.**

### 1. Federal Court / Commonwealth Courts Portal (best for the final orders)

- File number: **NSD1086/2021**

Title: *PETER DAVID SCHIFF v NINE NETWORK AUSTRALIA PTY LTD ACN 008 685 407 & ORS*

Finalised: 21 November 2023

- Direct list of orders:

https://t.co/GsF1i9JsqV

The key final document is the **consent orders of Justice Jackman dated 21 November 2023**. These state (in substance):

- Judgment entered for the Applicant (Schiff) against the Respondents in the sum of $550,000.

- The first and second respondents (Nine and The Age) to pay the Applicant’s costs on an ordinary basis until December 2021 and thereafter on an indemnity basis.

- Permanent removal of the Broadcast (and related videos).

Respondents listed include Nine Network Australia Pty Ltd, The Age Company Pty Ltd, **Nicholas McKenzie**, Charlotte Grieve, and Joel Tozer.

You can view/download the stamped orders from the portal (search by file number if the direct link needs refreshing).

### 2. AustLII (free full text of published reasons/judgments)

Search for “Schiff v Nine Network” on https://t.co/kj8wXmtYxT. Key ones include:

- *Schiff v Nine Network Australia Pty Ltd (No 2)* [2022] FCA 1120 (Jagot J, 23 September 2022) — the main liability decision finding that the *60 Minutes* broadcast conveyed several defamatory imputations.

https://t.co/GLPYUNcARz

(Word/PDF versions available on the Federal Court judgments site as well.)

- Subsequent interlocutory judgments by Jackman J (No 3, No 4, No 5, No 6, No 7, etc.) dealing with pleadings, discovery, costs, subpoenas, and case management. These form part of the series of orders/judgments Schiff has described.

AustLII pages usually offer HTML text you can copy plus links to original Word documents or PDFs.

### 3. Peter Schiff’s compilation

Schiff has posted links and hosted PDFs of several of the judgments/orders on his site, including a page titled something like “Peter Schiff Wins All Seven Defamation Judgments…” at https://t.co/lAZF0qxlpE. That can be a convenient single place to grab multiple documents.

### Practical tips for a Word document

- Download the PDFs or Word versions from the court sites / AustLII and insert them, or copy-paste the text (orders are short; reasoned judgments are longer).

- The final “win” is primarily the 21 November 2023 consent orders (judgment entered against the respondents, including McKenzie personally). There is no lengthy final trial judgment on damages because the matter was resolved by consent after earlier findings and interlocutory losses by the respondents.

- Earlier judgments (especially the 2022 imputation decision) establish that the broadcast carried defamatory meanings.

These are all publicly available Australian court records. Start with the Commonwealth Courts order list and the AustLII No 2 judgment for the core documents.

text:
A Sacred Place Still Being Built

There is a scene in the Gospel of John that begins in noise and ends in promise. Jesus enters the temple and finds commerce where reverence should stand. He drives out the traders and overturns the tables. The moment can look severe, yet its center is care. He wants the house of God to be a house of prayer, not a marketplace that forgets why people came.

That care reaches people who are trying. You may set out to be gentle and then speak too fast. You may plan a quiet prayer and then lose the quiet to worry. Failure of that kind does not place you outside grace. It places you in the very human story this Gospel knows well. God looks past the scattered coins of a hard stretch and sees the desire that brought you toward him in the first place.

A Promise Hidden in Plain Speech

In the middle of the tension, Jesus offers a line that still stops readers short. "Destroy this temple and in three days I will raise it up." Listeners picture timber, stone, and long years of labor. They cannot yet see what he means. He speaks of the temple of his body. He speaks of a death that will not keep him, and of a rising that will open worship to every seeking heart. The words sound impossible, and that is part of their gift. They teach us that God rebuilds what human eyes call ruined.

Hold that sentence beside your own unfinished efforts. A good intention can collapse under pressure. A kind plan can fray. None of that is the final architecture. The promise in those words is patient strength. What love intends, love can raise. The three days in the story become a sign for every season when hope needs more time than pride wants to give.

The Body as a Meeting Place

The deeper meaning moves from one building in Jerusalem to the life of Jesus himself. He becomes the place where God and humanity meet without a toll. After the resurrection, worship is no longer confined to a single court of stone. It lives in forgiven people, in shared bread, in mercy practiced at a kitchen table, and in the courage to begin again after a fall. Zeal for the Father's house becomes zeal for a clean heart, not a spotless performance.

This is good news for anyone who keeps trying and does not always arrive. The Gospel does not ask you to pretend the tables never tip. It asks you to trust the one who raises what has been brought low. Your imperfect yes still matters. A short prayer after a long mistake still matters. A quiet return to kindness still matters. God is not keeping a ledger meant to defeat you. God is raising a temple in you, and construction allows for repairs.

Hope You Can Carry

Let the scene encourage rather than accuse. The overturned tables point toward order, not shame. The startling promise points toward life, not threat. If your faith feels under renovation, you are not late and you are not lost. Stay near the words that outlast stone. What seems destroyed can be raised. What you offer in love, even when it comes with cracks, is held by the one who rebuilds from the inside.

text:
The meaning of this scene from Apocalypto is that, in the end, the white Christian man arrived to put an end to paganism and the widespread practice of human sacrifice among indigenous peoples—brown, black, and white—around the world.

In Maya and Aztec societies, captives and slaves were routinely dragged up temple pyramids, held down on stone altars, and had their chests cut open with obsidian knives so priests could rip out their still-beating hearts as offerings to the gods. Victims were also decapitated, thrown alive into sacred cenotes, or flayed; their skulls were displayed on racks, and in some cases parts of the bodies were eaten. These were not rare events—major temples could see thousands sacrificed in a single ceremony, and constant warfare was waged largely to capture more victims.

White pagan societies in Europe practiced their own aggressive forms of ritual violence. In the Roman world, human sacrifice was carried out in earlier periods and in moments of crisis, including the live burial of Gauls and Greeks after the Battle of Cannae, while the origins of the gladiatorial games lay in the ritual slaughter of captives as funeral offerings to the dead. Among Germanic tribes, archaeological evidence from bog bodies shows victims who were hanged, throat-cut, bludgeoned, or subjected to multiple forms of killing in overkill rituals; captives and slaves were offered as blood sacrifices to gods such as Odin, often drowned, stabbed, or left hanging from sacred trees, and prisoners taken in war were regularly killed to honor the gods and the dead.

Black pagan societies in Africa also practiced large-scale human sacrifice. In kingdoms such as Dahomey, Ashanti, Benin, and others, captives, slaves, and criminals were regularly killed as offerings to the gods and ancestors—often by beheading, throat-cutting, or live burial during annual festivals and royal ceremonies. Thousands could be sacrificed in a single custom; skulls and body parts were displayed, and warfare was frequently conducted to supply victims for these rituals.

Jews practiced paganism and human sacrifice. Kings Ahaz and Manasseh made their sons pass through the fire. People burned their children in the Valley of Hinnom. Solomon built high places for Chemosh and Molech. The Northern Kingdom set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan. Ahab and Jezebel promoted Baal worship. High places, Asherah poles, and foreign cults were repeatedly established and used. These acts are recorded in 2 Kings 16:3, 21:6, 1 Kings 11, 1 Kings 12, 1 Kings 16–18, Jeremiah 7 and 19, and elsewhere.

Across these cultures, the belief that the gods required human life and blood was widespread, and warfare often supplied the victims. With the coming of Jesus Christ, the New Testament, and the spread of Christianity, these sacrificial systems and the pagan practices that sustained them were nullified and destroyed. The New Testament declares that the death of Jesus is the final sacrifice that ends every blood offering, and Christian expansion suppressed and replaced these rites wherever it took hold. Christians themselves were also sacrificed and killed for refusing to participate in pagan rites and for working to stop them.

JESUS CHRIST IS KING.

text:
What water flows from the temple into the dry places of your faith?

Can sanctuary water turn your salt sea fresh and full of life?

Will every living creature multiply wherever this river reaches the sea?

Do trees on both banks offer fruit each month and leaves for medicine?

Dive into the temple river from Ezekiel 47, where water from the sanctuary makes the salt sea fresh and trees bear fruit for food and leaves for medicine.

Life Follows the Water in Ezekiel 47

A small stream can change a wide landscape. Ezekiel 47 gives us that picture with patience and beauty. Water leaves the temple. It travels east. It meets dry country and a bitter sea. Then living things thrive. Trees bear fruit. Leaves bring healing. The scene is large, yet it speaks to ordinary people. It speaks to anyone who wants to do good and does not always finish well. The water does not start as a flood. It starts at a threshold. That is already enough to begin hope.

What Can a Small Stream at the Door Still Do?

The vision opens at the entrance of the temple. Water flows from below the threshold. The temple faces east, so the stream moves toward the east. A guide then leads the prophet out by the north gate. They walk around the outside. They reach the outer gate that faces east. There the water comes out on the south side. The path is careful. It is also unstoppable. Holiness does not stay trapped behind a wall. It finds a way around the building. It keeps a direction.

This can comfort a person who feels stuck at the doorway of a good intention. You may want a kinder home. You may want a steadier life of prayer and Mass. You may want to make a wrong right. Then the week resists you. The reading does not mock that small start. Water under a threshold looks modest. It is already in motion. A sincere attempt can be the first stretch of a longer mercy. You do not have to manufacture a miracle. You can stay near the flow and let it widen.

Why Does a Bitter Sea Not Have the Last Word?

The guide describes the rest of the journey. The water flows toward the eastern region. It goes down into the Arabah. It enters the sea of stagnant waters. That sea is known for salt and stillness. Little can live in it. The promise refuses to stop there. When the stream enters, the water becomes fresh. The bitter place is not scolded. It is visited. It is changed.

Many people carry a stagnant corner. It may be a habit that returns. It may be a grief that feels old. It may be the quiet fear that your efforts do not count because they are uneven. This vision offers a kinder reading of that fear. The sea does not freshen itself by force of will. The river comes from the sanctuary and does the renewing. If you have tried and slipped, you are not disqualified. You are exactly the kind of landscape this water knows how to reach. Freshness is a gift that travels. It is not a prize for a perfect month.

What Does the Promise of Multiplying Life Mean?

One line gathers the hope of the whole passage. "Wherever the river flows, every sort of living creature that can multiply shall live". The sentence is generous. It does not pick a single worthy creature and ignore the rest. It speaks of life that can multiply. Where the water arrives, abundance follows. Fish become many. The sea turns from barren water to a living place.

Read that line as encouragement, not as pressure. You are not asked to prove your worth by endless output. The river does the giving. Your part is to let life have room. A patient conversation can multiply. A return to the sacraments after a long absence can multiply. A quiet choice to tell the truth can multiply. You may only notice one small creature that survives because mercy reached it. That still fulfills the promise. If yesterday felt thin, the river has not withdrawn. It still looks for every place where living things can grow.

How Can Monthly Fruit Steady an Uneven Effort?

The final scene rests on the banks. All kinds of trees grow there for food. Their leaves do not wither. Their fruit does not fail. They bear fresh fruit every month. The reason is plain. The water for them flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit is for food. Their leaves are for healing.

The monthly rhythm matters for people who are trying. Faith here is not one shining day followed by silence. It is a repeated gift. Some months you may see clear fruit. You forgive. You serve. You keep a promise. Other months the gift looks smaller. You get up again. You speak more gently. You ask for help. The vision honors both. Food strengthens a neighbor. A leaf heals a wound that is still tender. An imperfect person can offer either one.

The trees stand on both sides of the river. The blessing is not a private stream for a flawless few. It lines the path. Anyone who comes near can find food and healing. Your incomplete goodness can still nourish someone. Your decision to begin again can still be a leaf in a hard season. The sanctuary keeps sending water. The banks keep answering.

Where Can You Stand When the Work Feels Unfinished?

The overriding message is simple and kind. Life follows the water. The water comes from the holy place. It does not fear the bitter sea. It freshens what seemed stuck. It makes room for every sort of living creature to live and to multiply. It grows fruit that returns and leaves that heal.

You do not have to be the source. You can stand on the bank. You can let the stream from the sanctuary reach the tired parts of your life and the lives around you. A small prayer counts. A just action counts. A new beginning after a miss counts. The reading keeps finding the positive in a world that knows stagnation. Wherever this river flows, life gets another chance. Stay near that flow. Let it carry freshness farther than your strength can carry it alone.

🙏 @RCatholicPrayer

text:
LEAKED PROPOSAL SHOWS US READY TO HAND IRAN ENRICHMENT RIGHTS AND BILLIONS IN CASH

An Iranian journalist close to the regime claims he has the latest American offer to Tehran. Ali Gholhak says the proposal would let Iran keep uranium enrichment at 3.67 percent on its own soil, dilute its 400 kilograms of 60 percent material inside the country, free $6 to $10 billion in frozen assets, lift the US naval blockade, and reopen the Strait of Hormuz after Iran ends its role in the Saudi-Yemen fighting and lets IAEA inspectors back in.

These terms track earlier leaks from the same source and from Qatari-mediated drafts. Washington has spent months demanding zero enrichment and the removal of the high-enriched stockpile. The reported package drops both demands. It also trades cash and blockade relief for vague Iranian promises on Yemen and a temporary reopening of shipping lanes Iran itself has threatened.

Gholhak has called similar offers a clear American retreat after 18 months of harder lines. Iranian replies on the original post dismissed the package as a waste of time unless it also forces Israel out of southern Lebanon. US officials have not confirmed the text. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said days ago that some Iranian demands remain outrageous and that no breakthrough is near.

The 60 percent stockpile is the core problem. Material already at that level can be pushed to weapons grade in days, not months. Allowing any domestic enrichment, even at 3.67 percent, recreates the basic architecture of the 2015 deal that left Iran with a latent nuclear option. Releasing billions while the regime still funds proxies and refuses full transparency hands Tehran both money and time.

If the leak is accurate, the offer looks like classic process diplomacy: technical concessions and cash first, verification later, and regional behavior left to vague language. Iran has used every prior pause to expand capacity. The Strait reopening is not a gift to the West; it is a lever Tehran controls and can close again the moment the money arrives. Hardline sources inside Iran are already framing the package as proof that pressure works in their favor.

🇺🇸 U.S. Stocks Explained | How does Costco combine merchandise and membership?

Known for its large stores and bulk shopping, Costco is a membership-based warehouse retailer headquartered in Washington state, U.S. It also operates stores in Japan and trades in the U.S. under the ticker COST.

Its range goes beyond food and everyday essentials to include electronics, clothing and more. It also offers its own Kirkland Signature brand. To understand the company, look at how it sells, not just what it sells.

One feature is a selection focused on popular models, sizes and other variations. Costco combines volume purchasing, efficient distribution and streamlined warehouse operations with a strategy of selling large volumes at low prices. Many consumable products are sold by the case or in multipacks as part of this approach.

Membership is another part of the business. The amount paid for merchandise and the annual fee paid to be a member are different sources of revenue. Costco reports net sales and membership fees separately. But it would be too quick to conclude that every dollar of membership fees becomes profit. The company also incurs merchandise, labor, distribution and other costs.

When studying the business, look at product sales, whether members renew, and how operating costs change. A popular store does not, on its own, mean the stock is cheap or profits are guaranteed.

Adding “how does it sell?” to “what does it sell?” can change how you see a familiar company. Read Costco through both merchandise sales and its membership model.

text:
NYT: a Commerce probe of the Nvidia customer tied to an alleged Chinese spy was halted after Nvidia's lawyer invoked a top official. The Nvidia scandal has a new chapter, and this one is about Washington.

Commerce Department investigators spent months on Megaspeed, a Singapore data-center company suspected of smuggling Nvidia AI chips into China, before their work stopped abruptly last year, The New York Times reported Monday. Megaspeed is led by an executive US officials now believe is a Chinese spy and who had a relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

According to the Times, in August 2025 Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter emailed the agents seeking information about the case, saying Jeff Kessler, the Commerce under secretary who oversees export enforcement, had given Nvidia permission to reach out. Agents were alarmed. Within the department, current and former officials told the Times, some saw it as a breach of procedure that could taint the case. The investigation was then handed to the Justice Department, which asked Commerce to pause its work. Officials called the handoff "unusual and concerning."

The other sides dispute the framing. A Commerce official said Nvidia contacted employees directly, and that Kessler, when the email was forwarded to him, told them to handle the case "strictly by the book" and did not direct them to share information. Commerce says it acted by the book. Nvidia says it consults officials to help "halt any would-be smugglers." Megaspeed says it is running its own internal investigation and has offered to cooperate. Kessler did not comment.

The Times also reported that Commerce has not added a company to its entity list in more than a year, the longest gap in 18 years, and has not acted on proposals from other agencies to list Megaspeed. Trump was briefed in October 2025 that the executive was presumed to be a spy, the paper reported.

Nothing public shows that secrets were passed. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe they were, and the Justice Department is reportedly running a criminal inquiry into Megaspeed.

What to watch: whether congressional committees call Kessler, and Huang's answer by November 11 on a proposed closed-door House briefing.

text:
🇺🇲 🇷🇺 🇺🇦 On the night before the first US-Russia-Ukraine talks since February, Washington is selling cautious optimism.

A US official briefing reporters Monday said both Russia and Ukraine are privately showing some flexibility on a possible exchange of territory, Reuters reported. Publicly, both sides remain far apart. Kyiv wants Russian forces back to the original border. Vladimir Putin wants all of the Donbas region.

The official said territory would likely come last, after agreement on a postwar security architecture, and that security guarantees for Ukraine will be a major topic, including the potential for a NATO-style Article 5 defense commitment for Kyiv. "This is the first time I feel like we see real desire on the Russian side to finish," the official said. Envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner lead the US side and could travel to Russia to meet Putin after the two days of talks.

This is one anonymous official's read, and Moscow's public signals point the other way. Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said Russia will offer no new concessions. Putin aide Yuri Ushakov has floated a European security system in which former Warsaw Pact members and the Baltic states leave NATO. On Monday the Kremlin also insisted the talks stay trilateral, even as France says European officials will be on site.

Kyiv sends intelligence chief Rustem Umerov, with Kyrylo Budanov and David Arakhamia. Russia sends Vladimir Medinsky, military intelligence chief Igor Kostyukov and, for the first time, deputy foreign minister Sergei Ryabkov. The New York Times reported a ceasefire is not on this week's agenda.

What to watch: whether either side confirms any movement on territory, whether the Article 5-style language survives contact with Moscow, and whether Witkoff and Kushner head to the Kremlin next.

text:
In March 1568, in the Kremlin’s great cathedral, Ivan the Terrible came forward for a blessing. The Metropolitan of Moscow refused, and told the tsar why to his face.

Within two years he was dead in a monastery cell.

His name was Fyodor Kolychev, born in 1507 to an old Moscow boyar family. After his relatives were punished in a court conspiracy in 1537, he slipped out of Moscow in peasant clothes, herded sheep near Lake Onega, and became a monk on the Solovetsky Islands in the White Sea, taking the name Philip. As abbot from 1548 he built stone churches, mills and canals linking dozens of lakes.

In 1566 Ivan IV summoned him to be Metropolitan of Moscow. Since 1565 Ivan had run the oprichnina, a state within the state whose black-clad riders seized land and killed suspected traitors. Philip’s condition was that it be abolished. Ivan refused; pressed by the bishops, Philip agreed not to interfere in it. He was installed on 25 July 1566.

The killings went on. Philip pleaded in private; Ivan began to avoid him. On 22 March 1568 (Old Style), a Novgorod chronicle records, Philip openly opposed the tsar. Ivan came to the Dormition Cathedral with his oprichniki in black, and Philip would not bless him. In the historian Karamzin’s retelling, he said: “Here we offer sacrifice to God, while behind the altar innocent Christian blood is shed,” and, “I fear the Lord alone.”

Ivan had him tried; the verdict itself has not survived. On 4 November a council of bishops deposed him. On 8 November, the feast of the Archangel Michael, while Philip was serving the liturgy, the oprichnik Basmanov entered the cathedral and read out the verdict. They tore off his vestments, put him in a ragged habit and drove him off on a sledge. According to the historian Kostomarov, Ivan later sent him the severed head of his nephew in a leather bag.

Philip was exiled to the Otroch Monastery in Tver. On 23 December 1569, as Ivan marched on Novgorod, his enforcer Malyuta Skuratov came to the cell and asked a blessing for the campaign. According to Philip’s Life, he answered that God’s gift is not obtained by deceit, and Skuratov strangled him, then told the monks the cell had been too hot. Novgorod was sacked weeks later; contemporary Western estimates of the dead range from about 2,700 to 27,000.

In 1652 Tsar Alexis had a letter read before Philip’s relics at Solovki, begging forgiveness for the sin of his predecessor Ivan, done to Philip “out of envy and unrestrained fury” (translation). The relics were carried to Moscow and laid in the very cathedral where Philip had refused his blessing.

“We ought to obey God rather than men” (Acts 5:29). “Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul” (Matthew 10:28).

Would you have the courage to refuse a blessing to the most powerful man in your country?

Sources: Russian Wikipedia, “Philip (Kolychev)”; N. M. Karamzin, “History of the Russian State,” vol. 9; Wikipedia, “Massacre of Novgorod”; Wikimedia Commons.

text:
Julius Caesar ruled Rome openly for about five years and was murdered for it. 

His grand-nephew ruled for forty-four and died in his bed. The difference was a lesson. 

By early 44 BC, Caesar was dictator for life. He sat on a gilded chair, wore the purple, and had his image set among the statues of the kings. 

At the Lupercalia that February, Mark Antony offered him a diadem in public. Caesar pushed it away, but the damage was done. 

By the Ides of March, more than sixty senators were in on the plot, and Caesar took 23 wounds.

Octavian was eighteen, studying in Greece when the news arrived. He drew a conclusion that would shape the next four centuries. 

Romans hated the word rex, but they were far less bothered by what a king actually did. After Actium in 31 BC left him without a rival, he spent years building a system around that principle. 

In January 27 BC, he staged a famous scene. He announced that he was handing the state back to the Senate and people. 

The Senate, according to Cassius Dio, begged him to keep ruling, and he agreed to take the provinces where most of the army was stationed. They gave him a new name, Augustus, and a modest title, 'Princeps', first citizen. 

His own account of his reign claims that afterward he surpassed everyone in auctoritas, prestige, but held no more formal power than his colleagues in any office.

That sentence was carefully built, but the power was real. In 23 BC, he gave up the consulship he had held year after year and took two powers that required no office.

The first was superior imperium, giving his authority precedence over other governors in the provinces. The second was tribunician power, with its veto and personal inviolability, without requiring him to hold the office of tribune. 

One secured his command. The other embedded him in Roman politics. Neither sounded like a crown.

Everything else carried on. The Senate survived, trimmed from around a thousand members to six hundred. Consuls were still chosen, praetors still presided over the courts, and young nobles still climbed the ladder of offices. 

Augustus cut the army from perhaps 60 legions to about 28 and settled the discharged veterans on land.

His own Res Gestae says he paid for it personally, to the tune of hundreds of millions of sesterces. 

A state that looked like the Republic ran on his money and his soldiers. When people tried to give him more, he refused, and that was part of the performance. 

Suetonius says that in 22 BC, a crowd demanded he be made dictator, and he dropped to his knees and bared his chest, begging them not to.

It would be too simple to call it a swindle. Romans had lived through roughly eighteen years of civil war since Caesar crossed the Rubicon. 

Tacitus, no friend of the regime, admits that people accepted the new arrangement because it brought peace, and that the old order had stopped working. 

The facade held because it was partly true, and because Romans remembered what the alternative looked like. 

It also lasted. For about three centuries, emperors called themselves princeps and treated the Senate with outward respect. Open talk of a lord and master didn’t arrive until Diocletian. 

The consulship Augustus had preserved survived the fall of the western empire and was abolished by Justinian in 541.

Caesar wore the crown and died for it. 

Augustus refused it and founded a dynasty.

✒️The Five Reasons Why China Works🖊️

Zhang Weiwei

SHANGHAI – Is China’s extraordinary rise a model for economic reforms without political reform? Is China's own political system its Achilles heel? Is China's one-party rule doom doomed in the face of the growing challenges of a more diversified economy and an increasingly demanding society?

These questions preoccupy many people in the West once there is talk of China. Yet the assumptions on which these questions are based could be wrong, because from a Chinese perspective, a completely different understanding of China could emerge. China's political system of government, which is constantly adapting to new challenges through numerous smaller reforms, has proved crucial to the country's economic success. The following five aspects of Chinese governance deserve special attention:

First, the one-party rule

In fact, one-party rule in China is nothing new: during most of the past two millennia, since the country's first unification in 221 v. Chr., China almost always practiced a form of one-party leadership or the rule of a unified Confucian elite that was selected by state trials (Keju) and claimed to represent the majority, if not the entire population of the empire – or actually did.

In addition, it can be argued that China was better managed during most of these phases of one-party rule and was economically more prosperous than contemporary Europe. China only began to fall behind Europe when it closed its doors to the outside world and the industrial revolution of the 18th. Century missed. Today, however, the country is rapidly catching up with this backlog.

The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has largely followed this tradition and has built an impressive system for selecting executives based on merit and performance. For example, of the party's main decision-makers, six of the seven members of the Politburo Standing Committee had previously held the office of party secretary or governor at the provincial level at least twice. This means that before their promotion to their current offices in Beijing, they had managed on average areas with about 100 million inhabitants.

Today's CCP, like its predecessors in China's long history, claims to represent the entire nation, but has the task of restoring the country's status as a leading world power. Significant independent surveys, including those of the Pew Research Center and the Asian Barometer from the past decade, show a constant pattern: The Chinese central government enjoys a high degree of respect and support in its own country – over 75 percent. The portrayal, widely used in Western media, that China’s political system is on the verge of collapse, is, as is so often the case, far from the Chinese reality.

In this context, the term “party” could be inappropriate for the CCP, because it is by no means similar to political organizations such as the Republican or Democratic Party in the United States, which openly represent and compete with the interests of certain social groups. In line with China's own political tradition, the CCP has sought to represent the interests of the overwhelming majority of the population, which, at least so far, apparently accepts this role. This is largely because most people have experienced a significant improvement in their standard of living over the past three decades.

From this perspective, the CCP should be considered a party state or, in a hypothetical American context, a union of the Republican and Democratic Party, in which competition between ideas and competencies is the rule and consensus, as well as a pragmatic, results-oriented approach, are valued.

China is not a country-sized GDR waiting for a color revolution, as many people in the West imagine. Rather, it is a state of civilization: a connection from the oldest continuously existing civilization in the world and a large modern state, which in turn has emerged from the unification of hundreds of states throughout its long history. Perhaps it resembles a Roman Empire that would have persisted to the present day and united all its regional and cultural differences in a modern economy and under a centralized government, with the population speaking the same language as was the case with Latin.

Such a state could indeed become ungovernable and break apart if it adopted the Western model of political confrontation, as happened in the case of the Soviet Union – a lesson that China’s leadership apparently fully understood. China’s meritocratic system, which corresponds to its own tradition and its different adjustments, such as the widely used system of government according to the principle of “selection plus elections”, seems to work quite well for this country. Although it is imperfect, this system can compete with other political models worldwide.

Second, democratic centralism is a new type

China's success is inextricably linked to its fundamentally reformed decision-making process, which can be described as a democratic centralism of a new type or as a modern form of democratic centralism.

The previous decision-making process of the Soviet type was actually more focused on centralism than on democracy. However, China has improved it and, within its own system of democratic centralism, has institutionalized a procedurally linked mechanism of accountability.

In such a system, a typical fundamental decision, such as the five-year plan for national development, requires more than a year of comprehensive and interactive consultations. These take place at various levels of the Chinese state and society, in several consultation rounds according to the principle of “from the people to the people and back to the people”.

This decision-making process includes contributions from thousands of research and think tanks, state institutions, universities, renowned scientists and professionals. Even heated debates on social networks and on the microblogging platform Weibo are by no means unusual.

The decision to deepen the reforms, which was recently adopted at the third plenary session, is a good example of this. The editorial group, chaired by President Xi Jinping himself, sought comments from more than 100 institutions from across the country and received 2,500 proposals within six months. About 50 percent of it was taken over. During this process, all seven top politicians visited different regions of China to obtain information and conduct investigations in preparation for the deliberations on the decision.

The final decision therefore reflects a broad consensus of Chinese society on numerous issues, including public health reform, the adaptation of one-child policies, raising the retirement age, reforming the banking sector, education reform and abolishing the system of “re-education through labour.” Many decisions are made on the basis of the results of pilot projects.

Thanks to the higher legitimacy of the decision-making process, the state generally does not have to “sell” its decisions to the public, as is the case in the United States. Once decisions have been adopted in Beijing following such a procedure, they can usually be “studied and implemented” or further tested in the context of various pilot projects.

Third, the creation of demand

The institutionalised roundtables of consultations and the debates on policy measures in the context of fundamental decision-making processes raise numerous public expectations at regular intervals with regard to economic development, which are usually positive and less negative.

These expectations, in turn, generate new forms of demand, often of a medium and long-term nature. A typical Chinese five-year plan attracts the attention of large parts of the Chinese company, from private companies and state-owned enterprises to individual shareholders.

The fact that China has maintained an annual growth rate of over nine percent over more than three decades is inextricably linked to these regular and predictable cycles of expectation and demand creation. 
Fourth, the development-oriented administration
It is by no means wrong to claim that China has created its own development model. An essential feature of this model can be described as “development-oriented administration”, in contrast to traditional public administration.

China's national five-year plans and the CCP's annual economic conference are undoubtedly part of this development-focused administration. The same applies to the numerous local development strategies and plans.

Chinese universities could eventually offer courses and even degrees in the field of development-oriented administration, just as study programs of public administration are already widespread everywhere.

However, the case of China could be unique, since the Chinese state not only has Keynesian instruments such as fiscal and monetary policy within the framework of the “socialist market economy”, but also other levers that are not necessarily available in other countries. These include public ownership of land, as well as strategic resources and a largely efficient state sector. These instruments give the Chinese state greater opportunities to intervene in and influence the economy.

Fifth: minyi versus minxin

Everything previously said is based on the Chinese philosophy of the state leadership, which includes, among other things, two different terms: minyi and minxin. The first refers to the “public opinion”, while the second stands for the “hearts and consciences of the people” – an approximate translation. This second term was first written by Menzius (372–289 v. CHR.) formulated.

Minyi, public opinion, can be fleeting and change from one day to the next, while minxin, that is, the “hearts and consciences of the people”, is rather consistent and permanent, reflecting the general and long-term interests of a nation.

Over the past three decades, the Chinese state itself has practiced a state leadership based on the principle of minxin under the sometimes populist pressure of the minyi in general. As a result, China can plan for the next generation in the medium and long term, rather than limiting its planning horizon to the next 100 days or the next elections, as happened in many Western countries.

China continues to face numerous difficult challenges, from corruption to regional income disparities to environmental degradation. Still, China is in a better position than at any other time in its modern history.

Today, the country is the largest laboratory in the world for economic, social and political experiments. There is every reason to believe that China, with its ever-adjustable political system, will achieve its goal of rising to become the world’s largest economy in about a decade – with all the consequences this will have for both China itself and the entire world.
