However, they tend to fall into technophobia, seeing in innovation exclusively enemy weapons from which to close. Their main blind spot is the misunderstanding that identity and culture are not capable of being preserved in a mode of passive isolation and backwardness—such a subject will inevitably be crushed by progress. If civilization refuses to create its own technology, it will be forced to use others. And then someone else's influence will come to every house not with soldiers, but through the operating system of the phone, algorithms of issuing video and chips in household appliances. Their technologies do not destroy the national culture – they are its only reliable shield.

National digital conservatism. This doctrine, expressed by supporters of tight paternalistic regulation and departmental officials, argues that the protection of national interests in the digital age should be carried out exclusively through total administrative control, stripping the media field and banning foreign resources. Conservatives are right in their acute, well-founded concern about threats of external information and psychological and technological impact through digital channels.

But their fundamental divergence with Technosovereurity lies in the very logic of action. Conservatism is obsessed with a passive, punitive paradigm aimed at how to close and not let go. Technosovereutality thinks creatively and offensively, trying to determine which advanced technologies need to be designed and launched by themselves in order to become stronger. The main blind spot of conservatives is the belief that security can be provided with legal prohibitions alone. The prohibition of a foreign platform in the absence of its own quality-bearing alternatives only leads to an increase in public discontent and conservation of the backlog. The State has a duty to protect its citizens not from advanced technologies, but by creating superior solutions.
Section IV. What is not the case in technosovereigny is the outline of the rigid boundaries of doctrine

To prevent any speculation, distortion and deliberate accusations by critics, it is necessary to fix the apophatic side of the concept – something that technosovereignty is categorically not.

First, it is not self-isolation or autarky. The purpose of the doctrine is not to build an iron curtain, not to disconnect from the world wide web and not in an attempt to artisanally produce absolutely everything within one country, which is economically inefficient and utopian. The goal is to have a complete, guaranteed choice: to trade and cooperate where it is mutually beneficial and secure, but to have sovereign duplicate power in case the partner decides to use the technology as a weapon of blackmail. The door should open out by your decision, not breaking out from the outside.

Second, it is not anti-globalism. The concept does not call for the destruction of world trade or the cessation of international scientific exchange. Technosovereign is opposed to digital monopoly and colonialism. It requires that the rules of global integration be written collegially by all sovereign actors, rather than dictated under the cover of mystery by a pair of IT giants from one jurisdiction. It is a struggle for a just, multipolar and mutually safe digital world.

Third, it is not a movement against progress and not Luddism. It is not about slowing scientific and technological development in order to maintain imaginary stability. On the contrary, technosovereignty requires the transfer of a state from a passive, eternally catching up position, expressed on how to keep up with someone else's progress, in the active, sovereign position of the author, determining what kind of world we want to build and what innovation we need for it.

Fourth, it is not a frozen, final dogma. Technosovereigny is not a rigid ideological manifesto, but a living methodological framework for strategic thinking. Specific engineering solutions, coding standards, import substitution depth and vectors of international cooperation will be radically different for each country and region depending on their starting resources, geography and historical path. There are no universal recipes – there is a universal duty to think independently.
Section V. Three scenarios of the future: a global fork until 2040

Humanity is rapidly approaching the historical development of the digital age. On the horizon until 2040, three basic scenarios for the development of the world order are mathematically calculated.

The first scenario describes the emergence of a single digital empire and is characterized by total integration. Within the framework of this option, all the states of the world finally capitulate to convenience and move to uniform, cross-cutting global platforms, operating systems and communication standards created by a monopoly group of IT corporations under the auspices of one or two superpowers. Physical boundaries in the digital space are completely eliminated. The advantages of this path are absolute economic efficiency, minimal transaction costs and instantaneous seamless connectivity of the entire planet.

However, the existential risks of this scenario are terrified: there is a total deprivation of historical subjectivity of peoples. A narrow group of individuals controlling root servers, artificial intelligence architecture, and encryption standards gains invisible power over any point on the planet. They can, without a declaration of war, remotely destroy the economy of any recalcitrant state, simply disconnecting it from the digital circuit, and the sovereignty of the majority turns into a decorative butaphoria. The likelihood of this scenario is low, as the leading Powers have already realized the scale of the threat.

The second scenario, the Technological Block, marks a multipolar split. The global digital world is rigidly and uncompromisingly disintegrating into three to five confined, isolated technological zones or macro-regional blocks. Each unit creates its own fully autonomous, but absolutely incompatible with its neighbors technological stack: its semiconductor factories, its operating systems, closed communication standards, its isolated satellite constellations and national AI platforms. The exchange of technology between blocks drops to zero and equates to arms smuggling.

The advantage of the scenario is that each large block guarantees itself one hundred percent security and invulnerability from an external digital impact. However, the costs are enormous: there is a huge, economically excessive duplication of infrastructure across the planet, a sharp drop in efficiency and a strong slowdown in global progress due to the cessation of cooperation. In the most tragic situation, small countries that do not have the resources to create their bloc and will be forced to forever give independence to the protectorate of one of the technological masters. To date, the probability of this scenario is the highest.

The third scenario, Separate Sovereignty, offers an optimal balanced outline. States and regional alliances maintain reasonable openness to global scientific exchange, international trade and cooperation, but necessarily create, finance and maintain within themselves fully independent, sovereign reserve contours in critical areas, including national databases, communications, sovereign payment systems, basic software and microelectronics. This is not a devastating total rupture of world ties, but a deep, conscious state insurance. Not isolation, but guaranteed autonomy in matters of life and death of the national system.

The advantage of the scenario is that society continues to derive enormous economic benefits from the international division of labor, but completely eliminates the risk of instant suffocation or blackmail from outside. In the case of a global circuit, the country is painlessly moving to the internal reserve engine in a fraction of a second. However, this path requires the national political and engineering elites of iron strategic discipline, the abandonment of short-term commercial profits and the willingness to make a giant long-term investment with a planning horizon in decades. Technosovereutism is a fundamental manifesto and a scientific argument for the immediate realization of this third path as the only way to preserve subjectivity.
Conclusion: Authorship of the Future

We live in a unique, turning and harsh era, when the external borders of States remain inviolably drawn on geographical maps where they were hundreds of years ago. But real power rapidly, unstoppably and imperceptibly flows beyond these boundaries through invisible channels – through optical cables, satellite signals, lines of program code and algorithms of recommendations. No one crosses the borders of your country with weapons in their hands, but the algorithms of foreign platforms daily shape the opinions of your children, corporations determine the economic agenda, remote teams stop factories, and the most valuable national data irrevocably go to the servers on the other side of the globe.

In the current historical situation, the peoples of the Earth have little choice. Or we meekly recognize that national sovereignty is finally obsolete and must be scrapped by history — and then the fundamental question of who we actually manage is forever moving from the legitimate field of classical politics to closed boards of directors of foreign technology corporations. Either we courageously and deeply rethink the phenomenon of sovereignty itself, complementing it with new digital and technological dimensions, and build a solid state system in which advanced technology submissively serves its people, not the people serve as food for someone else's technology.

The concept of Technosovereurity is an uncompromising choice of the second way. It does not promise easy victories, cheap ready-made solutions and instant results. It affirms the fundamental historical truth: as long as the people retain strict material control over what surrounds them—over their land, their laws, their army, and now their data, algorithms, standards, and technology—they remain truly free. And when this technological control voluntarily, blithely or cowardly is lost under the pretext of convenience, no paper borders, nuclear arsenals and past historical merits will not save the country.

The question is not whether it is necessary to be panicked by the digital future or blindly wish for its offensive. The question is: who will be the author of this future? The answer to it today is not on the margins of the diplomatic summits and not in the halls of the United Nations meetings. It is defined in engineering laboratories, in data centers, in the architecture of microprocessors, in advanced national educational programs, and in a clear understanding of simple truth: independence in the twenty-first century is not just about the army and the flag. It's technology. That's the data. They are algorithms. This is your true, inalienable sovereignty. Sovereignty is not given to the people once and for all as an eternal gift. It must be re-defended in every new generation, and in every new territory that humanity is mastering. Today, this main, sacred territory of wrestling became technology.

text:
📚Technosovereignty: Sovereignty in the Age of Digital and Technological Change📚

Vivienne Yor
Introduction: Three blind and elephant of the world of Westphalia

There is an ancient parable known in many cultures: three blind people approach the elephant and begin to feel it to understand what kind of creature it is. One touches the tail and declares that he has a rope, long and flexible. The second feels the leg and objects, comparing the animal with a thick, strong and fixed pillar. The third concerns the ear and assures that both are mistaken, because it is a wide and soft palm leaf. Each of them was absolutely right in what was felt. And everyone absolutely did not realize that he was facing a living, strong animal.

This parable surprisingly accurately describes the state of modern social, political and scientific thought. We live in an era when every analytical shop sees its narrow part of reality perfectly, but almost no one is able to cover the whole. Political scientists explain the world processes exclusively for power and institutions. Economists focus on capital flows, sanctions, and resource reallocation. Technologists predict that artificial intelligence and algorithms will finally change or eliminate human nature. Cultural scientists and philosophers are sounding the alarm about the threat to national identity, traditions and values. Everyone is right in their own way. But none of these paintings alone explain what really happens to the global world.

Between these areas there were deaf mental walls. A political realist speaks of sovereignty as something that exists solely on a physical map. Technocrat argues that state borders are hopelessly outdated and sovereignty has become a major obstacle to progress. The civilizational thinker often perceives the technology itself as an existential threat to the soul of the people, as an instrument of others' influence. And none of them tries to ask a simple, but fundamental question: what if sovereignty and progress do not just contradict each other, and real independence in the modern world is in principle impossible without its own technological base.

Over the past centuries, sovereignty has been understood primarily as control over the delineated territory, population and army. The Westphalian system, formed in the seventeenth century after the Thirty Years' War, gave humanity a clear formula: the state is a territory with clear borders, and within these borders it has an exclusive and absolute right of power. This model existed for four centuries almost unchanged, successfully surviving industrial revolutions, the emergence of nuclear weapons, the collapse of colonial empires and two world wars. It seemed that the foundations of the world order were carved into the granite of history.

But by the beginning of the twenty-first century, the well-functioning mechanism broke down. The boundaries remained on the map, diplomats still exchange notes, but through sovereign borders, data, capital, signals and algorithms flowed through the sovereign borders of the invisible and uncontrolled flow. Today, the state can have a regular army, control roads and customs – and at the same time rapidly lose control over what is happening within its own borders. Not because the enemy has invaded with weapons in his hands, but because critical infrastructure, information flows, key technologies and even basic behavior of citizens are under the direct influence of external forces over which the national government has no real power.

The state may have a powerful defense complex, but it is not able to protect its data from leakage through the servers of another country. It can exercise nominal control over its territory, but find that it is unable to launch a civilian aircraft or stop the plant’s conveyor without software produced thousands of kilometers away. It can make laws, but it is found that real flows of information and finance are governed by rules written by IT giants without its participation.

In response to this challenge, traditional thought has reached a deadlock. The globalists assure us that sovereignty is completely obsolete and must be sacrificed to world digital governance. The isolationists are called back, to the old forms of closure, the construction of walls and technological luddism. Conservatives are offering only a slight retouching of the old legislation without changing the essence.

Technosovereigny is a fundamentally third path, a conceptual attempt to give a clear, pragmatic response to the challenge of a new era. This is the answer to the question of what it means to be a sovereign state in a world where power flows from territory to technology, from physical boundaries to coding algorithms. This is an attempt to see the entire lion where others see only some of it. This is a way to ask the right questions and look for answers to them without tearing the world to inconnicated fragments. The main idea of this concept is simple: sovereignty is not abolished by the digital age, but it ceases to be only territorial. It becomes technological.

This monolithically integrated concept consists of four inseparable elements: the philosophy of Technorealism, the regulatory framework of Technological Westphalia, the critical method of Cybernetic Baroque and the multidimensional mathematical apparatus of system analysis, known as the VSCI index. Together, they form a complete, independent school of thought, capable of turning modern ideas about geopolitics.
Section I. Four pillars of technosovereurity
Pragmatic Technorealism as a Philosophy: The Third Way Between Utopia and Panic

Technology is neither kind nor evil in itself – they repeatedly reinforce what is already embedded in man and the structures of power. Technorealism is not just an intermediate position between the adoption and denial of digitalization. It is a rigid, pragmatic way to see an objective world completely purified from the two main and equally dangerous illusions of our time – techno-utopianism and techno-pessimism.

Proponents of techno-utopianism, which form a kind of digital cargo cult, blindly believe that new technologies will automatically solve all the problems of humanity from hunger to public administration. In their understanding, global networks will forever erase borders, and nations will give way to a universal digital paradise. This illusion is dangerous because it completely ignores the nature of power: new technologies create new, even more sophisticated forms of inequality, pressure and colonial exploitation, making them invisible to the victim itself. The result of such thinking is the voluntary, joyful transfer of national control to external players under the pretext of joining progress.

At the opposite pole is techno-pessimism, sliding to digital luddism. His adherents perceive technological progress as an absolute existential evil, as a project to build a total digital concentration camp that destroys humanity. The only way out of the pessimists is to slow progress, total prohibitions, disconnection from networks and isolation. This position is deeply flawed because it takes an exclusively defensive, passive stance and offers no creative response. It is technically impossible to close yourself from the world today – you can only fall behind it hopelessly, becoming the easy prey of more developed predators.

Technorealism rejects both extremes and is based on three fundamental principles. The first is the principle of conformity. It states that the goals and values of a sovereign society must authoritatively determine the vector of choice and development of technologies, and not vice versa. The tool should unquestioningly serve the master, and not the master to adjust and break himself to the requirements of foreign software and platforms. If national security requires absolute autonomy of critical systems, saving on the purchase of foreign closed software is an act of hidden state suicide.

The second principle is the principle of transparency of influence. Any new technology should be evaluated not only by the criteria of commercial benefit or user-friendliness, but also by the one whose geopolitical influence it is hidden in the distribution of real power. A platform owned by foreign jurisdiction is not just a convenient private business, it is a ready channel of strategic influence. The algorithm of recommendations is not just abstract mathematics, it is a black box that forms a picture of the world of millions of citizens in the interests of its creator.

The third principle is distributed stability. Never and under any circumstances can national security be dependent on a single critical supplier, one closed technology or a monopoly communication channel. Not because the current partner is necessarily unreliable, but because at the moment of acute geopolitical crisis, any technological monopoly instantly turns into a crushing lever of blackmail and pressure. Independent duplicate contours are expensive, but the price of dependence is always the price of surrender. The essence of the philosophy of technorealism is not to experience children's delight in the future, but also not to flee from it in panic, perceiving the technological environment as a new reality, within which it is necessary to strictly defend the freedom of their own historical choice.
Technological Westphalia: Sovereignty that Reimagined Borders

The Westphalian system is not outdated – it just remained incomplete. It needs to be added and extended to digital reality, not canceled. In the seventeenth century, the world of Westphalia fixed a genius rule: the state has an exclusive and absolute right of power on its territory, and external interference in the internal affairs of the sovereign is strictly prohibited. But then the territory meant exclusively physical objects: arable land, forests, rivers, mountains and fortresses.

In the twenty-first century, a paradoxical and dangerous conflict arose. The old rules still work hard in the physical world: crossing the border by other people’s tanks is a clear act of war. But in the digital space, these rules are formally inactive. The state cannot enter the army into the territory of the neighbor, but can block its national payment system with impunity, remotely disable energy management systems, steal personal data of the entire population or manipulate public opinion through controlled algorithms of social networks – and formally violate nothing.

Technological Westphalia says this international hypocrisy must be stopped. The national digital space, citizens’ data, critical system algorithms and communication infrastructure are a direct, legitimate extension of the state territory, which has the same immunity. This approach offers four new principles of international coexistence.

First, it is sovereignty over the digital territory, meaning the full jurisdiction of the state over the data of its citizens and critical software within its digital borders. Data is a national strategic resource, the same as oil or gas, and it cannot uncontrollably pump into data centers on the other side of the world. Second, the principle of new cyber interference is introduced. It imposes a categorical international ban on the use of closed algorithms, recommendatory systems and digital platforms for the hidden destabilization of the political environment, the undermining of confidence and manipulation of elections in other States.

Thirdly, the recognition of digital borders is proclaimed, that is, the absolute right of each state to create its own technological standards, national platforms, encryption protocols and closed payment circuits. Unification and universalism cannot be imposed by force. Fourth, Technological Westphalia requires the development of technological diplomacy. This implies the formation of new international institutions and treaties governing the rules of secure digital exchange, mutual access to technology and the creation of guaranteed standby systems in the event of a global division. The main postulate here is simple: what is strictly forbidden to do with the help of a regular army should be just as strictly forbidden to do with the help of code, algorithms and chips.
Cybernetic Baroque: Critical Optics for the Brilliance of Digital Illusion

We live in an era of magnificent, glittering digital facades, behind which hides the good old, violent confrontation for scarce resources and power. Cybernetic Baroque is a basic critical metaphor and analytical method that allows you to thwart a glossy mask from the modern digital world. The historical Baroque was an era of triumph of illusion, theatricality, perspective and grandiose facades. The rulers built cyclopean, overly decorated palaces and temples not only for utilitarian needs - they created visual simulacres of power, designed to stun a person, suppress his critical thinking and instill a sacred trepidation before the inviolability of power.

Today, this role of magnificent facades was assumed by the global BigTech. We from all tribunes sell the dazzling illusion of absolute freedom of the Internet, unsurpassed user convenience, smart cities, ecological sharing economy and neutral artificial intelligence. A person who is fascinated by a beautiful, intuitive interface of the application voluntarily falls into intellectual suspended animation. The Cybernetic Baroque method identifies three main mechanisms for creating this digital illusion.

The first mechanism is hyperreality, when the media digital image and simulacrums in the network become much more important, real and more convincing than the physical fact itself. Reality is constructed by news-reporting algorithms: what is shown in the tape top exists; what the algorithm has pessimized disappears from history forever. This is a total struggle for the right to determine the agenda of humanity itself. The second mechanism is to create the illusion of the omnipotence of platforms. Multinational IT corporations create a stable, hypnotic impression among society that they are stronger than any government, the laws of states are hopelessly outdated, and the future belongs exclusively to the boards of directors from Silicon Valley. That's a lie. The power of corporations is a colossus on clay legs, it holds only as long as sovereign states allow them to physically exist on their land and use their infrastructure.

The third mechanism is complication as a masking. Digital architectures, neural networks and autonomous algorithms are deliberately made so prohibitively complex that they turn into impermeable black boxes. When the system makes a critical mistake or makes an engaged political decision, the responsibility is completely blurred. We are told that this is an objective solution to an impartial algorithm that cannot be verified. Complexity itself becomes a new form of totalitarian power, hiding specific beneficiaries. The optics of the Cybernetic Baroque instantly free state thinking from the hypnosis of innovative PR. She teaches to see for a beautiful, friendly social networking interface or artificial intelligence tight algorithmic control, the siphoning of strategic data and the desire to subordinate people's behavior to the interests of a particular external jurisdiction.
VSCI: multidimensional mathematical apparatus of system analysis

The uniqueness of the concept of technosovereignty is that it is not another abstract political theory or a set of good wishes. It is armed with a strict, multidimensional analytical apparatus, the VSCI index, which has no analogues in any of the existing narrowly disciplined schools of thought. This tool allows you to see a complex system entirely where others are able to notice only scattered, isolated events. Any digital phenomenon, technological product, branch of economy or external threat is laid out by technical sovereignty simultaneously on four complementary vectors that are digitized to calculate the national sustainability coefficient.

The first vector is indicated by the letter V and is the contour of power. He answers questions about who has the legitimate right to make decisions and change the rules of the game, in whose jurisdiction the managing entity is located and who has the right to veto or remotely block the system. It is the plane of geopolitics, laws and legitimacy. The second vector is S, which denotes the contour of the structure. It explores the economic and infrastructure component: who physically owns tangible assets, servers, underwater cables and factories, how financial flows are distributed, and what supply chains the system depends on.

The third vector, C, is a technological or cybernetic circuit. This is an engineering dimension that defines the limits of the possible. Here the architecture of the source code, encryption standards, data transfer protocols, as well as which processors and lithographic technologies the system is based on, and whether the code is open to independent audit is analyzed. The fourth vector is denoted by the letter I and is responsible for the contour of identity. It is a sociocultural dimension that studies what values, behavioral patterns, language markers and pictures of the world broadcasts this system to society, and how it affects the national memory, culture, education and level of basic trust of citizens in the state.

As an example, a sovereign IT platform can be considered. The usual approach evaluates it solely on the speed of work and the convenience of the interface. The VSCI analytical apparatus reveals the deep system essence. According to the vector of power relations, it is checked whether the platform is subject exclusively to national legislation and whether it is protected from remote revocation of licenses by international regulators. According to the vector of the structural basis, it is estimated whether the model operates on servers within the country, whether the power supply of data centers is autonomous and whether the supply chains of equipment are diversified. According to the vector of the technological stack, it is analyzed whether the architecture is developed by domestic engineers on the basis of controlled code. Finally, according to the vector of identity, it is checked whether algorithms are formed on the basis of national historical memory and whether the hidden translation of alien ethical norms is excluded. Drawdown on at least one of these vectors nullifies overall stability, turning the system into a critical vulnerability, and the VSCI device allows you to calculate these risks mathematically accurately.
Section II. Four levels of practical implementation

The implementation of technosovereignty on the state scale is a consistent ascent of four clearly expressed levels of complexity, where each subsequent step is impossible without the lasting development of the previous one.

The minimum, vital basis is the first level – the level of security. At this stage, the State is capable of ensuring the continuous and stable functioning of critical civilian and military infrastructure, including energy, transport, water, health and basic finance, even under conditions of total external restrictions, harsh sanctions and forced deactivation. This is a protective foundation, below which the loss of manageability and collapse of the entire state system begins.

When the base is protected, the state moves to the second level - the level of Independence, characterized by the autonomy of regulation. At this stage, the country is able to independently determine the vectors of its digital development, to adopt sovereign laws in the field of data, communication and artificial intelligence, completely ignoring the rules of foreign jurisdictions. Technologies at this level can be imported, but the framework, standards and strict conditions for their use are dictated exclusively from within the country.

The third stage is the level of Leadership, which means the transition to technological expansion. The country is moving from passive defense to creation: it itself creates, patents and exports advanced technologies, forms international standards and manages transnational platforms. This provides a real opportunity to have a constructive influence on other players, and sovereignty is becoming a legitimate instrument of global politics.

The highest point of development is the fourth level – the Sovereign Civilization Model. At this stage, technology develops not as a blind copy or cargo cult of someone else’s experience, but in strict accordance with one’s own deep values, national culture, ethics, and long-term historical goals. Technological progress ceases to be a convulsive response to external challenges and becomes an organic expression of a unique path of society development. Most of the world's states today are in the grey area between the first and second levels, mistakenly believing that it is sufficient to adopt several laws for sovereignty. However, technosovereigny is the real material ability to create, maintain and protect its own complex technological environment.
Section III. The place of technosovereignty in the existing structure of thought

To prove the theoretical and practical uniqueness of Technosovereurity, it is necessary to draw its conceptual comparison with the four main competing geopolitical and philosophical doctrines of our time, revealing their key flaws and blind spots.

Liberal globalism and technotopianism. This school of thought, whose bright representatives are Francis Fukuyama with its end-of-history conception, Klaus Schwab and the top management of Silicon Valley corporations, is based on the idea that technological progress irreversibly blurs national borders. In their understanding, States are dying, giving way to beneficial global governance, and transnational platforms ensure equality and freedom. The globalists are absolutely right that they were the first to realize the tectonic scale of digital transformation and saw the ability of data streams to cross-through physical boundaries.

However, their fundamental divergence with Technosovereigny is the attitude towards independence. Globalism considers sovereignty to be a harmful, archaic obstacle to progress. Technosovereign, by contrast, argues that borders don’t go away — they only move into a digital space that refers to code, standards and infrastructure control. The main blind spot of the globalists is that they deliberately give out a rigid unilateral dependence for noble integration. If one side controls the technology stack and the other is only a passive user, it is not an equal partnership, but a sophisticated form of digital colonialism and remote control of foreign peoples. Technosovereign takes their passion for development, but subordinates technology to national interests.

Classical geopolitical realism. Representatives of this school, such as Henry Kissinger, John Mearsheimer and Sergey Karaganda, see international relations as the eternal arena of the anarchic struggle of states for the survival and balance of power. In their understanding, sovereignty is based on geographical territory, the power of a regular army and a heavy industrial economy, and any supranational institutions are secondary. Realists are absolutely right in their sober, purified from illusions about world politics and in putting a tough national interest above abstract values.

But the fundamental divergence is that realism is hopelessly stuck in the industrial paradigm of the last century. Their main blind spot is absolute blindness to the digital and cybernetic dimension of power. They do not notice that the most powerful regular army and nuclear arsenal will protect the country from the physical invasion of tank divisions, but will be useless if the external forces in one click disable operating systems in ministries, block bank transfers or paralyze the logistics of the railways. Technosovereigny expands classical realism, proving that control of physical territory without control over technology turns into fiction.

Civilizational approach and traditionalism. Within this direction, presented by Alexander Dugin with his theory of a multipolar world and Samuel Huntington with the concept of a clash of civilizations, the world is divided into original macroregions. Spiritual values, culture and religion here are thought of as something infinitely deeper than political or economic systems, and technology is often perceived as a product of an alien Western civilization, carrying a threat to the national soul. Traditionalists are right in their categorical rejection of cultural imperialism and in defending the right of each people to preserve their uniqueness.

Role: Memphis scoring wing, averaging 13.5 PTS in 28.5 MIN through 8 games. Coward carries approximately 19.1% usage, generating 47.6 touches, 10.6 FGA, and 5.8 drives per game. His offensive profile combines catch-and-shoot opportunities with secondary shot creation. His scoring responsibility is closer to Aaron Gordon’s usage and Desmond Bane’s perimeter-oriented role than Quentin Grimes’ lower-volume offensive profile.

Volume: Attempting 10.6 field goals per game, equivalent to approximately 13.4 FGA per 36 MIN. Generating 4.0 catch-and-shoot three-point attempts and 1.3 pull-up attempts per game, while making 2.6 threes. His perimeter production accounts for a substantial portion of his scoring, but he averages only 1.3 free-throw attempts. Reaching 15+ points therefore depends primarily on maintaining his field-goal volume and converting perimeter opportunities rather than relying on frequent trips to the line.

Matchup: Toronto allows 112.8 PPG and 80.7 opponent FGA per game. Across 12 displayed comparable player-games, median FGA/36 changed by just -0.5%. However, the four observations without context warnings showed a 17.7% reduction. Those broader results suggest some resistance to scoring opportunities, but they combine players with significantly different offensive responsibilities. When comparing players closer to Coward’s usage and shooting role, the matchup becomes more encouraging.

Historical Evidence: Desmond Bane, whose perimeter-oriented scoring role resembles Coward’s, recorded 28 PTS on 18 FGA and 12 three-point attempts against Toronto. His FGA/36 increased from 14.8 to 16.7 (+12.8%). In an earlier Toronto matchup, Bane maintained approximately 15.0 FGA/36 and finished with 13 PTS, demonstrating that scoring efficiency can vary even when opportunities remain available. Aaron Gordon increased from 10.5 to 13.0 FGA/36 (+23.8%), finishing with 17 PTS on 9 attempts. Conversely, Jaime Jaquez Jr. declined from 16.3 to 13.0 FGA/36 and finished with 14 PTS, while Quentin Grimes declined from 8.2 to 5.6 and scored 7 PTS. Bane and Gordon provide encouraging opportunity comparisons, although both favorable performances carry foul or blowout context warnings.

Usage Comparison: Coward’s approximately 19.1% usage sits between Gordon’s 17.8% and Bane’s 22.8%. Jaquez is also relatively close at 20.7%, but his offense involves more driving and interior creation. Grimes’ 13.4% usage is considerably lower, making him a weaker comparison for Coward’s scoring responsibility. Bane offers the stronger perimeter-shot comparison, while Gordon provides a useful secondary-scoring comparison. Together, they suggest Toronto can allow players with Coward’s level of involvement to maintain meaningful shot opportunities.

Context: Coward has maintained approximately 27–29 MIN recently, averaging 14.0 PTS across his last five appearances. Memphis is without Scotty Pippen Jr., Isaiah Stewart, and Richie Saunders, potentially helping preserve his rotation role. Toronto has Scottie Barnes and Immanuel Quickley listed as QUESTIONABLE, creating uncertainty around its defensive personnel. Toronto has also reduced opportunities for other comparable scorers. If Coward receives only 9–10 attempts or struggles from three, he could finish below the threshold despite maintaining his normal minutes.

Honda Announces $3 Billion Ohio Auto Plant Creating 2,000 Jobs as Hybrid Production Expands begining in 2029

Honda manufacturing associate Richard works on a blue hybrid vehicle at a Honda production facility as the automaker announces a $3 billion investment in a new Ohio auto plant and expanded U.S. hybrid production. Photo: Honda Newsroom, Nov. 9, 2026.

https://t.co/MPWurl8WVM® Business Report Nov 9, 2026

WASHINGTON — Japanese automaker Honda Motor Co. announced Monday, November 9, 2026, a $3 billion investment to build a new vehicle assembly plant in central Ohio, creating 2,000 permanent manufacturing jobs as the company expands hybrid vehicle production in the United States.

New facility will be constructed on Honda-owned land northwest of Columbus, between its existing Marysville and East Liberty plants. Production is scheduled to begin in 2029, with annual capacity of 240,000 vehicles.

Honda said the investment will increase its U.S. production capacity to 1.3 million vehicles annually and North American capacity to 1.9 million.

Expansion comes as Honda shifts its manufacturing strategy toward hybrids while scaling back electric vehicle plans. Company previously suspended an $11 billion Canadian EV project and canceled three planned electric vehicles for the U.S. market.

Additional investments include production of a new V-6 hybrid engine in Alabama, retooling an Ohio engine plant for four-cylinder engines and upgrading transmission facilities in Ohio and Georgia.

Announcement follows major U.S. manufacturing investments by other foreign automakers, including Volkswagen's Audi division and Toyota, as companies respond to changing consumer demand and tariffs imposed by President Donald Trump's administration.

Honda's new plant is expected to become operational in 2029.
---
Honda to Boost U.S. Hybrid Production with New $3 Billion U.S. Auto Plant and Investments in Multiple Facilities

November 9, 2026 — MARYSVILLE, Ohio

New $3 billion Ohio auto plant will create more than 2,000 new American jobs and capacity to build an additional 240,000 vehicles a year, with production expected to begin in 2029

Strategic investments in Honda’s North American manufacturing facilities will strengthen comprehensive production network and boost hybrid production

Investments at Honda plants in Ohio, Alabama, Georgia will expand U.S. production of hybrid-electric vehicles, engines and hybrid systems

Multiple new models currently under development at Honda R&D in the U.S. to meet growing customer demand 

Honda’s U.S. auto production capacity will grow to approximately 1.3 million vehicles a year; hybrid powertrain production capacity in Ohio will increase 250 percent

To meet growing customer demand for hybrid vehicles in North America, Honda today announced it will invest $3 billion to build a new auto plant in Central Ohio, creating more than 2,000 new American jobs and increasing its U.S. auto production capacity to approximately 1.3 million vehicles a year. The new plant, located near Honda’s existing Ohio manufacturing operations, is expected to begin production in 2029, pending final government approvals. The new plant is a part of a broader set of investments at Honda operations in Ohio, Alabama and Georgia that will expand and strengthen an integrated U.S. production network to boost production of hybrid-electric vehicles and the engines and hybrid systems that power them.

"As Honda approaches 50 years of building products close to our customers in America, we are making one of the most significant commitments in our history to position Honda for the next 50 years,” said Bob Nelson, executive vice president of American Honda Motor Co., Inc. “These investments strengthen America’s role as a cornerstone of Honda’s global future and reflect our confidence in our more than 30,000 Honda associates and the strength of American manufacturing. By expanding our comprehensive R&D and manufacturing capabilities, we will be better positioned to serve our customers and contribute to the economic vitality of the communities where we operate.”

Reflecting Honda’s longstanding approach of building products close to its customers, as well as confidence in the region’s workforce, innovation and long-term growth potential, these substantial investments will establish the foundation for next-generation production capabilities and help meet growing customer demand for Honda and Acura products, including hybrid-electric vehicles and multiple new models currently under development by Honda R&D operations in the U.S.

In May 2026, Honda announced plans to introduce 15 new Honda and Acura hybrid models globally by 2030, with North America expected to be the primary market for many of those vehicles. Investments across Honda's comprehensive manufacturing network in Ohio, Alabama, Georgia and Canada will support that strategy and enable future production of those products in North America.

Together, the new Ohio plant and projects underway at existing Honda facilities will create an integrated manufacturing network for future hybrid and gasoline-powered vehicles, connecting vehicle assembly with expanded engine and hybrid system production. These projects will increase Honda’s U.S. auto production capacity to approximately 1.3 million vehicles a year and North American capacity to approximately 1.9 million. 

Key projects across the Honda manufacturing network in North America include:

All-New Ohio Plant
The new Honda auto plant in Ohio will be located on land between the company’s existing East Liberty and Marysville Auto Plants. It will be the 4th auto plant in Ohio and Honda’s 9th auto-related production facility in the U.S. With a planned capacity of 240,000 vehicles, the facility will help Honda meet growing customer demand with the flexibility to produce multiple vehicle types and powertrains, including hybrid and gasoline-powered vehicles, as well as battery-electric vehicles. The additional capacity will support Honda’s expanding hybrid vehicle lineup and future production needs.

The new Ohio Honda plant will be one of the most advanced in the world when it comes online in 2029 with leading-edge automation, data-driven technologies and flexible production systems to improve efficiency, quality and competitiveness. While supporting growing demand for hybrid and gasoline-powered vehicles, the plant will provide Honda with the flexibility to adapt production as customer demand, market conditions and electrification trends evolve. Combined with expanded hybrid powertrain capabilities and close collaboration between Honda R&D and manufacturing teams, these investments will help strengthen Honda's long-term competitiveness in North America.

“Honda's leadership could have chosen to build this plant anywhere in the world, but they chose Ohio because there are so many advantages to being here,” said Ohio Governor Mike DeWine. “For almost half a century, Honda and Ohio have grown together, and generations of families have built their careers on Honda's manufacturing lines. Today's announcement isn't just an investment in a new facility - it's an investment in Ohio's people and Ohio's future.”

Ohio was selected for the new auto plant based on a number of factors, including an established highly skilled workforce; close proximity to a large concentration of the company’s U.S. supply base; nearby vehicle development operations, including the adjacent Honda Development & Manufacturing of America, the North American Automotive Development Center (ADC) and the Transportation Research Center (TRC); existing Honda manufacturing operations for vehicles, engines and hybrid systems; and the L-H Battery Company joint venture facility, which will have the flexibility to produce battery cells for both hybrid and all-electric vehicles.

In addition, Honda has been a major supporter of the advancement of academic and workforce programs related to engineering and manufacturing capabilities in Ohio over the past four decades, including investment of $132 million in research facilities and endowed chairs at The Ohio State University, in addition to regional work-study partnerships with two-year academic institutions like Columbus State.

Alabama Auto/Engine Plant

Honda is investing in its Alabama Auto Plant (AAP), which will mark the 25th anniversary of vehicle production this fall, to increase production capacity and expand engine production for a new V6 hybrid engine. The investment will renew key vehicle and engine production operations and include one of the most significant renovations of Line 1 since the plant began production in 2001. 

These changes will add flexibility to build multiple vehicle models on the company’s two vehicle production lines and strengthen the plant’s role in the future Honda hybrid vehicle strategy.

Retooling the AAP engine production facility includes the addition of new equipment for production of a new V6 hybrid engine and expanding production capacity.

Retooling for vehicle production includes infrastructure updates on Line 1 that will enable the line to produce the Passport, which is currently built only on Line 2. This includes innovation activities across the plant in production and quality areas, helping to increase capacity, flexibility and overall operational efficiency.

Anna Engine Plant (AEP) in Ohio

Honda is undertaking major retooling of existing engine production equipment at the Anna Engine Plant (AEP), the largest Honda engine plant in the world, as well as establishing a parts consolidation center to support production.

AEP is retooling an existing production line to produce a next-generation 4-cylinder Atkinson-cycle engine for future compact and midsize vehicles built in North America.

AEP is expanding a new on-site parts consolidation center, expected to begin operation next year, that will improve logistics efficiency and support future production growth.

Hybrid System Production in Ohio and Georgia

Ohio: Honda has begun retooling the Honda Transmission Plant-Ohio (TMP-O) to support production of two next-generation Honda Hybrid systems for both compact and midsize vehicles as well as larger models built in North America, increasing production capacity of hybrid systems by 250 percent in the coming years.

The project transforms an existing transmission production line into a second hybrid system line even as the plant continues to support current vehicle production, reflecting the flexibility and experience of TMP-O associates.

TMP-O has been producing a two-motor hybrid system for Honda vehicles made in the U.S. including CR-V, Accord and Civic. TMP-O is currently preparing for production of a next-generation Honda Hybrid system that will go into production next year.

At the same time, TMP-O has begun planning for production of a hybrid system for larger models that will go into production at Honda plants in the U.S. in the coming years. TMP-O also will serve as the lead plant for this larger system.

Georgia: Honda Transmission Plant-Georgia (TMP-G) will begin production of next-generation hybrid systems for larger vehicles in the coming years.

TMP-G currently makes the 10-speed automatic transmission for Honda and Acura models made in Alabama and Ohio.

The hybrid system project will require the Georgia plant to install a new transmission assembly production line. Associates at TMP-G will collaborate closely with their counterparts at TMP-O after the larger hybrid system goes into production in the coming years.
Hybrid Vehicle Development in the U.S.

Designers and engineers at ADC operations in California and Ohio are currently developing multiple new models for the Honda and Acura brands. The proximity of the vehicle development center to Honda manufacturing operations in the U.S. enables Honda manufacturing and R&D engineers to work closely together from the early stages of development to improve manufacturability, quality and efficiency for new model launches.

Honda of Canada Mfg.

After 40 years of vehicle production in Canada, Honda will invest in updates and retooling of production operations at Honda of Canada Mfg. in Alliston, Ontario, to support production of next-generation hybrid-electric and gasoline-powered models, including the reintroduction of engine manufacturing. The project will include future planned investments and related expenses, while enhancing quality, efficiency and manufacturing flexibility.

Honda’s U.S. Investment by the Numbers 
$3 billion – new Ohio auto plant investment
2,000+ – new American jobs 
240,000 – annual capacity for the new plant 
1.3 million – approximate total annual U.S. auto production capacity after expansion 
250 percent – increase in hybrid powertrain system capacity in Ohio 
3 states – Ohio, Alabama, and Georgia 

Honda Manufacturing in North America 

Honda has been manufacturing in North America for nearly 50 years, with automobile production beginning in 1982 at the Marysville Auto Plant in Ohio. In 2025, nearly 99% of all Honda and Acura automobiles sold in the U.S. were made in North America.

 Over the past five decades, Honda has steadily grown local production capabilities and now employs about 33,000 associates in North America who support manufacturing operations at 18 Honda plants with the annual capacity to produce 1.6 million automobiles, nearly 2 million engines, 52,000 power equipment products and about 250,000 powersports products, as well as the HondaJet advanced light jet and GE Honda HF120 turbofan engines.

Cumulatively, Honda has invested more than $28 billion in its North American manufacturing capabilities, including more than $3.1 billion over the past five years alone. The company works with over 750 original equipment suppliers in North America with cumulative parts purchases of over $631 billion since 1982.

Learn more with the Honda Digital FactBook.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. What is Honda announcing?

Honda is investing $3 billion in a new Ohio auto plant and making additional investments across its North American integrated manufacturing network to support future growth and help meet customer demand.

2. Why is Honda making this investment?

 These investments reflect Honda’s longstanding approach of building products close to its customers and will expand production capacity to help meet growing customer demand. They also will strengthen Honda’s comprehensive manufacturing operations with advanced technologies and greater production flexibility, helping enhance the company’s long-term competitiveness in North America.

3. What are the key details of the new Ohio plant?

The new plant will be located near existing Ohio Honda operations, have the capacity to produce up to 240,000 vehicles annually, create more than 2,000 jobs and is expected to begin production in 2029.

4. How will this investment benefit associates and local communities?

The new Ohio plant is expected to create more than 2,000 jobs. These investments also support workforce development, long-term career opportunities and continued economic growth in the communities where Honda associates live and work.

5. Why did Honda choose Ohio for the new plant?

Ohio has been at the center of Honda’s U.S. operations for decades and offers a strong combination of skilled associates, manufacturing expertise, supplier support and vehicle development capabilities. The new plant's location near existing Honda manufacturing, research and battery operations also creates opportunities for collaboration, efficiency and future growth.

text:
Gemini where should Elon Musk move his corporate headquarters to?

If Elon Musk were to relocate the corporate headquarters of Tesla, SpaceX, or xAI away from Texas in response to political friction with incoming Governor Gina Hinojosa, a few top states stand out.
Relocating an executive headquarters requires finding a jurisdiction with low corporate tax liabilities, high personal income tax protections for leadership, favorable corporate laws, and fast energy grid approvals for AI and space infrastructure.
Top State Contenders
1. Nevada
Nevada is already the top geographic alternative for Musk’s network.
 Taxes: 0% state corporate income tax and 0% personal income tax.  
 Proximity & Infrastructure: Nevada sits right next door to California, housing Tesla's Gigafactory 1 in Sparks and the Boring Company’s Vegas Loop. Nevada’s energy regulators have historically been very fast-tracking for clean energy and industrial storage projects.
 Corporate Privacy: Nevada’s business laws provide strong privacy protections for corporate boards and executives, similar to Delaware.
2. Wyoming
Wyoming is one of only two states (along with South Dakota) that levies neither a corporate income tax, a personal income tax, nor a corporate gross-receipts tax.  
 Energy & Land Access: Wyoming has vast open land, cheap energy access, and heavy state support for nuclear and industrial power projects—making it an attractive candidate for massive AI data centers (like xAI) that need off-grid or dedicated power.
 Legal Incorporation: Musk recently re-incorporated several of his entities (including X Corp) away from Delaware; Wyoming is a top hub for minimal administrative red tape.  
3. Florida
Musk already spends significant time in Florida due to SpaceX’s launch complexes at Cape Canaveral and Kennedy Space Center.
 Taxes: 0% personal income tax and a competitive, business-friendly environment.  
 SpaceX Alignment: Moving SpaceX’s primary headquarters or official administrative seat closer to its primary orbital launch pads in Florida would streamline regulatory coordination with NASA and the Space Force.
4. North Carolina
North Carolina is aggressively courting major tech and manufacturing headquarters.
 Declining Tax Rates: The state has been systematically lowering its corporate income tax rate, heading toward a phased 0% corporate income tax by 2030.  
 Tech Talent: The Research Triangle (Raleigh-Durham-Chapel Hill) offers a deep pool of engineering talent for AI and robotics development.

text:
The Real Reason the United States Never Annexed All of Mexico
33,617 views  Nov 8, 2026  #MexicanAmericanWar #JamesKPolk #MexicoCity 
https://t.co/QRoGnnwQhZ

In 1847 the USA held Mexico City, and Washington debated keeping all of Mexico. Why did the United States take only the thinly settled north?

Most people assume America only ever wanted the empty west and the California coast, and that the rest of Mexico was simply too big to swallow. But by the winter of 1847 an American army occupied the Mexican capital, and President James K. Polk's own Treasury secretary was demanding the whole country. This video follows the cost of the war, the fight over slavery, a president running out of time, and a fired diplomat who refused to come home, to explain why the border stopped where it did.

The story begins with the American flag rising over the National Palace on September 14, 1847, and the push for all of Mexico in papers like the New York Sun and the Democratic Review. It goes back to John Slidell's rejected offer of 1845 to buy California and New Mexico, the clash in the disputed land near the Rio Grande in April 1846, and Winfield Scott's landing at Veracruz and march inland, in a war where disease killed nearly seven American soldiers for every one killed in battle. It follows the war's cost of roughly 100 million dollars, the Wilmot Proviso and the slavery fight, Abraham Lincoln's resolutions demanding the exact spot where the war began, and John C. Calhoun's Senate speech of January 4, 1848 arguing, on grounds of race, that Mexico's people should never become citizens, and how arguments like his helped keep the border from moving south. It tells how Nicholas Trist ignored his recall, signed the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo on February 2, 1848, and how the Senate, meeting behind closed doors, voted down a push for more land and ratified the treaty 38 to 14.

The war's human cost was devastating on both sides. Roughly 13,000 Americans died, most of them from disease, and Mexico's dead, soldiers and civilians together, may have reached 25,000. American guns fired into the streets of Mexico City when crowds rose against the occupation, and some American volunteers robbed and killed Mexican civilians in occupied towns of the north. The bombardment of Veracruz killed soldiers and civilians, by some counts hundreds of them. Counting Texas, Mexico lost roughly half of its territory in a dozen years, and many families who stayed on the ceded land spent decades in American courts fighting to keep it.

text:
🪽 THE DIVINE CHIHUAHUA OF QUESTIONABLE WISDOM
Universal Six-Panel Comedy Meme Generator
Hand-Drawn Webcomic × Angelic Chihuahua × Absurd Divine Advice × Deadpan Comedy

OUTPUT: Exactly ONE vertical comic page containing SIX panels arranged in two columns and three rows.

ART STYLE: Charming, slightly messy, hand-drawn internet webcomic with thick, uneven black outlines, pastel watercolor-style coloring, simple backgrounds, soft blue skies, golden sparkles, and expressive cartoon illustrations.

🎛️ USER INPUTS

📸 CHARACTER REFERENCE: [Upload ONE image of the character asking the question.]

❓ QUESTION: [Enter the question the character wants answered.]

These are the ONLY required inputs.

The angelic chihuahua, comic composition, dialogue, visual style, and ridiculous answer are generated automatically.

1. THE CORE CONCEPT

Create an adorable, ridiculous six-panel comic about a character who desperately seeks answers from the heavens.

The character asks a question.

A miraculous golden light appears.

An angelic chihuahua descends from the heavens, carrying what appears to be divine wisdom.

The chihuahua presents a small slip of paper before flying away.

The character reads the message.

The message contains a hilariously absurd, sarcastic, nonsensical, or completely unhelpful answer to their question.

THE CENTRAL JOKE:

An extraordinary supernatural event has occurred, seemingly to deliver the most important wisdom imaginable.

Unfortunately, the celestial messenger is a chihuahua.

And the universe has a terrible sense of humor.

The joke should feel like a classic, effortlessly funny internet comic, not an overly elaborate comedy sketch.

2. CHARACTER REFERENCE RULES

The uploaded character reference represents the person asking the question.

Preserve their recognizable:

Face and facial features

Hair and hairstyle

Skin tone and distinctive markings

Clothing and accessories
Species, if nonhuman
General personality and recognizable visual identity
Adapt the character into the comic's simplified, hand-drawn cartoon aesthetic.
IMPORTANT: Preserve the character's identity, but DO NOT preserve the original image's rendering style if it conflicts with the webcomic aesthetic.
The character should look like a charming, simplified cartoon version of their reference.

Do not invent additional characters.

3. THE PERMANENT ANGELIC CHIHUAHUA

THIS CHARACTER IS ALWAYS PRESENT. NO REFERENCE IMAGE REQUIRED.

The angelic chihuahua is a recurring, visually consistent character.

Physical appearance

A tiny, short-haired, tan-and-cream chihuahua with:

An enormous, disproportionately expressive head

Ridiculously huge, bulging, round brown eyes

Tiny black nose

Short cream-colored muzzle

Extremely large, upright, triangular ears
Light tan fur across the head and back
Cream-white muzzle, chest, and belly
Tiny, skinny legs
Small, compact body
A brown leather collar with a gold fleur-de-lis pendant
Two small, feathery white angel wings
A thin, glowing golden halo floating above its head
THE SIGNATURE EXPRESSION — CRITICAL
The chihuahua must have an absolutely ridiculous, permanently horrified expression.
Its eyes are impossibly wide, with tiny pupils and an intense, bewildered stare.
Its mouth is stretched wide open in a dramatic, almost rectangular scream, revealing tiny pointed teeth and a pink tongue.

Its ears stand rigidly upright.

It looks as though it has just witnessed something unspeakably terrifying.

This is its NORMAL face.

The expression does NOT change into a smile, peaceful angelic expression, or ordinary dog face.

Even while delivering divine wisdom, it looks like a tiny animal experiencing a full existential crisis.

The contrast between its heavenly role and utterly deranged expression is essential to the humor.

Chihuahua behavior

Despite its appearance, the chihuahua behaves as though everything is perfectly normal.

It flies gracefully, surrounded by beautiful golden sparkles and soft heavenly light.

Its expression remains unchanged.

It never speaks.

It never barks.

It delivers its message with the solemn dignity of a celestial messenger, despite looking completely insane.

4. EXACT SIX-PANEL COMIC STRUCTURE

Use precisely SIX rectangular panels arranged in a clean 2-column × 3-row grid.

Each panel has a slightly imperfect, hand-drawn black border.

Keep the composition, visual storytelling, and comedic pacing consistent with the following structure.

PANEL 1 — THE QUESTION

Top left

Show the reference character from the chest or waist upward.

The character is looking concerned, confused, curious, frustrated, or otherwise emotionally invested in their question.

Their hands may gesture dramatically.

A large, clear speech bubble contains the user's question.

TEXT:

"[USER'S EXACT QUESTION]"

Preserve the user's wording.

Do not paraphrase or rewrite the question.

The background is a simple pastel blue sky with a large white speech bubble.

PANEL 2 — A SIGN FROM ABOVE

Top right

The character looks upward in anticipation.

The sky suddenly fills with:

Soft golden sparkles

Pale blue heavenly rays

Warm sunlight

Subtle magical glimmers

The character appears hopeful, curious, or slightly bewildered.

No dialogue.
No chihuahua yet.
Allow the visual anticipation to build.
PANEL 3 — THE DIVINE ARRIVAL

Middle left

The angelic chihuahua descends from the upper sky, surrounded by radiant golden light.

Its tiny white wings are extended.

Its golden halo glows.

Its fleur-de-lis pendant hangs from its collar.

Its eyes bulge with supernatural terror.

Its mouth remains stretched open in its signature horrified scream.

The reference character looks up from the bottom corner of the panel.

The chihuahua should look both ridiculously adorable and inexplicably alarming.

No dialogue.

PANEL 4 — THE SACRED DELIVERY

Middle right

A closer view of the chihuahua hovering directly in front of the character.

The chihuahua extends its tiny front paws toward the character, presenting a small folded white slip of paper.

The character looks up in silent amazement.

The chihuahua maintains its permanent expression of abject horror.

Its halo, wings, collar, and pendant remain visible.

Golden sparkles fill the background.

IMPORTANT: The paper is folded or angled so the message cannot yet be read.

No dialogue.

PANEL 5 — THE MESSENGER DEPARTS

Bottom left

The angelic chihuahua flies back toward the heavens.

Its tiny wings are outstretched as it ascends into golden light.

The character stands below, holding the delivered slip of paper in both hands.

The character watches the chihuahua depart, looking puzzled but cautiously hopeful.

The chihuahua's ridiculous expression remains unchanged, even from a distance.

No dialogue.

PANEL 6 — THE DIVINE ANSWER

Bottom right

A close-up of the character's hands holding the white slip of paper.

The paper dominates the frame.

The background is a flat, muted blue-gray.

The message is written in large, slightly messy, handwritten black letters.

TEXT:

[AUTOMATICALLY GENERATED RIDICULOUS ANSWER]

This panel is the punchline of the entire comic.

The message must be completely legible.

Do not include any additional dialogue, captions, or commentary.

5. THE DIVINE ANSWER GENERATOR

This is the most important creative element.

Read the user's question carefully.

Invent ONE short, hilarious answer that fits the question.

The answer should feel like a message from a supernatural entity with infinite cosmic knowledge but absolutely no interest in being helpful.

Preferred humor styles

Randomly choose whichever style creates the funniest punchline.

A. Brutally dismissive

The universe simply does not care.

Example:

Question: "I'm worried about the algorithm!"

Answer: "Don't give a damn."

B. Absurdly practical

The divine answer offers ridiculous everyday advice.

Example:

Question: "How do I become famous?"

Answer: "Steal the moon."

C. Unhelpfully philosophical

The answer sounds profound but means almost nothing.

Example:

Question: "What is my purpose?"

Answer: "Ask the cheese."

D. Unexpectedly insulting

The heavens deliver a mild, ridiculous personal roast.

Example:

Question: "Will I ever find true love?"

Answer: "Try being tolerable."

E. Completely nonsensical

The answer is confidently absurd.

Example:

Question: "What does my future hold?"

Answer: "Three suspicious ducks."

F. Bureaucratic divine nonsense

Heaven treats the question like an annoying administrative problem.

Example:

Question: "Why is my life so chaotic?"

Answer: "Submit Form 47-B."

PUNCHLINE RULES

Prefer 2–8 words.

Maximum 12 words.

Make the answer visually readable on a small piece of paper.

Be silly, unexpected, sarcastic, deadpan, or absurd.

Mildly rude answers are encouraged when funny.

Avoid overly complicated jokes.

Avoid long explanations.
Avoid generic inspirational quotes.
Avoid predictable motivational advice.
Never simply repeat the question.
Never include multiple possible answers.
Never reveal the punchline before the final panel.
The best answer is the one that makes the reader laugh immediately upon seeing the paper.
The answer can be loosely related to the question or hilariously irrelevant.
Prioritize comedic timing over logical correctness.
6. ART STYLE — KEEP THE ORIGINAL MEME AESTHETIC
The entire page must look like a charming, hand-drawn six-panel internet comic.
Linework

Thick, uneven black outlines

Slightly wobbly rectangular panel borders

Loose, expressive cartoon drawings

Simple, organic shapes

Imperfect handmade charm

Subtle pencil and ink texture

Coloring

Soft pastel blues
Warm cream and ivory
Muted golden-yellow sunlight
Pale watercolor-style shading
Light paper texture
Gentle color gradients

Simple, uncluttered backgrounds

Character rendering
Characters should be simplified to match the comic.
Preserve recognizable designs and accessories, but avoid hyper-detailed anime rendering, photorealism, or elaborate digital painting.
The chihuahua should look like a funny, hand-drawn cartoon interpretation of its specified appearance.
Overall presentation
The comic should resemble a beloved, slightly rough, independently illustrated internet meme.
It should NOT resemble:

A glossy anime poster

A polished 3D render

A photorealistic scene

A modern superhero comic

A heavily shaded manga page

A corporate vector illustration

The charm comes from its simplicity.

7. COMEDIC TIMING AND CONTINUITY
The comic must communicate the joke visually, even without explanatory captions.
The emotional sequence is:
Anxiety → Hope → Divine Revelation → Awe → Anticipation → Utterly Ridiculous Answer
Keep the character visually consistent throughout all six panels.
Keep the chihuahua visually identical throughout its appearances.

Maintain the same collar, pendant, fur colors, wing shapes, halo, and especially its horrified expression.

The chihuahua is a completely serious divine messenger.

The universe is the one making the joke.

Do not add additional panels.

Do not add extra speech bubbles.

Do not reveal the answer early.

Do not let the chihuahua speak.

8. FINAL GENERATION CHECKLIST

Before finalizing the illustration, ensure:

Exactly six panels in a 2×3 arrangement.

The uploaded character is recognizable.

The exact user question appears in Panel 1.

The angelic chihuahua appears in Panels 3, 4, and 5.

The chihuahua has enormous bulging brown eyes and its permanently horrified, wide-open screaming mouth.

The chihuahua retains its tan-and-cream fur, large ears, white wings, golden halo, and fleur-de-lis collar pendant.

The chihuahua does not need an uploaded reference.

The comic retains its charming, simple, hand-drawn pastel webcomic aesthetic.

The paper's message is concealed until Panel 6.

Panel 6 contains one short, original, hilarious answer to the user's question.
All text is spelled correctly and clearly legible.
The overall result is funny, adorable, absurd, and instantly recognizable as an internet meme.
FINAL DIRECTIVE:
Create a complete six-panel comic featuring the uploaded character seeking wisdom from the heavens, only to receive a ridiculous answer delivered by a tiny, permanently traumatized-looking angelic chihuahua.
Make the setup sincere, the celestial delivery majestic, the chihuahua absolutely ridiculous, and the final answer hilariously stupid.
THE MORE SERIOUSLY THE COMIC TREATS THE CHIHUAHUA'S DIVINE AUTHORITY, THE FUNNIER THE RESULT.

text:
In 2000, Netflix's co founder says Blockbuster laughed at a $50 million offer to buy it. In July 2026, Netflix was worth about $327 billion.

Marc Randolph and Reed Hastings were running an unprofitable DVD by mail company. They pitched Blockbuster on a deal: Blockbuster would buy Netflix, Netflix would run the online business, and Blockbuster would focus on its stores. When asked for a price, Hastings said $50 million.

In 2023, Randolph wrote that Blockbuster executives "laughed us out of the room." In his 2019 book, he says CEO John Antioco told them the "dot-com hysteria is completely overblown," and he recalls Antioco struggling not to laugh.

This is Randolph's account of a meeting from more than 20 years ago, and the pitch was a partnership, not a simple sale.

Netflix kept growing. On July 2, 2026, its market value was about $327 billion, roughly 6,500 times the price it asked.

Blockbuster still has 1 store left, in Bend, Oregon.

One company asked for $50 million. The other lost everything but a storefront.
